The old lady saw Tim and said, "Come in, little boy. It's too icy outside to play. Have some soup so you don't spoil your fun." Tim went inside and had some soup. He felt warm and happy. Then, Tim went back outside and played in the snow until it was time to go home.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big jet that could fly in the air. The jet was a gift from their grandpa, who said it was very expensive and special. He told them to be careful with it and not to lose it.
One day, Tom and Lily decided to fly the jet over the fence, where they saw a big field with cows and sheep. They thought it would be fun to see the animals from the sky. They took turns to hold the remote and make the jet go up and down and left and right. They laughed and shouted as they watched the jet zoom over the field.
But then, something bad happened. The jet flew too far and they could not see it anymore. They tried to make it come back, but the remote did not work. They ran to the fence and looked for the jet, but they could not find it. They felt scared and sad. They knew their grandpa would be angry and sad too.
They did not know what to do. They did not want to tell their mom or dad, because they would be in trouble. They did not want to go to the field, because they were afraid of the cows and sheep. They sat on the grass and cried.
Then, they heard a noise. It was a whistle. They looked up and saw a man walking towards them. He had a big smile and a hat. He was holding something in his hand. It was their jet! He had found it in the field and brought it back to them.
"Hello, kids," he said. "Is this yours?"
Tom and Lily nodded. They were so happy and relieved. They ran to the man and hugged him. They thanked him for finding their jet.
The man smiled and winked. He whispered in their ears, "Don't worry, I won't tell your grandpa. But next time, be more careful with your expensive toy. It's not safe to fly it over the fence. You might lose it again, or worse, hurt someone or something."
Tom and Lily nodded again. They promised to be more careful with their jet. They took it from the man and walked back to their garden. They put the jet in a safe place and hugged each other. They learned their lesson. They were lucky to have their jet back, and to meet a kind man who helped them. They hoped to see him again someday.

Mary took the gum, put it in her mouth, and tried again. This time, she could make a big bubble. Everyone was so excited—Mary was so proud of herself!
The moral of the story is that you should never give up. With enough practice, you can succeed!

When he arrived, he saw a small sheep. The sheep said, "Hi, Tiger! I've been looking for you. Let's play together!" The tiger was so very happy to have a friend. He said, "Yes, let's play!" The sheep and the tiger played together for the rest of the day.
At night, the tiger asked the sheep to stay with him. But the sheep said, "No, I can't stay, I must go home now" The tiger was very sad. But he said goodbye and watched the sheep walk away.
The next day, the tiger heard the same voice calling to him. He raced to the same field, but it was not the sheep. It was a group of strong lions. The lions roared and said, "We want to eat you!" The poor tiger was too weak to fight them off, and he was eaten by the lions.
The End.

"Let's go, Anna!" Tom said. "Maybe we can find some toys or candy in the taxi."
Anna was scared. She knew they should not go near cars that were not theirs. But Tom was older and stronger. He pulled her by the hand and made her enter the taxi.
The taxi was empty. There were no toys or candy. Only some papers and a phone. Tom picked up the phone and pressed some buttons. He heard a voice.
"Hello, this is the taxi driver. Where are you? I need my taxi back. I have a job to do."
Tom was surprised. He dropped the phone and looked at Anna. Anna was crying. She wanted to go back to the park.
"Sorry, mister. We were just playing. We will leave now." Tom said.
But it was too late. The taxi driver was angry. He had seen them enter his taxi on his camera. He ran to the taxi and opened the door. He grabbed Tom and Anna and shouted at them.
"How dare you enter my taxi without permission? You are bad kids. You have no respect. You have made me lose my job. Now you will pay."
He locked them in the taxi and drove away. He did not care where he was going. He just wanted to teach them a lesson.
Tom and Anna were very scared. They did not know what he would do to them. They wished they had never entered the taxi. They wished they had listened to Anna. They were not lucky. They were in big trouble.

Once there was a foolish frog who liked to call from the top of a tree. He called out, "Hello!" all day long, but no one ever answered him. All the other animals thought he was being silly.
One day, a big bear happened to walk by and heard the frog calling out. The bear shouted, "Why do you call out so foolishly? No one can answer you way up there!"
The frog was embarrassed, but he answered, "I just thought maybe someone would answer."
The bear shook his head and said, "You should go down to where the other animals are. Then you will find people to talk to."
The frog thought about it and realized that the bear was right. He hopped away to the ground and never called out from the top of the tree again.
The moral of the story is that if you want to communicate with others, you need to go to where they are.

Anna liked to read books. She had many books in her bookcase. She was very intelligent. She knew many things from the books.
One day, she found a new book in her bookcase. It was very small and shiny. It had a picture of a fairy on the cover. Anna was curious. She opened the book and read the first page.
"Hello, little reader," the book said. "I am a magic book. If you want to have an adventure, say the magic word: 'Shrink!'"
Anna was surprised. She had never heard a book talk before. She wondered what would happen if she said the magic word. She was brave and adventurous. She said, "Shrink!"
Suddenly, everything around her became very big. She became very small. She was as small as the book. She saw the bookcase towering over her. She saw her toys and her bed and her door. They looked like mountains and valleys and caves.
"Wow!" Anna said. "This is amazing!"
"Welcome to the magic world," the book said. "You can explore and have fun. But be careful. There are also dangers and mysteries. And remember, you can only go back to your normal size if you say the magic word again."
Anna was excited. She wanted to see the magic world. She picked up the book and put it in her pocket. She climbed down from her desk and started her adventure. She saw many wonderful and strange things. She met friendly and scary creatures. She had many stories to tell. She was very happy.

Once upon a time there was a fox. The fox was very special, he was gifted. The fox loved to explore the world. Every morning, the fox would stretch, yawn and run around the meadow looking for adventure.
One day, the fox found a special present. It was a bright red ball. The fox was so happy and he wanted to show it off to all his friends. He held it tight and ran around the meadow with it.
But soon the fox heard a noise behind him. When the fox turned around he saw a giant bear. The bear was very tall and he was angry! He roared and growled at the fox. The fox was so scared that he lost his grip on the ball. The ball went flying away, out of sight.
The fox was so sad that he ran away and never saw the bear again. But the gifted fox never gave up hope. He still believes one day he'll find that special red ball again.

Once upon a time, there was a little round bug named Bobby. Bobby was a special bug because he could glow. Every night, Bobby would light up like a little star. His glow was warm and bright.
One day, Bobby met a new friend, a butterfly named Betty. Betty saw Bobby's glow and said, "Wow! You are so bright and warm! Can you show me how to glow like you?" Bobby smiled and said, "I can try to help you, but I think you are special in your own way."
Bobby and Betty played together all day. They laughed and had fun. When the night came, Bobby started to glow. Betty looked at her wings and saw that they were shining too! They both glowed together, lighting up the night sky. Bobby and Betty were happy to be friends and share their warm glow with each other.

One day, a little boy named Tim was playing with his toy bear. He saw something unknown on the bear's face. Tim looked closer and saw it was a tiny bug. He wanted to make the bug go away.
Tim said, "Go away, bug!" But the bug did not listen. So, Tim poked the bug. The bug got scared and flew away. But, it flew right into Tim's eye. Tim felt a little pain and began to cry.
His mom heard him and came running. She asked, "What's wrong, Tim?" Tim said, "A bug flew into my eye." His mom gently wiped his eye and the bug came out. Tim felt better and said, "Thank you, mom!" They both smiled and Tim went back to playing with his toy bear.

They had a question. They wanted to ask the dog if it wanted to play with them. But they did not know how to talk to the dog. They did not know if the dog could understand them. They did not know what the dog would do.
They decided to be brave. They walked slowly to the dog. They said hello to the dog. They smiled at the dog. They hoped the dog would smile back.
The dog wagged its tail. It licked their faces. It barked happily. It wanted to play with them. Lily and Tom were happy. They ran with the dog. They threw a ball for the dog. They petted the dog. They had a lot of fun with the dog.
They found out that the dog belonged to a lady who lived near the park. The lady was nice. She said they could play with the dog anytime they wanted. She said the dog's name was Max. Lily and Tom liked Max. They liked the lady. They thanked them for letting them play.
They went back to their homes. They felt peaceful. They had made a new friend. They had learned something new. They had answered their question. They had a good day.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill covered with snow. They wanted to climb the hill and slide down on their sleds. They put on their hats, coats, boots and gloves and ran to the hill.
They took turns to climb the hill, pulling their sleds behind them. It was hard work, but they had fun. They reached the top and looked around. They saw a big lake near the hill. The lake was frozen and looked like a shiny plate. They wondered if they could slide on the lake too.
They decided to try it. They got on their sleds and slid down the hill, very fast. They reached the lake and slid on the ice. It was fun, but also scary. The ice was thin and cracked under their sleds. They heard a loud sound and felt the ice break. They fell into the cold water.
They were scared and cold. They cried for help. They saw a man near the lake. He heard them and ran to them. He had a rope and threw it to them. He pulled them out of the water and wrapped them in a blanket. He took them to his house and gave them hot chocolate and cookies.
He told them that they were lucky. The lake was very icy and dangerous. They should not slide on the ice. They should only slide on the hill. They said they were sorry and thanked him. They learned their lesson and never slid on the lake again. They still liked to climb the hill and slide down on their sleds, but they stayed away from the icy plate.

She spent every day sitting in her silver seat, and she was always very happy.
The end.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to wander in the park. They saw many things: trees, flowers, birds, dogs, and people. Sometimes they stopped to play or talk, but they always stayed close to each other.
One day, they saw a big pond with ducks and fish. Lily wanted to feed them some bread, but Ben wanted to throw stones. Lily said, "No, Ben, that is bad. You will hurt them and make them scared. Give me some bread, please."
Ben said, "No, Lily, that is boring. I want to have fun. You have enough bread, give me some stones, please."
They both pulled at the bag, but it was heavy and wide. It ripped and everything fell out. The bread and the stones went into the pond. The ducks and the fish swam away. Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They started to cry.
Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and said, "Oh, Lily and Ben, what have you done? You wasted the bread and the stones. You scared the ducks and the fish. You tore the bag and made a hole. You need to say sorry and fix this."
Lily and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, ducks. Sorry, fish. Sorry, bag." They hugged each other and said, "Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Ben." They helped mom to pick up the pieces and mend the bag. They learned to share and be kind. They still liked to wander in the park, but they never threw stones again.

Once upon a time there was a fierce dinosaur. He was very big and liked to sit alone and roar. Every day he would sit outside the cave and defend his territory.
One day, a small bunny hopped by and noticed the dinosaur.
“Hello!” said the bunny, “What are you sitting there for?”
The dinosaur was annoyed by the bunny’s intrussion, but he replied with a loud roar.
“My cave is my territory and I must protect it. This is how I sit here every day.”
The bunny felt bad for the dinosaur, so he offered his help.
“I can protect this cave too! I am bigger than I look, and very fierce,” said the bunny.
The dinosaur was happy to get the help. But, he was also a bit jealous.
The next day, the bunny was sitting in front of the cave and the dinosaur was furious. He roared and roared until all his anger was gone.
But, the bunny was afraid and he ran away. The dinosaur was alone again, but this time he had learned a lesson.
He realised that being too fierce could never make up for being lonely. The moral of the story is that it’s better to be kind than to be fierce.

Once upon a time, there was a normal boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat cherries. One day, he found a big cherry tree in the park.
Tim saw a little girl named Sue under the tree. She was sad. "Why are you sad?" Tim asked. "I want to eat a cherry, but I can't reach them," Sue said.
Tim had an idea. He picked a cherry and split it in half. He gave one half to Sue and kept the other half for himself. They both ate the cherry and smiled. From that day on, Tim and Sue became best friends and shared cherries from the tree.

Lucy wanted to help the truck. She took her toy car and went outside. She pushed her car on the new start of the road. The truck driver saw Lucy and smiled. He thanked her for helping. Lucy felt happy and went back home to play with her toy car.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal elephant named Elmer. Elmer was always very gentle, even to the smallest of animals.
One day, Elmer's best friend, a little mouse, noticed a fly buzzing around Elmer's trunk. The little mouse reached up and slapped the fly away with his tiny finger. Elmer was so happy with his friend's loyalty that he gave the mouse a big hug.
The little mouse was embarrassed, but he smiled and squeaked, "You're a very loyal elephant Elmer, you're the best."
Elmer laughed and said, "Let me show you how loyal I can be too." Elmer reached out and gently slapped the mouse on the back. The mouse was shocked but giggled and said, "Thank you Elmer, thank you for being so loyal!"

Once upon a time, there was a furry automobile named Bobby. He loved being all shined and polished. Every morning, Bobby would go out for a ride, and when he came back, he would be all muddy.
But one day, Bobby didn't polish himself after his ride. His mommy got mad at him.
“Bobby, why don’t you polish yourself after each ride?” she asked him.
“Because, the mud on my fur makes me look cooler!” he said.
Mommy shook her head. “No, Bobby. It’s important to take care of yourself. That’s why you should always polish yourself after you go out!”
Bobby listened to his mommy and decided to be a little more tidy. So, each day he would make sure to polish himself after his rides.
The moral of the story is that it's important to take care of ourselves. We should always brush up after we do something, just like Bobby!

Once upon a time there was a wild kitten. It had soft white fur, bright eyes and a pink nose. One day, it was taking a stroll off in the woods, when it suddenly stumbled upon a paw! It was huge and furry.
Startled, the little kitten slowly crept closer to the paw, careful to not make too much noise. Suddenly, the paw moved! The wild kitten jumped back, frightened.
The paw belonged to a cute little bear! "Who are you?" the bear asked.
"I'm a wild kitten," the kitten said, nervously.
"Why did you stumble on my paw?" the bear asked.
"I'm sorry," the kitten said, shrinking away.
The bear smiled. "It's ok! You can be my friend."
The wild kitten happily accepted the friendship, and they took a stroll off in the woods together. From then on, they were the best of friends!

One day, a polite cat named Sam went for a walk. He saw a long line of little ants. The ants were walking in a straight line to their home. Sam thought they looked very cute.
Sam said to the ants, "Hi ants! I like your line. Can I walk with you?" The ants said, "Yes, Sam! You can walk with us. But please be careful not to cut our line."
As they walked, a big wind came and blew a leaf into the ants' line. The leaf cut the line and the ants were now in two groups. The ants were sad and didn't know what to do.
Sam felt bad and wanted to help. He had an idea. He picked up the leaf and moved it away from the ants. The ants could now walk in a line again. They were so happy and said, "Thank you, Sam!"
From that day on, Sam and the ants were good friends. They always played together and had fun. And Sam made sure to never cut their line again.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.
"Let's go, Tim!" Lily said. "Maybe we will find something fun!"
"OK, Lily!" Tim said. "But be careful. The hill is very high and steep."
They started to climb the hill. They held hands and helped each other. They saw birds and flowers and bugs. They heard the wind and the leaves. They felt happy and curious.
When they reached the top of the hill, they saw something that made them stop and stare. It was an enormous house. It was old and dark and scary. It had broken windows and doors and a big chimney. It looked like no one lived there.
"Wow, look at that house, Tim!" Lily said. "Do you think there is anyone inside?"
"I don't know, Lily," Tim said. "It looks very spooky. Maybe there are ghosts or monsters."
They were both afraid, but also curious. They wanted to see the house closer. They walked slowly towards the house. They heard a loud noise. It sounded like thunder.
"BOOM!"
They jumped and screamed. They looked at the chimney. They saw a cloud of smoke and sparks. They saw something else. It was a spirit. It was white and shiny and had wings. It flew out of the chimney and into the sky.
"Hello, children!" the spirit said. "Do you want to play with me?"
Tim and Lily were very surprised. They did not know what to say. They looked at each other. They looked at the spirit. They did not know if it was friendly or scary.
"Who are you?" Tim asked. "What are you?"
"I am a fairy," the spirit said. "I live in this house. I was making magic in the fireplace. But I made a mistake and caused a big explosion. I'm sorry if I scared you."
Tim and Lily felt less afraid. They thought the spirit looked nice and kind. They wanted to know more about it.
"Can you show us your magic?" Lily asked. "Can you do tricks?"
"Of course I can," the spirit said. "I can do many things. I can make things appear and disappear. I can change colors and shapes. I can fly and sing and dance. I can make you happy and laugh. Do you want to see?"
Tim and Lily nodded. They smiled. They forgot their fear. They wanted to play with the spirit. They followed it into the house. They had a lot of fun. They learned a lot of things. They made a new friend. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little monkey named Momo. Momo loved to eat bananas. One day, Momo found a big, yellow banana on the ground. Momo was very happy and wanted to eat it. But first, Momo wanted to find a good seat to sit and enjoy the banana.
Momo looked around and saw a big tree with a nice seat on one of its branches. Momo climbed the tree and sat on the seat. Just as Momo was about to eat the banana, a little bird flew by and said, "Hello, Momo! Can I have a piece of your banana?"
Momo was a persistent little monkey and did not want to share the banana. Momo said, "No, this is my banana!" The little bird was sad and flew away. Momo felt bad for the bird but still wanted the banana all to himself.
Suddenly, the branch Momo was sitting on broke! Momo and the banana fell to the ground. The banana split in half when it hit the ground. Momo was surprised and a little sad.
Then, the little bird came back and saw the broken banana. Momo realized that sharing is important. Momo said, "Here, little bird, you can have half of my banana." The little bird was happy, and they both enjoyed the banana together. From that day on, Momo learned to share and made many friends.

"Let's run, Tim!" Lily said. "The dog might find us!"
But Tim was too tired to run. He had crawled a lot and his legs hurt. He wanted to rest for a bit.
"No, Lily, I can't run. You go first. I'll follow you," he said.
Lily did not want to leave Tim alone. She was worried about him. But she was also worried about the dog. She did not know what to do.
She looked at the bush and saw a small hole. It was big enough for them to crawl through. Maybe it was a shortcut to their real house.
"Lily, look! A hole!" Tim said. "Maybe we can crawl through it and get away from the dog!"
Lily nodded. She grabbed Tim's hand and they crawled into the hole. They hoped it would lead them to safety.
But the hole was not a shortcut. It was a trap. It was the dog's house. The dog had dug it under the bush. He had heard Tim and Lily playing and wanted to catch them. He had waited for them to crawl into his hole.
As soon as Tim and Lily came out of the hole, they saw the dog. He was big and black and had sharp teeth. He growled and jumped at them.
Tim and Lily screamed. They were in big trouble. They wished they had run away when they had the chance.

Once upon a time, there was a young rabbit called Bob. Bob was very curious about his surroundings and he enjoyed looking around in the garden. One day, he found a very long staff lying in the grass. He was so excited that he decided to take it home with him.

"Mommy! Mommy!" they cried. "The celery is burning!"

"Are you okay, Sara and Ben?" Mommy asked. "You should never play with the stove. It is very dangerous. You could get hurt or start a big fire."

"Next time, if you want to cook, ask me first," Mommy said. "I will help you and teach you how to do it safely."
Sara and Ben agreed and thanked Mommy. They learned their lesson and ate their toast. They decided they liked jam better than celery.

They licked their fingers and made a face. The sauce was terrible! It was hot and spicy and made their mouths hurt.
They wanted to get rid of the sauce, so they looked for a place to hide it. They saw a big pot on the stove and thought it was empty. They poured the sauce into the pot and put the bottle back on the shelf. They ran away to their room and drank some water.
But the pot was not empty. It had soup that Mom was making for dinner. Mom did not know that Ben and Lily had put sauce in the pot. She stirred the pot and smelled the soup. She thought it smelled strange, but she did not check. She poured the soup into bowls and called Ben and Lily to the table.
Ben and Lily came to the table and saw the soup. They felt scared. They knew they had done something bad. They did not want to eat the soup. They did not want Mom to eat the soup. They did not know what to do.
Mom took a spoonful of soup and put it in her mouth. She spit it out and coughed. The soup was terrible! It was hot and spicy and made her mouth hurt. She looked at the pot and saw the sauce. She looked at Ben and Lily and saw their guilty faces. She realized what had happened.
She was angry and sad. She asked Ben and Lily why they had done that. Ben and Lily started to cry. They said they were sorry. They said they did not mean to ruin the soup. They said they were curious about the sauce. They said they loved Mom and did not want to hurt her.
Mom felt sorry for Ben and Lily. She saw that they were sorry. She saw that they were curious. She saw that they loved her. She decided to forgive them. She hugged them and said it was okay. She said she loved them too. She said they should not play with sauce again. She said they should always tell her the truth.
She threw away the soup and made some sandwiches for dinner. She gave Ben and Lily some milk and cookies. They ate and smiled. They were happy that Mom forgave them. They learned their lesson. They never played with sauce again.

When Tilly realised that she had shouted too loudly, she said in a gentle voice, "I'm sorry, Eli". Eli nodded and smiled at his friend.
But then, out of nowhere, a big white dog started barking and jumping around the garden. Eli was scared and he shouted at the top of his voice.
Tilly took hold of his hand and said: "It's okay, Eli, don't be scared. Come on, let's go and speak to the dog together".
So the two friends walked over to the friendly dog and petted it for a while. Before long, all three of them were friends.
Tilly and Eli looked at each other and smiled. Then they said sorry to each other and hugged.
The End.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. But then they see a big dog. The dog is barking and running towards them. Tom and Mia are scared.
"Run, Mia, run!" Tom says. He grabs Mia's hand and they run to the exit. The exit is a gate that leads to the street. But the dog is faster than them. It catches up with them and jumps on Tom.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cries. The dog bites his leg. It hurts a lot. Mia is crying too. She wants to help Tom, but she is weak. She cannot push the dog away.
"Help, help, help!" Tom and Mia shout. They hope someone will hear them and come to save them. They remain at the exit, holding each other.
Then they hear a whistle. It is a man. He is wearing a uniform and a hat. He is a dog catcher. He has a net and a leash. He runs to the dog and throws the net over it. He pulls the leash and drags the dog away.
"Are you okay, kids?" the man asks. He is kind and gentle. He looks at Tom's leg and gives him a bandage. He tells Mia to stop crying and gives her a hug.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Tom and Mia say. They are happy and relieved. The man takes them to their mom, who is waiting for them at the car. She is worried and angry.
"Where were you? What happened?" she asks. Tom and Mia tell her about the dog and the man. She thanks the man and hugs Tom and Mia.
"I'm sorry, mom. We were just playing. We didn't see the dog until it was too late," Tom says.
"It's okay, Tom. I'm glad you're safe. But next time, be careful and stay away from strange dogs. They can be dangerous," mom says.
"I know, mom. I learned my lesson. I don't like dogs anymore," Tom says.
"I still like dogs, but only nice ones," Mia says.
They get in the car and go home. They are tired and sore, but they are glad they have each other. They remain friends and siblings forever.

One day, a little girl named Mia saw a caterpillar on a leaf. She wanted to touch it, but she was afraid it might bite her. She asked her mom, "Can I touch the caterpillar, mom?"
Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can, but be gentle. Caterpillars are very small and soft. They don't bite, but they might tickle your fingers."
Mia nodded and reached out her hand. She managed to touch the caterpillar very lightly. It felt fuzzy and wiggly. She giggled and said, "It's so cute, mom. Can I keep it as a pet?"
Her mom shook her head and said, "No, honey, you can't. Caterpillars need to eat leaves and grow bigger. They also need to make a cocoon and turn into a butterfly. If you keep it, it won't be happy or healthy."
Mia frowned and said, "But I want to play with it, mom. It's my friend."
Her mom hugged her and said, "I know, sweetie, but sometimes we have to let go of our friends and let them be free. How about we make a picture of the caterpillar and hang it on your wall? Then you can always remember it and see how beautiful it will become."
Mia thought for a moment and then smiled. She said, "Okay, mom, that sounds good. Can we use green and yellow crayons? Those are the caterpillar's colors."
Her mom nodded and said, "Yes, we can. Let's go inside and get some paper and crayons. But first, let's say goodbye to the caterpillar and put it back on the leaf."
Mia waved to the caterpillar and said, "Bye, caterpillar. Thank you for letting me touch you. I hope you have a nice day and become a pretty butterfly."
The caterpillar wiggled its head and seemed to say, "Bye, Mia. Thank you for being gentle and kind. I hope you have a nice day and make a clean picture."

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to go on walks with their grandma. Grandma was elderly, but she was very kind and told them stories about the animals and plants they saw. One day, they went to a trail in the park that had many rocks and trees.
"Look, grandma, a big rock!" Lily said, pointing to a gray boulder. "Can we climb on it?"
"Be careful, dear," grandma said. "The rock might be slippery or have sharp edges. Hold my hand and I'll help you."
Lily took grandma's hand and climbed on the rock. She felt proud and happy. She waved to Ben, who was looking for bugs under a leaf.
"Come on, Ben, join us!" she called.
Ben looked up and saw Lily on the rock. He wanted to climb too, but he was afraid of falling. He shook his head and said, "No, thank you. I like the bugs."
Lily frowned. She thought Ben was missing out on the fun. She had an idea. She saw a smaller rock near the big one. She picked it up and threw it at Ben, hoping to make him laugh.
But the rock flew too fast and too far. It hit a branch that was holding a bird's nest. The nest fell to the ground, and the bird flew away, screeching.
"Oh, no!" Lily gasped. "I'm sorry, bird! I didn't mean to hurt you!"
Grandma, Ben, and Lily ran to the nest. They saw three eggs inside, cracked and broken. They felt sad and sorry for the bird and its babies.
"Lily, why did you do that?" grandma asked. "That was very naughty and mean. You scared the bird and ruined its home."
Lily felt ashamed and guilty. She realized she had made a big mistake. She wished she could take it back.
"I'm sorry, grandma," she said. "I just wanted to play with Ben. I didn't think about the bird."
Grandma hugged Lily and said, "I know, dear. But you have to be more careful and gentle with nature. Rocks are not toys. They can hurt people and animals. You have to learn to respect and love all living things."
Lily nodded and said, "I will, grandma. I will."
She looked at Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to scare you or the bugs. Do you forgive me?"
Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You're my sister. I love you."
He hugged Lily and said, "Let's go find another trail. Maybe we can see some flowers or butterflies."
Lily smiled and said, "OK, Ben. Let's go."
They took grandma's hand and walked away, leaving the rock and the nest behind. They hoped the bird would find a new home and be happy again. They learned a lesson that day, and they never threw rocks again.

They went back home and played together, never leaving each other's side again.

Finally, they found a patch with tall sunflowers. Tim loved the sunflowers. "Mom, this is the most interesting patch!" he said. His mom smiled and said, "You're right, Tim. Each patch is interesting in its own way. The moral is, we should appreciate the beauty in everything."
And from that day on, Tim always looked for the interesting things in every patch he saw.

"Let's guess what it is!" Tom says. "Is it a dog?" He asks.
"No, it is not a dog. Dogs do not have horns." Jen says.
"Is it a cat?" Jen asks.
"No, it is not a cat. Cats do not have beards." Tom says.
They think hard. They look at the animal. It is eating grass. It is jumping on a rock. It is dull. It is not colorful.
"I know what it is!" Tom says. "It is a goat!"
"Yes, you are right! It is a goat!" Jen says. "How did you guess?"
"I saw a picture of a goat in a book. It looks like this." Tom says. He shows Jen the book.
"Wow, you are smart!" Jen says. "Can we pet the goat?"
"Sure, let's pet the goat!" Tom says.
They go to the goat. They touch its fur. It is soft. They give it some grass. It is happy. It says "Baa! Baa!" again.
Tom and Jen smile. They like the goat. They make a new friend in the farm.

Just then he heard a voice calling out to him to help. It was an anchor man who had lost his anchor in the stormy sea. Joe instantly turned back. He asked the anchor man if he can help him look for his anchor. They began their search and after a while they found it. Joe quickly attached the anchor to the anchor man's boat.
The anchor man thanked him and told him: "It's important to never forget to lend a helping hand to those who need it." Joe smiled and thanked the anchor man for his words. Then Joe sailed away with a heart full of joy.
The story of Joe teaches us an important lesson. We should always be ready to pause and help those in need. When you lend a helping hand, you may end up having a happy heart.

Sara was a wealthy girl who had many toys and clothes. She liked to show off her things to her friends and make them feel bad. She did not like to share or help anyone. She thought she was better than everyone else.
One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a boy playing with a ball. The boy had a big bandage on his ear and looked sad. Sara wanted to take his ball and play with it. She ran to the boy and tried to grab his ball. The boy held on to his ball and said, "No, this is mine. Please leave me alone."
Sara was angry and shouted, "You are mean and ugly. You have a bad ear and no toys. I have many toys and I am pretty. Give me your ball or I will tell my mom." The boy did not let go of his ball and said, "You are rude and selfish. You have many toys but no friends. I have a good ear and a good heart. I don't need your ball or your mom."
Sara's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Sara and the boy fighting over the ball and asked them what was going on. Sara told her mom that the boy was mean and ugly and would not give her his ball. The boy told her mom that Sara was rude and selfish and wanted to take his ball.
Sara's mom was ashamed of Sara and said, "Sara, you should not be so greedy and unkind. You have enough toys and clothes at home. You should not want to take other people's things. You should be nice and friendly to everyone. You should not judge people by how they look or what they have. You should question yourself and see if you are doing the right thing."
Sara's mom took Sara by the hand and said, "We are going home now. You need to think about what you did and say sorry to the boy. You also need to give away some of your toys and clothes to people who need them more than you. Maybe then you will learn to be happy and grateful for what you have."
Sara felt sorry for what she did and said sorry to the boy. She also gave him one of her toys and said, "Here, you can have this. I hope you like it. I hope your ear gets better soon. Do you want to be my friend?" The boy smiled and said, "Thank you. I like it. My ear will be fine soon. Yes, I want to be your friend." Sara and the boy hugged and played with the ball together. Sara's mom smiled and said, "That's better. I'm proud of you, Sara. You have learned a valuable lesson today."
The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and unkind. Be nice and friendly to everyone. Don't judge people by how they look or what they have. Question yourself and see if you are doing the right thing. Be happy and grateful for what you have.

She said to herself, "I wonder what I can do with this squash?"
A friendly voice said, "You can eat it!"
Sarah looked around and saw an old lady smiling at her.
The old lady said, "My name is Daisy and I know how to make a delicious squash dish! If you want, I can show you how to cook it."
Sarah was excited and said, "Yes, please show me!"
So Daisy taught Sarah how to prepare the purple squash. After a few minutes it was ready and Sarah ate it all up.
Sarah thanked Daisy and said, "That was so yummy! I'm so glad I found this squash."
Daisy smiled and said, "Let's swing together for a bit before you go home."
So Sarah and Daisy swung together until the sun started to go down. Sarah waved goodbye to Daisy and skipped home with a full tummy.
The End.

Sara's mom says, "Oh, Lily. I'm sorry, too. I didn't mean to hurt your feelings. I just wanted to help you. Yoga is better when you wear something that lets you move and breathe. And you are a beautiful girl. You don't need to wear ugly clothes to be pretty."
Sara says, "Mom, you are right. Lily is beautiful. And she is my friend. I don't care what she wears. I just want to do yoga with her. Can we start now?"
Sara's mom says, "Of course, Sara. You are a good friend. And Lily, you are a good friend, too. I'm sorry I was rude to you. Please forgive me. And please join us for yoga. You can wear whatever you want. As long as you are happy and comfortable."

Sara's mom says, "That sounds like a good lesson, Lily. I think we can all learn from you. And I think we can all have fun doing yoga together. Let's begin."

Jane took her tools and fixed Sue's doll. Sue was very happy. She said, "Thank you, Jane. You are the best." Jane felt good because she could help Sue. From that day on, Jane and Sue became best friends. They played together and helped each other. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. Lucy was very adventurous and loved to explore her small town. One day, Lucy was walking down the street, looking for something new to explore. As she was walking, she glanced up and saw a small light up in the sky. She was very confused, as she'd never seen anything like it before.
Lucy decided to keep walking until she got close enough to the light to take a better look. As she got closer, she realized it was a very small airplane flying around. She was so excited at the sight, she couldn't help but smile as she watched it.
When Lucy got to the spot where the plane had been, she noticed that there was something else strange there. It was a small lip-shaped object near the ground. Lucy picked it up and realized it was a toy plane. She carefully took the plane in her hands and studied it.
Lucy felt very fortunate to have found such a special toy. She carefully added it to the other toys in her backpack and started walking back home. Lucy looked up at the sky and saw the small light plane flying around again. She smiled, grateful for her unexpected discovery.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to dress in her green clothes. Mia liked to play outside in her big yard. One sunny day, she saw a trail in the grass. She thought, "I want to see where this trail goes!" So, Mia put on her green dress and went outside.
Mia walked on the trail for a little while. She saw a big tree with a hole in it. Mia thought, "I wonder what is inside the hole?" She was very curious. She looked in the hole, but it was too dark to see. Mia knew she would have to come back later with a light.
The next day, Mia put on her green dress again and took a little light with her. She went back to the big tree on the trail. Mia shined the light into the hole and saw something shiny. It was a key! She took the key out of the hole and saw a little door at the bottom of the tree. Mia used the key to open the door, and she found a hidden playroom just for her! She was so happy that she had followed the trail and found the special surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little root that always wanted to make things to be happy. It loved searching for mud and making the most interesting shapes.
One day, when it was looking for some new mud, it came across a giant hill. It was so excited, it quickly ran up the hill to make something special.
But when it got to the top, it noticed something strange. There was a mean old bear sleeping up there. The root was so scared it didn't know what to do. It tried to run away but the bear growled and blocked its path. It had no choice but to stay.
Then the bear spoke in a gruff voice. "I'm the master of this hill!" it said. "You need to make me something special so I can be happy!"
The root tried to make something but it was so scared it couldn't focus. The bear got angry and shouted louder, "MAKE ME SOMETHING!"
The root was so alarmed, it suddenly lost all its jolliness. Instead of a happy moment, it was the last thing the poor root ever did.

Lily asked her friend, Tom, "Should I pick the flower? I am scared." Tom said, "Let's ask the flower if it's okay to pick it." They talked to the flower, but the flower did not talk back.
Just then, a little bird flew by and said, "Don't be scared, Lily! The flower wants you to pick it. It will be happy to go with you." Lily and Tom were surprised that the bird could talk! They thanked the bird and Lily picked the flower. The flower was happy and so was Lily. And they all played together in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a soft bunny named Bobo. Bobo loved to paint pretty pictures with his big, fluffy tail. One day, Bobo found a long cord in the grass.

Lily and Tom were at the beach with their mom and dad. They had a big bucket and a spade to make sand castles. Lily wanted to make a big castle with towers and flags. Tom wanted to make a small castle with a moat and a bridge.
"Let me use the spade, Lily!" Tom said. "You had it for a long time!"
"No, Tom, I need the spade to make the towers!" Lily said. "You can use your hands to make the moat!"
They started to pull the spade from each other. The spade broke in half. Lily and Tom both cried.
"Look what you did!" Lily said.
"It's your fault!" Tom said.
Mom and dad heard them and came over. They saw the broken spade and the sad children.
"What happened here?" Mom asked.
"They broke the spade!" Lily and Tom both said.
Mom and dad sighed. They took the broken spade and threw it in the trash. They hugged Lily and Tom and said, "It's okay, it was an accident. We can buy a new spade later. But now, you need to relax and share. There is plenty of sand for both of you. Why don't you work together and make one big castle?"
Lily and Tom looked at each other. They felt sorry for fighting. They nodded and said, "Okay, mom and dad. We will relax and share."
They took their bucket and went to find a good spot for their castle. They helped each other to make the walls, the towers, the moat, and the bridge. They found some shells and stones to decorate their castle. They were glad that they made up and had fun. They showed their castle to mom and dad, who smiled and praised them.
"That's a beautiful castle, Lily and Tom!" Mom said.
"You did a great job, Lily and Tom!" Dad said.
Lily and Tom hugged mom and dad and said, "Thank you, mom and dad. We love you!"

Once upon a time, there was a smooth basketball. The basketball lived in a big park. The park had a lot of trees, grass, and kids playing.
One sunny day, a boy named Tim found the basketball. Tim was very happy. He said, "Wow! A smooth basketball! Let's play!" Tim and the basketball played all day. They played with other kids too.
At the end of the day, Tim wanted to take the basketball home. But first, he had to weigh it. He put the basketball on a big scale. The scale said the basketball was not too heavy. Tim smiled and said, "You are perfect! Let's go home and play more tomorrow!" And they lived happily ever after.

Tim and Lily were friends who liked to play by the river. They often saw an otter who lived in the water. The otter was friendly and would swim near them and make funny noises. Tim and Lily loved the otter and named him Ollie.
One day, Tim and Lily went to the river as usual, but they did not see Ollie. They waited and waited, but Ollie did not come. Tim and Lily felt sad and worried. Where was Ollie? Was he hurt? Was he lost?
"Ollie, where are you?" Tim called out. "We miss you, Ollie!"
Lily was impatient. She did not like to wait. She wanted to see Ollie now. She decided to look for Ollie in the water. She took off her shoes and socks and stepped into the river.
"Wait, Lily, don't go!" Tim shouted. "The water is cold and deep. You might fall or get sick. Ollie will come back soon. He always does."
But Lily did not listen. She walked further into the water, looking for Ollie. She did not see the big rock that was under the water. She tripped over the rock and fell into the water. She screamed and splashed.
Tim ran to help Lily. He grabbed her hand and pulled her out of the water. Lily was wet and cold and scared. She cried and hugged Tim.
"I'm sorry, Tim. I was silly. I should have listened to you. I just wanted to see Ollie so much."
"It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you're safe. I want to see Ollie too, but we have to be careful. Maybe Ollie is busy or sleeping or eating. He will come back when he can. We have to be patient and wait for him."
Tim and Lily sat on the grass and dried themselves with their towels. They looked at the river and hoped to see Ollie soon. They did not know that Ollie was watching them from behind a bush. He had heard their calls and seen their fall. He felt sorry for them and wanted to cheer them up. He waited for the right moment and then jumped out of the water. He made a loud splash and a funny noise.
"Ollie!" Tim and Lily exclaimed. They were so happy to see Ollie. They ran to the edge of the water and waved at him. Ollie swam closer and waved back. He smiled and winked at them.
Tim and Lily smiled and winked back. They knew Ollie had missed them too. They thanked Ollie for coming back and told him they loved him. Ollie told them he loved them too and asked them to come back tomorrow. Tim and Lily agreed and said goodbye to Ollie. They walked back home, holding hands and singing. They were wet and cold, but they were also happy and warm. They had found their friend Ollie again.

Sara and Ben are playing restaurant in the garden. Sara is the chef and Ben is the waiter. They have a big menu with many dishes. Sara draws the dishes with crayons on paper.
"Hello, welcome to our restaurant!" Ben says to his teddy bear, who is the customer. "What do you want to eat today?"
Teddy bear does not answer, because he is a toy. Ben pretends he hears him. "You want the pizza with cheese and tomato? OK, I will tell the chef. Please wait here."
Ben runs to the kitchen, where Sara is busy. "Sara, Sara, we have an order!" he says. "The customer wants the pizza with cheese and tomato."
"OK, Ben, I will make it right away!" Sara says. She takes a paper plate and a paper circle. She glues some red paper on the circle for the tomato sauce. She cuts some yellow paper for the cheese. She puts the cheese on the sauce. She has made a pizza!
She gives the pizza to Ben. "Here you go, Ben. Be careful, it is hot!" she says.
Ben takes the pizza and runs back to the table. He is very happy. He wants to serve the pizza to the teddy bear. But he is not careful. He trips on a rock and falls down. The pizza flies in the air and lands on his head. He is covered with paper and glue.
"Oh no!" Ben says. He feels very embarrassed. He looks at the teddy bear, who is still sitting on the chair. He thinks the teddy bear is laughing at him.
Sara sees what happened. She runs to Ben and helps him up. She takes the pizza off his head and throws it away. She hugs him and says, "Don't worry, Ben. It was an accident. You are a good waiter. The teddy bear is not laughing at you. He is your friend. He still likes you."
Ben smiles and hugs Sara back. He says, "Thank you, Sara. You are a good chef. And a good sister. I still like you too."
They decide to make another pizza for the teddy bear. They hope he is not too hungry. They have fun playing restaurant again.

Lily and Max were at the farm with their mom and dad. They wanted to choose a squash for Halloween. They saw many squashes of different shapes and colors. Some were big and round, some were small and long, some were orange and yellow, some were green and white.
"Look, Lily, this one is funny!" Max said, pointing to a squash that had bumps and warts. "It looks like a frog!"
Lily giggled. "No, Max, that one is ugly! I want a smooth and shiny one. Like this one!" She picked up a squash that was bright orange and had a long stem.
"That one is boring, Lily. It looks like all the other squashes. I want a different one. Like this one!" He grabbed a squash that was dark and twisted and had a crooked smile.
"That one is scary, Max. It looks like a monster! I don't like it!" Lily said, frowning.
They both held their squashes and looked at each other. They could not agree on which one was better. They started to argue and tug at each other's squashes.
"Stop it, you two!" their mom said, coming over. "You can both choose a squash, but you have to be nice and share. Why don't you trade and see how you like the other one?"
Lily and Max looked at their mom and then at each other. They decided to try her idea. They swapped their squashes and held them in their hands. They looked at them closely and felt them with their fingers.
"Hey, this one is not so bad," Lily said, touching the bumps and warts on Max's squash. "It is kind of cool and funny."
"And this one is not so boring," Max said, admiring the smooth and shiny skin on Lily's squash. "It is kind of pretty and bright."
They smiled at each other and hugged. They thanked their mom and ran to show their dad their squashes. They were happy with their choices and could not wait to carve them for Halloween.

Once upon a time, there was a big bull. He was huge and proud. He rolled along the grassy meadows full of joy and excitement.
The bull spotted a small three year old boy. The boy said, "Hello, Mr. Bull! Can I play with you?"
The bull answered, "No thank you, little boy. I like rolling by myself."
The boy pouted and said, "That's not very nice of you. Shouldn't we share the meadow and have fun together?"
The bull thought for a moment and nodded, "Yes, you're right! Let's roll around together."
So the bull and the boy rolled around the meadows. They had so much fun, they danced and laughed and played the whole day long!
At the end of the day, the boy's mom picked him up. The boy turned to the bull, who was still happily rolling around, and shouted, "Goodbye, Mr. Bull! I am glad we shared the meadow!"
The moral of the story is to always share with others and to be kind to everyone. Even if it's something you enjoy doing alone, it's great to show others that we can have fun together.

Tom and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. One day, they saw a big bird in the park. It had a long neck, long legs and black and white feathers. It was an ostrich.
"Wow, look at that bird!" Tom said. "It is so big and funny!"
"Can we go and say hello?" Mia asked.
"OK, but be careful. It might be scared of us," Tom said.
They walked slowly towards the ostrich. The ostrich saw them and tilted its head. It was a nosy ostrich. It wanted to know what they were doing.
"Hello, bird. We are Tom and Mia. What is your name?" Mia said.
The ostrich did not answer. It opened its beak and made a loud noise. It sounded like a honk.
"Wow, you can honk! That is cool!" Tom said.
The ostrich honked again. It flapped its wings and ran towards them. It was not scared of them. It was angry at them.
"Uh-oh, it does not like us. Hurry, run!" Tom said.
Tom and Mia turned around and ran away. The ostrich chased them. It was faster than them.
"Help, help! The bird is after us!" Mia said.
They ran to the gate of the park. They saw their mom waiting for them. She had a big bag of popcorn.
"Mom, mom! There is a big bird in the park. It is an ostrich. It is nosy and angry. It honked at us and chased us. We are scared!" Tom and Mia said.
Their mom looked at the ostrich. It stopped at the gate and looked at them. It smelled the popcorn. It was a hungry ostrich. It wanted to eat the popcorn.
"Oh, dear. That is not a nice bird. It is a mean bird. It should not be in the park. It should be in the zoo. Come here, kids. Let's go home and have some popcorn. Maybe the bird will go away," their mom said.
She took their hands and walked away. The ostrich watched them go. It honked again. It was still hungry. It saw another bag of popcorn on a bench. It ran to the bench and ate the popcorn. It was a happy ostrich. It liked popcorn.

She showed the daisy to Ben, who was holding a bunch of roses. He looked at the bug and made a face.
"That's a slug," he said. "It eats the leaves and makes them smelly. You should remove it from the daisy."
Sara nodded and tried to pull the slug off the daisy. But it was sticky and slimy and did not want to let go. Sara pulled harder and harder, until the slug came off with a pop. She threw it away and wiped her hand on her dress.
"There," she said. "Now the daisy is not smelly anymore. It is pretty and yellow."
She put the daisy in her hair and smiled at Ben. He smiled back and gave her a rose.
"You are pretty and yellow too," he said. "Like the sun."

Mia swung her head back and forth. She replied, “No, Mama. I want to stay here. I want to weigh the earthquake.”
Mama smiled and thought for a moment. “All right, Mia. You can stay here, but don’t move too far away, okay?”
Mia grinned and got down on her hands and knees to feel the ground. She shook her head and said, “The ground is not moving, Mama. The earthquake is over.”

Mommy: "We have to look in the park. Maybe we can find him!".
But Spot was nowhere to be found. They returned home very sad.
John knew he had to be more careful with Spot. He promised to keep the leash in a better condition and improve his control over Spot.
But it was too late - Spot was gone and would never come back home. John was very sad and cried. Mommy hugged him tight and said, "Let's remember all the good times we had with Spot".

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. One day, they find a big tube in the garage. It is a regular tube, not a special one. But they think it is fun to crawl inside and pretend it is a tunnel.
"Let's go in the tube, Ben!" Lily says. She goes first and crawls to the other end. She waits for Ben to follow her.
But Ben is scared. He does not like the dark and the noise inside the tube. He does not want to go in. He stays outside and cries.
"Lily, Lily, come back!" he shouts. "I don't like the tube. It is too scary!"
Lily hears Ben cry. She feels sorry for him. She crawls back to him and gives him a hug.
"It's okay, Ben. The tube is not scary. It is just a regular tube. But if you don't like it, we don't have to play with it. We can play with something else. What do you want to play with?"
Ben stops crying. He looks around and sees his favorite truck. He smiles and picks it up.
"Let's play with the truck, Lily. We can make it go vroom vroom!"
Lily smiles too. She likes the truck as well. She takes another toy car and joins Ben.
"Okay, let's play with the truck and the car. We can make them race and beep beep!"
They play happily with their toys and forget about the tube. They are twins and they love each other.

As they rode, the zebra and the fox spotted a big, scary lion. The zebra was so frightened that he jumped off the fox's back and ran to hide.
"Don't be scared," said the fox. "I will protect you."
The lion roared at the fox, but the fox stood his ground and roared back. The lion gave up and ran away.
The zebra felt relieved and thanked the fox for protecting him.
"It's no problem," said the fox. "Now let's go back and enjoy the ride."
And with that, the two friends hopped back on the fox's back and continued the ride. They enjoyed the rest of the journey and went their separate ways when evening came. The zebra was glad he had made a new friend.

Once, there was a young boy who noticed a fountain just outside his house. He wondered, "Why are fountains so special?" He asked his father, who firmly replied, "Fountains are special because they make us feel safe and calm." The boy thought about this for a moment, but still couldn't understand why a fountain made he and his friends feel so safe. His father knelt down and said, "When you are thirsty and need a drink, a fountain can give you the water you need. Its safe, clean water will keep you healthy and happy."
The boy thought about this and nodded. From then on, he and his friends made sure to stay safe near fountains and drink from them as much as possible.
Moral of the story: Fountains provide us with safety, clean water and an opportunity to stay healthy and happy. Therefore, it is important to take care when near fountains and to take advantage of their special qualities.

"Hello, I am Tom's doll. What is your name?" Tom's doll said.
"Hola, yo soy la muñeca de Lily. Me llamo Rosa." Lily's doll said.
Tom and Lily smiled and made their dolls hug. They thought it was fun to learn new words from each other.
But then, a big dog came running towards them. It was barking loudly and had sharp teeth. Tom and Lily were very scared. They dropped their dolls and ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench.
"Mommy, mommy, help! There is a big dog and it wants to bite us!" Tom cried.
"Mami, mami, socorro! Hay un perro grande y nos quiere morder!" Lily cried.
Their mom hugged them and told them not to worry. She said the dog was just playing and did not mean to scare them. She said the dog belonged to a nice man who was looking for it.
"Sorry, kids, I hope my dog didn't frighten you. He is very friendly, but sometimes he gets impatient and runs away from me. His name is Rex." The man said as he came to get his dog.
"Lo siento, niños, espero que mi perro no los haya asustado. Es muy amigable, pero a veces se impacienta y se escapa de mí. Se llama Rex." The man said in Spanish.
Tom and Lily looked at the man and the dog. They saw that the dog was wagging his tail and licking the man's face. They felt less scared and more curious.
"Can we pet your dog?" Tom asked.
"Podemos acariciar a su perro?" Lily asked.
The man smiled and nodded. He said they could pet Rex if they wanted to. He said Rex liked children and could understand both languages.
Tom and Lily approached Rex slowly and gently. They touched his fur and his ears. Rex licked their hands and wagged his tail more. Tom and Lily laughed and said he was a good dog.
They thanked the man and said goodbye to Rex. They picked up their dolls and went back to their game. They decided to teach their dolls some words from the dog's language, like "woof" and "bark". They thought it was fun to learn new languages from different friends.

"Let's take some sugar," Ben says. "It is sweet and yummy."
"No, Ben," Anna says. "Mommy said sugar is bad for us. It can make our teeth hurt and our tummy ache. We should not take it."
"But I want some sugar," Ben says. He reaches for the jar. Anna tries to stop him.
"Ben, stop!" Anna says. "Mommy will be mad if she sees us. She will remind us of the rules. No sugar before dinner. Only fruits and water."
Ben does not listen. He opens the jar and takes a big spoon of sugar. He puts it in his mouth. He smiles.
"See, Anna, sugar is good," he says. "You should try some too."
Anna shakes her head. She does not want sugar. She wants to be a good girl. She hears Mommy's footsteps. She is coming to the kitchen.
"Ben, quick, put the jar back!" Anna says. "Mommy is here. She will see us."

"Ben, Anna, what are you doing?" Mommy says. "Did you take sugar from the jar?"
Ben looks down. He feels bad. He knows he did something wrong.
"I'm sorry, Mommy," he says. "I wanted some sugar. It was sweet and yummy."
Mommy sighs. She picks up the jar and the spoon. She wipes Ben's face with a napkin.
"Ben, sugar is not good for you," Mommy says. "It can make you sick and spoil your appetite. You should not take it without asking me. I have told you this many times. Why don't you listen?"
Ben does not know what to say. He feels sorry. He looks at Anna. She looks sad too.
"I'm sorry, Anna," he says. "I should have listened to you. You were right. Sugar is bad."
Anna nods. She hugs Ben. She forgives him.

Mommy smiles. She hugs them both.

"Yes, Mommy," Ben and Anna say. "We understand."

The dog saw the baby was sad and felt sorry. The dog gave the ball to the baby. They both played with the ball and were happy again. They played in the park until the sun went down.

One day, Tim's friends came to play. They saw Tim riding the stick and laughed. Tim felt embarrassed. He didn't want his friends to laugh at him. So, he put the stick down and played with his friends instead.
Later, Tim's friends saw the stick and wanted to try riding it too. They took turns pretending it was a horse. They all had so much fun! Tim felt happy and not embarrassed anymore. They all played together, riding the stick horse and laughing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She had an adorable cat named Fluffy. Amy and Fluffy loved to play together. They would run, jump, and climb all day long. They were the best of friends.
One day, Amy and Fluffy found a big network of ropes in the park. They thought it would be fun to play on it. As they climbed up and down, they met a talking bird named Chirpy. Chirpy said, "Hi! Do you want to play with me?" Amy and Fluffy were surprised but said, "Yes! Let's play together!"
As they played, Chirpy showed them a secret button hidden in the network. Amy, Fluffy, and Chirpy decided to press it. Suddenly, the ropes began to move and change. The network turned into a magical playground! They had so much fun playing on the slides, swings, and merry-go-round. They didn't think they would find such a wonderful surprise. And from that day on, Amy, Fluffy, and Chirpy became the best of friends, always playing together in their magical playground.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a big tree and Tim's mom said, "Let's sit under the tree and have a snack." Tim was very happy because he felt comfortable sitting on the soft grass.
While they were eating, they heard a funny sound. It sounded like gas. Tim looked around and saw a big, round ball. It was making the gas sound. Tim said, "Mom, look at the ball! It's making a funny sound!"
Tim's mom looked at the ball and smiled. She said, "That's not a ball, Tim. That's a balloon!" The balloon was making the gas sound because it was losing air. Tim laughed and said, "Silly balloon, you sound like gas!"
Just then, the balloon stopped making the gas sound and started to fly away. Tim and his mom were very surprised. They watched the balloon fly up into the sky until they couldn't see it anymore. Tim said, "Bye-bye, funny balloon!" And they both laughed as they finished their snack under the big tree.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys, but sometimes they are naughty. They do not like to share or listen to Mommy.
One day, Mommy gives them a new toy. It is a big, soft bear. It has a red bow and a shiny nose. Anna and Ben both want the bear. They start to pull and tug on it.
"Mine!" Anna says.
"No, mine!" Ben says.
They pull harder and harder. The bear makes a loud rip sound. The red bow falls off. The shiny nose falls off. Stuffing comes out of the bear. Anna and Ben stop and look at the bear. They feel sad and sorry.
Mommy hears the rip sound. She comes into the room. She sees the bear and the mess. She is not happy.
"What did you do?" Mommy asks.
Anna and Ben start to cry. They hug the bear and say sorry.
"We were naughty. We broke the bear. We are sorry, Mommy," they say.
Mommy sighs. She picks up the bow and the nose. She gets a needle and a thread. She sits on the couch and starts to fix the bear.
"Come here, Anna and Ben," Mommy says. "You need to learn to share and be nice. The bear is for both of you. You can take turns to play with it. And you can help me fix it."
Anna and Ben nod. They sit next to Mommy. They watch her sew the bear. They rub the bear's fur and say nice things to it.
"We love you, bear. We are sorry we hurt you. We will be good twins," they say.
Mommy smiles. She finishes sewing the bear. She gives it a hug and a kiss. She gives it to Anna and Ben.
"Here you go. The bear is fixed. Be gentle and kind with it. And with each other," Mommy says.
Anna and Ben hug Mommy and the bear. They say thank you. They promise to share and listen. They play with the bear on the floor. They are happy twins.

One day, a little girl named Amy found a box of shapes. She saw a square, a circle, and a triangle. She wanted to play a game with her friend, Tom. They wanted to match the shapes with the right holes.
Amy said, "Tom, let's see who can match the shapes the fastest!" Tom agreed, and they started to play. Amy tried to fit the square in the square hole, but it was too big. Tom tried to fit the circle in the circle hole, but it was too small. They both tried to fit the triangle in the triangle hole, but it didn't fit either.
They were sad and confused. Suddenly, Amy's big sister came in the room. She looked at the shapes and holes, then smiled. She switched the shapes around and tried again. The square now fit the square hole, the circle fit the circle hole, and the triangle fit the triangle hole.
Amy and Tom were happy and surprised. They learned that sometimes, you need to look at things in a different way to make them work. They thanked Amy's big sister and continued to play, knowing that they could solve problems by trying new things.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big yellow taxi on the street. They want to ride in the taxi.
"Let's catch the taxi!" Tom says.
"OK!" Sue says.
They run to the taxi. They do not look at the cars. They do not see the red light. They do not hear the horn.
CRASH!
A big blue car hits them. They fall on the ground. They cry. They hurt. The taxi driver and the car driver get out. They are angry. They yell at Tom and Sue.
"What are you doing? You are stupid! You are ugly! You are bad!" they say.
Tom and Sue are scared. They are sorry. They wish they did not run to the taxi.
A nice lady comes. She calls for help. She hugs Tom and Sue. She says, "Don't worry. You will be OK. But you should be careful. You should look and listen before you cross the street. You should not chase things that are not yours. You should be happy with what you have."
The moral of the story is: Be careful and be happy.

Lily and Max were playing with their toy rocket in the garden. They liked to make it zoom and fly in the air. They pretended they were astronauts going to the moon.
"Look, Lily, I can make the rocket go very high!" Max said, throwing the rocket with all his might.
"Wow, Max, that's amazing!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can I try too?"
"Sure, Lily, here you go." Max handed the rocket to Lily. "But be careful, don't let it get dirty."
Lily nodded and threw the rocket as hard as she could. But she threw it too far and it landed in a muddy puddle.
"Oh no, Lily, you made the rocket dirty!" Max said, running after it. "Now we have to wipe it clean."
"I'm sorry, Max, I didn't mean to." Lily said, following him. "Can you help me wipe it?"
"Okay, Lily, I'll help you." Max said, picking up the rocket. He and Lily used their sleeves to wipe the mud off the rocket. They tried to make it shiny again.
"There, that's better." Max said, looking at the rocket. "But now our sleeves are dirty."
"And our hands too." Lily said, looking at her fingers. "We need to wash them."
"Let's go inside and ask Mommy." Max said, holding Lily's hand. "Maybe she'll give us a tasty snack too."
"Good idea, Max." Lily said, smiling. "I'm hungry. And I love Mommy's snacks."
They ran inside, holding their rocket, and asked Mommy to wash their hands and sleeves. Mommy smiled and helped them. Then she gave them some cookies and milk. They ate them happily and thanked Mommy.
"Can we play with the rocket again, Mommy?" Max asked.
"Sure, you can, but only in the garden, okay?" Mommy said.
"Okay, Mommy, we will." Lily said.
They hugged Mommy and ran outside again, ready to play with their rocket. They had a lot of fun and forgot about the mud. They were happy.

"Tom, do you want to try my jelly?" Lily whispered. "It is rare and yummy. But don't tell Mom. It is a surprise."
Tom nodded. He was curious. He liked surprises. Lily took out her jelly and gave him a spoonful. Tom tasted it. It was sweet and sour and purple. He liked it very much.

One day, a little fish named Fin was swimming near the shore. He saw a big boat. The boat had a kind man. The kind man said, "Hello, little fish! Will you bow to me?"
Fin was scared and ashamed. He did not know how to bow. He swam away fast. As he swam, he met a wise old turtle. The turtle asked, "Why are you sad, Fin?"
Fin said, "A kind man asked me to bow, but I don't know how. I feel ashamed." The wise old turtle smiled and said, "Don't be sad. Just bend your head down like this." Fin tried and now he knew how to bow.
The next day, Fin swam back to the shore. He saw the kind man again. This time, Fin bowed to the man. The man was very happy. He gave Fin a beautiful shell as a gift. Fin learned that it is good to ask for help when you don't know something. And he was never ashamed to ask again.

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a little red car named Zoom. Zoom loved to drive fast and play with his friends. One sunny day, Zoom saw a small bird sitting on the ground looking sad and helpless.
Zoom went to the bird and said, "Hi, bird! Why are you sad?" The bird looked at Zoom and said, "I can't fly, and I don't know how to get back to my nest." Zoom wanted to help the bird, so he said, "Don't worry, bird! I will help you get back to your nest."
Zoom carefully let the bird sit on top of him. Then, they went around the park looking for the bird's nest. They talked to other animals and asked them if they knew where the bird's nest was. Finally, they found the nest high up in a tree.
Zoom drove as close to the tree as he could, and the bird hopped from Zoom to the tree. The bird was very happy to be back in its nest. "Thank you, Zoom!" the bird said. Zoom smiled and said, "You're welcome! I'm always here to help my friends."
From that day on, Zoom and the bird became best friends. They played together in the park every day, and they never felt helpless again.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the woods. One day, they found a cabin made of logs and stones. They wanted to see how big it was, so they decided to measure it.
Tom took a long stick and said, "I will measure the door. You measure the window, Lily." He put the stick next to the door and counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six. The door is six sticks long."
Lily took a shorter stick and said, "I will measure the window. You measure the roof, Tom." She put the stick next to the window and counted, "One, two, three. The window is three sticks long."
Tom took a longer stick and said, "I will measure the roof. You measure the wall, Lily." He put the stick on the ground and looked at the roof. He said, "The roof is too high. I can't measure it."
Lily took a shorter stick and said, "I will measure the wall. You measure the floor, Tom." She put the stick on the ground and walked along the wall. She counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. The wall is ten sticks long."
Tom took a longer stick and said, "I will measure the floor. You measure the chimney, Lily." He put the stick on the floor and walked across the cabin. He counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve. The floor is twelve sticks long."
Lily took a shorter stick and said, "I will measure the chimney. You measure the fire, Tom." She put the stick on the ground and looked at the chimney. She said, "The chimney is too high. I can't measure it."
Tom took a longer stick and said, "I will measure the fire. You measure the smoke, Lily." He put the stick near the fire and said, "The fire is hot. I can't measure it."
Lily took a shorter stick and said, "I will measure the smoke. You measure the air, Tom." She put the stick in the air and said, "The smoke is thin. I can't measure it."
Tom and Lily looked at each other and said, "We measured everything we could, but some things are too high, too hot, or too thin. We can't measure them."
They were tired from measuring, so they sat down on the floor and rested. They liked the cabin, but they liked their home more. They said, "Let's go back to our home. It is cozy and warm, and we don't need to measure it." They got up and walked back to their home, holding their sticks. They were happy and proud of their measuring adventure.

Sara and Tom were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and find things. Sometimes they found worms, or rocks, or coins. One day, they found something shiny and sharp. It was a razor.
"Look, Tom, I found a razor!" Sara said, holding it up.
"Wow, Sara, that's cool! Can I see?" Tom asked, reaching for it.
"No, Tom, it's mine! I found it!" Sara said, pulling it away.
"Please, Sara, just let me look. It won't hurt you, I promise!" Tom said, trying to grab it.
"Ow, Tom, you made me cut myself!" Sara cried, dropping the razor. She saw blood on her finger and started to cry.
"I'm sorry, Sara, I didn't mean to! Are you okay?" Tom said, feeling sorry.
They heard their mom calling them from the house. They ran to her, leaving the razor in the dirt.
"Mom, mom, Sara cut herself with a razor!" Tom said, pointing to Sara's finger.
"A razor? Where did you find a razor?" Mom asked, looking worried.
"In the yard, mom, we were digging and we found it!" Sara said, sniffling.
Mom took Sara's finger and cleaned it with a cloth. She put a band-aid on it and gave her a hug.
"That's a very dangerous thing to play with, Sara. You could get very sick if the razor is dirty and makes your finger rot. You should never touch a razor, okay?" Mom said, sternly.
"Okay, mom, I'm sorry. I won't touch a razor again," Sara said, nodding.
Mom looked at Tom and said, "And you, Tom, you should be more careful and not fight with your sister. You could have hurt her more. You should say sorry to her, okay?"
"Okay, mom, I'm sorry, Sara. I won't fight with you again," Tom said, hugging Sara.
Mom smiled and said, "That's good. Now, how about we go inside and have some cookies and milk?"
"Yay, cookies and milk!" Sara and Tom said, cheering.
They followed Mom inside, holding hands. They forgot about the razor in the yard. But the next day, when they went to dig again, they saw that the razor was gone. Instead, they found a purple flower growing in the dirt. They wondered who took the razor and planted the flower. They thought it was a nice surprise. They picked the flower and gave it to Mom. She smiled and said, "Thank you, Sara and Tom. You are very sweet." They smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mom. We love you." They hugged Mom and felt happy. They didn't miss the razor at all.

Tim's mom saw him playing and said, "Be careful, Tim! Don't drive too fast with Socky the car. You might get into trouble." But Tim didn't listen, and he kept driving Socky faster and faster.
Suddenly, Tim tripped and fell while running with Socky. He started to cry because his knee hurt. His mom came over and said, "I told you not to drive too fast, Tim. Now you're hurt and Socky is dirty. We need to wash him."
Tim was sad because he didn't listen to his mom. He had to say goodbye to Socky for a while as his mom washed the sock. Tim learned that he should listen to his mom and not drive too fast next time.

Lily liked to write with her crayons. She wrote on paper, on the wall, on the floor. She wrote her name, her cat's name, and shapes. She wrote every day.
One day, she found a skull in the garden. It was white and hard and had many teeth. She wondered who it belonged to. She decided to write on it. She wrote "Lily" and "cat" and a heart.
Her mom saw what she did and was very angry. She said, "Lily, that skull is expensive! It is from a museum. Dad borrowed it for his work. You can't write on it. It is not yours. It is very old and rare. You have to say sorry and clean it."
Lily felt bad. She did not know it was from a museum. She did not know it was expensive. She said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, dad. Sorry, skull. I will clean it." She took a cloth and some water and tried to wipe off the crayon. But it was hard to clean. The crayon was stuck.
Her dad came home and saw what happened. He was not angry. He smiled and said, "Lily, you are very creative. You like to write. That is good. But you have to write on things that are yours. Not on things that are not yours. Especially not on things that are expensive and from a museum. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, dad. I understand. I will write on my paper. And on my wall. And on my floor. But not on your skull. Or on anything else that is not mine. I am sorry."
Her dad hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. And I think the skull forgives you too. But let's try to clean it some more. Maybe we can use some soap and a brush. And then we will return it to the museum. And maybe we can see some other skulls there. And some bones. And some fossils. Would you like that?"
Lily smiled. She said, "Yes, dad. I would like that. I like skulls. And bones. And fossils. And I like to write. But I will be careful. And I will ask before I write on anything. Thank you, dad."
They cleaned the skull together and put it in a box. Then they went to the museum. They saw many skulls and bones and fossils. And they saw many pictures and words. Lily learned a lot. And she had fun. And she did not write on anything that was not hers. She was a good girl.

Ellie and the bird went to the tree where the bird's friend was stuck. Ellie used her long trunk to gently lift the bird's friend out of the tree.
