Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they find a big box in the park. The box has many things inside. They see books, clothes, toys, and a passport.
"What is this?" Anna asks, holding the passport.
"It is a paper that lets you go to other places," Ben says. "My mom has one. She went to a place with water and fish."
"Wow, that sounds fun," Anna says. "Can we go too?"
Ben shakes his head. "No, we need a plane to go. Planes are very expensive. We are poor. We do not have money for planes."
Anna feels sad. She wants to see water and fish. She has an idea. She looks at the box. She sees a big blue blanket. She takes the blanket and covers the box.
"Look, Ben," she says. "Now the box is a plane. We can pretend to go to the water and fish place."
Ben smiles. He likes to pretend. He gets inside the box with Anna. They close the flap.
"Ready?" Anna asks.
"Ready," Ben says.
They make plane noises. They pretend to fly. They pretend to see clouds and birds. They pretend to land near the water. They get out of the box. They see a pond. They see ducks and frogs.
"Look, Ben," Anna says. "There is water and fish here."
Ben sees a fish. He wants to catch it. He runs to the pond. He dives into the water. He splashes and laughs.
Anna laughs too. She joins him. They have fun. They forget they are poor. They are happy.

One day, however, the squirrel wasn't paying attention, he stumbled and all his things fell out of the file and scattered across the ground. He got so angry with himself and ran around trying to pickup all his things.
A big whale saw what had happened and said," You see, little squirrel, if you had kept your home organized, you wouldn't have made such a mess. It's better to neat and tidy all the time."
The squirrel took the wise whale's advice, and from then on he was careful and made sure that everything was in its place, keeping all his things in his file. The squirrel was always very happy and his home looked fine.
The moral of the story is that it pays to stay organized by keeping our things tidy and neat.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish corn cob. He was always getting into trouble and was always in a hurry to get things done. One day, he decided he wanted to shrink. So off he went to find a way to do it.
He searched high and low. He asked everyone he met, but no one seemed to know how to shrink. Frustrated, he finally decided to try something different. He closed his eyes and wished really hard that he could shrink.
Suddenly, he felt himself getting smaller and smaller. He opened his eyes and he was so tiny that he could hide between two stalks of corn! He was so excited that he jumped up and down.
From that day on, the foolish corn cob was very careful to wish only for things he could have.

Tom and his friends were scared of the big dog. They all began to scream and run away. The big dog chased after them, barking loudly. Tom was so scared that he forgot all about his math.

Ben was a lonely boy. He had no friends to play with. He liked to climb trees and look at the sky. He wished he had someone to talk to and share his dreams.
One day, he saw a big truck near his house. It had many tools and wood. Ben was curious. He went to the truck and saw a hammer. He liked the hammer. It was shiny and heavy. He wanted to try it.
He took the hammer and ran to his backyard. He saw a tall tree with a big branch. He thought he could make a treehouse there. He climbed the tree with the hammer in his hand. He started to hit the branch with the hammer. He wanted to make a hole for a door.
But he did not know how to use the hammer well. He hit the branch too hard and too fast. The branch cracked and broke. Ben fell down with the branch and the hammer. He landed on the ground with a loud thud. He hurt his arm and his leg. He cried out loud.
"Ben! What are you doing?" His mom heard his cry and came running. She saw him lying on the ground with the broken branch and the hammer. She was scared and angry. She picked him up and hugged him. She checked his arm and his leg. They were bruised but not broken. She was relieved.
"Ben, why did you take the hammer from the truck? That was not yours. That was for the workers who are building a new house next door. And why did you climb the tree with the hammer? That was very dangerous. You could have hurt yourself badly. You are very lucky."
Ben sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was lonely. I wanted to make a treehouse. I wanted to have a friend."
His mom felt sorry for him. She kissed his head and said, "I know, Ben. I know you are lonely. But you don't have to do things like that. You can make friends in other ways. You can go to the park and play with other kids. You can join a club or a class. You can talk to me or dad. We are your friends too."
Ben nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will try. Can I keep the hammer?"
His mom smiled and said, "No, Ben. You have to return the hammer to the truck. But I will buy you a toy hammer. You can use it to build things with your dad. He likes to build things too. Maybe you can make a treehouse together someday."
Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."
His mom said, "I love you too, Ben. Now let's go and say sorry to the workers and give them back their hammer."

Spot agreed and ran off to join the other dogs in their fun. But what Spot hadn't noticed was that the other dogs were eating a smelly old bowl of sour milk. Spot took a bite, and it was so sour that he yelped!
The other dogs just laughed and said, "You have to pay for breakfast, doggie!"
Spot ran back to his owner and his owner said, "See, Patience is a virtue! Next time, don't take a bite before you pay attention!"
Spot nodded and learned his lesson. From then on, he was more patient and paid closer attention to his surroundings.

"Oh no, our ball!" Sam cried.
"Look, the flame is burning the grass!" Lily said.
They were scared and ran back to the fence. They saw a man get out of the truck. He looked angry and sad. He walked to the ball and picked it up. He saw Sam and Lily behind the fence.
"Hey, kids, did this ball belong to you?" he asked.

"I'm sorry, I didn't see it. It was an accident. Are you OK?" the man said.
Sam and Lily nodded again. They were honest and brave.

The man smiled and gave them the ball. It was broken and burned, but he said they could keep it.
"It's OK, kids. Accidents happen. You were honest and told me the truth. That's good. Here, take this ball. It's a new one. You can bounce it and have fun. But be careful and don't bounce it over the fence again, OK?" the man said.

Ben and Sam were brothers who lived on a big farm. They liked to play outside with their dog, Spot. Sometimes they helped their dad with the farm work, like feeding the chickens and milking the cows.
One day, their dad asked them to help him pass the wheat to the truck. The wheat was yellow and soft, and it grew in a big field. Ben and Sam took big baskets and filled them with wheat. Then they carried them to the truck, where their dad was waiting.
"Good job, boys!" their dad said. "You are very strong and helpful. We have almost filled the truck with wheat. We will take it to the market and sell it."
Ben and Sam were happy to hear their dad's praise. They liked to make him proud. They went back to the field to get more wheat. But when they got there, they saw something strange.
There was a little girl sitting in the middle of the wheat. She was wearing a blue dress and had long brown hair. She looked sad and lonely. She did not see Ben and Sam.
"Who is she?" Ben whispered to Sam.
"I don't know," Sam whispered back. "Maybe she is lost. Maybe she needs help."
Ben and Sam decided to talk to the girl. They walked slowly towards her, trying not to scare her. Spot followed them, wagging his tail.
"Hello," Ben said softly. "What is your name?"
The girl looked up and saw Ben and Sam. She was surprised, but not afraid. She smiled a little.
"My name is Lily," she said. "Who are you?"
"We are Ben and Sam," Sam said. "We live on this farm. This is our dog, Spot. He is very friendly."
Lily reached out and petted Spot. He licked her hand. She giggled.
"I like your dog," she said.
"Thank you," Ben said. "Why are you here? Where are your mom and dad?"
Lily's smile faded. She looked down.
"I don't have a mom and dad," she said. "I live in the orphanage. It is a big house with many children, but no one loves us. Sometimes we go out to play, but we have to be careful. The lady who takes care of us is very mean. She hits us and yells at us. Today, she took us to the market, but I ran away. I was tired of being scared and sad. I saw this field and I liked it. It is so pretty and quiet. I wanted to stay here."
Ben and Sam felt sorry for Lily. They could not imagine living without a mom and dad, or being hit and yelled at. They wanted to help her.
"That is very sad," Ben said. "You should not be alone. You should have a family who loves you."
"Would you like to come with us?" Sam asked. "We can take you to our house. Our mom and dad are very nice. They will not hit you or yell at you. They will give you food and clothes and a bed. They will play with you and hug you. They will be your friends."
Lily looked at Ben and Sam with wonder. She could not believe what they were saying. She wanted to go with them, but she was afraid.
"Are you sure?" she asked. "Will they really like me? Will they let me stay?"
"Yes, we are sure," Ben and Sam said together. "They will like you. They will let you stay. They have a big heart and a big house. There is room for you. Come on, Lily. Trust us. We will be your brothers."
Lily thought for a moment. Then she nodded. She took Ben and Sam's hands and stood up. She left the wheat behind and followed them to the truck. Spot ran ahead, barking happily.
Their dad saw them and smiled. He knew what they had done. He was proud of them. He welcomed Lily with a hug and a kiss. He told her she was part of the family now. He told her he loved her.
Lily felt warm and happy. She had never felt like this before. She hugged Ben and Sam and their dad. She thanked them for saving her. She felt like she had found a home. She was not lonely anymore.

But then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and took the triangle up, up, up into the sky. Mr. Whiskers and Susie looked at each other, sad. Just when they thought the triangle was gone forever, a bird flew down and caught the triangle in its beak. The bird gave the triangle back to Mr. Whiskers and Susie. They were so happy and thanked the bird. Then they all played catch together, and it was the best day ever.

Lily took the book home and started to read it. As she read, she heard a small voice. "Hello," said the voice. Lily looked around and saw a tiny cat. It was the cat from the book! "How did you come out of the book?" asked Lily. The cat said, "I was waiting for someone to choose my book, and now I am here to play with you!"
Lily and the cat had lots of fun playing together. They played hide and seek, and they read more books. But then, something unexpected happened. When Lily tried to read another book, the words were all mixed up! The cat said, "Oh no, I think my magic made the print all funny!"
Lily and the cat worked together to fix the print in the books. They found a magic spell in one of the books, and the cat read it out loud. The print went back to normal, and the cat had to go back into its book. Lily was sad to say goodbye, but she knew she could always choose the cat's book again to visit her new friend.

Then she spotted a ladybug crawling near her feet. She was determined to catch it. She tried to grab the little bug but it was much too quick. Summer kept trying, but it wouldn't stay still.
At last, she had a plan. She took a big leaf and gently scooped up the ladybug. She was so proud of herself! She carefully cupped the ladybug in her hands, and smiled.
Summer was no longer sad. With her catch, she ran all the way back home.

So he tried to dive into the lake, to make his fur come back, but he could not swim. He kept trying but without any success. He kept wanting and wanting, but all his efforts were in vain.
Finally, an older otter swam up to the bald one and said, "My friend, don't worry. You may be bald, but you are still an otter, and nothing can change that."
The bald otter was filled with joy and thanked the older otter for the kind words. He finally accepted the fact that he was bald and started to swim around with the other otters. He was so happy just to be accepted, regardless of his baldness.

Fatima looked around, but she could not see an easy way out. "What are we going to do?" she asked.

So, they worked together and soon, they were able to move everything out of their way.
When they got back home, Fatima's mommy gave her some lotion and Fatima put it all over her body. She felt better and her skin was nice and soft again.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes, but their favorite was the big red truck. They liked to drive the truck around the house and pretend they were going on adventures.
One day, their mom cooked a delicious steak for dinner. She cut the steak into small pieces and put them on their plates. She told them to eat well and be thankful for their food. Tim and Sam loved steak and started to eat with big bites.
But then, Tim saw that Sam had a bigger piece of steak than him. He felt angry and jealous. He wanted to have the biggest piece of steak. He thought of a plan to get it. He said to Sam, "Hey, Sam, look at that amazing car on the TV. It can fly and shoot lasers. Do you want to see it?"
Sam loved cars and was curious. He looked at the TV and saw a shiny car flying in the air. He said, "Wow, that is amazing. I want to see it." He put down his fork and moved closer to the TV.
Tim smiled and quickly grabbed Sam's piece of steak. He put it in his mouth and chewed. He thought he was clever and happy. But then, he felt a pain in his throat. The piece of steak was too big and he could not swallow it. He started to cough and choke. He felt scared and sorry.
Sam heard Tim's cough and turned around. He saw Tim's face was red and he was holding his throat. He realized what Tim had done and felt angry and sad. But he also felt worried and wanted to help. He ran to Tim and patted his back. He shouted, "Mom, mom, Tim is choking. Help him, please."
Mom heard Sam's shout and came to the kitchen. She saw Tim was choking and quickly did the Heimlich maneuver. She pushed on Tim's belly and made him spit out the piece of steak. She hugged Tim and checked if he was okay. She said, "Tim, are you alright? What happened? Why did you take Sam's piece of steak?"
Tim felt ashamed and guilty. He looked at Sam and saw his tears. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry, mom. I was greedy and selfish. I wanted to have the biggest piece of steak. I lied to Sam and took his piece. But it was too big and I choked. I was wrong and stupid. Please forgive me."
Sam felt hurt and betrayed. He said, "Tim, you are my brother. I love you and I share with you. Why did you lie to me and take my piece of steak? You made me sad and you hurt yourself. You should not be greedy and selfish. You should be honest and kind."
Mom felt sad and disappointed. She said, "Tim, you made a bad choice. You were not thankful for your food and you were not fair to your brother. You broke the trust and the love between you. You should apologize to Sam and learn from your mistake. You should be grateful and generous."
Tim felt sorry and regretful. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry, mom. I apologize to you and I learn from my mistake. I will be grateful and generous. I will not be greedy and selfish. I will be honest and kind. I love you and I share with you. Can you forgive me?"
Sam felt touched and relieved. He said, "I forgive you, Tim. I love you and I share with you. You are my brother and we are friends. Let's hug and make up. Let's finish our dinner and play with our cars. But next time, don't lie to me and take my piece of steak. Okay?"
Tim nodded and hugged Sam. He said, "Okay, Sam. Thank you for forgiving me and helping me. You are my brother and we are friends. Let's finish our dinner and play with our cars. But next time, I will not lie to you and take your piece of steak. Okay?"
Mom smiled and hugged them both. She said, "Okay, boys. I'm glad you made up and learned your lesson. You are my sons and I love you. Let's finish our dinner and enjoy our food. But next time, I will cut the steak into equal pieces. Okay?"
They all nodded and laughed. They said, "Okay, mom. We love you and we thank you. Let's finish our dinner and enjoy our food. But next time, please cut the steak into equal pieces. Okay?"
The end.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with a long trunk. They wanted to climb it and see the birds.
"Can we go up, please?" Lily asked her mom.
"Be careful, okay? The trunk is very high and the branches are thin," her mom said.
Lily and Tom nodded and started to climb. They held on to the trunk and the branches. They saw many birds and leaves. They felt happy.
But then, the wind started to blow. The tree began to sway. The branches shook. Lily and Tom felt scared.
"Mom, help!" Tom cried. He felt dizzy and wanted to go down.
"Hold on, sweetie! I'm coming!" Mom said. She climbed up the tree and reached for Tom.
But as she did, a branch snapped. Mom and Tom fell to the ground. Lily saw them and screamed.
"Mom! Tom!" She trembled and cried. She wanted to go down too, but she was stuck.
"Help! Help!" She shouted.
A man heard her and came to help. He was a firefighter. He had a ladder and a helmet. He put the ladder against the trunk and climbed up. He reached for Lily and held her.
"Don't worry, little girl. You're safe now," he said.
He carried her down the ladder and gave her to her mom. Mom hugged Lily and Tom. They were bruised and scratched, but they were okay.
"Thank you, sir. You saved us," Mom said.
"You're welcome, ma'am. I'm glad you're all right," the firefighter said.
He smiled and waved. He went back to his truck and drove away.
Lily and Tom said goodbye to the tree. They learned a lesson. They would never climb a high trunk again. They would play on the swings and the slide instead. They felt dizzy no more. They felt happy again.

"Look, Ben, these are my drawings. Do you like them?" she asked.
Ben looked at the drawings. He saw a sun, a flower, a cat, and a family. He liked them, but he also saw something else. He saw an ugly drawing of a monster. It had big teeth, red eyes, and horns. It looked scary and mean.
"Who drew this?" he asked, pointing at the monster.
Anna frowned and took the folder back. She did not like the monster. She did not draw it. Someone else did. Someone who was mean to her at school. Someone who made fun of her and took her folder. Someone who ruined her drawings.
"That's Billy," she said. "He's a bad boy. He drew the monster on my last day of school. He said he would find me and scare me again. He said he knew where I lived."
Ben hugged his sister. He did not like Billy. He wanted to protect Anna. He had an idea.
"Don't worry, Anna. I have a plan. We can make the monster go away. We can make Billy go away. We can make a trap for him. Do you want to help me?" he asked.
Anna nodded. She wanted to help Ben. She wanted to make the monster go away. She wanted to be happy in the big house.
They went to the garage and found some things. They found a rope, a net, a bucket, and some paint. They made a trap for Billy. They put the folder with the monster drawing on the porch. They hid behind the bushes and waited.
They waited for a long time. They saw many people walk by. They saw a mailman, a lady with a dog, a boy with a bike, and a girl with a doll. They did not see Billy.
They were about to give up when they heard a familiar voice.
"Hey, look what I found. It's Anna's folder. I wonder what she has in here. Maybe some more of her stupid drawings."
It was Billy. He had followed them to the big house. He had seen the folder on the porch. He grabbed it and opened it. He saw the monster drawing and laughed.
"Ha, ha, ha. Look at this. It's the monster I drew for Anna. She must be so scared of it. I bet she cries every night. I should go and knock on her door and show her the monster. That would be fun."
He walked towards the door, holding the folder. He did not see the rope, the net, the bucket, and the paint. He did not see Anna and Ben behind the bushes.
They waited until he was close enough. Then they pulled the rope. The net fell on Billy. The bucket tipped over. The paint spilled on Billy. He was covered in red paint. He looked like the monster.
He screamed and dropped the folder. He tried to get out of the net, but he was stuck. He was scared and angry.
"Help! Help! Get me out of here! Who did this? Anna? Ben? Is that you? You little brats! I'll get you for this!"
Anna and Ben came out of the bushes. They smiled and laughed. They had made the monster go away. They had made Billy go away. They had made a trap for him.
They picked up the folder and the drawings. They tore up the monster drawing and threw it in the trash. They kept the other drawings and put them in their rooms.
They hugged each other and went inside the big house. They were happy and proud. They had made their rooms nice and cozy.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary little town, there lived a cat named Kitty and a dog named Doggy. They were good friends and played together every day. One day, they found a big, red ball in the park.
Kitty said, "I want to play with the ball first!" But Doggy disagreed, "No, I want to play with it first!" They started to argue and got into trouble. Their loud voices made the other animals in the park upset.
A wise, old owl saw the trouble and came to help. He said, "Kitty and Doggy, you should take turns playing with the ball. Sharing is caring." Kitty and Doggy listened to the wise owl and decided to share the ball. They took turns playing with it and had lots of fun.
From that day on, Kitty and Doggy always shared their toys and played together happily. They learned that sharing is a good thing and it keeps everyone out of trouble. And all the animals in the ordinary little town were happy too.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring, and it keeps us out of trouble.

Sam and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big billboard with a picture of a toy car. The billboard said, "Buy this car and have fun!"
"Wow, I want that car!" Sam said.
"Me too!" Tom said.
They ran to the store where the billboard was. They asked the man in the store how much the car was.
"Ten dollars," the man said.
Sam and Tom looked at each other. They only had five dollars each. They were sad.
"Can we have the car for five dollars?" Sam asked.
"No, you can't. The price is ten dollars," the man said.
"Please, mister, we really want the car," Tom said.
The man shook his head. He did not care.
Sam had an idea. He whispered to Tom, "Let's offer him something else. Maybe he will trade with us."
"OK, what do we have?" Tom whispered back.
They looked in their pockets. They had some candy, a ball, and a sticker.
"Let's offer him the candy and the ball and the sticker," Sam said.
They went to the man and showed him what they had.
"Will you trade the car for these things?" Sam asked.
The man looked at the things. He smiled. He was greedy.
"Sure, I will trade with you," he said. He took the candy and the ball and the sticker from Sam and Tom. He gave them the car.
Sam and Tom were happy. They thanked the man and ran outside with the car.
They played with the car for a while. They made it go fast and make noises.
But soon, they noticed something was wrong. The car was broken. One of the wheels was loose. The battery was dead. The car did not work anymore.
Sam and Tom were angry. They felt cheated.
They went back to the store. They wanted their things back.
But the man was gone. He had closed the store. He had taken their things and left.
Sam and Tom cried. They had lost their things and their money. They had no car and no fun.
They learned a hard lesson. The man was not fair. The billboard was a lie. The car was a trap.

"What?" Ben asked, opening his eyes.

Tim sat down and started counting. "One, two, three," he counted. As he counted, Tim started to feel sleepy. His eyes felt heavy, but he wanted to count all the beans. Tim's friend, Sam, came to play. Sam saw Tim and the beans.
"Hi, Tim! What are you doing?" asked Sam. Tim yawned and said, "I am counting beans, but I am so sleepy." Sam smiled and said, "Let's count together. It will be fun!" So, Tim and Sam counted the beans together. They counted one, two, three, and more.
As they counted, Tim did not feel sleepy anymore. They laughed and counted all the beans. When they finished, they had counted one hundred beans! Tim and Sam were very happy. They put the beans away and played together all day. And when it was time for bed, Tim and Sam were both very sleepy. They said goodnight and went to sleep, dreaming of counting more things together.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl called April. She wanted to play with her friends, but she couldn't catch up with them. Her friends would laugh and run away, teasing her about her size. One day, April was walking alone in the park when she saw a bottle of lotion on the grass.
Suddenly, she heard a voice from behind her, saying, "Pick up the lotion, April." It was an old woman. April was embarrassed, but she picked up the lotion and handed it to her.
The old woman smiled and said, "It's okay, sweetheart. Everyone has their own unique gifts. Your gift is your kindness and heart, not your size. Don't let your friends make you feel bad about being chubby. Remember to use your heart and strength to shine in life."
April smiled and nodded in agreement. She thanked the old woman and they hugged. April felt happy and comfortable in her own skin again. She realized that her friends may tease her, but she could use her heart to shine like a star.
The moral of this story is that even if other people may try to tear you down, don't worry. You have your own strengths and gifts, and those make you special!

One day, a little boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a big giant in the park. The giant was very tall and had a terrible face. Tim was scared, but he wanted to talk to the giant.
Tim walked up to the giant and said, "Hello, Mr. Giant. Why do you have a terrible face?" The giant looked at Tim and replied, "I am sad because I have no friends. Everyone is scared of me."
Tim felt bad for the giant. He didn't want the giant to be sad. So, Tim said, "Don't panic! I will be your friend." The giant smiled and they played together all day. Now, the giant had a happy face and a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a small child who lived in a house with many doors. Every day, the child would look at all these doors, wondering what was behind them. But the doors were too big and heavy, so the child couldn't open them.
One day, the child decided to lean against one of the doors. The door suddenly opened and the child saw something surprising: a small room filled with toys!
The child was so excited, but then realized that those toys didn't belong to them. So the child simply closed the door, learning that some things belong to others and it's not right to take them without permission.
The child leaned against the door one more time, promising to themselves that they would never open any of the doors without permission from the grownups.
The moral of the story is that it's important to respect other people's possessions and never take anything without asking.

Once upon a time, there was a big, dependable fish named Bob. Bob liked to swim all day. He lived in a beautiful fountain in a park. Many kids came to the park to see him swim.
One day, a little girl named Lily came to the park. She saw Bob swimming and said, "Hi, Bob! Can you swim fast?" Bob smiled and swam very fast around the fountain. Lily laughed and clapped her hands.
Suddenly, it started to rain. The rain filled the fountain with more water. The water got so high that it spilled out. Bob swam out of the fountain and into a puddle. Now, Bob could swim in the park with the kids. Everyone was happy and surprised. They played with Bob all day.

One day, a chubby cat named Tom saw a leak in his home. He was sad because the water made his toys wet. He told his friend, a little bird named Sue, "I don't like the leak. It makes my home wet."
Sue said, "Don't mind the leak, Tom. Let's play outside!" But Tom was worried. He knew the leak would get bigger if they didn't fix it. So, Tom and Sue looked for something to stop the water.
They found a big rock and put it on the leak. But the water still came out. Then, they found a big stick and tried to stop the water, but it didn't work. Tom was very sad.
Just then, a big, strong dog named Max came. He saw Tom and Sue and asked, "What's wrong?" Tom told Max about the leak. Max said, "I can help!" He went to his home and brought back some mud.
Max, Tom, and Sue put the mud on the leak. The water stopped! They were all happy. The twist was that Max, who was always mean to Tom, helped him. Now, they were all friends and played together every day.

Lily had a magic car. She thought, "I will use my magic car to reverse and see the moon." She got in her car and said the magic word, "Reverse!" The car went up, up, up into the sky.
As Lily got closer to the moon, she saw something strange. The moon was not round like she thought. It was a big, smiling face! The moon said, "Hello, Lily!" Lily was so surprised. She laughed and talked with the happy moon. Then, she went back home to tell her friends about her new moon friend.

Tom loved to zoom his toy car on the floor. He made loud noises with his mouth as he pretended to drive fast and crash into things. He zoomed his car under the table, over the rug, and around the chair. He was having so much fun.
But then he saw something disgusting on the floor. It was brown and sticky and smelled bad. It was his baby sister's poop. She had taken off her diaper and made a mess. Tom felt sick. He did not want to zoom his car near the poop.
He tried to go around it, but he was not careful. He zoomed his car too close to the poop and it got stuck. He pulled and pulled, but it did not come out. He started to cry. He did not want to touch the poop. He wanted his car back.
His mom heard him cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the poop and the car and understood. She said, "Oh, Tom, I'm sorry. That's disgusting. Let me help you." She put on gloves and took the car out of the poop. She threw the poop in the trash and cleaned the car with soap and water. She gave the car back to Tom and hugged him.
Tom felt better. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best." He smiled and kissed her cheek. He zoomed his car again, but this time he stayed away from the poop. He learned his lesson. He was happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to smell the flowers and look for bugs. Lily saw a green plant with small leaves. She picked one and smelled it. It was mint. She liked mint.
"Look, Ben, I found mint!" she said, holding the leaf. "Do you want to try?"
Ben nodded and took the leaf from Lily. He put it in his mouth and chewed. It was fresh and cool. He smiled and said, "Mmm, mint is good!"
Lily picked another leaf and ate it too. She saw a shiny thing under the mint plant. It was a coin. She picked it up and showed it to Ben.
"Wow, a coin!" Ben said. "Maybe it is magic!"
Lily and Ben decided to make a wish with the coin. They closed their eyes and wished for something. Lily wished for a new doll. Ben wished for a big cake.
They opened their eyes and looked at the coin. It was gone. It had vanished.
"Where did it go?" Lily asked, surprised.
"I don't know," Ben said, confused.
They looked around, but they could not find the coin. They felt sad. They had lost their magic coin.
"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said. "It was my fault. I wished for something too big."
"No, I'm sorry, Ben," Lily said. "It was my fault. I wished for something too silly."
They hugged each other and said they were still friends. They did not need a magic coin to be happy. They had each other and the mint. They picked some more leaves and ate them. They felt better. They went back to playing in the garden. They forgot about the coin. They did not know that it was still there, hidden under the mint plant, waiting for another wish.

Mom and Dad saw Tom's hand. It was red and swollen. They were worried too. They wrapped his hand in a towel and took him to a doctor.
The doctor gave Tom some medicine and a bandage. He said that Tom would be fine, but he should not touch jellyfish again.
Tom learned his lesson. He said he was sorry to Mia and Mom and Dad. He said he would not touch jellyfish again. He said he would only play with real balloons.

The little bird listened to the crab's warning and thanked him. They both played on the sand, far away from the big waves. The lonely crab was not lonely anymore. He had a new friend to play with on the sandy beach. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had many toys, but her favorite was a big, round ball. One day, Lily felt troubled. She could not fit her big ball into her toy box. She tried and tried, but it just would not fit. Lily was sad.
Lily's mom saw her sad face and asked, "Why are you troubled, Lily?" Lily said, "My ball won't fit in my toy box." Her mom thought for a moment and said, "Let's find a new place for your ball."
They looked around the house and found a big basket. They put the ball in the basket, and it fit! Lily was so happy. But then, something unexpected happened. The ball started to bounce all by itself! It bounced out of the basket and around the house.
Lily and her mom were surprised. They chased the ball and laughed as it bounced from room to room. At last, they caught the ball and put it back in the basket. Now, Lily had a new place for her ball and a fun story to tell her friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One day, they find a big box in the garage. They want to see what is inside.
"Let me open it!" Ben says. He pulls the box.
"No, me!" Anna says. She pushes the box.
They tug and shove until the box falls over. It makes a loud noise. They hear their mom coming.
"Uh-oh," Ben says. "We are in trouble."
"Quick, hide!" Anna says. They run behind some old clothes.
Mom comes in. She sees the box on the floor. She is angry.
"Who did this?" she asks. "Anna? Ben? Where are you?"
Anna and Ben are quiet. They hope mom will not find them.
Mom looks around. She sees a shoe sticking out from behind the clothes. She walks over and pulls the clothes away. She sees Anna and Ben.
"Here you are," she says. "Why did you make a mess?"
Anna and Ben are scared. They do not want to be punished.
"Sorry, mom," Anna says. "We wanted to see what was in the box."
Mom looks at the box. She sees a label that says "Fragile". She opens the box. She sees a vase that is broken.
"Oh, no," she says. "This was a gift from grandma. She sent it for our birthday. It was very special."
Anna and Ben feel bad. They did not know it was a gift. They did not mean to break it.
"Mom, we are sorry," Ben says. "We did not know. We were curious."
Mom sighs. She is sad, but she is also glad that Anna and Ben are honest.
"I know, sweeties," she says. "But you should listen to me when I tell you not to touch things in the garage. They can be dangerous or valuable. You could get hurt or ruin something."
Anna and Ben nod. They understand.
"We will listen, mom," they say. "We promise."
Mom hugs them. She is still angry, but she loves them.
"I love you, too," she says. "But you still have to clean up this mess. And you have to write a letter to grandma and say sorry."
Anna and Ben agree. They help mom pick up the pieces of the vase. They write a letter to grandma and draw a picture of a new vase. They hope grandma will forgive them. They learn to be more careful and respectful. They are good twins.

Tom and Lily were playing in the living room. They had many toys, but they liked to draw with pens and paper. They made pictures of their family, their pets, and their dreams.
"Look, I drew a big house with a garden and a pool," Lily said, showing her paper to Tom. "I want to live there when I grow up."
"That's nice," Tom said, but he felt uncomfortable. He did not have a pen. He had lost his pen yesterday, and he did not tell his mom. He was afraid she would be angry. He wanted to draw, too, but he only had a pencil.
"Can I use your pen, please?" he asked Lily.
"No, this is my pen," Lily said. "You have a pencil. Use that."
"But I like pens better. They are more colorful and shiny. Please, Lily, can I have a turn?" Tom begged.
Lily shook her head. She did not want to share her pen. She liked it too much. She thought it was the best pen in the world.
Tom felt sad and angry. He did not like Lily anymore. He wanted to take her pen and run away. But he knew that was wrong. He tried to think of something else to do.
He saw his mom in the kitchen. She was making cookies. He liked cookies. Maybe she would give him one. He got up and walked to the kitchen.
"Mom, can I have a cookie?" he asked.
"Sure, honey, you can have one. But first, wash your hands," his mom said.
Tom washed his hands and took a cookie. It was warm and sweet. He felt better.
"Mom, can I tell you something?" he asked.
"Of course, what is it?" his mom said.
Tom looked at his mom. He felt nervous. He did not want to make her angry. But he also did not want to lie. He decided to tell the truth.
"Mom, I lost my pen yesterday. I'm sorry. I don't know where it is," he said.
His mom smiled. She hugged him.
"Thank you for telling me, Tom. I'm not angry. I'm proud of you. You were honest and brave. That's more important than a pen. Don't worry, we can buy you a new pen. But next time, be more careful with your things, okay?" she said.
Tom nodded. He felt relieved and happy. He hugged his mom back.
"Thank you, mom. I love you. You are the best mom in the world," he said.
"I love you, too, Tom. You are the best son in the world," she said.
They ate their cookies and talked. Tom did not mention Lily or her pen. He did not care about them anymore. He had his mom and his cookie. He was happy.

One day, there was a big race in the forest. All the animals came to watch. Bob and Tim ran together in the race. They ran as fast as they could, and in the end, they both won! All the animals cheered for their victory. Bob and Tim were so happy that they could run fast together.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to run and play in the grass. One sunny day, Max went outside to play with his ball. He was very happy.
While Max was playing, he started to sneeze. "Achoo! Achoo!" Max sneezed and sneezed. He didn't know why he was sneezing so much. Max felt frustrated. He just wanted to play, but the sneezing made it hard.
Max's friend, a little bird named Lily, saw that Max was sad. She wanted to help him. Lily told Max to try playing in a different part of the grass, away from the flowers. Max listened to Lily and moved to a new spot. The sneezing stopped! Max was happy again, and he could play with his ball without any more sneezes. Max and Lily played together in the grass all day long.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They had a small magnifying glass that made things look bigger.
"Look, Ben, I found a ladybug!" Lily said, holding the glass over a red and black insect. "It has six legs and spots."
"Wow, let me see!" Ben said, taking the glass from Lily. He examined the ladybug carefully. "It is very pretty. Do you think it can fly?"
"I don't know. Maybe we can find out." Lily said. She gently picked up the ladybug and put it on her palm. She blew softly on it. The ladybug opened its wings and flew away.
"Bye, ladybug!" Ben and Lily said, waving.
They heard a crackle and saw a spark in the bushes. They ran over to see what it was. They saw a small fire burning some dry leaves.
"Oh no, fire!" Lily said, scared. "It is hot and dangerous. We have to tell Mommy!"
"Yes, let's go!" Ben said, grabbing Lily's hand. They ran to the house and shouted for Mommy.
Mommy came out and saw the fire. She quickly got a bucket of water and poured it over the fire. The fire went out and only smoke was left.
"Thank you, Mommy!" Ben and Lily said, hugging her.
"You're welcome, my loves. But you have to be careful in the garden. Fire can start from a spark and hurt you and the plants. Do you understand?" Mommy said, looking at them.
"Yes, Mommy. We understand. We're sorry." Ben and Lily said, nodding.
Mommy smiled and kissed them. "It's okay. I'm glad you're safe. Now, how about some warm cookies and milk?" She said, leading them inside.
"Yay, cookies and milk!" Ben and Lily said, happy. They followed Mommy and forgot about the fire. They only remembered the ladybug and how it flew away.

Once upon a time, in a cheerful forest, there lived a little bunny named Binky. Binky loved to play with his friends, the birds and the squirrels. Binky found a great hiding spot under a bush. He was very quiet, so his friends could not find him. But Binky did not see the mean fox coming. The fox saw Binky and wanted to catch him. Binky was so scared that he ran as fast as he could. He ran and ran, but he tripped and hurt his leg.
Binky's friends saw what happened and they wanted to help. A wise old owl told them about a magic plant that could heal Binky's leg. The friends went on a big adventure to find the magic plant. They climbed trees, crossed rivers, and even faced the mean fox. But they were brave and worked together.
Finally, they found the magic plant and brought it back to Binky. They put the plant on his hurt leg, and it started to heal. Binky was so happy that he could play with his friends again. The mean fox never bothered them again, and the cheerful forest was safe and happy once more.
From that day on, Binky and his friends knew they could face any threat together. They were always there to help each other, and they lived happily ever after in the cheerful forest.

Once upon a time, there was a family of four birds. They lived in a big tree in the forest. One day, the birds heard a strange ringing noise coming from the ground. The youngest bird was curious and wanted to investigate. She flew down to the ground and saw a big trap. It had deep, dark holes and was making a ringing sound.
The young bird said to her family, "What is that unknown thing?"
Her mother replied, "That's a trap. It's used to catch animals. You must fly away now, because you don't want to get caught in it!"
The young bird flew back to the tree and stayed away from the trap. She was glad that she didn't get caught in the mysterious ringing trap. And the family stayed safe in the tree.

"That's so cool!" Jamie said with glee. But then suddenly, as if from out of nowhere, a giant lightning strike came crashing down. It hit the pan and before the two friends could do anything the kitchen had filled with smoke.
Sam and Jamie were very scared. Then Sam noticed that the popcorn was still there. He bravely walked over and the pair quickly started gobbling it up.
But then it became obvious that something was wrong. The popcorn was wet and soggy, and it had a terrible taste.
"Oh no!" Jamie sighed sadly. "Our popcorn is ruined!" And with that, the two friends sadly went home feeling disappointed at their failed attempt.

Lily laughed too. "You are good at counting, Ben! Let's play again!"
They hugged and went back to their fort. They had fun playing hide and seek with their pillows.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a restless fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim all day long. One sunny day, Fin met a new friend, a turtle named Tim. Tim was slow but very kind.

"Sure!" said Fin, and they swam and played together.

Fin and Tim listened to Wally and shared the pizza. They learned that sharing is good and that friends should not fight. The pizza was very tasty, and they swam happily together, now best friends.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play and have fun. But they do not like to help Mom and Dad. They think it is hard and boring.
One day, Mom and Dad go out. They say, "Ben and Jen, you are big now. You can stay at home alone. But you have to do some things. You have to clean your room, wash the dishes, and make some food. We will be back soon."
Ben and Jen say, "OK, Mom and Dad. We will do it." But they do not mean it. They think it is easy. They think they have a lot of time. They think they can play first and do the things later.
They play with their toys, watch TV, and read books. They have a lot of fun. They forget about the things they have to do. They do not look at the clock.
Soon, they are hungry. They go to the kitchen. They look for some food. But they do not find any. They do not know how to make food. They do not know how to use the stove, the oven, or the microwave. They do not know how to open the cans, the jars, or the boxes. They do not know how to cut, peel, or chop. They only see some bread, some cheese, and some apples. They think it is not enough. They think it is not good. They think it is not fun.
They are sad and angry. They say, "We want some pizza, some cake, and some ice cream. We want some yummy food. We do not want this food. This food is bad. This food is boring."
Then, they hear a sound. It is the door. Mom and Dad are back. They see Ben and Jen in the kitchen. They see the bread, the cheese, and the apples. They see the dirty room, the unwashed dishes, and the undone things. They are not happy. They say, "Ben and Jen, what did you do? You did not do the things we asked you to do. You did not make any food. You did not clean, wash, or make. You only played, watched, and read. You did not listen to us. You did not respect us. You did not care about us."
Ben and Jen feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom and Dad. We were wrong. We did not think. We did not do. We only wanted to have fun. We did not know how to make food. We did not know how hard it is. We did not know how good it is. We did not appreciate it. We did not thank you for it."
Mom and Dad hug them. They say, "We forgive you, Ben and Jen. We love you. But you have to learn. You have to think before you act. You have to do before you play. You have to know how to make food. You have to know how to clean, wash, and make. You have to listen to us. You have to respect us. You have to care about us. You have to appreciate what you have. You have to thank us for what we give you."
Ben and Jen nod. They say, "We will learn, Mom and Dad. We will think, do, know, listen, respect, care, appreciate, and thank. We will be good. We will help you. We will eat the bread, the cheese, and the apples. We will clean our room, wash the dishes, and make some food. We will have fun, but not too much. We will love you, too."
The moral of the story is: Think before you act, do before you play, and appreciate what you have.

"Look what you did to Anna! You broke her!" Lily yelled.

The dove was scared of the children. It flew away from the tree. Lila and Ben ran after it. They threw their ball at the dove. The ball hit the dove and made it fall to the ground.
"Got you, dove!" Ben shouted. He picked up the dove and held it in his hands. The dove was hurt and scared. It tried to flap its wings, but it could not fly.
Lila and Ben looked at the dove. They saw blood on its feathers. They saw fear in its eyes. They felt sorry for the dove. They felt ashamed of what they did.
"Sorry, dove," Lila said. "We did not mean to hurt you. We were bad."
They put the dove gently on the grass. They hoped it would get better. They hoped it would fly again.
They heard a voice behind them. It was their mom. She saw what happened. She was angry and sad.
"What did you do to the dove?" she asked. "Why did you hurt it?"
Lila and Ben did not answer. They hung their heads. They knew they were in trouble.
Mom took them by the hand. She returned the ball to the park. She returned the children to the car. She returned the dove to the vet. She hoped the vet could help the dove. She hoped the children learned their lesson.

Tom and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to crawl under the bushes and pretend they were animals. Tom was a lion and Mia was a rabbit. They made noises and chased each other.
One day, they saw something shiny under a big bush. They crawled closer and saw it was a saw. It had a long blade and a wooden handle. It looked attractive to them. They wanted to touch it and see what it could do.
"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "It's a saw. We can use it to cut things."
"No, Tom, that's dangerous!" Mia said. "Mum and Dad said we can't play with tools. They can hurt us. We should leave it alone."
But Tom did not listen. He grabbed the saw and tried to pull it out. It was heavy and stuck. He pulled harder and harder. Mia was scared and cried.
"Tom, stop it! You'll get hurt!"
Suddenly, the saw came loose and Tom fell backwards. The blade cut his arm and he screamed. Blood came out and stained his shirt. Mia ran to him and hugged him. She was sorry and scared.
"Mum! Dad! Help!" she shouted. "Tom is hurt!"
Mum and Dad heard the noise and came running. They saw Tom and Mia and the saw. They were shocked and angry. They took Tom inside and bandaged his arm. They called the doctor and scolded him.
"Tom, what were you thinking?" Mum said. "You know you can't play with a saw. It's very dangerous. You could have lost your arm or worse. You're lucky it's not too deep. You have to be more careful and listen to Mia. She was right."
"I'm sorry, Mum," Tom said. "I was curious. It looked attractive. I wanted to try it. I didn't mean to hurt myself or scare Mia. I love her. She's my best friend."
"I know, Tom," Mum said. "But you have to be more sensible. A saw is not a toy. It's a tool for grown-ups. You can play with other things that are safe and fun. And you have to respect Mia. She's your sister and she cares about you. She was brave and smart. You should thank her."
Tom looked at Mia. She was still holding his hand. She had tears in her eyes. She smiled at him.
"Tom, I'm glad you're okay," she said. "I'm sorry I cried. I was afraid. I love you. You're my best friend."
Tom smiled back. He felt sorry and grateful. He hugged her.
"Mia, I'm sorry I didn't listen to you," he said. "You were right. A saw is dangerous. I won't touch it again. I love you. You're my best friend."
Mum and Dad smiled. They were relieved and proud. They hugged them both.
"That's good, Tom and Mia," they said. "We love you. You're our best friends."

"Hello, hello, hello!" He heard Sam's voice.
"Meow, meow, meow!" He heard Lily's voice.
He heard more noises and words. He was not happy. He was angry. He went to the living room and saw Sam and Lily playing with their toys.

"We didn't know it was your record. We just wanted to have fun," Lily said.

Once upon a time, there was a small red car. Tom the driver of the car loved nature, so he decided to take a drive in the countryside.
Driving down a clear road, he saw a field full of beautiful wildflowers. Tom stopped, opened the car door and stepped out. He grabbed handfuls of the soft petals and smiled.
Suddenly, he heard a voice behind him. It was George, a small frog, hopping along. "Hey, Tom," said George. "Why are you picking those flowers?"
Tom explained to George why he was picking the flowers. "I love nature," he said. "I just wanted to remember this beautiful moment of the field filled with wildflowers."
George hopped closer and smiled. "That's nice of you. Just don't forget to put the flowers back on the plant after you've taken them. It's important always to share nature with others!"
Tom thanked George and agreed not to forget. He then grabbed the flowers gently and put them back on the plants before getting back in his car.
Tom always remembered the lesson he learned that day: always share nature with others so that others may enjoy its beauty.

"No, Tom, don't!" Lily said. "It is dangerous. It can hurt you or him. We should go away."
But Tom did not listen to Lily. He was curious and brave. He walked into the house and reached for the pistol. He did not notice that the man was waking up. He did not notice that the man was angry and scared. He did not notice that the man grabbed the pistol and pointed it at him.
"Hey, kid, what are you doing here?" the man shouted. "Get away from my pistol! This is my house! Go away or I'll shoot!"
Tom was scared and sorry. He dropped the pistol and tried to run away. But it was too late. The man pulled the trigger and shot Tom in the chest. Tom fell to the ground and did not move. He was bleeding and hurt. He was dying.
Lily screamed and cried. She ran to Tom and hugged him. She called for help. But no one heard her. No one came. She was alone with Tom and the man. She was sad and afraid. She wished they never went to the hill. She wished they never saw the house. She wished they never saw the pistol. She wished Tom was alive.

The moral of the story is to listen to your mom and dad. They understand things that you may not.

Then they heard their mom coming. She opened the door and saw them. She saw the ball, the jar, the olives, and the glass. She was not happy. She said, "What happened here? Who did this?"
Sara and Ben looked at each other. They did not want to lie. They did not want to blame each other. They wanted to be humble and tell the truth. They said, "We did it, mom. We are sorry. She said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be nice and gentle. And you can't jump on it." Tom agreed. He said, "OK, Lily. I will be nice and gentle. And I won't jump on it. Let's make the best fort ever."
They worked together to make a new pillow fort. They used more pillows and blankets. They made it bigger and stronger. They made a door and a window. They put some toys and books inside. They were happy and proud of their fort.
They invited their mom to see their fort. Mom said, "Wow, what a wonderful fort! You two did a great job. I'm proud of you both. Can I join you in your fort?" Lily and Tom said, "Yes, mom. You can join us. But you have to be nice and gentle. And you can't jump on it." Mom laughed. She said, "OK, I will be nice and gentle. And I won't jump on it. Let's have some fun in your fort."
The moral value of the story is: Be respectful of other people's work and feelings. Don't ruin what they have made. Apologize when you make a mistake. Work together to create something better. Have fun with your family.

The next day, Tim got a call from Sam. "I got the shell!" said Sam. "But there was something inside!" Tim was surprised. "What was inside?" he asked. Sam laughed and said, "A little hermit crab! It is so cute!" Tim and Sam were happy. The shell had a new friend inside.

Once upon a time, there were three friends - Lizzie, Ben, and Sam. One day, they decided to go on a hike together. As the kids walked along, they spotted a rare mosquito.
"Look!" Lizzie said, pointing at the mosquito.
"Wow, it's special!" Ben said.
Sam smiled and said, "Let's take a closer look!"
Together, the friends ran to the mosquito. They bent down and watched it buzzing around in the sun.
Suddenly, Lizzie said, "Let's try and catch it!"
The others nodded and said in unison, "Let's try!"
They grasped at the air, but the mosquito was too quick. Ben shook his head, "It's too fast! We can't catch it!"
Lizzie had an idea. She said, "Let's keep trying and repeat the same thing over and over again."
Ben and Sam agreed, so the friends repeated their actions again and again. After repeating their actions for a few minutes, the mosquito flew into Ben's hands.
The kids laughed and cheered. Sam said, "That was rare! We caught it!"
The friends happily took the mosquito with them and continued their hike.

"Yes, Mom, we're okay," Tom said.

Dad looked at the truck and saw the driver. He was a bad man who wanted to ruin the parade. He had a mask and a gun. He got out of the truck and pointed the gun at the people.
"Give me all your money and jewels, or I'll shoot!" he shouted.
But then, something good happened. A big hero came out of the crowd. He was a policeman who was watching the parade. He had a badge and a gun. He ran towards the bad man and tackled him. He took his gun and handcuffed him.
"Stop, you're under arrest!" he shouted.
The people cheered and clapped. The policeman was a hero. He saved the parade and the people. Tom and Mia were very happy. They thanked the policeman and gave him a hug.
"Thank you, Mr. Policeman, you're awesome!" Tom said.
"Thank you, Mr. Policeman, you're amazing!" Mia said.
The policeman smiled and lifted them up. He put them on his shoulders and walked with Mom and Dad. They joined the parade again. The floats, the clowns, and the bands started again. The parade was noisy, but it was also fun. Tom and Mia had the best day ever.

Lily ate her lunch as fast as she could. After she finished, her mommy gave her a cookie. Lily was so happy. She shared the cookie with her little brother, and they both enjoyed it very much.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big box of cars, dolls, blocks and animals. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a shiny red car that made a loud noise when you pushed a button. It also had a light on the front that looked like a spark.
Lily and Tom both wanted to play with the new car. They started to fight over it and pull it from each other. The car was not very strong and it broke in half. The noise stopped and the light went out. Lily and Tom were very sad and angry. They blamed each other for breaking the car.
Their mom heard them crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken car and the twins with tears in their eyes. She asked them what happened and they told her their story. She was not happy with them. She said they were naughty for fighting and breaking the toy. She said they had to share and be kind to each other. She said she would try to restore the car, but they had to say sorry and hug each other first.
Lily and Tom felt sorry for what they did. They said sorry and hugged each other. They also said sorry to the car and hoped it would work again. Their mom took the car and went to the kitchen. She found some glue and tape and fixed the car. She brought it back to the twins and pushed the button. The car made a loud noise and the light came on. It looked like a spark.
Lily and Tom were very happy and thanked their mom. They decided to take turns playing with the car and share their other toys. They learned their lesson and never fought over the car again. They also learned a new word: restore. It meant to make something good again. They liked that word and the car. They played with it every day and had fun.

Lily was tired. She had played a lot with her toys and her dog. She wanted to rest. She saw her grandpa sitting in his big armchair. He was reading a book.
"Grandpa, can I sit with you?" Lily asked.
"Of course, my dear. Come here." Grandpa smiled and opened his arms. Lily climbed on his lap and snuggled against him. Grandpa closed his book and hugged her.
"Grandpa, can you rock me?" Lily whispered.
"Sure, I can rock you. Do you like to rock?" Grandpa asked.
"Yes, I like to rock. It makes me feel cozy and happy. And I like to hear your heartbeat." Lily said.
Grandpa smiled and kissed her head. He started to rock gently in his armchair. Lily closed her eyes and listened to his heartbeat. She felt cozy and happy too. She fell asleep in his arms. Grandpa rocked her and sang a soft song. He loved his granddaughter very much.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a little wolf. This wolf was very useful to his friends. He loved to help them in any way he could. One day, the little wolf saw a big tree with a red ball stuck in it. He knew his friend, the squirrel, loved red balls.
The little wolf had an idea. He saw a long stick on the ground. He thought that if he could wave the stick, he could get the red ball down. He picked up the stick and tried to reach the ball. But the stick was not long enough. The little wolf did not give up.
The next day, the little wolf found an even longer stick. He was very excited. He went back to the big tree and waved the long stick. This time, it worked! The red ball fell down. The squirrel was so happy to have his red ball back. The little wolf felt proud to be useful to his friend. And they played with the red ball all day long.

One day, Nina wanted to put on a hat by herself. It was a thin cotton hat with a bow. Her mom sat down on the floor next to her while Nina tried to pick it up.
"I think you can do it Nina," her mom said with a smile.
Nina grabbed the hat and carefully put it on her head. Her mom cheered with excitement when she saw it.
"You did it!" she said. "That was so good!"
Nina was so proud of herself. She twirled around in her new hat and smiled from ear to ear.
From then on, Nina wore her hat everywhere. Her mom continued to encourage her to try new things - and that little thin hat continued to bring her great pride.

As they played, the other animals in the forest saw that the lion was not so scary. They stopped being scared of the lion's roars and came to play with him too. The lion was no longer bitter and did not disturb the animals anymore. They all became good friends and played happily in the forest together.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy cat named Tom. Tom did not like to play with the other cats. He just liked to sit and watch them. One day, Tom saw a big bowl of yogurt on the table. He wanted to eat it all by himself.
Tom jumped on the table and started to eat the yogurt. He was very happy. Then, a little girl named Sally saw Tom eating the yogurt. Sally said, "Tom, you should not eat all the yogurt by yourself. You should share with the other cats."
Tom did not want to share, but he saw that Sally was right. So, he let the other cats come and eat the yogurt with him. The other cats were very happy. They all ate the yogurt together. After eating, the cats started to rub their heads on Tom. Tom felt good and was not grumpy anymore. From that day on, Tom played with the other cats and they all became good friends.

One day, a little dog named Spot felt an urge to play. He saw a round ball and felt very happy. Spot picked up the ball and ran to his friend, a big dog named Max.
"Max, let's play!" Spot said. Max felt anxious because he was scared of the ball. He had never played with a round ball before. But he wanted to be brave for his friend Spot.
Max tried to play with the round ball, but he was still anxious. Spot saw this and had an idea. They played a new game, where Max would chase Spot, and Spot would carry the ball. Max had fun and wasn't scared anymore. In the end, both dogs were happy, and they played together every day.

Once upon a time in a far away land, there lived a little girl named Lilly. Lilly loved to go on adventurous journeys.
One day Lilly decided to go explore the forest. As she stepped into the forest, she noticed lots of berry bushes. She was so excited to see all of the different kinds of berries.
She went over to the berry bushes and began to pick the biggest and juiciest berries. She was very careful not to pick too many though, so the animals could enjoy them too.
As she finished picking the berries, it started to rain. Lilly needed to find a place to cover up with. She looked around, but it was difficult!
Luckily, she found a big tree to cover her up. She ran over to it and hugged it tightly. The rain stopped and Lilly smiled. She was so happy she found a place to cover up and eat her yummy berries.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big kayak near the lake. It was red and shiny and had two paddles. They were curious and wanted to try it.
"Can we go in the kayak?" Tim asked Sam.
"I don't know. Maybe we should ask Mom first," Sam said.
But Tim was too excited. He ran to the kayak and climbed inside. He grabbed a paddle and started to splash the water.
"Come on, Sam, it's fun!" Tim shouted.
Sam was scared. He did not want to get in trouble. But he also did not want to miss the fun. He followed Tim and got in the kayak. He took the other paddle and tried to copy Tim.
The kayak started to move on the lake. Tim and Sam laughed and yelled. They did not see the big rock in front of them. They did not hear Mom calling them.
"Tim! Sam! Come back! It's not safe!" Mom said.
But it was too late. The kayak hit the rock and flipped over. Tim and Sam fell into the water. They were wet and cold and scared. They cried for help.
Mom ran to the lake and jumped in. She swam to Tim and Sam and pulled them out. She hugged them and checked if they were okay.
"Are you hurt?" Mom asked.
"No, Mom, we're sorry," Tim and Sam said.
Mom was angry and relieved. She took them to the shore and wrapped them in towels.
"Why did you go in the kayak without asking me?" Mom asked.
"We were curious. We wanted to have fun," Tim and Sam said.
"Curious is good, but you have to be careful. You could have been hurt or lost. You have to listen to me and follow the rules. Do you understand?" Mom said.
"Yes, Mom, we understand. We won't do it again," Tim and Sam said.
Mom smiled and kissed them. She took them home and gave them hot chocolate.
The moral of the story is: Curiosity is good, but safety is important. Always ask for permission and follow the rules.

Ben and Lily are best friends. They like to play together in the park. One day, they see a big sign on a tree. The sign has many words on it. Ben and Lily want to read the words.
"Let's plan how to read the sign," Ben says. "We can use our books and our toys to help us."
"OK," Lily says. "But we have to be honest. We can't make up words that are not on the sign."
They take out their books and their toys and start to look at the sign. They point to the words and try to say them. Some words are easy, like "park" and "tree". Some words are hard, like "reservation" and "prohibited".
"What does this word mean?" Ben asks, pointing to "prohibited".
"I don't know," Lily says. "Maybe it means something fun, like 'slide' or 'swing'."
"No, Lily, that's not honest," Ben says. "We have to say we don't know if we don't know. Maybe we can ask someone who knows."
They look around and see a man walking his dog. He looks friendly and kind.
"Excuse me, sir," Ben says. "Can you help us read this word?"
The man smiles and stops. He looks at the sign and says, "Sure, I can help you. This word is 'prohibited'. It means you are not allowed to do something."
"Like what?" Lily asks.
"Like climbing the tree, or picking the flowers, or leaving trash on the ground," the man says. "The sign says you have to respect the park and the nature."
"Oh, I see," Ben says. "Thank you for helping us."
"You're welcome," the man says. "You are very smart and curious. And you are honest, too. That's very good."
Ben and Lily thank the man again and wave goodbye. They are happy they learned a new word. They are also happy they are honest friends. They decide to play in the park and follow the sign. They have a lot of fun.

He had wanted the lollipop all to himself, but now he had lost it forever. He felt so sad and delicate.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make pretend stories with their dolls and cars. They were having fun and making a lot of noise.
Mom was in the kitchen, making dinner. She had a lot of things to do. She had to chop the vegetables, boil the water, bake the chicken, and set the table. She liked to keep everything organized and clean.
She heard Sara and Tom laughing and shouting in the living room. She smiled and thought they were cute. But then she heard a loud bang. She ran to see what happened.
She saw Sara and Tom standing in front of the refrigerator. The door was open and the food was all over the floor. Some of the food was broken or spilled. Sara and Tom looked scared and guilty.
"What did you do?" Mom asked, in a stern voice.
"We were hungry," Sara said, in a small voice.
"We wanted a snack," Tom said, in a smaller voice.
"You disturbed the refrigerator!" Mom said, in a louder voice. "You made a big mess! You wasted the food! You were naughty!"
Sara and Tom started to cry. They knew they did something wrong. They were sorry.
"We're sorry, Mom," Sara said, in a sobbing voice.
"We're sorry, Mom," Tom said, in a sniffling voice.
Mom sighed and calmed down. She was angry, but she also loved them. She knew they were still learning.
"It's okay, Sara and Tom," Mom said, in a softer voice. "But you have to listen to me. You can't touch the refrigerator without asking me. You can't take the food without permission. You can't make a mess without cleaning it up. Do you understand?"
"Yes, Mom," Sara and Tom said, in a nodding voice.
"Good. Now help me pick up the food and put it back in the refrigerator. Then we can have dinner together. And maybe a little snack later, if you behave."
"Okay, Mom," Sara and Tom said, in a happy voice.
They hugged Mom and said they loved her. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. They worked together to fix the refrigerator and make it organized again. Then they had dinner and enjoyed their food. They learned their lesson and did not disturb the refrigerator again.

Lily liked to collect things. She had a box full of shiny stones, feathers, buttons, and stickers. She liked to look at them and show them to her friends. One day, she saw a bottle of lotion on her mom's dresser. It was pink and had a picture of a flower on it. Lily thought it was pretty and wanted to have it. She took the bottle and put it in her box.
Later, her mom came to her room and asked, "Lily, have you seen my lotion? I need it for my skin. It is dry and itchy."
Lily felt guilty. She knew she should not take things that were not hers. But she did not want to give up the lotion. She said, "No, mom, I don't know where it is. Maybe you left it somewhere else."
Her mom looked sad and said, "Okay, I will look for it. But if you find it, please tell me. It is very important to me."
Lily nodded, but she did not tell the truth. She hid the lotion under her pillow and hoped her mom would not find it.
That night, it was very dark in her room. Lily was scared of the dark. She wanted to turn on the lamp, but she could not reach it. She wished she had her mom's lotion. It smelled nice and made her feel calm. She thought, maybe if she used some of the lotion, her mom would not notice. She reached under her pillow and grabbed the bottle. But as she opened it, she spilled some of the lotion on her bed. It was sticky and wet. Lily felt bad. She had made a mess and wasted the lotion. She realized she had been selfish and dishonest. She decided to tell her mom the truth and say sorry.
She got out of her bed and went to her mom's room. She knocked on the door and said, "Mom, I have something to tell you. I took your lotion and I lied to you. I'm sorry. I wanted to have it because it was pretty, but I did not need it. You need it more than me. Here, you can have it back. I'm sorry I spilled some of it."
Her mom hugged her and said, "Thank you, Lily, for telling me the truth. I'm glad you gave me back my lotion. I forgive you. But you should not take things that are not yours. It is wrong and it can hurt someone's feelings. Next time, you can ask me if you can borrow something, and I will share it with you. Okay?"
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I'm sorry. I love you."
Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Now, let's go clean up your bed and put some lotion on your skin. It will make you feel better."
Lily smiled and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you."
They went to Lily's room and cleaned up the mess. Then they put some lotion on their skin and smelled the flower. Lily felt happy and peaceful. She learned that it is better to be honest and generous than to be greedy and sneaky. She also learned that her mom's lotion was not just pretty, but also useful and soothing. She decided to collect things that she really liked and needed, and not things that belonged to others. She also decided to share her things with her friends and family, and not hide them under her pillow. She thought, maybe her mom would let her use some of her lotion sometimes, if she asked nicely. She hoped so. She liked the lotion very much.

"Let's play catch!" Lily said. She picked up a soft ball and threw it to Tom.
"Okay!" Tom said. He caught the ball and threw it back to Lily. They smiled and laughed as they tossed the ball to each other.
But then, the ball hit a lamp and the lamp fell down. It made a loud noise and broke into pieces. Lily and Tom stopped playing and looked at the mess.
"Oh no!" Lily said. "Mom will be mad!"
Tom was scared. He did not want to get in trouble. He said, "Let's hide!"
They ran to their room and hid under the bed. They hoped Mom would not find them.
But Mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the broken lamp and the ball on the floor. She was not happy.
She called, "Lily! Tom! Where are you?"
Lily and Tom did not answer. They stayed under the bed and held their breath.
Mom looked around and saw their feet sticking out from under the bed. She said, "I see you. Come out now."
Lily and Tom crawled out from under the bed. They looked at Mom with sad eyes. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We were playing catch and we broke the lamp. We did not mean to."
Mom sighed. She said, "I know you did not mean to, but you have to be careful. You could have hurt yourselves or started a fire. And you should not hide from me. You should tell me the truth."
Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We love you."
Mom hugged them. She said, "I love you too. But you have to help me clean up this mess. And no more playing catch inside. You can play catch outside when the sun comes out."
Lily and Tom agreed. They helped Mom clean up the mess. They learned their lesson. They waited for the sun to come out and have fun.

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks in the living room. They want to build a big tower, but they run out of blocks. They look around for more things to use.
"Look, there is a wire on the floor," Ben says. He picks up the wire and tries to bend it into a shape. "We can use this to make our tower stronger."
Anna shakes her head. "No, Ben, that is not a good idea. The wire is not for playing. It can hurt you. It can make sparks and fire. Mama told us to stay away from the wire."
Ben frowns. He likes the wire. He thinks it is fun and shiny. He does not want to listen to Anna. He wants to use the wire for his tower.
"Anna, you are not wise," he says. "The wire is fine. It will not hurt me. It will make our tower the best. Come on, let us try it."
Anna is scared. She does not want to try the wire. She does not want to make Ben angry, either. She thinks of a way to make him happy.
"Ben, I have a better idea," she says. "Why don't we suggest to Mama to buy us more blocks? Then we can build a bigger and safer tower. And we can use the wire for something else. Maybe we can make a necklace or a bracelet with it. What do you think?"
Ben thinks for a moment. He likes the idea of more blocks. He likes the idea of making a necklace or a bracelet with the wire. He smiles and nods.
"Okay, Anna, that sounds good," he says. "Let us go and suggest to Mama. Maybe she will say yes."
They put down the wire and the blocks and run to the kitchen, where Mama is making cookies. They tell her their idea and ask her nicely. Mama is happy to see them getting along. She hugs them and agrees to buy them more blocks. She also tells them to be careful with the wire and to never touch it without her help. Anna and Ben are happy and thank her. They go back to the living room and wait for the cookies to be ready. They decide to play with their toys until then. They are wise children.

Sara tried to make Ben feel brave. She said, "It's not scary, it's fun. You can hold my hand and we can go together. Come on, Ben, let's go on the slide." She pulled Ben by the arm, but he did not move. He shook his head and said, "No, no, no. I don't want to go on the slide."

Jack and Jill were good friends. They liked to play on the hill and fetch water from the well. One day, Jack had a big idea. He wanted to invite Jill to his house for dinner. He thought his wife would be happy to meet her.
He ran to Jill and said, "Jill, Jill, come with me. I have a surprise for you. I want you to meet my wife. She is very nice and makes good food. Will you come to my house for dinner?"
Jill was curious and excited. She said, "Yes, Jack, I will come with you. I want to meet your wife too. What is her name?"
Jack smiled and said, "Her name is Mary. She is very humble and kind. She loves animals and flowers. You will like her a lot."
They walked to Jack's house, holding hands. They saw a small cottage with a garden and a fence. Jack opened the door and said, "Mary, Mary, I have a guest for you. This is Jill, my friend from the hill. She came to have dinner with us."
Mary came out of the kitchen and greeted them. She was wearing a blue dress and a white apron. She had a big smile and a warm voice. She said, "Hello, Jill, I am so happy to meet you. You are very welcome to our home. Come in, come in, the food is almost ready."

She saw a cat on the sofa, a dog by the fire, and a bird in a cage. She saw roses and tulips and daisies in vases. She said, "Mary, you have a beautiful home. I love your animals and flowers. Mary thanked her and said, "They are my friends too. I take care of them and they make me happy. I am glad you like them. You can play with them after dinner, if you want."

Jill was glad that Jack invited her to his house. She thought he had a lovely wife. She thought they were a happy family. She hoped to visit them again soon.
