One day, a little girl named Anna went for a walk with her dog, Spot. They saw a big hedge with many flowers and bees. Anna liked the flowers and wanted to pick one for her mom. She reached for a yellow flower, but it was too high. She tried to pull it, but it was too strong.
Spot saw Anna pulling the flower and barked. He wanted to help her. He ran to the hedge and jumped. He bit the flower and pulled hard. He was stronger than Anna, but the flower was stronger than him. He pulled and pulled, but the flower did not come out. Instead, he pulled the whole hedge!
The hedge was enormous and heavy. It fell on the ground with a loud thud. It made a big mess. The flowers and the bees were gone. The hedge blocked the road and the sidewalk. Anna and Spot were scared. They heard people and cars coming. They did not know what to do.
A man came out of the house behind the hedge. He saw the hedge on the ground and Anna and Spot near it. He was angry. He shouted at them and asked them why they pulled his hedge. Anna and Spot felt sorry. They told him they wanted a flower for mom. The man calmed down. He told them they should not pull things that are not theirs. He told them they should ask before they take something. He told them they should be careful and respectful of nature. He told them they should help him fix the hedge.
Anna and Spot learned their lesson. They apologized to the man and helped him put the hedge back. They worked hard and made the hedge look nice again. The man thanked them and gave them a flower for mom. He told them they did a good job. Anna and Spot were happy. They thanked the man and went home. They gave the flower to mom and told her what happened. Mom hugged them and told them she was proud of them. She told them they were good and honest. She told them they should always remember the moral of the story: do not pull what is not yours.

As they walked, they met a big snake. The snake was not friendly. The snake wanted to eat the girl and the lion. The lion tried to protect the girl, but the snake was too strong.
In the end, the snake ate the girl and the lion. It was a very sad day in the forest. The lion could not help the girl and they could not find her home.

But then, something unexpected happened. The little girl started to dance and sing too! The big daisy and the other flowers had never seen a person dance and sing like them. Lily and Max are twins. They like to play together. Today, they have to go to the salon for a haircut. They do not like haircuts. They think haircuts are scary and noisy.
They sit in the car with Mom. Mom says, "Don't worry, kids. Haircuts are not scary. They are fun and make you look nice." Lily and Max do not believe Mom. They hold hands and look out the window.
They arrive at the salon. Mom takes them inside. They see a lady with scissors and a comb. She smiles and says, "Hello, I'm Sue. I'm going to give you a haircut. Who wants to go first?" Lily and Max shake their heads. They do not want to go first.
Mom says, "How about Lily? She has long hair. She can go first and show Max how brave she is." Lily does not want to be brave. She wants to run away. But Mom picks her up and puts her on a big chair. Sue puts a cape around her neck. She says, "Don't be afraid, Lily. I'm going to cut your hair a little bit. It won't hurt. It will tickle."
Lily hears the scissors snip snip snip. She feels the hair fall on the cape. She closes her eyes and hopes it will be over soon. She hears Max say, "Lily, you are doing great. You are so brave. I'm proud of you." She opens her eyes and sees Max smiling at her. He looks alert and curious. He is not scared anymore.
Sue says, "All done, Lily. You look beautiful. Do you want to see?" She holds a mirror in front of Lily. Lily sees her new haircut. It is shorter and neater. She likes it. She says, "Thank you, Sue. I like my haircut. It is not scary. It is fun." She hops off the chair and hugs Mom. She says, "Mom, you were right. Haircuts are not scary. They are fun and make me look nice."
Mom says, "You're welcome, Lily. You are very brave. Now it's Max's turn. Are you ready, Max?" Max nods. He is ready. He wants to have a haircut like Lily. He says, "Yes, Mom. I'm ready. I want to be brave like Lily." He climbs on the chair and smiles at Sue. He says, "Hi, Sue. I'm Max. I want a haircut, too." Sue says, "Hi, Max. I'm glad you want a haircut. You are very brave, too. Let's get started." She picks up the scissors and the comb. She says, "Don't worry, Max. I'm going to cut your hair a little bit. It won't hurt. It will tickle." Max hears the scissors snip snip snip. He feels the hair fall on the cape. He laughs and says, "It does tickle. It feels funny." He hears Lily say, "Max, you are doing great. You are so brave. I'm proud of you." He looks at Lily and says, "Thank you, Lily. You are brave, too. I'm happy we have haircuts." Lily says, "Me, too, Max. We look nice. We are twins with haircuts." They giggle and hug each other. Mom says, "You are both very brave and very nice. I'm proud of you, too. You are twins with haircuts and smiles." She pays Sue and thanks her. She says, "Let's go home and show Dad our haircuts. He will love them." Lily and Max say, "Yes, Mom. Let's go home. We love our haircuts." They hold hands and walk to the car. They are happy and not scared anymore. They are twins with haircuts and smiles. The end.

Sara liked to help her mom bake cakes. She liked to watch the mixer go round and round and make the batter smooth and fluffy. She liked to smell the sweet and yummy things that mom put in the bowl. She liked to lick the spoon and taste the chocolate or vanilla.
One day, mom said, "Sara, today we are going to bake a special cake for your grandma. She is coming to visit us and we want to make her happy. Do you want to help me?"
Sara nodded and clapped her hands. She ran to the kitchen and put on her apron. She helped mom measure the flour, the sugar, the eggs and the butter. She poured them into the big bowl and turned on the mixer.
But the mixer was too loud and too fast. It made a scary noise and splashed the batter all over the counter and the floor. Sara got scared and started to cry. She ran to mom and hugged her.
Mom turned off the mixer and hugged Sara back. She said, "It's okay, Sara. Don't be afraid. The mixer is just a tool. It helps us make the cake, but sometimes it can be noisy and messy. That's why we have to be careful and relax when we use it. Relax means to calm down and breathe. Can you relax with me?"
Sara nodded and tried to relax. She breathed in and out with mom. She felt better and stopped crying. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't mean to make a mess."
Mom said, "It's okay, Sara. I'm not mad at you. You are a good helper and a brave girl. We can clean up the mess together and finish the cake. Do you want to do that?"
Sara nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, mom. I want to make grandma happy. I love her and I love you."
Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sara. Come on, let's go back to the kitchen and have some fun."
They went back to the kitchen and cleaned up the mess. They added some more ingredients and turned on the mixer again. This time, Sara was not afraid. She watched the mixer with curiosity and wonder. She helped mom pour the batter into the pan and put it in the oven. She helped mom decorate the cake with frosting and sprinkles. She made a pretty heart with her name and grandma's name on it.
When the cake was done, they put it on a plate and waited for grandma to arrive. Sara was proud of her cake and excited to see grandma. She hoped grandma would like it and be happy.
Grandma came and hugged Sara and mom. She saw the cake and said, "Oh, what a beautiful cake! Did you make it, Sara?"
Sara nodded and said, "Yes, grandma. I helped mom. I used the mixer and I made a heart for you. Do you like it?"
Grandma smiled and said, "I love it, Sara. You are such a sweet and talented girl. Thank you for making me this wonderful cake. You made me very happy."
Sara smiled and said, "You're welcome, grandma. I'm happy too. I love you."
They all sat down and ate the cake. It was delicious and moist. They laughed and talked and had a good time. Sara learned that baking cakes can be fun and rewarding, but also that she has to relax and be careful when she uses the mixer. She also learned that making someone happy is a great way to show love and kindness. She was glad that she helped mom and made grandma happy. She was a good helper and a brave girl.

The old lady smiled. She said: "I can tell you some secrets of the woods if you want." John nodded. The old lady said: "If you go deeper into the woods you will see a house as wealthy as your own. You must come see me again."
John thanked the old lady and went off deep into the woods. He kept walking until he saw the house. It was huge, just like his own. He was excited to explore it and see the secrets.

Sam was sad and did not want to let the reindeer go. He thought his mom was bad and did not love him. He cried and hugged the reindeer. He said he loved the reindeer and wanted to be with it forever. The reindeer licked Sam's face and made a soft noise. It seemed to say it loved Sam too, but it had to leave.
Sam's mom was not bad. She loved Sam very much and wanted him to be happy. She also wanted the reindeer to be happy and free. She explained to Sam that the reindeer had a family and a home in the forest. She said the reindeer was only visiting their yard for a little while. She said the reindeer would come back next winter and maybe bring some friends.
Sam understood and felt better. He said goodbye to the reindeer and thanked it for being his friend. He watched the reindeer run away and disappear into the trees. He smiled and waved. He knew the reindeer would grow big and strong and happy in the forest. He hoped to see it again someday. He also knew his mom was good and loved him very much. He hugged his mom and went inside to have some hot chocolate.

But then, something unexpected happened. A big boat came near the reef. The boat dropped a big net into the water. Bob and Tim swam very fast, but the net caught them. They tried to get free, but they could not. The boat took them away from their home.
Bob and Tim were very sad. They missed their friends and the brilliant reef. They wished they could go back home. But they were stuck in the boat's net, and they could not escape.

But when she got to school, the mean kids saw her and started to tease her. They said she looked like a clown. They said she was crazy and ugly. They said she should go home and change. They made fun of her and made her cry.
Lisa ran to the bathroom and locked the door. She felt very bad and alone. She wished she had a friend who liked her and her fashion. She wished the mean kids would stop being mean.
Then she heard a knock on the door. She heard a voice. It was a girl from her class. Her name was Amy. Amy said, "Lisa, are you okay? Can I talk to you?"
Lisa was scared. She thought Amy was one of the mean kids. She thought Amy wanted to tease her more. She did not answer. She stayed quiet.
Amy said, "Lisa, please answer. I'm not here to be mean. I'm here to be your friend. I like your fashion. I think you are very pretty and fun. I want to play with you and learn from you. Can I see your clothes? Can I try your hat?"
Lisa was surprised. She did not expect Amy to say that. She did not know Amy liked her and her fashion. She felt a little bit of hope and curiosity. She wondered if Amy was telling the truth. She wondered if Amy was really her friend.
She decided to answer. She said, "Okay, Amy. You can come in. But be nice. Don't laugh at me."
Amy said, "I won't laugh at you, Lisa. I promise. I think you are awesome."
She opened the door and saw Amy. Amy had a big smile. She hugged Lisa and said, "Thank you, Lisa. You are very brave and kind. You are my new best friend."
Lisa smiled back. She felt happy and warm. She said, "Thank you, Amy. You are very sweet and smart. You are my new best friend too."

They walked out of the bathroom and back to the class. They held hands and smiled. They did not care what the mean kids said. They liked themselves and each other. They had fashion and friendship. They were normal and special.

The little bird and plane soared together for a while. The sun started to set and the bird started to feel tired. It said goodbye to the plane and flew back down the hill. It made it back home before the sun had gone down.
The little bird was happy, content that it had had such a wonderful day of soaring.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play pretend in the park. One day, they saw a big poster on a wall. It had a picture of a rhinoceros. The poster said: "Come and see Rocco, the famous rhinoceros, at the zoo!"
"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "I want to see Rocco. He has a big horn and a big nose. He must be very strong and brave."
"Me too," Ben said. "But we have to ask our moms first. Maybe they can take us to the zoo tomorrow."
They ran to their moms, who were sitting on a bench. They asked them if they could go to the zoo. Their moms said yes, but they had to be good and do their chores first. Lily and Ben were very happy. They hugged their moms and said thank you.
The next day, they went to the zoo with their moms. They saw many animals, like monkeys, lions, and elephants. But they were most excited to see Rocco, the famous rhinoceros. They followed the signs to his enclosure. They saw a big fence and a big sign that said: "Do not feed or touch the animals. They may bite or hurt you."
Lily and Ben looked for Rocco. They saw him in the corner, lying on the grass. He was very big and gray. He had a big horn and a big nose. He looked very strong and brave. But he also looked very bored and sad.
"Hi, Rocco!" Lily said. "We came to see you. You are famous. You are on a poster. Do you like being famous?"
Rocco did not answer. He did not look at Lily. He did not move. He just sighed.
"Maybe he is sleepy," Ben said. "Or maybe he is hungry. Do you think he likes carrots? I have a carrot in my backpack. Maybe I can give him one."
Ben opened his backpack and took out a carrot. He walked closer to the fence. He reached out his hand to give the carrot to Rocco.
"Ben, no!" Lily said. "You can't do that. The sign says do not feed or touch the animals. They may bite or hurt you. Come back here!"
But Ben did not listen. He wanted to make Rocco happy. He wanted to be his friend. He threw the carrot over the fence. He hoped Rocco would catch it and eat it.
But Rocco did not catch it. He did not eat it. He did not like carrots. He liked leaves and grass. He saw the carrot flying over the fence. He got angry. He did not like people throwing things at him. He did not like being famous. He wanted to be free. He wanted to be alone.
He got up from the grass. He ran to the fence. He saw Ben standing there, smiling. He did not smile back. He opened his mouth. He showed his teeth. He made a loud noise. He twisted his horn. He pushed the fence. He broke it. He got out. He chased Ben.
Lily screamed. Ben screamed. Their moms screamed. The other people screamed. The zookeepers ran. They tried to stop Rocco. They tried to catch him. They tried to calm him down. But Rocco was too fast and too angry. He ran out of the zoo. He ran into the street. He ran away.
Lily and Ben were scared. They hugged their moms. They cried. They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They never tried to feed or touch a rhinoceros again. They never forgot Rocco, the famous rhinoceros, who twisted his horn and broke free.

The gorilla smiled and agreed. Then they hugged, and the gorilla went on her way.

But Sarah was not listening. She was too scared and confused. She quickly pulled the invention’s plug without being careful. And then, Sarah got another shock.
Her mom was very sad and angry. She said: "Sarah, I told you to be more patient. But you were not listening. Now you must face the consequences of your actions.”
The moral of the story is: always listen to your parents and be patient. Otherwise, you may suffer the consequences.

Once upon a time, there was a big, friendly dog named Max. Max lived in a house with a family. Max loved to protect his family. He would always keep them safe from anything scary. Max's favorite place to play was upstairs.
One sunny day, Max was playing upstairs with his favorite toy. Suddenly, he heard a strange noise outside. Max looked out the window and saw an enormous bird in the yard. The bird was so big that Max had never seen anything like it before! Max knew he had to protect his family from this strange creature.
Max ran downstairs and barked at the enormous bird. The bird looked at Max and started to laugh. Max was confused. Why was the bird laughing? Then, the bird said, "Don't be scared, Max. I'm not here to hurt anyone. I'm a friendly bird who loves to play!" Max was surprised, but he decided to trust the bird. They played together all day, and Max learned that not everything big and strange is scary. Sometimes, the unexpected can bring new friends and fun adventures.

"Max, can you help me sit on the big chair to read this big book?" Lily asked. Max barked and wagged his tail. He had a fun idea. Max let Lily sit on his back, and they jumped up onto the big chair together.
As they started to read the big book, a little bird flew in and took the book away. Lily and Max were sad and didn't know what to do. They decided to work together to get the book back from the bird. They made a plan and climbed up a tree to reach the bird's nest.
When they got to the nest, they found the bird crying. The bird said, "I'm sorry I took your book. I just wanted to learn how to read too." Lily and Max felt bad for the bird and decided to teach it how to read. They all sat together on the big chair and read the big book.
In the end, Lily, Max, and the bird became good friends. They learned that sharing and helping each other is better than being mad. And they all enjoyed reading the big book together.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys on the rug. They have cars, dolls, blocks and books. They are having fun and making noises.
"Vroom, vroom, my car is fast!" Ben says.
"My doll is pretty, she has a dress and a hat!" Anna says.
They play for a long time, until their mom calls them for lunch.
"Anna, Ben, come and eat, it's time for lunch!" Mom says.
Anna and Ben run to the kitchen. They are hungry and want to eat. They forget their toys on the rug.
They eat soup, bread and cheese. They drink juice and water. They talk to mom and dad.
"Did you have fun playing?" Mom asks.
"Yes, we did, we have many toys!" Anna says.
"What did you play with?" Dad asks.
"We played with cars, dolls, blocks and books!" Ben says.
They finish their lunch and say thank you. They want to go back to play.
But when they go to the living room, they see a big mess. Their toys are not on the rug. They are all over the floor, the sofa, the table and the lamp. Some are broken, some are dirty, some are missing.
"What happened?" Anna cries.
"Who did this?" Ben shouts.
They look around and see a big dog. The dog is wagging its tail and panting. The dog has a car in its mouth and a doll in its paw.
"Bad dog, bad dog, give us our toys!" Anna and Ben say.
The dog drops the car and the doll and runs away. It goes to the door and barks.
Mom and dad come to see what is wrong. They see the dog and the mess.
"Oh no, this is Rex, our neighbor's dog. He must have sneaked in when we opened the door for lunch. He likes to play with toys, but he doesn't know how to be gentle. He is not a bad dog, just a silly dog." Mom says.
"I'm sorry, kids, your toys are ruined. We will talk to our neighbor and get you new toys. Don't be sad, it's not your fault. You just forgot to put them away." Dad says.
Anna and Ben are still sad, but they understand. They hug mom and dad and say it's okay.
They are clever kids, they learn from their mistake. They will not forget their toys on the rug again. They will put them in a box or a basket. They will also be careful with the door and the dog. They will still have fun playing, but they will also be tidy and safe.

"What is that smell?" asked Mary.
"It's a Magic Tree, and it has magical fruit," said Jack.
The friends decided to try the fruit, so they each picked some and ate it. It had a strange taste, but it was delicious.
"Let's have some more!" said John.

Thus ends their adventure of the weird island.

Once upon a time, there was a mixer. The mixer was not happy. It lived in a kitchen with a harsh man. The man was not nice to the mixer. He used it every day to mix things.
One day, the mixer said to the man, "Please be nice to me. I am tired." The man did not listen. He just laughed and said, "No! You are a mixer. You must mix."
The man kept using the mixer. The mixer got more and more tired. It was not strong anymore. One day, the mixer could not mix anymore. It stopped working. The man was angry. He threw the mixer away. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was only three years old, and her biggest dream was to become a sailor.
So one day, Jane's mommy took her to the seaside. She was so excited! Jane's mommy watched as Jane ran along the beach, picking up shells and giggling.
At the end of the beach, Jane came upon an anchor. It was rusty and worn, but it was so beautiful! She wanted to keep it, so she asked her mommy: "Can I make it mine?"
Her mommy smiled and said "Yes, of course, my love". Jane was so happy and clapped her hands. She hugged the anchor and carried it back home.
When she got home, Jane was ready to begin her journey on the big blue sea. To make sure she didn't get lost, she decided to use the anchor as her light. With a head filled with dreams, Jane sailed away, on her imaginary boat.

Lily loved to glow. She had a special dress that had tiny lights on it. When she pressed a button, the lights would flash and sparkle. She felt like a fairy princess when she wore it.
One day, she wanted to show her dress to her friend Max. She put on her dress and ran to his house. She knocked on the door and waited. Max opened the door and smiled. He saw her dress and said, "Wow, you glow!"
"Thank you, Max. Do you want to play with me?" Lily asked.
"Sure, come in. I have something to show you too." Max said. He led her to his room. He had a tray with many things on it. He had a toy car, a ball, a book, and a cupcake.
"What is this?" Lily asked, pointing to the tray.
"This is my treasure tray. I keep my favorite things here. Do you want to see?" Max said.
"Yes, please." Lily said. She looked at the tray and saw something that made her eyes widen. It was a necklace with a heart pendant. The pendant was shiny and pink. It looked like a jewel.
"What is that?" Lily asked, pointing to the necklace.
"That is my gift for you. I made it myself. It is a glow necklace. Look." Max said. He picked up the necklace and put it around Lily's neck. He pressed a button and the pendant lit up. It matched Lily's dress.
Lily gasped. She felt a warm feeling in her chest. She looked at Max and said, "Thank you, Max. It is adorable. I love it."
Max smiled. He was happy that Lily liked his gift. He said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are my best friend. You make me glow."

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was only three years old and he loved to nap. One day, Jack's parents told him it was time for his nap. He put on his pajamas, brushed his teeth and crawled into his long, pink bed. As he was about to close his eyes, he noticed something strange on top of his dresser. It was an ashtray that he had never seen before!
"What is this strange new object in my room?" tears came to his eyes.
Jack's mom noticed the distress in her little boy's voice, so she flew to his side and scooped him up in a warm hug. She explained that an ashtray was for putting ashes from a cigarette into. Jack had no idea what cigarettes were, so his mother explained that cigarettes made smoke and that smoking was bad for his health.
After his mother's explanation, Jack's tears disappeared, and he was ready and eager to take his long nap. He rested his sleepy head on his pillow, closed his eyes, and drifted off to dreamland.

She also told them a lesson. She said, "Eating too much of anything is not good for you. You should always be moderate and grateful for what you have. And you should always be kind and generous to others. Do you understand?"
Tom and Lily nodded and said they understood. They said they would not repeat their mistake. They said they would share their cherries with their friends next time. They learned their lesson and felt happier.

Ben follows her. He presses some keys too. They make different sounds. "Doo, dee, doo!" he says. "This is cool!"
They play with the piano for a while. They make up songs and sing along. They laugh and clap. They are very happy.
Then, they see a big ruler on the floor. It is long and thin and has numbers on it. "What is this?" Ben asks.
"I think it is for measuring things," Lily says. "Let's measure the piano!"
They pick up the ruler and put it on the piano. They try to see how long it is. But the piano is longer than the ruler. They move the ruler to the end of the piano and try again. But the piano is still longer than the ruler.
"How can we measure the piano?" Ben asks. "It is too big!"
"Maybe we can use our feet," Lily says. "We can walk from one end to the other and count our steps."
They put the ruler down and start walking on the piano. They step on the keys and make more sounds. "One, two, three, four!" they count. "This is hard!"
They keep walking and counting. They reach the other end of the piano. They look at each other and smile. "We did it!" they say.

Lily and Ben freeze. They look at the piano. They look at the ruler. They look at each other. They are scared.

"Mommy, we are sorry!" they say. "We were just playing with the piano. We wanted to measure it. We didn't mean to make noise."
Mommy looks at them. She sees their faces. They are sad and sorry. She sighs. She puts down the spoon and the pot. She hugs them.
"It's okay, my loves," she says. "I know you were curious. But the piano is not a toy. It is very expensive and delicate. You could have broken it or hurt yourselves. You should always ask before you touch something that is not yours."
Lily and Ben nod. They understand. They say sorry again. They promise to be careful next time.
Mommy smiles. She kisses them. She says she loves them. She says she has a surprise for them. She gives them each a bowl of soup. It is warm and tasty. It is not too spicy.
They eat the soup. They say thank you. They are happy again.
They love Mommy. They love the piano. They love measuring things. They love each other.

"Ben, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to make you upset," Lisa said.
Ben looked at Lisa and saw that she was sincere. He felt a little better.
"It's okay, Lisa. I'm sorry too. I shouldn't have thrown the shirt on the ground," Ben said.
Lisa smiled and hugged Ben. "I love you, Ben. You are my twin and my best friend. You can like whatever you want, even dresses. I don't mind."
Ben smiled and hugged Lisa back. "I love you too, Lisa. You are my twin and my best friend. You can like whatever you want, even shirts. I don't mind."
They went back to the clothesline and finished folding the clothes together. Mom saw them and praised them for being helpful and kind.
"Thank you, Lisa and Ben. You are such good children. I'm proud of you," mom said.
Lisa and Ben felt happy and proud. They learned that they could be different and still love each other. They also learned that they should respect each other's choices and feelings. They decided to share their clothes and play dress-up together. They had fun and laughed a lot. They were happy twins.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with toys. One day, they saw a big package outside their door. It had their names on it and a picture of a train. They were very happy and ran to open it.
"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "It has a train, a track, a station, and a bridge. Let's test it and see how it works."
"Okay, but be careful," Lily said. "We have to share and not break anything."
They took out the train and the track and set them up on the floor. They put batteries in the train and turned it on. The train started to move and make noises. It went around the track and over the bridge. Tom and Lily clapped and cheered.
"This is so fun!" Tom said. "I want to drive the train. Give me the controller."
"No, it's my turn," Lily said. "You had it first. Let me have it."
They both pulled on the controller and started to fight. The train went faster and faster. It bumped into the station and knocked it over. It crashed into the bridge and broke it. The train fell off the track and stopped working.
Tom and Lily stopped fighting and looked at the mess. They felt very sad and sorry. They had ruined their new toy. They wished they had been nicer to each other.
They heard a knock on the door. It was their mom. She had been out shopping. She saw the package and the broken toy. She was very angry and disappointed.
"What did you do?" she asked. "This was a gift from your grandma. She sent it to you because she loves you and misses you. She wanted you to have fun and learn. But you were selfish and careless. You did not share and you did not take care of your toy. You are very poor children."
Tom and Lily felt ashamed and guilty. They knew their mom was right. They had been bad. They wanted to say sorry to their mom and their grandma. They wanted to fix their toy and play nicely. They hugged each other and cried.
"Mom, we are sorry," they said. "We love you and grandma. We will be good and share and take care of our toys. Please forgive us."
Mom hugged them and wiped their tears. She was still angry, but she also loved them. She wanted them to learn from their mistake and be better children.
"I forgive you, but you have to work hard to make it up," she said. "You have to help me clean up this mess. You have to write a letter to grandma and tell her what happened and how sorry you are. You have to save your money and buy a new toy for yourselves. And you have to promise me that you will never fight over a toy again."
Tom and Lily nodded and agreed. They helped mom clean up the mess. They wrote a letter to grandma and put it in an envelope. They put their piggy banks on the table and counted their coins. They promised mom that they would never fight over a toy again.
They learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that toys are not as important as family and friends. They learned that sharing and caring are better than fighting and breaking. They learned that being good and grateful are better than being poor and sorry.

So one day he decided to go, but there was something blocking him. He was very frustrated and couldn't move. He waited and waited, but nothing changed.
But then a magical thing happened! He suddenly floated above the ground and flew to the field! He touched the trees, smelled the flowers and smiled as he saw the big sky above him. He was so happy to be in his dream.
The End.

Jill and her mom were going on a visit. Jill loved to visit because it was always fun.
“Mom, can I take my toy?” asked Jill.
“No sweetie, toys can break on the visit,” her mom replied.
Jill was sad but she refused to cry. She knew that being kind was the right thing to do.
“Mom, can I at least take my teddy bear? Pleeeease,” asked Jill.
Her mom smiled and said, “Ok, you can bring one bear. That's very kind of you. Now let's go!”
Jill was excited. She ran to get her bear and hopped into the car. She couldn't wait to start their visit!

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park to play. He saw other kids playing a game. They were all players in the game. Tim wanted to join them, but he was scared. He stood near a tree and watched them play. He wished he could be brave like them.
A small girl named Sue came up to Tim and whispered, "Do you want to play with us?" Tim looked at her and whispered back, "I want to, but I am scared." Sue smiled and said, "Don't be scared. We can play together, and I will help you."
Tim and Sue joined the game with the other players. At first, Tim was still scared, but with Sue's help, he started to have fun. They played and laughed together. The other kids saw how well Tim and Sue played and wanted to be friends with them too.
In the end, Tim learned that it is okay to be scared, but with a little help from a friend, you can be brave and have fun. The players all became good friends, and they played happily in the park every day.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lily. She loved to swim in the river. She would become very happy when she got to swim in the river. One day, she wanted to swim even deeper but she noticed a stupid fish swimming around. She tried to catch it but it was very fast. She kept trying until she finally caught it. She became so excited and took it home. Her mum was shocked to see her with a fish. Lily thanked her mum and then went back to the river. She understood that the stupid fish just wanted to swim and be free. From that day onwards, Lily promised to never take another fish out of the water and to let them swim free.

Ben and Lily like to play chess. Chess is a game with black and white pieces. They have a big board with squares. They move the pieces on the board and try to catch the king.
One day, Ben and Lily are playing chess in the living room. Lily is very good at chess. She is smart and careful. Ben is not so good at chess. He is clumsy and forgetful. He often knocks over the pieces or forgets the rules.
"Ben, you can't do that!" Lily says. "You can't move your knight like that. It has to go in an L shape."
"Oops, sorry!" Ben says. "I forgot. Can I try again?"
"No, you can't. That's cheating. You have to act fair when you play chess." Lily says. She is angry and frowns.
Ben feels bad. He doesn't want to make Lily angry. He wants to have fun and be friends. He thinks of a way to make Lily happy.
"Hey, Lily, I have an idea. Why don't we act like the chess pieces? We can pretend to be kings and queens and knights and rooks. We can make funny noises and move around the room. That would be fun, right?" Ben says.
Lily thinks for a moment. She likes to act and pretend. She likes to make funny noises and move around the room. She smiles and nods.
"OK, Ben, that sounds fun. Let's act like the chess pieces. But you have to be careful and not knock over anything." Lily says.
"OK, Lily, I will be careful. I promise." Ben says.
They put away the chess board and the pieces. They start to act like the chess pieces. They have a lot of fun and laugh a lot. They are happy and friends again.

Once upon a time, in a small, noisy town, there lived a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and make them talk to each other. One day, Lily found a small box of powder in her mom's room. The powder was soft and pretty, like magic dust.
Lily wanted to play with the powder, so she took it to her room. She sprinkled the powder on her toys, hoping it would make them come to life. But nothing happened. Lily started to frown because her toys were not talking like she wanted them to.
Just then, her mom came into the room and saw the mess. She told Lily that the powder was not magic, but it was for her mom's face. Lily felt sad, but her mom gave her a big hug. They cleaned up the powder together and then played with the toys, making them talk and laugh. Lily's frown turned into a big smile, and they had a fun day in their noisy little town.

Once upon a time, there was a little jellyfish named Jilly. Jilly lived in a gloomy part of the sea. She felt sad because she had no friends to play with. One day, Jilly decided to go on an adventure to find a friend.
As Jilly swam, she met a kind fish named Fin. Fin asked, "Why are you sad, Jilly?" Jilly replied, "I have no friends to play with in the gloomy sea." Fin smiled and said, "I'll be your friend, Jilly!"
Jilly and Fin played all day. They swam fast, they played hide and seek, and they laughed a lot. At the end of the day, Jilly was so happy to have a new friend. She gave Fin a big kiss on his cheek. From that day on, Jilly and Fin were the best of friends, and the sea didn't feel so gloomy anymore.

Ben is a bald boy who likes to sleep a lot. He has a big bed with a blue blanket and a soft pillow. He also has a teddy bear that he hugs when he sleeps.
One night, Ben hears a noise outside his window. He opens his eyes and sees a big bird with yellow feathers and a long beak. The bird is flapping its wings and making a loud sound. Ben is scared and wants to hide under his blanket.
"Who are you?" Ben asks the bird.
"I am a motion bird," the bird says. "I can fly very fast and very far. I like to see different places and things. Do you want to come with me?"
Ben thinks for a moment. He likes to sleep, but he also likes to see new things. He wonders what the bird can show him.
"Where will you take me?" Ben asks.
"I will take you to the moon," the bird says. "The moon is a big ball of light that shines at night. It is very beautiful and quiet. You will like it there."
Ben is curious about the moon. He has seen it in the sky, but he has never been there. He decides to go with the bird.
"Okay, I will go with you," Ben says. "But can I bring my teddy bear?"
"Of course you can," the bird says. "He can be your friend on the moon."
Ben gets out of his bed and grabs his teddy bear. He climbs on the bird's back and holds on tight. The bird flies out of the window and into the night. Ben feels the wind on his face and the motion of the bird. He is happy and excited.
Soon, they reach the moon. The moon is bigger and brighter than Ben imagined. He sees craters and rocks and stars. He feels the moon's cold and smooth surface. He and the bird explore the moon and have fun.
After a while, Ben feels sleepy. He yawns and rubs his eyes.
"I want to sleep now," Ben says.
"Okay, you can sleep here," the bird says. "I will watch over you and keep you warm."
Ben lies down on the moon and covers himself with his blue blanket. He puts his teddy bear next to him and cuddles with him. He closes his eyes and falls asleep.
The bird smiles and sings a soft lullaby. He is glad that he met Ben and that they had a nice adventure. He hopes that Ben will dream of the moon and of him. He hopes that they will meet again.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful little boy named Tim. Tim loved ice-cream more than anything in the world. One sunny day, he went to the park with his mom to play and eat ice-cream.
At the park, Tim saw a big, strong man. The man was angry and wanted to destroy things. Tim was scared, but he wanted to help the man feel happy. So, he walked up to the man and said, "Hi, I am Tim. Do you want some ice-cream?"
The man looked at Tim and then at the ice-cream. He thought for a moment and said, "Yes, I would like some ice-cream. Thank you, Tim." The man took a bite of the ice-cream and smiled. The ice-cream made him feel happy and he didn't want to destroy things anymore.
From that day on, the man and Tim became good friends. They would go to the park and eat ice-cream together. Tim learned that sometimes, all it takes is a little bit of kindness and a cheerful heart to make someone happy. And the big, strong man learned that ice-cream could make even the angriest person feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who was three years old. One day, she was playing with her toys in her garden. Suddenly, she noticed a small, pale flea. She was very surprised to see it and asked her mom, "Mom, what is this?" Her mom replied, "It's a flea, sweetie, and it must have come from somewhere nearby." Sarah thought for a while and then said, "Will you bring me a cup of water please?" Her mom was confused and asked, "Why do you need a cup of water, Sarah?" Sarah smiled and said, "I want to bring this little pale flea some water." Her mom smiled and agreed to bring the cup of water. Sarah filled the cup with water and gently set the flea in it. The flea happily swam around and Sarah smiled. She had made a new friend!

One day, Tim went to the park to ride his bicycle. But when he got there, he could not find his bicycle. Tim was sad because he thought he had lost his bicycle. He looked under the trees and behind the flowers, but he could not find it. Tim felt very sad and started to cry.
Just then, Tim's friend, Sarah, came to the park. She saw Tim crying and asked what was wrong. Tim told her he lost his bicycle. Sarah wanted to help, so they looked for the bicycle together. Soon, they found the bicycle behind a big tree. Tim was so happy! He thanked Sarah for helping him find his bicycle. Lily liked to play dress up. She had many costumes in her closet. She had a fairy costume, a pirate costume, a princess costume, and more. She liked to pretend she was different people and have fun.
One day, she wanted to wear her fairy costume. She put on the wings, the dress, and the wand. She felt very pretty and happy. She decided to go outside and show her friends.
But her mom warned her. She said, "Lily, it is cold outside. You need to wear a coat and a hat. You will get sick if you don't." Lily did not want to wear a coat and a hat. She said, "But mom, I am a fairy. Fairies don't wear coats and hats. They fly and sparkle."
Her mom said, "I know, Lily, but you are not a real fairy. You are a little girl. And little girls need to stay warm and healthy. Please, listen to me and put on your coat and hat. You can still be a fairy with them."
Lily thought about it. She did not want to get sick. She did not want to make her mom sad. She loved her mom. She said, "Okay, mom. I will wear my coat and hat. Thank you for caring about me." She gave her mom a hug and a kiss.
Her mom smiled and said, "You are welcome, Lily. I love you very much. You are a very good and grateful girl. Now, go and have fun with your friends. And be careful with your wand. Don't poke anyone with it."
Lily nodded and said, "I will, mom. I love you too." She put on her coat and hat and went outside. She still felt like a fairy. She flew and sparkled with her friends. They all liked her costume. They all had a good time. Lily was happy.

Lily and Ben are youth. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they go to the park with Mom and Dad. They see a big slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They run and laugh and have fun.
"Look, Lily, I can go very fast on the slide!" Ben says. He climbs up the ladder and slides down. "Whee!"
"Wow, Ben, you are brave!" Lily says. She follows him and slides down too. "This is fun!"
They play on the slide for a long time. Then they go to the swing. Mom pushes them gently and they feel like they are flying. They giggle and shout.
"Higher, Mom, higher!" Ben says.
"Be careful, Ben, don't fall!" Mom says.
They swing for a long time. Then they go to the sandbox. They find some buckets and shovels and make sand castles. They decorate them with sticks and stones and flowers. They pretend they are kings and queens.
"Look, Lily, I made a big castle!" Ben says. He shows her his sand castle. "It has a tower and a gate and a flag!"
"Wow, Ben, your castle is nice!" Lily says. She shows him her sand castle. "Mine has a bridge and a moat and a crown!"
They admire each other's castles. Then they see a dog running towards them. The dog is brown and furry and has a long tail. It looks friendly, but it is silly. It jumps into the sandbox and knocks over their castles. It barks and wags its tail.
"Hey, dog, stop!" Ben says. He tries to chase the dog away. "You ruined our castles!"
"Bad dog, bad!" Lily says. She tries to save her crown. "Go away!"
But the dog does not listen. It thinks they are playing. It licks their faces and rolls in the sand. It makes a big mess.
Mom and Dad see what is happening. They come to help. They apologize to the owner of the dog, who is also in the park. They say sorry to Lily and Ben. They hug them and wipe their faces.
"It's okay, Lily, Ben, don't be sad," Mom says. "The dog did not mean to be naughty. It was just silly."
"Maybe we can make new castles later," Dad says. "Or we can play something else. What do you want to do?"
Lily and Ben look at each other. They are not angry anymore. They are tired. They yawn.
"Can we go home, Mom, Dad?" Lily says. "We are sleepy."
"Me too," Ben says. "We played a lot today."
Mom and Dad smile. They pack their toys and books. They hold Lily and Ben's hands. They walk to the car.
"Yes, let's go home," Mom says. "You had a busy day. You need a nap."
They get in the car. They buckle their seat belts. They drive away. Lily and Ben close their eyes. They dream of slides and swings and sand castles. And silly dogs.

As Spot ran, he did not see the big rock in his way. He tripped and fell. Spot was hurt and sad. A kind girl saw Spot and wanted to help him. She knew how to heal his hurt leg. The girl put a soft bandage on Spot's leg and told him to rest.
After a few days, Spot's leg was all better. He was happy and thankful to the girl. Spot learned that it is important to be careful and watch where you are going. He also learned that there are kind people who can help you when you are hurt. The moral of the story is to be careful and always be grateful for the help you receive.

One day, a big, red ambulance was driving down the street. It was going fast because it had to help someone who was hurt. The driver was very careful, but there was a careless cat that ran into the street.
The driver saw the cat and stopped the ambulance. "Oh no, little cat! You must be more careful," said the driver. The cat looked up at the driver and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't see you coming. Can you help me find my way home?"
The driver agreed to help the cat. He led the cat through the streets, looking for the cat's home. They walked and walked, but they couldn't find it. Then, something unexpected happened. The cat turned into a magical fairy!
"Thank you for helping me," said the fairy. "As a reward, I will grant you one wish." The driver wished for everyone in the town to always be safe and careful. The fairy waved her wand, and the wish came true. From that day on, no one in the town was ever careless again.

Once upon a time, there was an old radish. He was happy living in the garden all by himself, until one day he had a terrible fall.
The old radish was so scared, he began to cry. Just then, a little boy came by and said, "Don't cry, old radish. I can help you."
The old radish looked up at the boy. "Do you really think you can help me?" he asked.
The little boy smiled and said, "Sure! Get on my back and I'll take you to the garden."
So the old radish climbed onto the boy's back, and the boy carried him back to the garden. Once they arrived, the old radish waved goodbye with a big smile on his face.
From then on, the old radish made sure to be extra careful so he would never fall again.

Anna was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a lot of dolls, cars, and books. But her favorite toy was a red car that could drive very fast. She liked to pretend that she was a driver and go on adventures with her car.
One day, she was playing with her car in the living room, when her mom called her for lunch. "Anna, come and eat your soup, it's getting cold!" her mom said. Anna did not want to stop playing, so she said, "No, mom, I'm busy. I have to drive to the zoo with my car." Her mom was not happy. She said, "Anna, you have to eat your soup. It's good for you. And you have to share your toys with your brother. He wants to play with your car too."
Anna did not listen to her mom. She said, "No, mom, this is my car. It's mine. It's expensive. I don't want to share it with anyone." She drove her car away from her mom and her brother. She was very rude.
But as she was driving, she did not see the table leg. She crashed her car into the table leg and broke it. The car was not working anymore. Anna was very sad. She cried and cried. She said, "Oh no, my car, my car. It's broken. What will I do?"
Her mom came and saw what happened. She said, "Anna, I'm sorry your car is broken. But you should have listened to me. You should have eaten your soup and shared your car with your brother. Now you have no car and no soup. And you have to go to the doctor to check your head. You might have hurt yourself when you crashed."
Anna realized that her mom was right. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was wrong. I should have been nice and obeyed you. Can you please fix my car and give me some soup?" Her mom said, "I'll try to fix your car, but I don't know if I can. And I'll warm up your soup, but you have to eat it fast. And you have to say sorry to your brother and let him play with your toys sometimes. Do you understand?" Anna said, "Yes, mom, I understand. I'm sorry, brother. Can we play together?" Her brother said, "Yes, Anna, we can play together. I'm sorry too. I know you love your car. Maybe we can find another toy to drive to the zoo." Anna smiled and hugged her brother. She learned her lesson. She learned to be kind, to share, and to listen to her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a modest little cat named Mimi. She lived in a small house with her best friend, a tiny mouse named Tim. Mimi and Tim loved to play together all day long. They played hide and seek, and tag, and many other fun games.
One day, Mimi and Tim found a big box in the house. They wanted to see if they could both fit inside the box. Mimi jumped in first, and then Tim tried to jump in too. But, oh no! The box was too small for both of them to fit inside. Mimi and Tim started to worry. They didn't want to play in the box if they couldn't both fit.
Mimi had an idea. She said, "Tim, let's go find a bigger box so we can both fit inside and play together." Tim agreed, and they went on a hunt to find a bigger box. They looked in the kitchen, the living room, and the bedroom. Finally, they found a big box in the garage. Mimi and Tim were so happy! They both jumped inside the box and played together all day long. And they never had to worry about fitting in the box again.

Lily liked to sign her name in her diary. She had a pink diary with a lock and a key. She wrote about her day, her friends, and her dreams. She drew pictures of flowers, stars, and animals. She felt happy when she signed her name at the end of each page.
One night, Lily heard a scary noise in her room. It sounded like a growl. She was afraid. She hid under her blanket and held her diary tight. She hoped the scary noise would go away.
She peeked out of her blanket and saw a big shadow on the wall. It looked like a monster. She screamed and ran to the door. She tried to open it, but it was locked. She was trapped.
She heard the scary noise again. It was coming from her closet. She saw the door open slowly. She saw two yellow eyes and a big mouth. She was very scared.
She remembered her diary. She had an idea. She opened her diary and showed the monster the pages. She pointed to her name and said, "This is me. Lily. I am not afraid of you. You are not real. You are just a shadow. Go away."
The monster looked at the diary. It saw the words and the pictures. It saw Lily's name. It felt confused. It did not understand. It did not like the diary. It made a loud noise and ran back to the closet. It slammed the door.
Lily was brave. She unlocked the door and ran to her mom and dad. They hugged her and told her they were proud of her. They said the monster was just a bad dream. They said the diary was her friend. They said she could sign her name as many times as she wanted. Lily smiled and felt safe. She loved her diary.

Sam and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the backyard. They liked to make them zoom and crash and honk. Sam had a red car and Lily had a green car. They pretended they were racing on a big road.
"Look at me, I'm so fast!" Sam said, making his car go forward and backward. "You can't catch me, Lily!"
"Yes, I can!" Lily said, making her car follow Sam's. "My car is green, like the grass. It can hide and sneak up on you!"
They chased each other around the yard, having fun. But then, Sam's car got stuck in a hole. He tried to make it move, but it wouldn't. He got angry and pulled hard on his car.
"Hey, be careful!" Lily said. "You might break your car!"
"I don't care!" Sam said. "It's a stupid car! It can't even get out of a hole!"
He pulled harder and harder, until his car snapped in half. He threw the pieces on the ground and started to cry.
Lily felt sorry for Sam. She went over to him and gave him a hug.
"It's okay, Sam," she said. "I know you're sad. But you shouldn't be so rough with your toys. They can get hurt, too."
She picked up the pieces of Sam's car and brought them to him.
"Maybe we can fix it," she said. "Or maybe we can share my car. It's still green and good."
Sam looked at Lily and wiped his tears. He felt bad for being mean to his car and to Lily.
"Thank you, Lily," he said. "You're a good friend. I'm sorry I was mad. Can we still play?"
Lily smiled and nodded. She handed him one half of her car.
"Sure, we can still play," she said. "But let's be gentle and careful. And let's reverse our cars sometimes, so they don't get stuck in holes."
They agreed and started to play again, reversing their cars every few inches. They learned to be kind to their toys and to each other. They had more fun that way.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a shiny silver ball in their toy box. They both wanted to play with it, but there was only one ball.
"Give me the ball, Lily!" Tom said. "I saw it first!"
"No, Tom, I want the ball!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and round!"
They pulled and tugged at the ball, but neither of them would let go. They started to yell and cry, and their mom heard them.
"What is going on here?" Mom asked. "Why are you fighting over a ball?"
"Mom, Tom is trying to take the ball from me!" Lily said.
"Mom, Lily is trying to take the ball from me!" Tom said.
Mom looked at the ball and shook her head. "This is not a toy, children. This is a silver ornament that belongs to Grandma. She gave it to me to keep it safe. It is very old and fragile, and you could break it if you are not careful."
Tom and Lily felt sorry for what they had done. They did not know that the ball was not a toy, and that it was special to Mom and Grandma. They let go of the ball and hugged each other.
"We are sorry, Mom," they said. "We did not mean to be bad. We just wanted to play with the ball."
Mom smiled and hugged them back. "I know, children. But you should not fight over things, even if they are toys. You should share and take turns, and be kind to each other. That is what makes you happy and jolly, not what you have."
Tom and Lily nodded and agreed. They learned their lesson, and decided to play with their other toys instead. They also promised to be more careful with Grandma's silver ball, and to ask Mom before they touched anything that was not theirs. Mom was proud of them, and gave them each a kiss. They were a jolly family again.

Sam was a rat who lived in a cage. He was very hungry. He wanted to eat the cheese that was on the table. But he could not get out of the cage. The cage had a lock and a key.
One day, a boy came to the room. He saw the cheese and wanted to eat it. He took the key from the shelf and opened the cage. He said, "Hello, rat. Do you want some cheese?"
Sam was happy. He nodded his head. He ran out of the cage and jumped on the table. He bit the cheese. It was very good. He said, "Thank you, boy. You are very nice."
The boy smiled. He said, "You are welcome, rat. You are very cute." He gave Sam some more cheese. He said, "But you have to go back to the cage soon. My mom will be angry if she sees you here."
Sam understood. He said, "Okay, boy. I will go back to the cage. But can you leave the key here? Maybe you can come back tomorrow and give me some more cheese."
The boy nodded. He said, "Sure, rat. I will come back tomorrow. But you have to be quiet and not make a mess. And don't eat the cheese that is in the fridge. It is old and it will make you sick. It will rot in your tummy."
Sam agreed. He said, "Okay, boy. I will not eat the cheese that is in the fridge. I will only eat the cheese that you give me. You are my friend."
The boy and Sam hugged. They were happy. They ate some more cheese and then Sam went back to the cage. The boy left the key on the shelf and said goodbye. He said, "See you tomorrow, rat."
Sam said, "See you tomorrow, boy." He curled up in the cage and fell asleep. He dreamed of cheese and friendship.

The next day, Jane went to her new school. She was still a little nervous, but she thought of Bob and felt better. She talked to the other kids at school and made new friends. Jane had a great day and couldn't wait to talk to Bob about all the fun stuff she did at school.

Once upon a time, there was a bee who wanted to go on an adventure. She flew and flew until she came to a hive. She was tired from all the flying, so she decided to take a rest.
Suddenly, something scary came out of the hive - it was a giant bear! The bee was so scared that she ran and ran as fast as she could. She flew away and kept going until she was too tired to fly anymore.
Finally the bee came to a big, flowery meadow. She was still tired, but she was safe again. She found a nice place to land and take a nap. After she had a good sleep, the bee was no longer tired and she was ready for her next adventure.

As they played, Max started to feel tired. He could not run as fast as before. Lily noticed and asked, "Are you okay, Max?" Max looked at her and barked softly. Lily's mom was a doctor, and she told Lily that Max might have a lung problem. They took Max to the vet to get better. The vet gave Max some medicine, and soon he was running and playing with Lily again.

The next day, the cauliflower woke up and was very happy. It learned that with the help of friends, anything is possible.

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big box under a tree. They opened the box and saw many things inside. There were toys, books, clothes, and candy.
"Wow, look at all these things!" Anna said. "Can we take some?"
"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe they belong to someone."
Anna saw a bag of mints in the box. She loved mints. She took the bag and opened it. She ate a mint and smiled.
"Mmm, these are good!" she said. "Do you want one?"
Ben nodded. He liked mints too. He reached for the bag, but Anna pulled it away.
"No, these are mine!" she said. "You can have something else."
Ben felt sad. He thought Anna was not very thoughtful. He looked at the box and saw a scarf. He liked the scarf. It was red and soft. He took the scarf and wrapped it around his neck.
"Look, I have a scarf!" he said. "It is warm and nice."
Anna saw the scarf and wanted it. She did not like her mints anymore. She wanted the scarf. She grabbed the scarf and tried to pull it off Ben's neck.
"Give me the scarf!" she said. "It is better than the mints!"
Ben did not want to give the scarf. He liked the scarf. He held on to the scarf and tried to keep it on his neck.
"No, it is mine!" he said. "You have the mints!"
They pulled and pulled the scarf. The scarf was tight around Ben's neck. He could not breathe. He felt dizzy and scared. He tried to say something, but he could not.
Anna did not notice. She was angry and greedy. She pulled and pulled the scarf. She wanted the scarf.
The scarf was too tight. Ben could not breathe. He fell to the ground. He did not move. He did not make a sound.
Anna finally got the scarf. She was happy. She put the scarf around her neck. She looked at Ben and smiled.
"Ha, I have the scarf!" she said. "It is mine!"
She did not see that Ben was not breathing. She did not see that Ben was not alive. She did not see that she had killed her friend.

One sunny day, a little fish named Fin was swimming in the big sea. Fin wanted to be famous. He saw a net and thought, "If I jump in the net, I will be famous!"
A wise old fish named Mr. Whiskers saw Fin. He swam over and said, "Fin, don't go in the net! It's not safe!" Fin felt sad, but Mr. Whiskers encouraged him. "You can be famous in other ways. Help others and be kind."
Fin listened to Mr. Whiskers. He swam around the sea, helping his friends. He helped a crab find his home, and he cheered up a sad jellyfish. Soon, everyone knew Fin as the kindest fish in the sea.
The other sea animals loved Fin. They told stories about how he helped them. Fin became famous for being kind and helpful, not for jumping in the net.
The moral of the story is: You can become famous by being kind and helpful to others.

"I don't know, Tom," Lily said. "It looks too fast and scary. What if I fall or hurt myself?"
"You won't, Lily, I promise. Trust me, I'll catch you at the bottom. Don't be stubborn, just try it once. You'll like it, I'm sure."
Lily looked at Tom. He was her best friend and he always kept his promises. She trusted him, but she was still scared. She took a deep breath and sat down on the slide. She closed her eyes and let go.
Lily felt a rush of speed as she slid down the slide. She screamed and laughed at the same time. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She opened her eyes and saw Tom waiting for her at the bottom. He smiled and held out his arms.
Lily reached the end of the slide and flew into Tom's arms. He hugged her and spun her around. They both giggled and cheered.
"See, Lily, I told you it was fun!" Tom said. "You did great! You're very brave!"
"Thank you, Tom, you were right!" Lily said. "It was fun! You're very fast and strong!"
They hugged again and then ran back to the slide. They slid down again and again, enjoying the speed and the thrill. They trusted each other and had a lot of fun. They were best friends.

The old man had to act quickly! He ran into the lake and distracted the crocodiles as Sophie ran away with the rice. Sophie was so happy and thankful for the old man's help. From then on, she was extra careful when searching for anything in the future.

The bike looked at the motor's writing and said, "This is great! You are a smart motor. You can write about anything you want."

Tom and Sue were playing with their toys in the park. They had a ball, a doll, a car and a bear. They liked their toys very much. They were their original toys, not like the ones in the shop.

"OK," Sue said. "But be careful not to lose it."
They threw the ball back and forth, laughing and shouting. They did not see the thief who was hiding behind a tree. He was a bad man who wanted to take their toys.
When Tom threw the ball high in the air, the thief ran out and grabbed it. He also took the doll, the car and the bear. He put them in a big bag and ran away.
"Hey, stop!" Tom and Sue cried. "Those are our toys! Give them back!"
But the thief did not listen. He was faster than them and soon he was out of sight.

"Who was that man?" Sue asked. "Why did he take our toys?"
"He was a thief," Tom said. "He was a very mean and greedy thief. He wanted to have our toys, even though they were ours. He did not care about us."
"That's not fair," Sue said. "We worked hard to get our toys. We saved our money and did our chores. We loved our toys. They were our original toys, not like the ones in the shop."

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a big bottle of bubble soap and a wand. They blew many bubbles in the air. They liked to watch the bubbles fly and pop.
"Look, Lily, a big bubble!" Tom said. He pointed to a bubble that was bigger than his head. "Let's catch it!"
They ran after the big bubble. They tried to touch it gently with their hands. But the bubble was too fast and too high. It flew over the fence and into the woods.
"Let's follow it!" Lily said. She was curious and brave. She climbed over the fence and ran into the woods. Tom followed her. He was clever and careful. He looked around for dangers and signs.
They saw the big bubble land on a pile of leaves. They ran to it and reached for it. But before they could touch it, a squirrel jumped out of the leaves and popped the bubble with its teeth.
"Hey, that's our bubble!" Tom shouted. He was angry and sad. He liked the big bubble.
"Sorry, kids, I thought it was a nut," the squirrel said. He was hungry and cheeky. He liked to eat nuts.
"That's not a nut, that's a bubble. A bubble is made of air and soap. You can't eat it," Lily said. She was smart and polite. She knew a lot of things.
"Oh, I see. Well, I'm sorry for popping your bubble. Do you want another one?" the squirrel said. He felt sorry and friendly. He wanted to make up.
"Yes, please," Tom and Lily said. They smiled and nodded. They liked to make new friends.
The squirrel ran to a nearby tree and came back with a small nut. He gave it to Tom and Lily.
"Here, this is a nut. A nut is made of wood and seed. You can bury it or plant it," the squirrel said. He was generous and helpful. He liked to share.
"Thank you, squirrel. This is a nice nut. We will bury it and maybe it will grow into a tree," Tom and Lily said. They were happy and grateful. They liked to learn new things.
They dug a small hole in the ground and buried the nut. Then they said goodbye to the squirrel and went back to the garden. They blew more bubbles and played until it was time to go home. They had a fun and adventurous day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a bald man named Tom. Tom loved to ring the big bell in the town square. Every day, he would go to the square and ring the bell for all to hear. One day, it rained a lot, and there were many puddles on the ground.
Tom saw a big puddle on his way to the bell. He thought, "I must jump over this puddle to get to the bell." But he was not sure if he could make it. He tried to find another way, but the puddle was too big. Tom knew he had to try.
Tom took a big step back and ran fast. He jumped high and far to get over the puddle. "I did it!" he said with a smile. But then, he heard a small voice from the puddle. "Hey, you splashed me!" It was a little frog.
"I am sorry," said Tom. "I did not see you there. I was trying to get to the bell." The frog looked at Tom and said, "It is okay. I like the sound of the bell, too. Can I come with you?" Tom smiled and said, "Yes, let's go ring the bell together."
From that day on, Tom and the frog became good friends. They would ring the bell together and make the town happy. And every time it rained, Tom would help the frog find a new puddle to play in.

So, Lucy set out with a picnic basket on her way to the coast. Along the way, she spotted something that made her very curious. It was an old anchor. She had never seen one before! She wondered why it was there, what it was used for, and why it was so big.
When Lucy reached the shore, she saw many different kinds of creatures, like starfish, snails and crabs. Lucy asked them all: "Why is that anchor there?" But none of the sea animals could answer her questions.
Suddenly, Lucy saw a big, healthy shark swim by. She asked him the same question: "Why is that anchor there?"
The shark answered, "Well, young one, that anchor was placed there to keep ships safe during storms. Of course, they need to be big and strong to do the job!"
Lucy was in awe. She was so thankful that the shark had answered her question. She had learned an important lesson about the shore that day.

Oscar was a sad little mouse. He had been locked up in a dark, cold frame for days. He had been forgotten by the people that used to love him.
Suddenly, he heard a voice outside.
“Let me in! Please!” Oscar squeaked.
The door opened and a friendly face peered in. It was his best friend, Anna.
“I’ve been looking for you everywhere!” Anna said. She smiled and unlocked the frame.
Oscar hopped out and hugged her. He was so happy to see her.
“Don’t worry,” Anna said. “You’ll never have to be sad or locked up like this again. I’ll make sure of it.”

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a loud horn. The truck is different from the cars they know. It has a big box on the back and a long arm on the front.
"Wow, look at that truck!" Lily says. "What is it doing?"
"I don't know," Tom says. "Let's go closer and see."
They run to the truck and see a man inside. He is wearing a yellow hat and a blue shirt. He is holding a big stick with buttons. He pushes a button and the long arm moves. It picks up a big trash can and puts it in the box.
"Hello, kids," the man says. "Do you like my truck?"
"Yes, we do," Lily and Tom say. "It is very cool. What is your name?"
"My name is Sam," the man says. "I am a trash collector. I take the trash away and make the park clean."
"That is a good job," Lily says. "Can we help you?"
"Sure, you can," Sam says. "But you have to be careful. The truck is very big and loud. When I push this button, the horn will shout. Do you want to hear it?"
"Yes, please," Lily and Tom say.
Sam pushes the button and the horn shouts. "BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!"
Lily and Tom cover their ears and laugh. They like the horn. It is fun and different. They say thank you to Sam and wave goodbye. They go back to play in the park. They are happy. They have a new friend.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily shouted. "We are stuck in the refrigerator!"
They banged on the door and cried, but no one heard them. They felt very cold and scared and helpless. They wished they had listened to Mommy and not played with the refrigerator.
After a while, Mommy came to the kitchen and heard some noises from the refrigerator. She opened it and saw Tom and Lily shivering and sobbing.
"What are you doing in there?" Mommy asked. "You could have frozen to death!"
"We are sorry, Mommy. We wanted some ice cream and we got stuck in the refrigerator," Tom and Lily said.
Mommy hugged them and took them out of the refrigerator. She wrapped them in warm blankets and gave them some hot chocolate.
"Never play with the refrigerator again. It is very dangerous and you could get hurt. The refrigerator is not a toy. It is for keeping food fresh," Mommy said.
"We understand, Mommy. We will never play with the refrigerator again. We learned our lesson," Tom and Lily said.
Mommy kissed them and told them she loved them. She was glad they were safe and sound.
The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not meant for playing. They could be harmful and cause trouble. Listen to your parents and follow their rules. They know what is best for you.

The puppy ran off, so the girl started running after him. She ran around the whole park, but she could not find him anywhere. She was about to cry when she finally saw him behind a bush. He was busy cleaning himself.
The girl was so relieved and ran to him. She hugged him tightly and said, "Please don't run away again. I was so scared!"
The puppy looked at her with his big eyes and gave her a big kiss. From then on, she never let go of his leash.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a lion with an attractive mane. He was very proud of his mane. He would walk around the jungle and roar loudly so everyone could see and hear him.
One day, the lion found a shiny razor on the ground. He picked it up and said, "I can use this to make my mane even more beautiful!" He carefully used the razor to trim his mane, making it look even more attractive.
As the lion walked through the jungle, he met a little monkey. The monkey looked at the lion's mane and said, "Wow, your mane is so pretty! I heard you roar and I wanted to see you." The lion smiled and roared again, happy that his attractive mane and loud roar made a new friend.

Bee was a very independent little bee. She liked to fly far away from the hive and find new flowers to chew. She did not like to listen to the queen bee or the other bees who told her to stay close and work together.
One day, Bee flew to a big garden full of roses. She saw a red rose that looked very sweet and juicy. She flew to it and started to chew on its petals. She did not notice that there was a spider hiding in the rose. The spider saw Bee and wanted to catch her for his lunch.
"Hello, little bee," the spider said in a friendly voice. "Do you like this rose? It is very tasty, isn't it?"
Bee was surprised to hear the spider. She looked up and saw his eight legs and his big fangs. She felt scared and tried to fly away. But the spider was faster and threw a sticky web around her. He pulled her closer to his mouth.
"Help! Help!" Bee cried. "Let me go, spider! You are mean and hungry!"
But the spider did not let her go. He laughed and said, "No, little bee, you are my lunch. You should have stayed with your hive and your friends. They would have helped you. But you were too independent and foolish. Now you will pay for your mistake."
Bee felt very sorry and sad. She wished she had listened to the queen bee and the other bees. She wished she had not flown so far away and chewed on the rose. She wished she had a friend to save her.
Suddenly, she heard a loud buzz. She saw a swarm of bees flying towards her. They were her hive mates. They had heard her cry and came to help her. They stung the spider and cut the web with their sharp teeth. They freed Bee and flew away with her.
"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Bee said to her hive mates. "You are my friends and my family. I am sorry I was so independent and stubborn. I will never fly away from you again. I will work with you and listen to you. I love you all."
The hive mates smiled and hugged Bee. They were happy to have her back. They flew back to the hive and shared their honey and stories. Bee learned her lesson and became a better bee. She still liked to chew on flowers, but she always stayed close to her hive and her friends.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the park. There is a stream in the park. The stream has water and rocks and fish.
One day, Tom and Sam play a game. They pretend to be soldiers. They have sticks for guns. They hide behind trees and bushes. They try to catch each other.
"Bang, bang, I got you!" Tom shouts. He runs to Sam and points his stick at him.
"No, you missed!" Sam says. He runs away and jumps over the stream.
"Come back, you coward!" Tom says. He follows Sam and tries to jump over the stream too. But he slips on a rock and falls into the water.
"Help, help, I'm wet!" Tom cries. He drops his stick and splashes in the water.
Sam hears Tom and runs back to him. He sees Tom in the water and laughs.
"Ha, ha, you fell in the stream!" Sam says. He reaches out his hand and helps Tom out of the water.
"Stop laughing, it's not funny!" Tom says. He is wet and cold and angry.
"Sorry, sorry, I'm sorry!" Sam says. He hugs Tom and gives him his stick.
"Here, take your gun. You are a brave soldier. You did not surrender." Sam says.
Tom smiles and hugs Sam back.
"Thank you, you are a good brother. You did not leave me." Tom says.
They walk back to their mom. She has a towel and a snack for them. She dries them and feeds them. She tells them she loves them.
They love her too. They love each other. They are happy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. One day, they find a big box in the hall. It has a label that says "Test. Do not open."
"What is this?" Sara asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a gift for us," Ben says.
They look at each other and smile. They drag the box to their room. They open it carefully. Inside, they see a lot of fancy clothes. There are dresses, hats, shoes, and coats. There are also some masks, wigs, and glasses.
"Wow! Look at all these things!" Sara says.
"Let's try them on!" Ben says.
They take out the clothes and lay them on the bed. They start to dress up. Sara puts on a pink dress, a hat with feathers, and a pair of high heels. Ben puts on a suit, a tie, a hat with a flower, and a pair of glasses. They look at themselves in the mirror and laugh.
"We look so funny!" Sara says.
"We look so fancy!" Ben says.
They pretend to be different people. They talk in funny voices and make up stories. They have a lot of fun.
Meanwhile, Mom and Dad come home. They see the box in the hall. They see the label that says "Test. Do not open."
"Oh no! That's the box from the costume shop. We were supposed to return it today. It was for a test for a play," Mom says.
"Let's go and get it. Maybe they didn't open it," Dad says.
They go to the twins' room. They open the door. They see Sara and Ben in their fancy clothes. They see the bed covered with clothes. They see the mirror with lipstick marks. They are shocked.
"Sara! Ben! What have you done?" Mom says.
"We were playing. We found the box. It had fancy clothes. We wanted to try them on," Sara says.
"We didn't know it was a test. We thought it was a gift. We had fun," Ben says.
Mom and Dad look at each other. They don't know whether to be angry or amused. They see the twins' innocent faces. They see the joy in their eyes. They decide to be kind.
"Well, you did make a mess. But you also made us laugh. And you have a lot of imagination. So we won't be mad. But you have to help us clean up. And you have to say sorry to the costume shop. And you have to promise not to open any more boxes without asking," Mom says.
"OK, Mom. OK, Dad. We're sorry. We promise. Can we keep one fancy thing each?" Sara says.
"Please, please, please?" Ben says.
Mom and Dad think for a moment. They nod.
"OK, you can keep one fancy thing each. But only one. And only if you clean up. Now, let's go and put everything back in the box," Dad says.
Sara and Ben hug Mom and Dad. They say thank you. They pick their favorite fancy thing. Sara picks the hat with feathers. Ben picks the glasses. They put the rest of the clothes in the box. They help Mom and Dad carry the box to the car. They go to the costume shop. They say sorry. They return the box. They go home. They put their fancy things in their closet. They play with their toys. They are happy.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play in the garden. They liked to smell the flowers and look for bugs. One day, they saw a big green plant with many leaves. Lily said, "What is this? It smells good."
Tom said, "I don't know. Maybe it is a herb. My mom uses herbs to cook. She says they make food tasty and healthy."
Lily said, "Can we pick some and take it to your mom? Maybe she can make us a snack."
Tom said, "Okay. But we have to be careful. Some plants are not good to touch or eat. They can make us sick or hurt us."
Lily and Tom kneeled down and started to pull the leaves from the plant. They did not know that the plant was poison ivy. It had a sticky sap that made their skin itch and burn. They filled their pockets with the leaves and ran to Tom's house.
They showed the leaves to Tom's mom and said, "Look, mom, we found a herb in the garden. Can you make us a snack with it?"
Tom's mom looked at the leaves and gasped. She said, "Oh no, this is not a herb. This is poison ivy. It is very bad for you. How did you get this?"
Lily and Tom said, "We picked it from the garden. It smelled good. We thought it was a herb."
Tom's mom said, "You should never pick plants that you don't know. They can be dangerous. You have to wash your hands and face right now. And throw away those leaves. They can make you very sick."
Lily and Tom felt scared and sorry. They ran to the bathroom and washed their hands and face. But it was too late. They already had red rashes and blisters on their skin. They felt very itchy and sore. They cried and wished they had listened to Tom's mom. She was reliable and knew what was good and bad for them. They learned a hard lesson that day.
