As Tom climbed higher, something unexpected happened. Sue's magic wand started to glow. Suddenly, the tree grew taller and taller. Tom was now at the top of the tree, and he could see the whole town. Sue and Tom were amazed by the magic. They learned that sometimes, when you dare to try new things and are persistent, magic can happen.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a cave. The cave was big and dark. Tim was scared, but he wanted to see what was inside. So, he took a deep breath and went in.
Inside the cave, Tim met a friendly bear named Ben. Ben was sad because his friend, a bird named Bella, was jealous. Bella could fly high, but she wanted to live in a big cave like Ben. Ben said, "I wish Bella wasn't jealous. I want her to be happy."
Tim thought for a moment and said, "I know, let's pray!" So, Tim and Ben sat down and prayed. They asked for Bella to be happy and not jealous anymore. After they prayed, they went to find Bella.
When they found Bella, she was smiling. Bella said, "I'm not jealous anymore. I'm happy because I can fly and see the beautiful sky. We can all be friends and play together!" Tim, Ben, and Bella played all day and had lots of fun. They were happy to be friends and share their gifts with each other.

Tim went to his friends and showed them the magazine. They all looked at it together, taking turns to see the pictures. They laughed and talked about the stories inside. Tim felt happy because he shared his magazine with his friends.
The moral of the story is that sharing can bring happiness and make new friends.

Mia's big brother, Tom, saw her trying. He wanted to help. Tom shook the tree too. The tree shook and shook, and the peach fell down. Mia and Tom were happy. They shared the peach and it was very yummy.

Lily liked to write in her diary every day. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her feelings. She kept her diary under her pillow, so no one could see it. She thought it was her secret.
One day, her big brother Tom found her diary. He was bored and curious. He opened it and read some of the pages. He laughed at what Lily wrote. He thought it was silly and childish. He decided to have some fun with it.
He ran to the living room, where Lily was playing with her dolls. He waved the diary in the air and shouted, "Look what I found! Lily's diary! Do you want to hear what she writes?" Lily was very anxious. She did not want Tom to read her diary. She did not want anyone to hear her diary. She felt angry and scared.
She jumped up and ran to Tom. She tried to grab the diary from his hand. But Tom was taller and stronger. He pushed her away and threw the diary across the room. It landed on the fireplace, where there was a fire burning. The diary caught fire and started to burn.
Lily screamed and cried. She watched her diary turn into ashes. She felt very sad and hurt. She lost her secret. She lost her diary. She hated Tom. Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He did not mean to burn the diary. He only wanted to tease Lily. He did not know how much it meant to her. He tried to hug her and say sorry. But Lily pushed him away and ran to her room. She did not want to talk to him. She did not want to see him. She did not forgive him.

But, this time he noticed something strange, there was a mouse peeking out of the little hole. He screamed with joy and told his mom about it.
At first, his mom was surprised and then she burst out laughing. It turns out she knew the mouse was there all along and that was why she asked him to unpack his toys everyday! The little boy was so happy to have the mouse in his toy-box and they became great friends.

Once upon a time, there was a fast dog named Max. Max loved to race with his friends. One day, Max saw a big tray in the kitchen. He thought it was a toy, so he took it outside to play.
Max showed the tray to his friends. "Look at my new toy!" he said. His friend, a wise old cat named Whiskers, looked at the tray and shook his head. "That's not a toy, Max. It's a tray for food. Be careful with it," Whiskers warned. But Max didn't listen. He thought Whiskers was just being stupid.
Max and his friends started to race with the tray. They ran and ran, having so much fun. But then, Max tripped and fell. The tray flew into the air and landed with a big crash. The tray was broken into pieces. Max felt sad and knew he should have listened to Whiskers.
Max went to Whiskers and said, "I'm sorry I didn't listen to you. You were right about the tray." Whiskers patted Max on the head and said, "It's okay, Max. We all make mistakes. Now you know to be more careful next time."
From that day on, Max always listened to his wise friend Whiskers. And they raced together, but only with their toys, not with trays.

Mama and Daddy were in the garden on a warm evening. The sun was in the distant sky and the birds were singing in the trees. A little squirrel was gathering nuts, when suddenly the wind picked up and the leaves started to scatter.
Mama said, "Look at the beautiful leaves, scatter!"  Daddy nodded and smiled.
Little Molly giggled and quickly ran outside, flapping her arms and spinning around. She watched the way the leaves scattered as the wind blew. When she opened her eyes, she saw the sun setting in the distance.
Mama rubbed Molly's back and said, "It's time to go inside now, the evening is getting late."
Molly smiled and said, "Look, the leaves are still scattering!" And with that, she twirled and ran as fast as she could back inside.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play together. One day, they had a party for their birthday. They had cake, balloons, and presents. They were very happy and proud.
They invited their friends from the park. They played games and sang songs. They had a lot of fun. But Anna and Ben also liked to explore. They wanted to see what was in the other rooms.
They said to their mom, "Can we wander around the house?" Their mom said, "Yes, but be careful. Don't touch anything that is not yours. And come back soon."
Anna and Ben nodded. They held hands and wandered around the house. They saw the kitchen, the bathroom, the living room, and the bedroom. They saw many things that were new and interesting. They saw a vase, a clock, a lamp, and a pillow.
They came to the last room. It was the office. They saw a big desk, a chair, a computer, and a bookshelf. They saw a shiny trophy on the shelf. They wanted to see it closer.
They climbed on the chair and reached for the trophy. But they were too small. They slipped and fell. The trophy fell too. It broke into pieces. They heard a loud noise.
They were scared. They ran back to the party. They saw their mom. She looked angry. She said, "What did you do? Why did you break the trophy? That was daddy's prize. He worked very hard for it. He was very proud of it."
Anna and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We just wanted to see it. We didn't mean to break it. We are sorry, daddy."
Their mom hugged them. She said, "I know you are sorry. But you should not wander around the house without permission. You should not touch things that are not yours. You should be careful and respectful. Do you understand?"
Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "We understand, mom. We will not do it again. We love you, mom. We love you, daddy."
Their mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. You are my twins. You are my pride. Now, let's go back to the party. And let's say sorry to daddy too."

Once upon a time, in a big, green landscape, there was a little bunny named Bob. Bob loved to eat tasty carrots. One sunny day, Bob went out to find some tasty carrots for lunch.
While Bob was hopping around, he saw a big, round thing on the ground. He had never seen anything like it before. Bob started to panic because he didn't know what it was. He ran back to his bunny hole to hide.
Later, Bob's friend, a wise old owl, came to visit him. Bob told the owl about the big, round thing he saw. The owl laughed and said, "Don't panic, Bob! That's just a big, tasty apple!" Bob and the owl went back to the apple, and they both had a tasty snack. The unexpected thing turned out to be a yummy treat for both friends.

Once there was a soldier who lived in a very distant land. He was feeling very hot and sweaty because the sun was shining so brightly.
The soldier knew of a special place where he could get relief from the heat. So, he set off on his horse to the place he'd heard about.
As he got closer, he saw a sparkling river ahead of him. When he reached the river, he couldn't believe how wonderfully cool the water felt on his skin.
He exclaimed, "Ahh! I knew I would find relief here!"
He sat by the riverbank and dipped his feet in the water. Slowly but surely, he began to feel the heat of the day fading away.
A small voice spoke up from behind him. It was a little girl with a basket of apples. She said, "Sir, would you like some of my apples? I picked them myself!"
The soldier smiled and replied, "Thank you! I would love some apples to go with this cool, dry air here. I think it will make the perfect snack!"
The little girl smiled, and the soldier enjoyed his delicious snack by the river. He was grateful for the comforting distance from the scorching sun in his distant land.

Once there were two friends, Sue and Bob. They both loved to study.
One day, they went to the market to buy some food. Bob looked at all the different fruit, but what caught his eye was the rare avocado.
“I want to buy the avocado,” Bob said.
But Sue said, “No Bob, it’s too rare and too expensive. Let’s buy something else.”
Bob was very sad and didn’t know what to do. He really wanted the avocado.
But then Sue had a good idea. “Why don’t we study about avocados? Then we can learn about them without having to buy one.”
Bob liked Sue’s idea and so they spent the day studying about avocados.
At the end of the day, Bob felt very happy. He had learned a lot and still had some money left over.
The moral of the story is that sometimes it’s better to learn about something than to buy it. You can get a lot of satisfaction out of learning and it can save you money too!

Sue and Ben the bear went to visit their friends. They gave hugs, shared toys, and played fun games. All of Sue's friends were very happy. At the end of the day, Sue and Ben went back home, feeling good about their thoughtful day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play games with his friends. One day, they decided to play a game to see who could release their toy car the fastest. The one who won would get a big prize.
"Ready, set, go!" shouted Tim. All the kids released their toy cars. The cars raced down the street. Tim's car was very fast, but his friend Sam's car was even faster. Sam's car reached the finish line first.
"Yay, I win!" said Sam, with a big smile. "What's the prize?" Tim handed Sam a box. Inside the box was a big, disgusting, slimy frog. Sam screamed, "Eww! That's disgusting!" All the kids laughed and had a lot of fun that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Alex. One day, Alex wanted to be a superman and he put on dad’s cape and ran around the house. Suddenly, he stopped at the kitchen. He opened the cupboard and saw a bottle of oil inside.
He asked his dad, “Can I play with this?”
Dad said, “Yes, but don’t forget to put it back when you’re done.”
Alex took the bottle of oil and ran around. He was so busy playing he forgot to put the oil back.
The next morning, Alex decided to play superman again. But when he opened the cupboard, he saw a mess. The oil had spilled everywhere and it was very soft.
Dad was angry and said, “You should not forget things like this. Now, we have to clean up this mess.”
Alex was so sorry and he was scared of his dad. He started to cry.
That was when Alex learnt that if he does not follow dad’s instructions, bad things will happen.

One day, a big dog named Max went for a walk. Max was a popular dog in the park. All the little kids loved to play with him. Max liked to chew on sticks and play with his ball. Today, Max saw a new seat in the park. It was big and red. Max wanted to sit on it.
Max went to the seat and said, "I want to sit." But when he tried to sit, he fell off. Max was sad. He tried again and again, but he could not sit on the seat. A little girl named Lily saw Max and came to help. She said, "Max, let me help you."
Lily held Max's paw and helped him sit on the seat. Max was happy. He said, "Thank you, Lily." Then, something unexpected happened. The seat started to move! It was a swing! Max and Lily laughed and played on the swing all day. They had so much fun, and the new swing became very popular in the park.

One day, a purple bird flew up to the sky. He was so happy and he flew higher and higher. Soon, he was very far away from his family.
At first it was great but after a while, the bird got scared. He wanted to be back home with his family.
He tried flying back down but every time he flew down, the wind seemed to push him back up. He started to cry.
Suddenly, a soft voice came through the wind. It said, "Little bird, flap your wings and increase your speed."
The bird did as he was told and the wind no longer pushed him back. He was able to fly down until he reached his family. They were so glad to see him and he was glad to be home.

Sam and Lily are twins. They like to play outside when it is hot. Mom gives them a big melon to share. She says, "Be nice and behave. Do not make a mess with the melon."
Sam and Lily take the melon to the yard. They cut it with a knife. They see the red and juicy inside. They say, "Yum!" They each take a big piece and bite it. The melon is sweet and cold. It makes them happy.
But then Sam sees that Lily has a bigger piece than him. He feels mad. He says, "That is not fair. Give me some of your melon." Lily says, "No, this is mine. You have enough." They start to fight. They pull and push the melon. They make a lot of noise.
Mom hears them and comes outside. She sees the melon on the ground. She sees the juice and seeds on their clothes and faces. She sees their angry and sad eyes. She says, "Oh no! What have you done? You did not behave. You wasted the melon. You made a mess. You hurt each other. You are not nice."
Sam and Lily feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We were greedy and mean. We did not share. We did not behave. We love the melon. We love each other. Can we have another melon, please?" Mom says, "No, you cannot have another melon. You have to learn your lesson. You have to clean up the mess. You have to hug and say sorry to each other. You have to be nice and behave. Maybe next time you can have another melon, if you are good." Sam and Lily do what Mom says. They hope they can have another melon soon. They hope they can be nice and behave.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Sally. Sally was three years old. She liked to pretend. She loved to pretend that she was going on all kinds of adventures.
One day, Sally decided to pretend to explore a forest. She imagined the forest to be dark and mysterious. She was scared, but she was brave and wanted to keep exploring.
Sally walked and walked, until she came to a very tall tree. It was so tall that it seemed to reach the sky. Suddenly, she heard voices. She couldn't believe it!
"Who's there?" she called out.
"It's us!" a tiny voice said. Sally looked up and saw a group of little fairies sitting on the branches of the tree.
"We wanted to make sure you have a safe journey. Don't be scared," said the fairies.
Sally was amazed. She thanked them and then pretended she was a brave explorer until it was time to go home.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were king and queen of the flowers. They wore crowns made of daisies and grass. They had a big castle made of cardboard boxes.
One day, they saw a big bee flying near their castle. It was black and yellow and had a sharp sting. Lily was scared of the bee. She said to Ben, "Look, a bee! It is scary. It can hurt us. We should run away."
But Ben was not scared of the bee. He said to Lily, "No, we should not run away. We are king and queen. We can warn the bee to go away. We can say, 'Bee, this is our castle. You cannot come here. Go away or we will make you go away.'"
Lily did not think this was a good idea. She said to Ben, "Ben, no. The bee will not listen to us. It will be angry. It will sting us. Please, let us run away."
But Ben did not listen to Lily. He stood up and shouted at the bee, "Bee, this is our castle. You cannot come here. Go away or we will make you go away."
The bee did not like Ben's shout. It flew closer to Ben and buzzed loudly. It was ready to sting Ben. Ben was scared now. He wished he had listened to Lily. He said to Lily, "Lily, help me. The bee is scary. It will hurt me. Let us run away."
Lily grabbed Ben's hand and pulled him away from the bee. They ran to their house and closed the door. They were safe now. They hugged each other and said, "We are sorry. We should have listened to each other. We should not have played near the bee. It was scary. We are glad we are okay."
The end.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park with her daddy. They played on the swings, the slide, and the seesaw. Lucy was very happy and having lots of fun.
Suddenly, Lucy saw a small, helpless bird on the ground. She wanted to help the bird, so she called out, "Daddy, look! The bird needs our help!" But her daddy didn't hear her. He was talking to another daddy at the park. Lucy felt sad and didn't want to ignore the bird.
Lucy decided to help the bird by herself. She gently picked up the bird and put it in her pocket. Then, she ran to her daddy and said, "Daddy, I found a bird that needs our help!" Her daddy looked surprised and asked, "Where did you find this bird, Lucy?" Lucy told him about the bird on the ground.
Her daddy smiled and said, "That's great, Lucy! You did a good job helping the bird. But guess what? The bird is not helpless, it's just a baby learning to fly!" Lucy felt happy that she helped the bird and now it could learn to fly with its family. From that day on, Lucy and her daddy always looked for ways to help others at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved yummy food. His mommy made him yummy food all week. One day, Tim saw a big, yummy cake on the table. His mommy said, "Tim, don't eat that cake yet! It is for later."
Tim really wanted the cake. He waited and waited, but he could not stop thinking about the cake. He thought, "I cannot surrender to the cake. I must be good." But Tim could not wait any longer. He took a big bite of the yummy cake.
But, oh no! The cake was not yummy at all. It was yucky! Tim's mommy came in and laughed. "That cake was not for eating, Tim! It was a play cake made of mud!" Tim learned that sometimes, it is better to wait and not surrender to yummy things.

One day, a big race was going to happen in the town. All the animals were very excited. They all wanted to win the race. The race would start when the sun came up. The sky would be pretty at sunrise.
A little rabbit was sure he would win. He was very fast. He saw a big turtle who wanted to race too. The rabbit thought this was interesting. He knew the turtle was slow. The rabbit knew he would win.
The race started at sunrise. The rabbit ran fast but then got tired. He saw the turtle was far behind. So, the rabbit took a nap. When he woke up, he saw the turtle near the finish line. The rabbit ran as fast as he could, but the turtle won the race. The rabbit learned that slow and steady can sometimes win the race too.

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig holes and find rocks and bugs. Lily had a regular hammer that she used to break the rocks. Ben had a shovel that he used to make the holes.
"Look, Lily, I found a big worm!" Ben said, holding up his shovel.
"Wow, Ben, that is a big worm!" Lily said. "Can I see it?"
Ben nodded and gave Lily his shovel. Lily put the hammer down and took the shovel. She looked at the worm and smiled.
"Can I touch it?" she asked.
"Sure, Lily, you can touch it. It is soft and slimy," Ben said.
Lily reached out her hand and touched the worm. It wriggled and tickled her fingers. She giggled and touched it again.
Suddenly, they heard a loud splash. They turned around and saw that the hose was on. It was spraying water everywhere. The water was soaking the yard and their toys.
"Oh no, the hose!" Lily cried.
"Who turned it on?" Ben asked.
They ran to the hose and tried to turn it off. But it was too hard. They could not twist the knob. The water kept coming out.
"Help, help!" they shouted.
But no one heard them. Mom and Dad were inside the house. They were busy making lunch. They did not know that the hose was on.
The water soaked Lily and Ben. It soaked their clothes and their shoes. It soaked their holes and their rocks. It soaked their bugs and their worm.
And it soaked Lily's hammer. The hammer was made of metal. The water made it rust. The hammer turned brown and ugly. It did not work anymore.
Lily and Ben were very sad. They lost their worm. They ruined their hammer. They were wet and cold. They had no fun.
The end.

Once upon a time, in a warm and sunny place, there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to play outside with her friends, the birds and the squirrels. One day, Mia found a big red ball. She was very happy and wanted to play with it.
Mia set the ball on the ground and kicked it high into the sky. As the ball went up, up, up, a bird flew by and said, "Hello, Mia! What a nice ball you have. Can I play too?" Mia smiled and said, "Yes, bird! Let's play together!"
As they played, the sun began to set. The sky turned orange and pink, and the air felt cool. Mia and the bird took a break to catch their breath. They sat on the grass and took in the oxygen from the trees around them. Mia said, "Thank you for playing with me, bird. I had a lot of fun!" The bird replied, "Thank you, Mia! I had fun too. Let's play again tomorrow!" And so, they promised to play together again the next day, under the warm sun and the big blue sky.

Once upon a time, there was a big bull named Billy. Billy was not very nice. He would always push the other animals around. One day, a small bird named Bobby came to the farm. Bobby saw Billy push the other animals and said, "I hate it when you do that."
Billy looked at Bobby and said, "Why do you care? I am big and strong, and they are small and weak."
Bobby was careful and thought for a moment. He said, "You should be nice to them. If you are nice, they will be your friends."
Billy thought about it and decided to try being nice. He stopped pushing the other animals, and soon, he had many friends. The farm was a happy place.
The moral of the story is: Be kind to others, and they will be kind to you.

Timmy and his mom were playing outside in the snow. He had a big container of clay and some stale cookies.
"Mom, look at how icy the snow is! Can I make snow angels?" said Timmy excitedly.
"That sounds like fun. But let's part the clay first, so it's ready to make into something after," said his mom.
Timmy grabbed his shovel and began to part the clay into small, round pieces. He was so focused that he hadn't noticed how icy the snow had become.
Suddenly, he felt something slick under his feet. He looked down and saw that he had slipped and fallen on the icy snow.
"Oh no! Are you ok, Timmy?" His mom asked, running over to him.
"Yes, I'm ok. I just got a little slippery," he said, laughing.
His mom helped him up and brushed off the snow, then the two of them started to make snow angels together.
The clay would have to wait.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Ali and Malu. They were always playing together and having fun. Ali spent much of his time leaning against his parent's car. He loved the feeling of being close to them.
One day as Ali was leaning against the car, he felt a bit restless. He went to see his best friend Malu, who was always happy and full of fun ideas.
“Hi Ali!” shouted Malu. “Do you want to play a game?”
Ali thought for a moment. “Sure! What about?”
“Let’s go explore the big field behind your house," suggested Malu.
“Yay!” said Ali happily.
They quickly ran to the big field and were soon exploring every corner, having lots of fun. After a while, Ali suddenly felt tired, so he leaned against a big tree.
“I'm so tired,” Ali said to Malu. “I want to go back home and sleep.”
“Let’s go home,” said Malu in agreement.
So Ali and Malu returned to Ali’s house and said goodbye. Ali felt a lot better after their brief adventure and was soon fast asleep, dreaming of new and exciting things to explore with Malu.

But today, the sky was gray. There were no shapes, no colors, no rainbows. Lily felt sad. She wanted to see something pretty in the sky. She looked at her brother, Tom. He was playing with his kite. Once upon a time, there was a charming girl called Little Star. She was only three years old and loved to play outside.

"No no!" shouted her mother. "Don't shoot the gun!"
But it was too late. Little Star had already pulled the trigger, and a bullet flew through the air.

Sara and Ben like to play in the garden. They see many flowers and bugs. They see a butterfly with blue and yellow wings. It is very pretty. They want to catch it.
They run after the butterfly. They try to grab it with their hands. But the butterfly is fast and smart. It flies away from them. It goes to another flower. Sara and Ben follow it.
They see a big net on the ground. It belongs to Tom, the gardener. He uses it to gather leaves and trash. Sara and Ben have an idea. They take the net and run to the butterfly. They throw the net over the butterfly. They think they have caught it.
But they are wrong. The net has a hole in it. The butterfly escapes through the hole. It flies away again. Sara and Ben are sad. They drop the net and sit on the grass.

Tim didn't want to surrender, so he tried again. He pushed his bicycle up the hill. It was still hard, but he didn't give up. At last, Tim made it to the top of the hill. He was so happy and proud of himself. He learned that even when things are tough, we should never surrender.

Once upon a time, there was a little spark. The spark was harmless and liked to play with his friends. One day, the spark met a new friend named Sleep.
"Hi Sleep!" said the spark. "Do you want to play with me?"
Sleep smiled and said, "I like to help people rest. Do you want to see how I do it?"
The spark was curious and said, "Yes, please show me!"
Sleep took the spark to a quiet place where a little girl was getting ready for bed. Sleep gently touched the girl's head and she fell asleep. The spark watched as the girl slept peacefully.
From that day on, the harmless spark and Sleep became best friends. They played together every day and helped people feel happy and rested. And they all lived happily ever after.

Tom's friend, Sue, saw that Tom was hurt. She said, "Tom, let me help you heal your arm." Tom did not want help, but he let Sue help him. They put a bandage on his arm. After that, Tom was not so bossy. He learned that it is good to let others help sometimes.

Mia and Leo were playing in the backyard. They had a big cooler with ice and juice and snacks. They liked to pretend they were camping and having a picnic.
"Let's cook some hot dogs on the grill," Mia said. She took out two hot dogs and put them on a plate. She gave Leo a fork and a knife.
"Okay, but be careful. The grill is very hot," Leo said. He followed Mia to the grill. He helped her turn it on and put the hot dogs on the metal. They sizzled and smelled good.
They waited for a few minutes and then Mia said, "I think they are ready. Let's put them in buns and add some ketchup."
They took the hot dogs off the grill and put them in buns. They squeezed some ketchup on them and took a big bite.
"Mmm, these are yummy," Mia said.
"They are," Leo agreed. "But you know what? You are chubby. You eat too many hot dogs."
Mia frowned. She did not like Leo's words. She was not chubby. She was just right.
"No, I'm not. You are mean. And you are skinny. You need to eat more hot dogs," she said.
They started to argue and yell. They did not want to share the cooler or the snacks. They did not want to play together anymore.
Mom heard them and came outside. She saw them fighting and the mess they made. She was not happy.
"What is going on here? Why are you fighting? And why did you leave the grill on? That is very dangerous," she said.
Mia and Leo looked at Mom. They felt sorry. They knew they did wrong.
"We are sorry, Mom. We were playing and cooking hot dogs. But then we said mean things to each other. We did not mean it. We are friends," Mia said.
"Yes, Mom. We are sorry. We were having fun. But then we got mad. We love each other. We are sorry," Leo said.
Mom smiled. She was glad they were sorry and they loved each other. She hugged them and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to be careful and kind. And you have to clean up this mess. And you have to turn off the grill. And you have to share the cooler and the snacks. And you have to eat some fruits and vegetables too. Hot dogs are not good for you if you eat too many."
Mia and Leo nodded. They said, "Okay, Mom. We will do that. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom."
They cleaned up the mess and turned off the grill. They shared the cooler and the snacks. They ate some apples and carrots too. They were happy and full. They decided to play something else. They did not fight anymore. They were good friends. The end.

Tom says, "I am the farmer. You are the helper. You have to do what I say." Sam nods. He likes to help. Tom gives him a toy cow. He says, "Take the cow to the barn. It is cold outside. The cow needs to be comfortable."
Sam takes the cow to the box. He puts it inside. He sees a toy horse, a toy pig and a toy sheep. They are all in the box. He thinks, "The barn is too small. The animals are not comfortable. They need more space."

Once upon a time, there was a little frog who lived in a small pond. He was always cold and wished he had a blanket. One day, he saw a leaf floating in the pond, and he decided to manage the leaf and wrap it around himself to keep warm.
At first, the leaf kept the little frog warm, but then the rain started and the leaf quickly became wet. The little frog got very cold again, and he was feeling sad.
The little frog knew that if he wanted to stay warm at all times, he needed to find something more durable than a simple leaf. He looked around, but there was nothing available. Then he noticed other frogs swimming nearby who had colorful pieces of clothing on.
The little frog thought to himself, “If all the other frogs have clothes to keep them warm, then I must find something too”. So he gathered all the nearby leaves, and he managed to create a blanket for himself. Now, whenever he felt cold, he had his special leaf blanket to keep him warm.
The moral of the story is that if you manage and use your resources wisely, you can always find a way to make the most of what is available to you.

He sees Sara and Ben on the slide with the melon.

He is angry and loud.
Sara and Ben are scared and sorry.
They did not know the melon was his. They did not mean to make him mad.
They slide down and give him the melon.
"We are sorry, mister. We thought the melon was free. We were hungry and wanted some melon," Sara says.
"Yeah, we are sorry. We did not ask if we could have some melon. We did not permit ourselves to take it," Ben says.

They are happy and full again.
They learn a lesson and make a friend.

The plumber hears them and says, "Stop that! You will break the door. Go and play somewhere else. I will be done soon."
Lily and Tom are bored. They do not know where to play. They look around the house and find a box of tools. They have an idea. They take the tools and go to their room. They pretend to be plumbers and repair their toys.

Their mom comes home and sees the mess. She is angry and shocked. She says, "What have you done? You have destroyed your toys. You are not plumbers. You are naughty. You need to clean up and apologize."
Lily and Tom are sorry. They did not mean to be bad. They just wanted to play in the bathroom. They say, "We are sorry, mom. We wanted to see the plumber and the sink. We thought we could repair our toys. We will clean up and say sorry to our toys."
Mom hugs them and says, "I understand, but you need to be careful and respectful. The plumber is working hard to fix the bathroom. You need to wait until he is done. Then you can play in the bathroom again. But only with water and bubbles and songs. No tools, okay?"
Lily and Tom nod and say, "Okay, mom. We love you. We love the bathroom. We love the plumber. We love our toys. We will be good."

Mom came into the room and saw the mess. She was not happy. She saw the snake on the floor and the dough on everything.
"Tim and Mia, what have you done?" Mom said. "You made a big mess with the dough. You did not take care of your toys. You did not listen to the rules. You have to punish."
Tim and Mia felt bad. They knew they did wrong. They said sorry to Mom.
"We are sorry, Mom," Tim said. "We just wanted to play with the snake."
"We did not mean to make a mess," Mia said. "We will clean it up."
Mom nodded. She said, "You have to clean up the mess. And you have to put the dough back in the box. And you have to play with the dough only on the table. That is your punish. Do you understand?"
Tim and Mia nodded. They said, "We understand, Mom. We will do our punish."
They took the snake and the dough and cleaned up the mess. They put the dough back in the box. They played with the dough only on the table. They learned their lesson. They did not make a big snake again.

"Wow, what a charming earring!" Lily said. "I wonder who it belongs to."
She put the earring in her ear and ran to show her mom. But on the way, she met her friend Max. Max was a little boy who lived next door. He liked to play with Lily and share his toys.
"Hi, Lily!" Max said. "What do you have in your ear?"
Lily smiled and showed him the earring. "I found it in the garden. It is so pretty, don't you think?"
Max looked at the earring and frowned. "That's my mom's earring!" he said. "She lost it yesterday and was very sad. She looked everywhere for it."
Lily felt sorry for Max's mom. She did not want to make her sad. She took the earring out of her ear and gave it to Max.
"Here, you can have it back. I'm sorry, I did not know it was your mom's. I hope she will be happy now."
Max took the earring and hugged Lily. "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. My mom will be very happy. And you know what? You are charming even without the earring. You are my best friend."
Lily hugged Max back. "You are welcome, Max. You are my best friend too. And you are charming even without your hat. Let's go play together."
They ran to the swing and had fun. They were happy to have each other and to discover new things.

Ben was very scared. He had to go to the hospital for an operation. He did not like the hospital. It was big and noisy and smelled funny. He did not want to leave his mom and dad.
"Ben, it's time to go," his mom said. She held his hand and gave him a hug. "Don't worry, the doctors and nurses are very nice. They will help you feel better."
Ben nodded, but he felt a big lump in his throat. He grabbed his teddy bear and followed his mom to the car. He looked out the window and saw the trees and the birds and the sky. He wished he could stay outside and play.
When they got to the hospital, a nurse came to greet them. She smiled and said, "Hi, Ben. I'm Nurse Amy. I'm going to take you to your room. You can bring your teddy bear with you."
Ben did not smile back. He clutched his teddy bear and walked with the nurse. He saw other kids in the hall. Some of them had bandages and tubes and machines. He wondered what was wrong with them.
Nurse Amy showed him his room. It had a bed, a chair, a table and a TV. She said, "This is where you will stay until your operation. You can watch TV or read a book or play with your toys. Do you have any questions?"
Ben shook his head. He did not want to talk. He wanted to go home.
Nurse Amy said, "OK, then. I'll be back soon to check on you. If you need anything, just press this button." She pointed to a red button on the wall. "And remember, you are very brave and strong. You can do this."
She left the room and closed the door. Ben sat on the bed and hugged his teddy bear. He felt very alone and sad. He wished he could see his mom and dad.
He closed his eyes and tried to imagine something else. He imagined he was in a spaceship, flying to the moon. He imagined he was a pirate, sailing the seas. He imagined he was a superhero, saving the world. He imagined he was anything but a sick boy in a hospital.
He felt a little better. He opened his eyes and saw his teddy bear. He said, "You know what, Teddy? We can do this. We are brave and strong. We will have the operation and then we will go home. And then we will be fit and healthy and happy. Right?"
Teddy did not answer, but Ben felt him nod. He smiled and gave him a kiss. He said, "I love you, Teddy. You are my best friend."
He lay down on the bed and turned on the TV. He watched a cartoon and laughed. He felt a little less scared. He knew he was not alone. He had his teddy bear and his mom and dad and Nurse Amy. He had his imagination. He had his hope. He was ready.

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play pretend. They had a big box of toys and clothes that they used to imagine different things. One day, they decided to imagine that they were pirates on a ship, looking for treasure.
Ben put on a hat and a coat and said, "I am the captain of this ship. You are my mate, Mia. We have to find the treasure before the bad pirates do." He gave Mia a scarf and a sword and told her to follow him.
Mia put on the scarf and the sword and said, "Yes, captain. Where is the treasure?" She followed Ben to the kitchen, where he pointed to a jar of jam on the counter.
"There it is, mate. The treasure of the red island. It is the best jam in the world. We have to get it before the bad pirates see it." Ben said.
He climbed on a chair and reached for the jar, but it was too high for him. He tried to pull it down, but it was too heavy for him. He grunted and strained, but he could not move it.
Mia saw that Ben was having trouble. She wanted to help him, but she also wanted to be the captain. She said, "Let me try, captain. I am strong. I can get the treasure."
She climbed on the chair and pushed Ben aside. She grabbed the jar and tried to lift it, but it was too heavy for her too. She groaned and struggled, but she could not move it either.
Ben was angry that Mia pushed him. He said, "Hey, that's not fair. You are not the captain. I am. Give me the treasure. It is mine."
Mia was angry that Ben yelled at her. She said, "No, it is not. You are not the captain. I am. I found the treasure first. It is mine."
They both held the jar and pulled and tugged, but it did not budge. They both shouted and argued, but they did not listen. They both wanted the treasure for themselves.
They did not notice that their mom came into the kitchen. She saw them fighting over the jam and said, "What are you two doing? Stop that right now. You are making a mess and a noise. You are not pirates. You are my children. And you have to share."

The mother replied, "No sweetheart, the stove is too hot. It could make you very weak. You must stay away from it."
The little boy pouted and sat down sadly. After a while, he saw that his mom was busy. He decided to add the wood to the stove. Just as he was about to touch the stove, his mom screamed out, "No!"
But it was too late. The little boy started to feel weak and he quickly ran away from the stove. The mother took the little boy to safety, and she scolded him for disobeying her.

The moral of the story is that even if we have things that make us different or clumsy, our friends will always be there to help us. And when we work together, we can find a way to fix any problem.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big clock on a tower. The clock has a face and two hands. It makes a loud sound every hour.
"Look, Tom, the clock is fat!" Sam says. He points to the clock. "It has a big belly and a round head."
Tom laughs. He thinks the clock is funny. He says, "Let's march to the clock. We can pretend we are soldiers."
Sam nods. He likes to pretend. He says, "Okay, Tom, let's march. One, two, one, two."
Tom and Sam march to the clock. They lift their feet high and swing their arms. They make noises with their mouths. They sound like drums.
The clock sees Tom and Sam. It smiles. It likes to see children play. It says, "Hello, Tom and Sam. You are good marchers. Do you want to hear a song?"
Tom and Sam stop marching. They look at the clock. They are surprised. They say, "Yes, please, Mr. Clock. We want to hear a song."
The clock says, "Okay, then. Listen carefully. I will sing a song about the time. When I finish, you can tell me what time it is."
The clock sings a song. It says, "Ding dong, ding dong, I am the clock on the tower. I tell you the time every hour. Ding dong, ding dong, now it is ten o'clock. How many times did I ring? Can you count the knocks?"
Tom and Sam listen to the song. They count the knocks. They say, "You rang ten times, Mr. Clock. It is ten o'clock."
The clock says, "Very good, Tom and Sam. You are smart children. You can count and tell the time. I am proud of you."
Tom and Sam smile. They are happy. They say, "Thank you, Mr. Clock. You are a nice clock. You can sing and tell the time. We are glad to meet you."
The clock says, "You are welcome, Tom and Sam. You are nice children. You can march and play. I am glad to meet you too. Come back and visit me again."
Tom and Sam say, "We will, Mr. Clock. Goodbye for now."
They wave to the clock. They march back to the park. They have fun. They are friends.

The little girl was confused. She asked the old man, "What is it for?"
The old man replied, "You will receive many blessings if you use it wisely."
The grandchild thanked him but had no idea what he meant. She thanked him, took the rake and gave him a hug.
As the months went by, the little girl successfully used the rake to clean up the garden. Gradually, she started to receive all sorts of blessings - a bushel of fresh vegetables, beautiful flowers and a generous supply of firewood.
At some point, the man visited her again, and he said, "Now you know what I meant when I gave you the rake. I knew you would receive many blessings if you used it wisely."
The little girl was so thankful for her thoughtful present. From that moment on, she always raked the garden, proving that the old man had been right all along.

"Me too!" Tim says.

Mom smiles. She hugs Tim and Jen. She says, "That's better. I love you, Tim and Jen. The man will be here soon to fix the cable. Then you can watch TV for a little bit. But not too much, OK?"
Tim and Jen nod. They say, "OK, Mom. We love you too."
They go to the table and pick up the books and crayons. They start to read and draw. They are not grumpy anymore. They are happy.

“Yes!” Sammy replied.
His mom said, “Listen carefully, I’m only going to say this once.”
Sammy tried to focus, but he was too excited. All he could hear was the anticipation buzzing around in his head.

Sammy cocked his head and waited – something in his mom’s voice made him pause.
“Good luck, Sammy,” she said.
Sammy grinned. His mom always said “good luck” whenever he was about to do something big, and this certainly was big. He was ready. He was ready to do the task.

John was a little boy who loved to play outside. One day, he and his father went for a walk in the woods. As they walked, John kept noticing something pale and squishy on the ground. He asked his father what it was, and his father said, "That's mud, John. You can squeeze it and it changes shape."
John thought this was an exciting discovery. He began to stomp in the mud and laugh as it squished between his toes. Everywhere he looked was mud and he loved playing in it. His father simply watched and smiled.
As they continued along the trail, John noticed something small sticking out of the mud. He bent down carefully and reached to pluck it out. When he saw what it was, he gasped. "Dad, look! It's a pale frog! It's so cool!"
John's father came over and leaned down next to him so that he could get a better look. Gentle, he said, "John, see how it's stuck in the mud? You can help it out if you want to. Try to squeeze the mud around it so it can free itself."
John carefully followed his father's instructions and, after a few gentle squeezes, the frog hopped away from the mud and towards a nearby stream. He jumped for joy, happy to help his new friend. Little did he know it was only the beginning of many wonderful adventures with animals.

Grandma was an elderly lady who lived in a large house. She loved to explain things to her grandchild. One day, Grandma explained to the 3-year-old that winter was coming. She said that during winter, it was very cold and she would need to put on a big coat. Grandma also explained that she needed to garden and then harvest her vegetables before it turned cold.
The 3-year-old was so excited to learn about winter. She asked lots of questions, like how long the cold season would last. Grandma explained that winter usually lasted several months, but she would bring warm blankets, hats, and gloves to help keep her warm. The gorilla said, "I am stuck in the cage and I can't get out!"

The gorilla said, "You must find the key to solve this problem!"
Sarah thought for a moment, then she said, "I will go look for it!"
So, Sarah searched around and after a few minutes, she found the key! She quickly opened the cage and let the gorilla out.
The gorilla thanked Sarah and said, "You were so brave and you solved my problem. Thank you!"
Sarah smiled and said, "You're welcome."
She was very proud of herself for helping the gorilla.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play games. Sometimes they play with cards, sometimes they play with blocks, sometimes they play with balls. They have fun, but they also want to win. They are competitive.
One day, they play a game with white cards. The cards have pictures of animals on them. Anna and Ben have to match the cards that have the same animal. They take turns to flip two cards and see if they match. If they match, they keep the cards. If they do not match, they put them back. The one who has more cards at the end wins.
Anna flips a card. It has a picture of a cat. She flips another card. It has a picture of a dog. They do not match. She puts them back.
Ben flips a card. It has a picture of a bird. He flips another card. It has a picture of a bird too. They match. He keeps the cards.
"Ha! I got a pair!" Ben says. He is happy.
Anna is not happy. She wants to get a pair too. She flips a card. It has a picture of a fish. She flips another card. It has a picture of a fish too. They match. She keeps the cards.
"Ha! I got a pair too!" Anna says. She is happy.
Ben is not happy. He wants to have more cards than Anna. He flips a card. It has a picture of a cow. He flips another card. It has a picture of a pig. They do not match. He puts them back.
Anna flips a card. It has a picture of a cow. She remembers where the other cow card is. She flips it. They match. She keeps the cards.
"Ha! I got another pair!" Anna says. She is very happy.
Ben is very sad. He knows he cannot win. He has no more cards. Anna has more cards. She wins.
"Anna, you are good at this game. You win." Ben says. He is a good friend.
"Thank you, Ben. You are good too. You got a pair of birds. I like birds. Do you want to play again?" Anna says. She is a good friend too.
"Yes, I want to play again. Maybe I can win this time. Or maybe we can play a different game. Do you want to play with blocks?" Ben says.
"OK, let's play with blocks. I like blocks. We can build a house or a tower or a bridge. We can have fun." Anna says.
They put the white cards away. They get the blocks. They play with the blocks. They are still competitive, but they are also friendly. They are happy. They are friends.

One day, Anna and Ben were playing with clay. They liked to make different shapes and animals with the clay. They also liked to feel the texture of the clay. It was soft and smooth and squishy.
"Look, I made a cat!" Anna said, showing Ben her clay cat. It had ears, eyes, a nose, a mouth, and a tail.
"Wow, that's a nice cat!" Ben said. "Can I lend your clay for a minute? I want to make a dog."
"Sure, you can lend my clay," Anna said. She gave Ben some of her clay. "But don't use all of it, okay? I still need some for my cat."
"Okay, I won't use all of it," Ben said. He took some of Anna's clay and started to make a dog. He made a head, a body, four legs, and a tail.
But then, he saw that Anna's cat had a very long tail. He thought that his dog should have a long tail too. So he took some more of Anna's clay and added it to his dog's tail. He made the tail longer and longer and longer.
"Hey, that's my clay!" Anna said, when she saw what Ben was doing. "You said you won't use all of it, but you did! Now I don't have enough clay for my cat!"
"I'm sorry, Anna," Ben said. "I just wanted to make a long tail for my dog. Here, you can have some of my clay. It's blue and green and yellow. It has a different texture. It's hard and rough and bumpy."
Anna looked at Ben's clay. She didn't like the colors or the texture. She wanted her own clay back. She felt sad and angry.
"No, thank you," she said. "I don't want your clay. I want my clay. You should give me back my clay. You are not a good friend. You are a bad friend."
Anna and Ben started to argue. They raised their voices and said mean words to each other. They forgot to have fun with the clay. They forgot to share and be kind.
Then, they heard a voice.
"Children, what's going on here?" It was their teacher, Mrs. Lee. She came to see what was wrong.
"Ben took all of my clay and made a long tail for his dog!" Anna said.
"Anna gave me her clay and then she wanted it back!" Ben said.
Mrs. Lee looked at the clay cat and the clay dog. She saw that they were both very nice, but they were also very different. She saw that Anna and Ben liked different things. She saw that they were both upset and hurt.
"Children, I understand that you both worked hard on your clay animals. They are very creative and beautiful. But I also see that you both made a mistake. You didn't respect each other's clay. You didn't listen to each other's wishes. You didn't say sorry or thank you. You didn't act like good friends. You acted like little children."
Anna and Ben felt ashamed. They knew that Mrs. Lee was right. They knew that they had been rude and selfish. They knew that they had hurt each other's feelings. They knew that they had to make up.
"Anna, I'm sorry for taking your clay. I should have asked you first. I should have given you some back. I should have been more careful. Can you forgive me?" Ben said.
"Ben, I'm sorry for yelling at you. I should have been more generous. I should have let you use some of my clay. I should have been more polite. Can you forgive me?" Anna said.
They looked at each other. They saw that they were both sorry. They saw that they were both friends.
"Yes, I forgive you," they said at the same time. They smiled and hugged.
"Good, I'm glad that you forgave each other," Mrs. Lee said. "Now, why don't you try to play with the clay together? Maybe you can learn from each other. Maybe you can mix the colors and the textures. Maybe you can make something new and fun."
Anna and Ben nodded. They agreed to play with the clay together. They decided to share and learn and have fun. They decided to be good friends. They decided to act like big children.

"Let's drink it," Tom said.

He took a sip and made a sour face too. He spat it out and said, "Yuck! You're right. This is too sour!"

"Nothing, Mom," they said.

Mom was angry and said, "You know you're not supposed to touch the tree. The lemons are not ripe yet. They are sour and bad for you. You could get sick. You have to wait until they are ready. You have to listen to me."

Tom and Sam felt sorry and said, "We're sorry, Mom. We won't do it again."
They went to their room and sat on their beds. They felt sour in their mouths and in their hearts. They learned that they should not urge to do things that are wrong. They should obey their Mom and be patient.

Soon the birds started to cheer and fly away. Sue kept going and soon she met a new friend. Her friend asked her to play a game of tag and Sue was scared. But then Sue remembered the birds and their message. She knew that she was brave and that she shouldn't quit. So she smiled and said yes.
Sue and her new friend had so much fun playing tag. Sue was no longer scared or shy. She opened up and made a new friend. It was the best birthday ever!

Andy wanted to show the jewel to his friends, so he carried it back to his ant hill. His friends also thought the jewel was very pretty. They all smiled and played with the jewel. But soon, they forgot about finding food for their family.
After a while, the ant family became hungry. The ants realized that they had spent too much time playing with the jewel and not enough time finding food. They felt sad and knew they had to work together to find food again.
The ants decided to put the jewel away and went back to their busy work. They found food for their family and everyone was happy again. The ants learned that it is important to work together and not get distracted by pretty things. And every time they smiled, they remembered the lesson they learned from the shiny jewel.

Once there was a small bird who was very happy. He was always singing and hopping from branch to branch.
One day the bird wanted to try something new and took a short journey. He flew high in the sky and soon landed in a strange place.
The place was hot, but the bird didn't worry. He started to explore, but he quickly realised it wasn't like the place he had left. The land was harsh, the sun too hot and there were no trees or other birds.
The bird felt sad, so he decided to go back home. On his way, he met a wise old owl. The owl looked at the bird carefully and said, “What are you doing so far away?” The bird told the owl all about his journey.
The owl thought for a while and then said, “You have received a valuable lesson today. If a place looks harsh, it's best not to explore it. You must always be careful and remember the home you were born in.”
The bird felt happy again. He thanked the wise owl, and soon after he flew back home to his family and friends. He never forgot the valuable lesson he had received.

"You are welcome, Tom. You are a nice friend too. Come on, let's go home and wash up," Lily says.

Tom and Mia were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they found a lime on the ground. It was green and round.
"Look, a lime!" Tom said. "I want it!"
"No, I want it!" Mia said. "I saw it first!"
They both grabbed the lime and pulled. They did not want to share. They got angry and shouted.
"Let go, it's mine!" Tom said.
"No, it's mine!" Mia said.
They pulled harder and harder. The lime was not strong. It broke in half. Juice squirted in their eyes. It was sour and stung. They dropped the lime and cried.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom said.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Mia said.
They rubbed their eyes and looked at each other. They were not happy. They were not friends anymore.
A dog came by. It was brown and furry. It smelled the lime on the ground. It liked limes. It picked up the lime and ran away.
"Hey, that's our lime!" Tom said.
"Come back, dog!" Mia said.
They ran after the dog. They wanted their lime back. They did not care about their eyes.
The dog was fast and loyal. It did not want to give up the lime. It ran to its owner. Its owner was a big man. He was mean and scary.
"Who are you?" the man said. "Why are you chasing my dog?"
"We want our lime!" Tom said.
"Your lime?" the man said. "This is not your lime. This is my dog's lime. He found it fair and square."
He looked at the lime. It was half and wet. He did not like limes. He threw the lime away.
"Go away, kids!" the man said. "Or I'll slap you!"
Tom and Mia were scared. They did not want to be slapped. They ran away. They did not get their lime. They did not have fun. They did not say sorry. They did not play in the park. They had a bad day.

Soon the bunny saw a big tree with a hollow in it. The bunny held the pistol tight and fired a few shots. Then he hopped inside the hole and the fox was confused. He had no idea the bunny had a pistol!
The fox snapped his jaws at the bunny, but the bunny smiled. He had saved himself from the fox with his smooth pistol.

"Look, the slide is empty. Let's go there first!" Sue says. She likes to slide fast.
"Okay, but I want to go on the big wheel too. It goes very high!" Tom says. He likes to see far.
They run to the slide. They take turns to go up and down. They laugh and scream. They have a lot of fun.
"Your turn, Tom!" Sue says. She gives him a push.
Tom springs on the slide. He slides very fast. He feels the wind in his hair. He sees the fair below him.
"Wow, this is great!" Tom says. He smiles.
He reaches the end of the slide. He jumps off. He looks for Sue.
But Sue is not there. He sees a man. The man is holding Sue's hand. The man is taking Sue away.
"Hey, stop! That's my friend!" Tom says. He runs after them.
He catches up with them. He pulls Sue's hand. He shouts at the man.
"Let go of her! She's not yours!"
The man looks at Tom. He looks angry. He says: "She is mine. I paid a high price for her. She's my prize."
Tom does not understand. He does not know what a prize is. He only knows that Sue is his friend. He does not want to lose her.
He kicks the man. He kicks him hard. The man drops Sue's hand. He groans. He runs away.
Tom hugs Sue. He says: "Are you okay? I'm sorry. I should have stayed with you."
Sue hugs Tom. She says: "I'm okay. Thank you. You are brave. You saved me."
They hold hands. They walk back to the slide. They see a lady. The lady is wearing a badge. The badge says: "Fair Manager."
The lady smiles at them. She says: "Hello, children. I saw what happened. You did very well. That man was a bad man. He wanted to kidnap you. He is gone now. The police are looking for him. You are safe now."
Tom and Sue feel relieved. They say: "Thank you, lady. You are nice."
The lady says: "You are welcome, children. You are very good friends. You deserve a reward. How about a free ride on the big wheel?"
Tom and Sue are happy. They say: "Yes, please!"
They go to the big wheel. They sit in a basket. The basket goes up and down. They see the whole fair. They see the balloons, the clowns, the cotton candy, and the animals. They also see the slide, the merry-go-round, and the gate.
They wave at the lady. The lady waves back. They smile at each other. They are glad. They are friends. They are safe. They are having fun.

"I'm glad we got to explore this forest together," said Elsa.

Lily and Max nodded and took the knife. They carefully pried the oyster open and looked inside. They gasped. There was a pearl, but not a white one. It was a pink one. And it was very cute.
"Wow, it's so pretty," Lily said.
"It's amazing," Max said.
They showed the pearl to their mom and dad, who were also surprised and happy. They said it was a rare and special find. They said Lily and Max could keep it as a souvenir of their beach day.
Lily and Max smiled and hugged each other. They decided to share the pearl and take turns wearing it as a necklace. They thanked the oyster for giving them such a beautiful gift. They said they were sorry for opening it and hoped it was not too angry. They put the oyster back in the water and said goodbye.
They had a wonderful day at the beach. They learned to behave and respect the animals. And they found a cute pink pearl. They were very lucky.

One day, the older brother had had enough and told his brother to be quiet during their playtime. Frustrated, the younger brother stormed out of the room and started throwing things on the floor.
The tutor, seeing this in the doorway, calmly said, “Young man, it is not nice to destroy things in anger. It would be better to be quiet and think about how you are feeling. It is more important to find peaceful solutions to problems than to be loud and act out.”
The younger brother listened and realized that the tutor was right. From then on, he made sure to stay quiet, find peaceful solutions, and to be respectful of his brother. The brothers learned an important lesson about the value of peace.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a shy bird named Tim. Tim was afraid to fly high in the sky. He would watch other birds soar and wish he could do the same. Tim lived on a hill, and every day he would look up at the sky and dream of flying.
One day, Tim met a wise old bird named Mr. Owl. Mr. Owl saw that Tim was sad and asked him what was wrong. Tim told Mr. Owl that he was too shy to fly high in the sky like the other birds. Mr. Owl smiled and told Tim a secret. He said, "Tim, you can soar just like the other birds if you believe in yourself and try."
Tim thought about what Mr. Owl said and decided to give it a try. He took a deep breath and started to flap his wings. Slowly, Tim began to rise off the ground. He felt the wind on his face and the sun on his back. Tim was finally soaring high in the sky, just like the other birds!
From that day on, Tim was no longer shy. He learned that if he believed in himself and tried, he could do anything. All the other birds were so happy for Tim, and they all played together in the sky. The moral of the story is to always believe in yourself and never give up, even when you are shy or scared.

"Look, Ben, I made a poppy!" Sara says, holding up her red paper flower. "It is pretty and bright. Do you like it?"
Ben looks at Sara's poppy. He feels sad and angry. He does not have a poppy. He only has a bad paper ball. He wants to have a poppy too. He grabs Sara's poppy and runs away.
"Hey, give it back!" Sara shouts, chasing Ben. "That is my poppy! You are mean!"

But the poppy is not strong. It is only paper. It breaks in Ben's hand. The petals fall to the floor. The poppy is gone.
Ben looks at the broken poppy. He feels sorry and sad. He did a bad thing. He hurt Sara's poppy. He hurt Sara's feelings. He does not want to be mean. He wants to be nice.
He goes back to Sara. He gives her the broken poppy. He says, "I am sorry, Sara. I was wrong. I should not have taken your poppy. Can you forgive me?"
Sara looks at Ben. She sees his sorry face. She sees the broken poppy. She feels sad and mad. But she also feels kind and good. She does not want to be mean. She wants to be nice.
She says, "It is okay, Ben. I forgive you. You made a mistake. But you said sorry. That is good. We can make a new poppy together. Do you want to learn how to fold paper?"
Ben nods. He says, "Yes, please. I want to learn how to fold paper. I want to make a new poppy with you. Thank you, Sara."
Sara smiles. She says, "You are welcome, Ben. Come on, let's fold paper. It is fun."
They sit down and fold paper. They make a new poppy. They make a new hat, a new boat, a new plane. They play with paper. They are happy. They are friends.

Ben and Lily wanted to help Mom make a cake for Dad's birthday. Mom said they could serve the cake after dinner, but they had to follow her rules. She gave them a big bowl, a spoon, a cup, and a bag of flour.
"First, we need to measure the flour," Mom said. "Fill the cup to the top, then pour it in the bowl. Do it four times. Can you do that?"
Ben and Lily nodded. They took turns filling the cup and pouring the flour. They counted together: one, two, three, four. The bowl was full of white powder.
"Good job!" Mom said. "Now we need to add some eggs, milk, sugar, and butter. I'll do that part. You can watch and stir."
Mom cracked some eggs and put them in the bowl. She poured some milk from a carton. She scooped some sugar from a jar. She cut some butter from a stick. She told Ben and Lily to stir everything together until it was smooth and yellow.
Ben and Lily stirred and stirred. They liked how the flour changed into batter. They licked the spoon and smiled. It tasted sweet.
"Almost done!" Mom said. "Now we need to bake the cake. I'll put it in the oven. You can help me decorate it later."
Mom poured the batter into a round pan. She put the pan in the oven. She set the timer for 30 minutes.
Ben and Lily waited and waited. They smelled the cake baking. It smelled yummy. They wanted to serve it to Dad right away.
But Mom said they had to wait until the timer beeped. Then they had to let the cake cool down. Then they had to spread some frosting on top. Then they had to write "Happy Birthday Dad" with some sprinkles.
Ben and Lily did everything Mom said. They worked hard and had fun. They made the cake look pretty and colorful.
Finally, the cake was ready. Mom put some candles on it. She lit them with a match. She carried the cake to the table.
Dad came home from work. He saw the cake and smiled. He hugged Ben and Lily and Mom.
"Wow, what a perfect cake!" he said. "Did you make it for me?"
Ben and Lily nodded. They were proud and happy.
"Yes, we did!" they said. "We measured, we stirred, we baked, we decorated. We did it all!"
"Thank you so much!" Dad said. "You are the best helpers ever. Now let's serve the cake and enjoy it together."
Ben and Lily clapped and cheered. They sang "Happy Birthday" to Dad. They helped him blow out the candles. They cut the cake and ate it. It was delicious.
They had a wonderful birthday party. They loved their Dad. They loved their Mom. They loved their cake. It was a perfect day.

There once was a little boy who wanted to bake something special. He searched and searched until he finally found a recipe he liked. He was excited to start baking but quickly realized he needed help. He asked his mom for help and she kindly agreed.
The little boy and his mom gathered all the ingredients and started baking. After a few hours the cake was ready. They took it out of the oven and carefully sliced it up into pieces.
The little boy was so proud of his cake he wanted to show his dad when he got home from work. When his dad finally arrived, the little boy eagerly asked him to try the cake he made. But his dad just shook his head and said he wasn't interested.
The little boy was so ashamed he couldn't look at his dad. He quietly put the pieces back in the oven to hide them.
This story teaches an important lesson - when it comes to fulfilling dreams, it's best to have people who will support and encourage us in the process. If we don't have those people, our dreams can quickly become something to feel ashamed of.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big red truck with a loud siren. It was a fireman truck. They ran to see it.
"Wow, look at the fireman truck!" Tom said. "It has a long hose and a ladder. I want to be a fireman when I grow up."
Lily nodded. She liked the fireman truck too. But she saw something else. She saw a big black dog sitting next to the truck. It had a shiny collar and a friendly face. It was a fireman dog.
"I want to pet the fireman dog!" Lily said. She walked towards the dog.
Tom followed her. He wanted to pet the dog too. But he also wanted to tease Lily. He thought it was funny.
"Be careful, Lily!" Tom said. "The fireman dog might bite you. He is hungry. He likes to eat little girls like you."
Lily stopped. She looked at Tom. She looked at the dog. She felt scared.
"Really?" Lily asked. "Is the fireman dog hungry? Does he bite?"
Tom laughed. He thought he was clever. He said, "Yes, he is hungry. He bites. He will chase you and eat you. Run, Lily, run!"
Lily started to cry. She ran away from the dog. She ran to her mom. She hugged her mom and told her what Tom said.
Tom felt bad. He saw Lily crying. He saw the fireman dog looking at him. He saw the fireman coming out of the truck. He heard the fireman say, "Hey, kid, what did you say to my dog? He is not hungry. He does not bite. He is a good dog. He helps me save people. He is my friend. Why did you tease that little girl?"
Tom felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, fireman. I'm sorry, fireman dog. I'm sorry, Lily. I was just joking. I didn't mean to scare her. I like the fireman truck. I like the fireman dog. I want to be your friend too."
The fireman smiled. He said, "It's okay, kid. I'm glad you like the fireman truck and the fireman dog. But you should not tease people. It is not nice. It can hurt their feelings. You should be kind and respectful. Do you understand?"
Tom nodded. He said, "I understand, fireman. I will not tease people anymore. I will be kind and respectful. Can I pet your dog?"
The fireman said, "Sure, you can pet my dog. His name is Sparky. He likes to be petted. He is very gentle. He will not bite you. He will lick you."
Tom walked to the dog. He petted his fur. He felt his tongue. He smiled. He said, "Hi, Sparky. You are a good dog. You are a brave dog. You are a fireman dog. I'm sorry I teased you. Can you forgive me?"
Sparky wagged his tail. He licked Tom's face. He barked. He said, "Woof, woof. I forgive you. You are a good kid. You are a smart kid. You are a fireman kid. Let's be friends."
Tom and Sparky became friends. Lily and her mom came back. They saw Tom and Sparky playing. They joined them. They all petted Sparky. They all thanked the fireman. They all learned a lesson. They all had fun.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to swing, slide and run on the grass. They saw some ducks in the pond and wanted to feed them some bread.
"Mom, can we go to the pond?" Lily asked.
"Sure, but stay close to me and don't go near the water," mom said.
Lily and Ben took some bread from mom and walked to the pond. They saw the ducks swimming and quacking. They threw some bread to them and the ducks came closer.
"Look, mom, the ducks like the bread!" Ben said.
"Yes, they do. But be careful, don't throw too much or they will get sick," mom said.
Lily and Ben nodded and threw some more bread. They saw a big duck with a pink head and a pink neck. It was very pretty and different from the other ducks.
"Wow, look at that duck! It's pink!" Lily said.
"It's so cute! I want to touch it!" Ben said.
Ben moved closer to the pond and reached out his hand to the pink duck. The pink duck saw Ben and got scared. It flapped its wings and splashed water at Ben. Ben got wet and cold. He started to cry.
"Mom, help! The duck is mean!" Ben shouted.
Mom heard Ben and ran to him. She saw the pink duck and the water. She picked up Ben and hugged him.
"Ben, are you okay? What happened?" mom asked.
"The duck, the duck! It hurt me!" Ben sobbed.
Mom looked at the duck and saw that it was not a duck. It was a flamingo. It had escaped from the zoo and came to the pond. It was not used to people and got nervous.
"Ben, that's not a duck. That's a flamingo. It's a bird that lives in warm places. It didn't mean to hurt you. It was just scared," mom explained.
"A flamingo? But it looks like a duck. And it's pink!" Ben said.
"Yes, it's pink. But it's not a duck. It's a different kind of bird. It has a long neck and long legs. And it eats shrimp. That's why it's pink," mom said.
"Shrimp? Like the ones we eat?" Lily asked.
"Yes, like the ones we eat. But we don't eat flamingos. They are very rare and beautiful. We should leave it alone and let it go back to the zoo," mom said.
"Okay, mom. I'm sorry, flamingo. I didn't know you were not a duck. I hope you find your home," Ben said.
The flamingo heard Ben and stopped flapping. It looked at Ben and Lily and mom. It nodded its head and flew away. Lily and Ben waved goodbye to the flamingo. They learned something new today. They learned that not all birds are ducks. And they learned that pink is a nice color for a bird. But they also learned that they should not panic when they see something different. They should be calm and curious and respectful. And they should always listen to mom.

"Yes, let's go!" Lily said.

"Wow, this is so cool!" Tom said.

"OK, how about Mars?" Lily said.
"OK, but only if there are no cats there," Tom said.

One day, Lily's mom said they had to go to the store. Lily did not want to go. She wanted to stay and play with her teddy bear and eat spaghetti. She asked her mom if she could stay.
"No, Lily, you have to come with me. We need to buy more spaghetti and other things. It won't take long, I promise. You can bring your teddy bear with you, okay?"
Lily was not happy, but she nodded. She put on her coat and shoes and grabbed her teddy bear. She followed her mom to the car. She hoped they would come back soon.
At the store, Lily's mom put her in a cart and pushed her around. Lily saw many things, but she did not care. She only wanted spaghetti. She held her teddy bear tight and looked around. She saw a big sign that said "Spaghetti". She pointed to it and said, "Mom, look! Spaghetti!"
"Yes, Lily, I see it. We're going to get some, don't worry. But first, we need to get some milk and eggs and bread. Can you help me find them?"
Lily tried to help, but she was bored. She wanted to go home and eat spaghetti. She wished she could stay and play with her teddy bear. She did not notice when her mom turned the corner and left her alone in the cart. She did not notice when a man came and took her teddy bear from her arms. She did not notice until she heard a voice say, "Hey, kid, this is mine now."
Lily looked up and saw a mean man holding her teddy bear. He had a big nose and a dirty beard and a scary smile. He laughed and ran away with her teddy bear. Lily was shocked and scared. She screamed, "No! Give me back my teddy bear! Mom! Mom!"
Lily's mom heard her scream and came running. She saw the man with the teddy bear and chased him. She yelled, "Stop! Thief! Give me back my daughter's teddy bear!"
The man ran faster, but he did not see a banana peel on the floor. He slipped and fell and dropped the teddy bear. Lily's mom caught up and grabbed the teddy bear. She gave it back to Lily and hugged her. She said, "I'm so sorry, Lily. I should have never left you alone. Are you okay?"
Lily nodded and hugged her mom and her teddy bear. She said, "I'm okay, mom. But I was very worried. I thought I lost my teddy bear forever. He loves spaghetti, you know."
Lily's mom smiled and said, "I know, Lily. I love spaghetti too. And I love you more. Come on, let's go home and make some spaghetti. And maybe some cookies too. How does that sound?"
Lily smiled and said, "That sounds great, mom. I love you too. And I love spaghetti. And cookies. And my teddy bear."
They left the store and went home. They made spaghetti and cookies and ate them together. They played with the teddy bear and read a story. They were happy and safe. They never wanted to leave each other again. They always wanted to stay.

Tom and Lily were playing in the living room. They saw a big candle on the table. It was red and smelled nice. Tom wanted to touch it, but Lily stopped him.
"No, Tom, don't touch the candle. It is hot and can hurt you," Lily said.
"Why is it hot?" Tom asked. He liked to question everything.
"Because it has fire inside. Fire makes light and heat, but it can also burn things," Lily explained.
"Where does fire come from?" Tom asked again.
Lily thought for a moment. She did not know the answer. She decided to ask their mom, who was in the kitchen.
"Mom, where does fire come from?" Lily called.
Mom came to the living room. She saw the candle and smiled.
"Fire comes from a match or a lighter. You need to strike them to make a spark. Then the spark catches the candle wick and makes fire. But you should never play with matches or lighters. They are dangerous," Mom said.
"Can we see how you make fire?" Tom and Lily asked together.
Mom nodded. She took a match from a box and struck it on the side. A small flame appeared. She held it near the candle and lit it. The candle glowed brighter.
"Wow, that's amazing!" Tom and Lily said.
Mom blew out the match and put it back in the box. She told Tom and Lily to be careful around the candle and not to touch it. She said it was a rare candle that their grandma gave them for Christmas. It had a special scent that reminded her of home.
Tom and Lily looked at the candle with wonder. They smelled the nice scent and felt the warmth. They thanked Mom for showing them how to make fire. They learned something new and had fun.

Once there was a purple bear named Bob. Bob really loved to play and have fun. One day, Bob went to the park and saw so many good things to play with. He found a big purple ball and couldn't wait to squeeze it. Bob was so excited he jumped up and down and started to play.
"Don't squeeze too hard!" said a voice. It was Bob's mom. "I don't want you to get hurt," she said.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to run, jump and hide behind the trees and flowers. They saw a big gate at the end of the garden. They wondered what was behind it.
"Let's go and see," said Lily. "Maybe there is something fun to do."
"OK," said Ben. "But we have to be careful. Mom and Dad said we should not go too far."
They ran to the gate and opened it. They entered a new landscape. There were hills and rocks and streams and animals. They saw a cow, a sheep, a horse and a dog. They were amazed.
"Wow, this is so pretty," said Lily. "Look at the cow. She has a bell around her neck. Can we touch her?"
"Maybe," said Ben. "But we have to be nice. She might be scared of us."
They walked slowly to the cow and said hello. The cow looked at them and mooed. She let them pet her soft fur. She was friendly.
"Hello, cow," said Lily. "You are so big and nice. Do you like living here?"
The cow nodded and mooed again. She licked Lily's hand with her tongue. Lily giggled.
"Look, she likes you," said Ben. "She is giving you a kiss."
They heard a voice behind them. It was a man. He was wearing a hat and boots. He had a stick in his hand. He was the farmer.
"Hello, kids," he said. "What are you doing here?"
They turned around and saw him. They were scared. They thought he might be angry.
"We are sorry, sir," said Ben. "We were just playing. We found the gate and entered this landscape. We did not mean to bother you or your animals."
The farmer smiled. He was not angry. He was kind.
"That's OK," he said. "I'm glad you like my farm. It is a beautiful landscape, isn't it? I work hard to take care of it and make it useful. The cow gives me milk, the sheep gives me wool, the horse helps me plow and the dog guards me. They are my friends."
He walked to the cow and patted her head. He took the bell from her neck and gave it to Lily.
"Here, you can have this," he said. "It is a gift. It makes a nice sound when you shake it. It will remind you of the cow and the farm."
Lily took the bell and thanked him. She was happy. She shook the bell and it jingled.
"Thank you, sir," she said. "This is a lovely gift. We like your farm and your animals. They are very nice too."
The farmer nodded and waved. He told them to come back anytime. He said he would show them more things on the farm. He said he would teach them how to be useful too.
Lily and Ben said goodbye and ran back to the gate. They entered the garden again. They were excited. They told Mom and Dad about their adventure. They showed them the bell. They said they had made a new friend. They said they had learned something new. They said they had seen a wonderful landscape.
