His mom kneeled down in front of her son and put her hands on his shoulders. She smiled and explained, "When we 'store' something, it means we put it in a place to keep it safe. So, when we put our groceries in the scale, we are 'storing' them in the store."

Johnny and his mom were walking in the park. They had been there many times before and Johnny always loved the sounds of the water birds, the green trees and the soft grass under his feet.
"Look mommy, what's that?" asked Johnny as he pointed to a strange tree with long sharp leaves at the end of its branches.
His mother smiled and said, "That's a palm tree. See how the leaves look like hands?"
Johnny nodded and smiled. He glanced back to the tree. "Can I climb it?"
Mom hesitated. She looked at her son with a patient expression. She then nodded and said, "Yes. But I promise you that if it starts to get too hard, you'll come down. Ok?"
Johnny smiled and quickly ran to the foot of the tree. The trunk was smooth and slippery, but Johnny was determined. With patient movements and lots of concentration, he slowly made his way up the trunk. He reached the top and felt proud of himself. He called down to his mom to show her he had made it. His mother smiled and gave him a thumbs up. Johnny smiled and waved back before slowly making his way back down the trunk.
He had kept his promise and was proud of what he had achieved.

The butterfly shook his head. "That does not matter," he said. "You still have many petals left, and they are very lovely. And you still smell very sweet. You are a wonderful flower, Lily. You should not be ashamed."

Tom was a cricket who liked to drink juice. He lived in a big garden with many flowers and fruits. Every day, he would hop from one plant to another and sip the sweet juice from the petals and the seeds.
One day, he saw a new fruit that he had never seen before. It was round and red and shiny. It looked delicious. Tom wanted to try it. He hopped closer and closer to the fruit, until he reached it. He bit a small piece and tasted it. It was very sour and bitter. Tom did not like it at all. He spat it out and made a face.
Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. It was a bird who had seen him. The bird wanted to eat him. Tom was scared. He tried to run away, but the bird was faster. It flew towards him and opened its big beak.
Tom thought he was going to be eaten. He closed his eyes and waited. But then, he felt something wet and sticky on his back. It was juice. The fruit that he had bitten had squirted juice on him. The juice was sour and bitter for Tom, but it was also sour and bitter for the bird. The bird did not like it either. It spat out Tom and flew away.
Tom was safe. He was also very wet and sticky. He looked for a place to clean himself. He saw a pond nearby. He hopped to the pond and dipped himself in the water. The water was cool and fresh. Tom drank some of the water. It was delicious. He felt happy and thirsty. He drank more and more water, until he was full and clean.
Tom learned a lesson that day. He learned that not all fruits are good to drink. He also learned that sometimes, water is the best drink of all. He decided to stick to the flowers and the seeds that he knew and liked. He also decided to be more careful of birds and other dangers. He thanked the fruit for saving him, even though it was sour and bitter. He hoped that the bird would find something else to eat, something that was delicious for it. He hopped away, looking for his friends. He wanted to tell them his story.

They tried to push, pull, twist, and turn the metal thing, but nothing happened. It just made noises and sparks. They got dirty and tired.
"This is junk," Max said, throwing a wire away. "It can't do anything. It's boring."
"Maybe we need help," Lily said, looking around. "Maybe someone knows what this is and how to make it work."
She saw a tall man walking on the street. He had a hat, a coat, and a bag. He looked like he knew a lot of things.
"Hey, mister!" Lily shouted, waving her hand. "Can you help us? We found this junk in the yard and we don't know what it is."
The tall man stopped and looked at them. He smiled and walked towards them. He looked at the metal thing and his eyes widened.
"Wow," he said, "you kids found a treasure. This is not junk. This is a radio. A very old and rare radio. It can play music and talk to people far away. But it needs batteries and a speaker to work. I have some in my bag. Do you want me to show you how to fix it?"
Lily and Max nodded, excited. They wanted to hear music and talk to people far away. They guessed it would be fun.
The tall man opened his bag and took out some batteries and a speaker. He connected them to the radio and turned it on. A sound came out of the speaker. It was music. Lily and Max clapped and danced. They liked the music. It was happy and catchy.
"Thank you, mister," Lily said, hugging the tall man. "You are very nice and smart. You made the junk work."
"You're welcome, kids," the tall man said, hugging them back. "You are very brave and curious. You found a radio. And you know what? This radio is very special. It belonged to my grandfather. He gave it to me when I was a kid. He told me stories about how he used it to listen to the news and the songs during the war. He told me to keep it safe and pass it on to someone who would appreciate it. And I think I found that someone. You."
He handed the radio to Lily and Max. They looked at him, surprised and happy.
"Really?" Max asked. "You want us to have it?"
"Really," the tall man said, nodding. "It's yours. You can keep it and play with it and learn from it. And maybe one day, you can pass it on to someone else who will love it too. Just like my grandfather did for me."
Lily and Max smiled and hugged the radio. They thanked the tall man again and again. They guessed he was the best mister in the world. They guessed they were the luckiest kids in the world. They guessed they had the best radio in the world. And they were right.

Bill and his father were sitting at the dinner table. Bill's dad had a plate of steak in front of him, while Bill had a plate with mashed potatoes. Bill observed the steak, and it looked and smelled delicious.
"Dad, can I have some of your steak?" asked Bill.
"No," replied his dad.
"But why not?" asked Bill.
His dad smiled and said, "You don't like steak. Remember last time, you said it was disgusting?"
Bill thought for a minute then nodded his head. He remembered it had tasted bad and he hadn't liked it.
"Okay, I'll just eat my potatoes," said Bill.
But then, something strange happened. His dad began to cut a piece of the steak and put it on Bill's plate.
"What are you doing, Dad?" asked Bill.
"I'm giving you a chance to change your mind. Why don't you try it again? I think you'll like this one better," said his dad.
Bill was excited, and he took a nibble of the steak. It was not disgusting at all, it was delicious! He smiled and said, "You were right Dad, this steak is really tasty!"
Bill had learned that it was okay to give something a second chance, and to not judge something based off of one experience.

Lily did not listen. She pulled the jar down. But it was too heavy for her. The jar slipped from her hands and fell on the floor. It broke into many pieces. The cookies spilled everywhere.
"Oh no!" Lily cried. "We broke the jar! Mom will be angry!"
Ben was scared too. He heard Mom coming. He ran to the living room and hid behind the sofa. Lily stayed in the kitchen. She did not know what to do.
Mom came into the kitchen. She saw the broken jar and the cookies. She was not happy. She looked at Lily.
"Lily, what happened here?" Mom asked.
Lily was sorry. She did not mean to break the jar. She wanted to tell Mom the truth. But she was afraid. She did not reply.
Mom waited for Lily to reply. She saw Lily's face. She knew Lily was sorry. She also knew Lily was cold. The kitchen was cold. Mom felt sorry for Lily too.
Mom sighed. She picked up Lily and hugged her. She said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you did not mean to break the jar. But you should have asked me first. And you should have listened to Ben. He was trying to help you. Next time, be more careful, okay?"
Lily nodded. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I love you."
Mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, Lily. Now let's clean up this mess. And then we can have some cookies. But not too many, okay?"

Mom and Lily cleaned up the mess. They threw away the broken jar and the bad cookies. They saved some good cookies for later. They went to the living room. They found Ben behind the sofa. They invited him to join them. They all had some cookies and milk. They were happy.

They look at each other and think. They remember that they have a post in the corner of the room. The post is tall and strong and has a hook on the top. They have an idea.
"Let's use the post!" Tom says.
"Yes, let's use the post!" Sam agrees.
They run to the post and take it. They bring it to the tower and try to put it on the top. They think that the post will make the tower taller and better.
But they are wrong. The post is too heavy and big for the tower. The tower can't hold the post. The tower falls down and breaks. The blocks scatter everywhere. Tom and Sam are shocked and scared.
They hear a loud voice. It is their teacher. She is angry and disappointed.
"What are you doing?" she asks. "Why did you take the post? The post is not a toy. The post is for hanging coats and hats. You broke the tower and made a mess. You are not good friends. You are selfish and greedy. You need to learn to share and be happy with what you have."
Tom and Sam feel ashamed and sorry. They realize that they made a mistake. They should not have taken the post. They should have been happy with the blocks. They should have shared and cooperated with each other.
They apologize to their teacher and to each other. They help to clean up the mess and to fix the tower. They promise to be better friends and to respect the things that belong to others.
They learn a lesson. They learn that adding more things is not always good. They learn that being happy with what they have is more important. They learn that sharing and cooperating with others is more fun. They learn that the post is not a toy.

Tom and Mia tell the duck about the rock. They say they want to take it home, but they cannot.
The duck nods. "I see. But do you know that this rock is not yours? It belongs to the park. It is part of nature. It helps the plants, the animals and the water. If you take it away, you will hurt the park. And you will hurt yourselves. You will not be happy with something that is not yours."
Tom and Mia look at the duck. They look at the rock. They look at the park. They think about what the duck said. They feel sorry.
"You are right, duck," Tom says. "We are sorry. We did not think about the park. We only thought about ourselves. We will not take the rock. We will leave it here, where it belongs."
Mia agrees. "Yes, duck. We are sorry. We will not be greedy. We will share the rock with the park. We will come and visit it, but we will not touch it."
The duck smiles. "That is very good, children. You are very smart and kind. You have learned a lesson. The rock is a mineral, but it is also a friend. A friend of the park, and a friend of you. You can enjoy it, but you cannot own it. That is the way of nature."
Tom and Mia smile too. They thank the duck and say goodbye. They run, swing, slide and climb. They are happy. They have learned a lesson. They have learned to respect nature and to be grateful for what they have.

But Tommy did not want to play or read. He wanted to sit on the seat. He saw an empty seat next to the barber. He thought it was the same as the one he liked. He ran to the seat and climbed on it. He pushed a button and the seat went up.
The barber was surprised and angry. He said, "Hey, kid, what are you doing? Get off that seat! That's not for you! That's for the lady who is getting her hair dyed!"
But Tommy did not listen. He pushed another button and the seat went down. He pushed another button and the seat tilted back. He pushed another button and the seat sprayed water on his face.
Tommy screamed and cried. He was wet and scared. The lady who was getting her hair dyed screamed and cried too. She was wet and angry. Her hair was ruined. The barber was wet and furious. He yelled at Tommy and his dad. He said, "Get out of my shop! You have to pay for the damage! You have to pay for the lady's hair! You have to pay for the seat!"

His dad said, "I'm sorry too, Tommy. I should have watched you better. I hope you learned your lesson. Next time, you have to wait for your turn and listen to the barber."
Tommy nodded. He learned his lesson. He hoped the lady and the barber would forgive him. He hoped he would get stickers again.

"Can we share it?" Lily asked. "I am hungry too."
"Share? No way!" Ben said. "This is my acorn. I found it first. You can find your own."
Ben was very greedy and careless. He did not want to share with his sister. He ran away with the acorn in his mouth. Lily was sad and angry. She followed him and shouted.
"Ben, that is not fair! You are being mean! Give me some of the acorn!"
But Ben did not listen. He climbed up the tree with the acorn. He wanted to eat it all by himself. He did not see the big owl that was watching him from another branch. The owl was hungry too. It saw the acorn and thought it looked very yummy.
The owl swooped down and grabbed Ben and the acorn in its claws. Ben was scared and dropped the acorn. He tried to escape, but it was too late. The owl flew away with him and ate him.
Lily saw what happened and cried. She wished she had shared the acorn with Ben. She wished he had not been so greedy and careless. She wished he was still alive. She picked up the acorn and buried it under the bush. She did not want to eat it anymore. She went back to the tree and hugged her mother. She learned a hard lesson that day. Sharing is better than being selfish.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little seed, who was looking for a place to grow. The seed tried to find a place but there was nowhere to go.

The seed thought for a moment and then said: "I will try anyway."
So the seed planted itself deep inside the fridge and it started to grow and grow. Soon, the seed had grown into a beautiful flower!
The flower looked out of the fridge, and saw the sunlight in the sky. It smiled and was so happy that it had found a place to be, despite the cold temperature.
The moral of the story is to never give up, even if the conditions seem difficult. If you stay strong and brave, then you can always find a way to make something beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved orange lollipops. One day, she went to the store with her mom to buy her favorite treat.
At the store, Amy saw a big orange lollipop. She said to her mom, "Mom, can I have that lollipop, please?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can have it, but you must share it with your brother Tom."
Amy was happy and ran to get the lollipop. But then, she tripped and the lollipop fell on the ground. Amy was sad and started to cry. Her mom came to help her.
Amy's mom had a magic word to reverse things. She said the word, and the lollipop was back in Amy's hand, clean and safe. Amy was so happy, she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, Mom!"
Amy and her mom went home, and Amy shared the big orange lollipop with her brother Tom. They both enjoyed the sweet treat and played together all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a room full of toys and junk. He loved to play with his toys, but he did not like to clean up. His mom told him that he needed to take care of his fragile toys, or they would break.
One day, Tim's mom gave him a big box. She said, "Tim, you need to fill this box with all the junk in your room." Tim did not want to, but he knew his mom was right. So, he started to pick up his toys and put them in the box. He was careful with his fragile toys, so they would not break.
As Tim filled the box, he found toys he had not seen in a long time. He realized that when he took care of his things, he could enjoy them more. He also learned that it was important to clean up his room and not let junk pile up. Tim felt proud of himself for filling the box and keeping his fragile toys safe. The moral of the story is to take care of your things and keep your space clean, so you can enjoy what you have.

Lily was a new girl in the big school. She was a little scared, but she wanted to make friends. She saw a boy with a red hat sitting at a desk. She walked up to him and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. What is your name?"
The boy looked up and smiled. He said, "Hi, Lily. I'm Ben. Welcome to the big school. Do you like it here?"
Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, it is nice. But it is also big and loud. I don't know where to go."
Ben said, "Don't worry, I can help you. I know where everything is. Do you want to see the playground?"
Lily said, "Yes, please. That sounds fun."
Ben said, "OK, let's go. But first, we have to be careful. We have to hold hands and look both ways before we cross the hall. There are many people and things moving around. We don't want to bump into them or get lost."
Lily said, "OK, I will be careful. You are a good friend, Ben."
Ben said, "You are a good friend, too, Lily. Come on, let's go have fun." He took her hand and they walked to the playground. They were happy and excited. They had found a new friend in the big school.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box in the garage. The box has a zip on it. They want to see what is inside.
"Can we open it?" Mia asks.
"OK, but be careful," Tom says. He pulls the zip. The box opens. There are many things in the box. There are books, clothes, and toys. Tom and Mia are happy. They take out the things and look at them.
"Look, a flashlight!" Tom says. He picks up the flashlight and turns it on. It makes a bright light. He shines it on the wall.
"Wow, cool!" Mia says. She takes a ball and throws it to Tom. Tom catches the ball. He throws it back to Mia. They play catch with the ball and the flashlight.
But then, Tom drops the flashlight. It falls on the floor. It breaks. The light goes out. It is dark in the garage. Tom and Mia are scared. They cannot see anything.
"Tom, where are you?" Mia cries.
"I'm here, Mia. Don't worry," Tom says. He tries to find the zip on the box. He wants to close the box and go out. He feels the box with his hands. He finds the zip. He pulls it. The box closes. He pushes the box. He makes a hole in the wall. He sees some light. He crawls out of the hole. He sees Mia. He helps her out of the hole.
"Are you OK, Mia?" Tom asks.
"Yes, I'm OK, Tom. Thank you," Mia says. They hug each other. They are happy. They run to the house. They tell their moms what happened. Their moms are not angry. They are glad that Tom and Mia are safe. They give them cookies and milk. Tom and Mia smile. They are still friends. They like to play with toys. But they do not play with the big box anymore.

The fox went to the houses and took things when the people were not looking. The people were sad and did not want to play games anymore. They wanted their things back. They worked together to find the fox and get their things back. The fox was caught and said sorry. The people forgave the fox and they all became friends. The city was happy again and they all learned to share and not be too competitive.

"I got you a surprise," his father said. He zipped open the bag and pulled out a bright yellow kite.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a big tree with a parrot in it. The parrot was very glad. It was singing a happy song. Tim wanted to play with the parrot. So, he said, "Hi, parrot! Can we play together?"
The parrot said, "Yes, Tim! Let's play a game. I will say a word, and you sort the things I say into two groups. One group will be for things that are big, and the other group will be for things that are small."
Tim was excited to play. The parrot said some words like "car", "bug", "house", and "toy". Tim sorted them into the big and small groups. They were having a lot of fun.
But then, something unexpected happened. The parrot said a word that Tim did not know. The word was "elephant". Tim was confused. He did not know if an elephant was big or small. He asked the parrot, "What is an elephant? Is it big or small?"
The parrot laughed and said, "An elephant is very big, Tim! It's the biggest animal on land!" Tim was happy to learn something new. He sorted the elephant into the big group. They both laughed and kept playing their game.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big yellow slide that looked like fun. They ran to the slide and took turns going down. Lily liked the slide, but Ben was scared.
"Come on, Ben, it's not scary!" Lily said. "It's fun!"
Ben shook his head. He did not want to go on the slide. He saw something mysterious at the top of the slide. It was dark and furry and had big eyes. It looked like a monster.
"Lily, look! There's a monster on the slide!" Ben said. He pointed at the top of the slide.
Lily looked up and saw the mysterious thing. She was not scared. She knew what it was. It was a cat. A big, fluffy cat.
"That's not a monster, Ben. That's a cat!" Lily said. "It's probably cold and lonely. Let's go say hello."
Lily climbed up the slide and reached the cat. The cat was shivering. It was cold and hungry. Lily petted the cat and spoke softly to it.
"Hello, kitty. What's your name? Are you lost?" Lily asked.
The cat purred and rubbed its head against Lily's hand. It liked Lily. It was happy to have a friend.
Ben watched from the bottom of the slide. He saw that the cat was not a monster. It was just a cat. He felt silly for being scared. He wanted to pet the cat too.
"Can I come up, Lily?" Ben asked.
"Sure, Ben. Come on up. The cat is nice. It won't hurt you." Lily said.
Ben climbed up the slide and joined Lily and the cat. He petted the cat and smiled. The cat purred and licked his face. It liked Ben too. It was happy to have two friends.
Lily and Ben hugged the cat and decided to take it home. They asked their mom if they could keep the cat. Their mom said yes. They were very happy. They named the cat Yellow. Yellow was happy too. He had a new home and a new family. He never shivered again.

Suddenly, the weather began to change. Dark clouds filled up the sky and the wind got really cold. Spot shivered as the icy air hit her face, but she continued to work.

The moral of this story is that it is not wise to do something without your parents' permission. If something is dangerous, it is better to stay away from it. Remember: people who are brave are not always the most foolish ones.

"Can we play, Mom?" Lily asked.
"Yes, but first we need to seat on that bench and eat our lunch. You are hungry, right?" Mom said.
Lily and Tom nodded. They were hungry. They followed Mom to the bench. Mom gave them sandwiches and juice. They ate and drank.
Near the bench, there was a vendor. He had a cart with ice cream and candy. He smiled at Lily and Tom.
"Hello, little ones. Do you want some ice cream or candy? They are very yummy," he said.
Lily and Tom looked at the vendor. They liked ice cream and candy. They wanted some.
"Mom, can we have some ice cream or candy?" Tom asked.
Mom shook her head. "No, you just ate your lunch. You don't need more sugar. It is not good for your teeth and your tummy. Maybe later, if you are good."
Lily and Tom felt sad. They wanted some ice cream or candy. They looked at the vendor again. He winked at them.
"Come on, don't be shy. I have a special offer for you. You can have one ice cream or candy for free. Just come to my cart and take one. Your mom won't notice. She is busy with her phone," he said.
Lily and Tom felt tempted. They looked at Mom. She was busy with her phone. They looked at the vendor. He smiled at them. They looked at each other. They had a bad idea.
They got up from the bench. They walked to the cart. They reached for the ice cream and candy. They thought they were clever.
But Mom saw them. She was not busy with her phone. She was watching them. She was angry.
She got up from the bench. She walked to the cart. She grabbed Lily and Tom by their hands. She scolded them.

Tim said, "I don't know. Maybe you can. Try to remove the hat."
Lily tried to remove the hat, but it was stuck. She pulled and pulled, but it did not come off. She said, "It is too hard. I can't remove it. Can you help me, Tim?"

Tim said, "A tool is something that helps you do things. Like a hammer or a scissors. But we don't have any tools here. Maybe we can ask someone."
They looked around and saw a squirrel. The squirrel was holding an acorn in its mouth. It saw Tim and Lily and ran away. Tim and Lily followed the squirrel. They wanted to ask the squirrel how to remove the hat from the acorn. They thought the squirrel would know, because it ate acorns. They ran after the squirrel, but the squirrel was faster. It climbed up the tree and disappeared.

"No, no, it is too slippery and cold. You might fall and hurt yourself, or the ice might break and you might drown. It is not safe," their parents said.
"But we want to have fun! We want to slide and skate and make snowballs!" Tom and Lily whined.
"Sorry, but you have to listen to us. We know what is best for you. You can play on the grass or on the swings or on the slide. There are many other things to do in the park," their parents said.
Tom and Lily were very angry and sad. They did not want to play on the grass or on the swings or on the slide. They wanted to play on the ice. They thought their parents were mean and boring. They decided to sneak away from them and go on the ice anyway.

Suddenly, Tom heard a loud splash. He turned around and saw that Lily had fallen into the hole. She was in the water, and she was very scared and cold. She screamed and cried and tried to get out, but the ice was too slippery and sharp. She could not keep her head above the water.
"Help, help, Tom, help me!" Lily shouted.
Tom was very scared too. He did not know what to do. He wanted to help Lily, but he did not want to fall into the water too. He wished he had listened to his parents. He wished he had not been so greedy and selfish. He wished he had been more kind and generous.
He ran to the edge of the pond and called for his parents. He hoped they would hear him and come and save Lily. He hoped it was not too late. He hoped Lily would be okay. He hoped she would forgive him. He hoped they would learn to be happy with what they had. He hoped they would never play on the ice again.

When the cake was done, they took it out of the oven. Spot said, "Let's eat it outside by the grill!" They went outside and sat down by the grill. Fluffy said, "This is the best cake ever!" They both laughed and enjoyed their tasty cake.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. They have a big box. They pretend it is a car. They take turns to drive and be the postman.
One day, Lily is the postman. She has a bag of letters. She says, "I have to rush. I have to deliver the post to everyone." She runs to the box. She puts a letter in the slot. She knocks on the box. She says, "Post for you, Ben!"
Ben is inside the box. He is the driver. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good postman." He takes the letter. He opens it. It is a picture of a flower. He smiles. He says, "Lily, you are a good artist. I like your flower."
Lily says, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good driver. I like your car." She runs to the next box. She does the same thing. She puts a letter in the slot. She knocks on the box. She says, "Post for you, Mom!"
Mom is in the kitchen. She hears the knock. She says, "Who is it?" She goes to the window. She sees Lily. She says, "Hello, Lily. What do you have for me?"
Lily says, "Post for you, Mom!" She gives Mom the letter. Mom opens it. It is a picture of a heart. She hugs Lily. She says, "Lily, you are a gentle and sweet girl. I love your heart."
Lily says, "I love you, Mom." She runs to the last box. She says, "I have one more letter. I wonder who it is for." She looks at the box. It is big and red. It has a sign. It says, "Santa."
Lily says, "Wow! This is for Santa! I have to be very careful. I have to be very quiet. I have to be very fast." She tiptoes to the box. She puts the letter in the slot. She knocks on the box. She says, "Post for you, Santa!"
Santa is in the box. He is hiding. He is a surprise. He hears the knock. He says, "Ho ho ho! Who is it?" He opens the box. He sees Lily. He says, "Hello, Lily. What do you have for me?"
Lily says, "Post for you, Santa!" She gives Santa the letter. Santa opens it. It is a picture of a star. He smiles. He says, "Lily, you are a clever and kind girl. I like your star."
Lily says, "Thank you, Santa. You are a nice and funny man. I like your beard." She hugs Santa. She says, "Merry Christmas, Santa!"
Santa says, "Merry Christmas, Lily!" He gives Lily a present. He says, "This is for you. You are a good postman. You made everyone happy today."
Lily opens the present. It is a book. It has stories. She says, "Thank you, Santa. I love stories. I love you, Santa."
Santa says, "I love you, Lily. You are a special girl. You have a big heart. You have a bright star. You have a wonderful family. You have a happy life." He waves to Lily. He says, "Goodbye, Lily. See you next year."
Lily waves to Santa. She says, "Goodbye, Santa. See you next year." She runs to the garden. She shows her book to Ben and Mom. They are happy. They read the stories together. They have a cozy and merry time.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys. They have a big ball that looks like a planet. They like to roll it and bounce it and pretend they are in space.
"Look, Lily, this is Earth. It has blue and green and white on it," Tom says, pointing at the ball.
"I like Earth. It is pretty and has animals and flowers and candy," Lily says.
"Me too. But do you know what else is in space? There are other planets. Some are big and some are small. Some are hot and some are cold. Some are red and some are yellow and some are purple," Tom says.
"Wow, that is amazing. Can we see them?" Lily asks.
"Maybe. If we push the ball very hard, it will fly in the air and go to the other planets. Then we can see what they are like," Tom says.
"OK, let's try. But be careful. We don't want to break the ball or hurt anyone," Lily says.
They both stand up and hold the ball together. They count to three and then push the ball as hard as they can. The ball flies in the air and makes a big arc. It goes over the fence and lands in the neighbor's yard.
"Wow, that was fun. Do you think it reached another planet?" Tom asks.
"I don't know. Maybe. But I hope it is a sweet planet, with lots of yummy things to eat," Lily says.
They run to the fence and look over. They see the ball lying on the grass. Next to it, they see a big cake with frosting and sprinkles. The neighbor is having a birthday party.
"Look, Tom, it is a sweet planet. And they have cake. Can we have some?" Lily asks.
"Sure, why not. Let's go and say hello. Maybe they will share," Tom says.
They climb over the fence and run to the ball and the cake. The neighbor sees them and smiles.
"Hello, kids. What are you doing here?" he asks.
"We are sorry. We were playing with our planet ball and we pushed it too hard. It flew over here. We didn't mean to crash your party," Tom says.
"That's OK. I don't mind. Your planet ball is very cool. And you are welcome to join us. We have plenty of cake and ice cream and balloons. Do you want some?" he asks.
"Yes, please. Thank you. You are very nice," Lily says.
They take their ball and follow the neighbor to the table. They have some cake and ice cream and balloons. They make new friends and have a lot of fun. They think the sweet planet is the best planet ever.

The bee learned that day that being smart is more than just having a clever plan – it's also being kind and mindful of others.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big hole in the ground. They want to know what is inside.
"Let's catch something in the hole!" Ben says. He has a net and a jar.
"OK!" Lily says. She has a flashlight and a rope.
They go to the hole and shine the light inside. They see many bugs and worms. They also see something shiny and round.
"What is that?" Lily asks.
"I don't know. Let's catch it!" Ben says.
He lowers the net into the hole and tries to scoop up the shiny thing. But it is too fast and slippery. It rolls away from the net.
"Hey, come back!" Ben says.
Lily ties the rope to the jar and lowers it into the hole. She hopes the shiny thing will go inside. But it does not. It bounces off the jar and rolls to the other side of the hole.
"Wow, it is so light and bouncy!" Lily says.
They try again and again, but they cannot catch the shiny thing. They are getting tired and frustrated.
"Maybe we should give up," Ben says.
"No, we can do it!" Lily says. "We just need a better plan."
She thinks for a moment. Then she has an idea.
"I know! Let's use the flashlight!" she says.
She turns off the flashlight and puts it in the jar. Then she lowers the jar into the hole again. She waits for a few seconds. Then she turns on the flashlight.
The shiny thing sees the light and gets curious. It rolls towards the jar and goes inside. Lily quickly pulls up the jar and closes the lid.
"Yay, we did it!" she says.
"Let me see, let me see!" Ben says.
They look at the jar and see the shiny thing. It is a silver ball. It sparkles in the light.
"It is so pretty!" Lily says.
"Where do you think it came from?" Ben asks.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a treasure!" Lily says.
They are very happy and proud. They decide to keep the ball as a secret. They hide the jar under a bush and go back to play. They promise to come back and visit the ball later. They wonder what other things they can catch in the hole.

Tim ran to the river and filled a bucket with water. He jogged back to Mr. Brown and threw the water on the fire. They worked together, and soon the fire was gone. Mr. Brown thanked Tim for his help. They both felt happy that the fire was out and that they had become friends.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She was a daughter who loved to play in the park. One day, Lily saw a big, red ball appear near a tree. She was very happy and ran to get it.
On her way, a foolish bird flew down and took the ball. Lily was sad and asked the bird to give it back. The bird said, "If you share your snack with me, I will give you the ball." Lily thought about it and said yes.
Lily shared her snack with the bird, and the bird gave her the ball. They played together all day. Lily learned that sharing can make new friends and make everyone happy.

They all looked so pretty and graceful in their new clothes. They decided to stay and play together, all wearing the same clothes. And they had the best day ever.

There was a little boy, Tommy, that was three years old. He was a happy boy that loved to play games.
One day, Tommy wanted to play a game, so he asked his mom, "Can we play a game, Mom?"
His mom was busy making dinner, so she said, "I'm sorry, Tommy, we can't play right now. I'm too busy."
Tommy thought for a moment and then declared, "Let's play a game with clapping!"
His mom was surprised and asked, "What kind of game can you play with clapping?"
Tommy beamed and said, "We can play clap and jump! I'll clap my hands and you jump!"
His mom laughed, and they both clapped their hands and jumped. When they finished, Tommy applauded and said, "That was so much fun!"
His mom smiled and said, "It was a lot of fun! We should play this game again."
Tommy agreed, and they both clapped and cheered.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Tim. Tim had a lime tree in his yard. The tree had many small limes on it. Tim liked to eat the limes, but he did not like to share.
One day, Tim's friend Sam came over to play. Sam saw the small limes and asked Tim if he could have one. Tim did not want to share, so he did not tell Sam about the limes. Sam was sad, but he did not say anything.
Later, Tim went to pick a lime to eat. But he found that all the limes were gone. A big bird had come and taken them away. Tim was very sad. He wished he had shared the limes with Sam. Now, he had no limes at all. The moral of the story is to always share with your friends.

"Look, I have more wool than you!" Lily said, holding up her paper pile.
"No, you don't. I have more!" Ben said, showing his paper pile.
They started to argue and pull each other's paper wool. The toy sheep watched them with sad eyes.
"Stop it, Lily and Ben!" Mama said, coming into the room. "You are not being nice to each other or to the toy sheep. The sheep need their wool to keep warm and look graceful. How would you feel if someone took your hair?"
Lily and Ben looked at each other and felt sorry. They said sorry to Mama and to the toy sheep. They put the paper wool back on the sheep and hugged them.
"Can we play something else, Lily?" Ben asked.
"Sure, Ben. Let's play something else." Lily said.
They put away the scissors and the paper and picked up their toy cars. They smiled and played together. The toy sheep smiled too. The end.

One day, a boy named Tim went for a walk with his dog, Max. They went down a trail in the woods near their home. Tim saw a crazy-looking bug with many legs. He picked it up and showed it to Max. "Look, Max! A crazy bug!" Tim said.
As they walked, they met a girl named Sue. Tim wanted to tell Sue about the crazy bug, but he did not mention it because he was shy. Sue saw that Tim was quiet, so she talked to him. "Hi, I'm Sue. What's your name?" she asked. Tim told her his name and showed her the crazy bug.
Sue laughed and said, "That's not a bug, Tim! That's a toy!" Tim felt silly, but he was happy that he talked to Sue. They became good friends and played with the toy bug together.
The moral of the story is that even if you feel shy, it's good to talk to new people. You might find a new friend and have fun together. And sometimes, things are not what they seem, like the crazy bug that was really a toy.

Lily liked her scarf very much. It was red and soft and warm. Her grandma made it for her birthday. Lily thought her grandma was very thoughtful.
One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a boy playing with a ball. He looked cold and sad. Lily wanted to be nice to him. She ran to him and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?"
The boy looked at Lily and smiled. He said, "Hi, I'm Ben. Yes, I want to play with you. You have a nice scarf. Can I touch it?"
Lily nodded and let Ben touch her scarf. He felt it and said, "It's so soft and warm. Can I have it?"
Lily was surprised. She said, "No, you can't have it. It's mine. My grandma made it for me."
Ben frowned and said, "But I'm cold and I don't have a scarf. You have to share with me. That's what nice people do."
Lily shook her head and said, "No, I don't have to share with you. You can't own my scarf. It's special to me."
Ben got angry and said, "Fine, then I'll take it from you." He grabbed Lily's scarf and pulled it hard. Lily screamed and tried to hold on to it. But Ben was stronger and he ripped the scarf from Lily's neck. He ran away with it, laughing.
Lily cried and ran to her mom. She told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm so sorry, Lily. That was very mean of him. He shouldn't have taken your scarf. He should have asked nicely or found his own scarf."
Lily sobbed and said, "But I liked my scarf. It was from grandma. I want it back."
Her mom said, "I know, honey. I liked it too. But I don't think we can get it back. He's gone now. Maybe we can make another scarf with grandma. But it won't be the same."
Lily nodded and said, "It won't be the same. I miss my scarf. I miss grandma. I wish Ben was more thoughtful."

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy boy. He was a daydreamer, always wishing he could sail across the ocean. One day, he decided it was time to make his dream come true. He dug up a gray boat from his backyard and took it down to the beach. There, he put the clumsy boat in the water, and before long he was off sailing across the ocean.
The boy was having a great time, sailing swiftly and feeling the salt breeze on his face. In no time, he had sailed so far he could no longer see land. Suddenly, he could feel the strong winds pushing him farther from home. As he sailed, the skies grew darker and gale force winds began to blow.
The boy tried to turn his boat around, but it was no use. He was caught in the middle of a perilous storm and the waves were becoming more and more fierce. He clung to the boat, hoping the storm would soon pass. Then, suddenly, the storm clouds cleared and the sun shone bright and warm. The boy was unharmed and found himself safe on the shore of a distant land.
The boy thanked his lucky stars and realized that his clumsy little boat had been more powerful than he had ever imagined. With a smile, he jumped back into the boat and sailed off once again into the unknown.

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play in the dark. They had a flashlight that they shared, but sometimes they fought over it. One night, they decided to play hide and seek in their room, and Ben took the flashlight with him.
Mia looked for Ben, but she could not find him. She heard him giggle, but she could not see him. She felt scared and lonely in the dark. She wished she had the flashlight too.
"Ben, where are you?" she called. "Please, let me have the flashlight. I can't see anything."
Ben did not answer. He was hiding under the bed, and he thought it was funny to make Mia scared. He turned on the flashlight and made it glow under the bed. He saw Mia's feet walking around the room, and he laughed.
Mia saw the light under the bed, and she ran towards it. She thought Ben was there, and she wanted to hug him. But when she reached the bed, she bumped her head on the frame. She cried out in pain and dropped to the floor.
Ben heard Mia cry, and he felt sorry. He crawled out from under the bed, and he saw Mia holding her head. He gave her the flashlight, and he said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I was mean to you. Are you okay?"
Mia took the flashlight, and she looked at Ben. She saw his face, and she smiled. She said, "I'm okay, Ben. Thank you for the flashlight. I love you."
Ben hugged Mia, and he said, "I love you too, Mia. You are my twin, and you are unique. We should share the flashlight, and we should not scare each other."
Mia nodded, and she said, "You are right, Ben. We should be kind to each other, and we should have fun together."
They turned on the flashlight, and they made it glow in the dark. They played with the light, and they made shapes and shadows on the wall. They laughed and talked, and they felt happy and safe.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring, and kindness is better than meanness.

Lily liked to whistle. She whistled when she played, when she ate, and when she slept. She whistled all the time. But not everyone liked her whistling. Her brother Ben did not like it. He said it was too loud and rude. He said it hurt his ears and made him angry.
One day, Ben had a plan. He took Lily's whistle and hid it under his bed. He thought she would stop whistling and leave him alone. But he was wrong. Lily looked for her whistle everywhere. She asked her mom, her dad, and her dog. No one knew where it was. She was very sad and cried.
Ben heard her cry and felt bad. He knew he did a bad thing. He took the whistle from under his bed and went to Lily's room. He knocked on the door and said, "Lily, I have something for you. I'm sorry I took your whistle. It was not nice. It was rude. Your whistle belongs to you. You can whistle if you want to. I will try to be more kind and listen to you."
Lily opened the door and saw Ben holding her whistle. She smiled and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, Ben. I'm sorry I whistled too much. It was not nice. It was rude. I will try to be more quiet and respect you. You are my brother and I love you."
They both learned a lesson. They learned to share and care for each other. They learned to be polite and not rude. They learned to whistle and listen. They were happy.

His mom said, "Yes, you can have the puzzle. But you have to solve it by yourself, okay?" Tim was very happy and said, "I will solve it, I promise!"
When they got home, Tim opened the puzzle box. But instead of puzzle pieces, there were cookies inside! Tim was surprised and said, "Mom, there are cookies in the box, not a puzzle!" His mom laughed and said, "Oh no! We must have picked up the wrong box at the store. But that's okay, we can eat the cookies and go back to the store to find the right puzzle for you to solve."
Tim and his mom ate the cookies and went back to the store. This time, they made sure to find the right box with the puzzle inside. Tim solved the puzzle with a big smile on his face. And from that day on, he always checked the label on the box before buying anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She lived in a small village near the oasis. One day, Sally decided to go to the oasis by herself to explore. As she got closer, she saw an old man mixing something strange into the water. She was scared and wanted to run away, but the man looked up and saw her.
"Come here, little one," he said gruffly.
Sally was frightened. She didn't want to go any closer.
"Come here, I said!" the old man said even louder this time.
Sally slowly walked towards him. As she got closer, she realized he was mixing a strange potion into the oasis. Sally was very scared and she wanted to run away. But it was too late.
The old man grabbed Sally and threw her into the oasis. She screamed for help but no one came. The strange potion started to fill her body and she began to feel an odd sensation of burning. The last thing Sally remembered before she passed out was a wicked laugh coming from the old man.
The next day, the villagers from Sally's village found her body floating lifelessly in the oasis. They were horrified and sad. Sadly, Sally was gone forever. The old man had mixed a deadly potion into the oasis and Sally had paid the price.

Lily and Ben are very competitive. They want to be the first to reach the flag. They jog faster and faster. They pass many other kids. They are almost at the flag.

"It hurts, Ben. I can't jog anymore." Lily says.
"That's okay, Lily. The race is not important. You are important. You are my friend. Let's go to your mom. She will make you feel better." Ben says.
He holds Lily's hand and walks with her to her mom. Her mom hugs her and puts a band-aid on her knee. She says: "You are very brave, Lily. And you are very lucky to have a good friend like Ben."
Lily smiles and says: "Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. You are my best friend."
Ben smiles and says: "You're welcome, Lily. You are my best friend too."
They hug and say: "We are both winners. We are both safe. We are both happy."

"Or a fort for our soldiers," Tom said.

"Who is there? What are you doing with my wood?" the voice asked.
Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know who the voice belonged to. They hid behind the wood and whispered to each other.
"Who do you think it is?" Tom asked.
"I don't know. Maybe it is a monster," Lily said.
"Or a witch," Tom said.
They were very quiet and hoped the voice would go away. But the voice spoke again.
"Come out, come out, wherever you are. I won't hurt you. I just want to talk to you," the voice said.
Tom and Lily peeked over the wood and saw a face. It was not a monster or a witch. It was an old man with a long beard and a kind smile. He was holding a book in his hand.
"Hello, children. I'm sorry if I scared you. I'm Mr. Fox, the owner of this wood. I use it to make toys and books for children like you. Do you want to see some of them?" he asked.
Tom and Lily nodded. They were curious and not afraid anymore. They came out from behind the wood and followed Mr. Fox to his workshop. There they saw many wonderful things. There were cars and trains and planes made of wood. There were dolls and animals and puzzles made of wood. There were books and stories and pictures made of wood.
"Wow, these are amazing," Tom said.
"How do you make them?" Lily asked.
"I use my tools and my imagination. And I also use this," Mr. Fox said, pointing to his book. "This is my book of wisdom. It has many words and ideas that help me create and learn. Do you want to hear some of them?"
Tom and Lily nodded again. They liked to hear new words and ideas. They sat down with Mr. Fox and listened to him read from his book. He read them stories and poems and riddles. He asked them questions and made them guess and think. He taught them new words and meanings and sounds. He made them laugh and wonder and dream.
Tom and Lily had a lot of fun with Mr. Fox and his wood. They learned many things and made a new friend. They decided that Mr. Fox was a very wise and kind man. And they also decided that wood was a very good thing to play with.

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to paint. They had many colors and brushes to make pictures. One day, they decided to paint each other's arms with different patterns.
"Can I paint your arm, Sam?" Lily asked.
"Sure, Lily. You can paint my arm. What color do you want to use?" Sam said.
"I want to use red and blue. They are my favorite colors. And I will make stripes and dots on your arm. It will look nice," Lily said.
"OK, Lily. And I will use yellow and green. They are my favorite colors. And I will make circles and stars on your arm. It will look nice, too," Sam said.
They started to paint each other's arms carefully and gently. They had fun and laughed as they saw their arms change colors and shapes. They were happy and proud of their work.
But then, they heard a voice.
"What are you doing, kids? You are making a mess!" It was Lily's mom. She saw the paint on their arms, clothes, and floor. She was angry and upset.
"Lily, Sam, you should not paint your arms. That is not easy to wash off. And you should not paint on the floor. That is not easy to clean up. You should only paint on paper. That is easy to throw away. You should be careful and respectful when you paint. Do you understand?" Lily's mom said.
Lily and Sam felt sorry and ashamed. They did not mean to make a mess. They only wanted to have fun and be creative.
"Yes, mom. We understand. We are sorry. We will not paint our arms or the floor again. We will only paint on paper. And we will help you clean up the mess. Please forgive us," Lily and Sam said.
Lily's mom sighed and smiled. She was not angry anymore. She knew they were good kids who made a mistake.
"OK, kids. I forgive you. I know you like to paint. And I like your paintings. But you have to be careful and respectful when you paint. Painting is fun, but it is also a responsibility. Do you agree?" Lily's mom said.
"Yes, mom. We agree. Painting is fun and a responsibility. We will be careful and respectful when we paint. Thank you, mom," Lily and Sam said.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of forgiveness, kindness, and friendship. It also shows the consequences of being mean and selfish.
Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story uses foreshadowing when it says that Ben and Mia were almost ready to put the last block on top, implying that something might happen to stop them. It also uses setup and payoff when Tom trips on a block and falls down, which is a result of his own action of breaking the tower.

Tom and Lily stopped crying and smiled back. They realized they had been silly and mean to Fluffy. They hugged him and said they were sorry.

Fluffy was happy. He jumped on their bed and invited them to join him. They cuddled and played with him until they fell asleep. They dreamed of having more fun adventures with Fluffy, but without quarreling.

Sue's mom saw her panic and came to help. She picked up the spoon and told Sue that it was okay. She said that even though the stove was difficult to use, Sue could still help in other ways. Sue felt better and helped her mom by setting the table. They had a fun time cooking together.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy named Tom. Tom loved adventure and never stayed in one place for too long. One day, Tom wanted to explore outer space, so he asked his mom if he could he borrow her rocket ship. She said yes, so Tom loaded up the rocket ship and flew away.
As Tom soared through the night sky, he noticed that there were so many twinkling stars! He pointed and said, "Wow! That one looks like a planet!" Tom felt so excited, he decided to go and explore it.
When Tom reached the planet, it was so big and colourful. He said, "Whoa! I must be really adventurous to come here!" He spent some time exploring and collecting rocks from the planet.
Suddenly, he heard a loud noise from behind him. It was his mom calling him back. "Time to go home, Tom!" she said. So Tom waved goodbye to the planet and soared back to his house in the night sky.

Joe was so sad that he didn't feel grateful anymore. He had made a mistake and it had a bad ending.

As the barber cut the hair, the monkey's face changed. It was not fierce anymore. The monkey was a little girl! The girl said, "Thank you, barber. You helped me turn back into a girl by cutting my hair." They both smiled and became friends.

Once upon a time there was a humble steel turtle. He liked to stand on his head and look up at the sky. One day he heard a noise, he looked to see what it was. It was a big, shiny, silver bird flying above him.
The turtle was fascinated by the bird and said, "Wow! You can fly so high and so fast! Can I fly too?"
The bird smiled and said, "I'm sorry, little one. I wish I could show you, but I am made of steel and you are made of soft skin, so flying is not for you."
The turtle was quite sad but understood the bird. He thanked the bird for talking to him and watched it fly away. Then, he took a deep breath, put his head up high, and stood on two feet. He may not have been able to fly, but he could still do many things!

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy cars and trucks. They have a big box of fuel for their toys. Fuel makes the toys go fast and make noise.
One day, they are playing in the backyard. Tom has a red car and Sam has a blue truck. They race each other on the grass. Tom says, "My car is faster than your truck. I will win the race."
Sam says, "No, my truck is stronger than your car. I will win the race."
They zoom and beep and honk their toys. They have fun.
But then, Tom's car stops. It does not go anymore. It does not make noise. Tom looks at his car. He sees that it has no fuel left. He says, "Oh no, my car has no fuel. I need more fuel."
Sam stops his truck. He sees that his truck has a lot of fuel left. He says, "Ha ha, my truck has fuel. I win the race."
Tom feels sad. He says, "That is not fair. You have more fuel than me. Can you share some fuel with me?"
Sam thinks. He remembers that Tom is his brother. He remembers that they love each other. He remembers that sharing is good. He says, "Okay, I will share some fuel with you. We can both play with our toys."
He gives some fuel to Tom. Tom puts the fuel in his car. His car goes again. It makes noise. He says, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good brother. You are mighty."
Sam smiles. He says, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good brother too. You are mighty."
They hug each other. They play with their toys again. They do not care who wins the race. They are happy.

Anna loved to look at the stars at night. She liked to see how they twinkled and made shapes in the sky. Sometimes, she heard a sound from the big tree near her window. It was an owl who lived there. Anna wanted to talk to the owl and ask him many questions.
One night, she decided to stay up late and wait for the owl. She put on her warm pajamas and her cozy slippers and climbed on her bed. She opened her window and looked at the tree. She saw two big eyes and a round head. It was the owl!
"Hello, owl!" Anna said. "You are very adorable. Can I ask you a question?"
The owl looked at Anna and tilted his head. He said, "Hoo, hoo, hoo. What is your question, little girl?"
Anna smiled and said, "I want to know about the stars. How many are there? What are they made of? Do they have names?"
The owl thought for a moment and said, "Hoo, hoo, hoo. That is a big question, little girl. The stars are very many and very far. They are made of fire and light. They have names, but I do not know them all. Some are called the Big Bear, the Little Bear, the Swan, and the Hunter."
Anna listened with wonder and said, "Wow, that is amazing, owl. Thank you for telling me. Can I ask you another question?"
The owl nodded and said, "Hoo, hoo, hoo. You can ask me one more question, little girl. Then you must go to sleep. It is late and you need to rest."
Anna thought hard and said, "Okay, owl. My last question is: do you have a friend? Do you like to play with other owls?"
The owl smiled and said, "Hoo, hoo, hoo. Yes, I have a friend. She is another owl who lives in the next tree. We like to play and hunt together. Sometimes, we sing to each other. She is very adorable, too."
Anna clapped her hands and said, "That is wonderful, owl. I am happy for you and your friend. You are very lucky. I have a friend, too. She is a girl who lives in the next house. We like to play and draw together. Sometimes, we sing, too. She is very adorable, too."
The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, hoo. I am happy for you and your friend, too. You are very lucky. Friends are very important. They make us happy and help us learn. You are a very smart and kind little girl. I like you very much."
Anna said, "Thank you, owl. I like you very much, too. You are a very wise and friendly owl. I hope to see you again. Good night, owl."
The owl said, "Good night, little girl. Sweet dreams, Anna."
Anna closed her window and snuggled in her bed. She looked at the stars and the owl one more time and smiled. She felt very happy and sleepy. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of stars and owls and friends.

Lila and Tom are playing in the garden. They like to pretend they are explorers in the desert. They have a tent, a map, and a water bottle. They also have a cactus that Lila's mom gave them. She said it is a special plant that can live in very dry places.
"Look, Tom, this is our cactus. It is important for our adventure. It can supply us with water if we get thirsty," Lila says, holding the cactus carefully.
"Wow, that is cool, Lila. How do we get the water from the cactus?" Tom asks, curious.
Lila thinks for a moment. She remembers what her mom told her. "We have to cut the cactus with a knife and squeeze the juice out. But we have to be careful not to touch the spikes. They can hurt us," she says.
"OK, let's try it. Do you have a knife?" Tom says, excited.
Lila shakes her head. "No, I don't. Mom said knives are dangerous for kids. We have to ask her first," she says.
"OK, let's go ask her then. Maybe she can help us," Tom says.
They run to the house, holding the cactus. They find Lila's mom in the kitchen. She smiles when she sees them.
"Hi, kids. What are you doing with the cactus?" she asks.
"Mom, we are explorers in the desert. We need water from the cactus. Can you help us?" Lila says.
"Sure, I can help you. But you have to be very careful with the cactus. It has sharp spikes that can poke you. And the juice is not very tasty. It is bitter and sour. You might not like it," she says.
"We don't mind, Mom. We want to try it. It is important for our adventure," Tom says.
"OK, then. Let's go to the sink. I have a knife and a bowl. I will cut the cactus and squeeze the juice for you. You can watch, but don't touch," she says.
They follow her to the sink. She cuts the cactus and squeezes the juice into the bowl. She gives them each a spoon and a glass of water.
"Here you go, kids. This is the cactus juice. You can taste it, but be careful. It might make you pucker your lips. And drink some water after. It will help you wash it down," she says.
Lila and Tom take a spoonful of the juice. They put it in their mouths and make a face. It is bitter and sour. They pucker their lips and spit it out. They drink some water and make a sound.
"Yuck, Mom. That is gross. How can anyone drink that?" Lila says.
"I told you, kids. It is not very tasty. But it is good for you. It has vitamins and minerals. And it can supply you with water in the desert. But you don't have to drink it. You have plenty of water in your bottle," she says.
"Thanks, Mom. We appreciate your help. But we don't want any more cactus juice. We will stick to our water bottle. It is much better," Tom says.
They hug their mom and thank her. They take their water bottle and their cactus and go back to the garden. They continue their adventure in the desert. They are happy and thirsty no more.

But then, she heard a loud noise. It was the basement door slamming shut. She looked up and saw a shadow. It was her mom, and she looked angry. She said, "Lily, what are you doing here? You are supposed to be in bed! You are in big trouble, young lady!"
Lily felt scared and sorry. She dropped the doll and the book and ran to her mom. She hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, mom, I was just playing. I wanted to see what was in the basement. I was adventurous."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. Now, let's go back to your room and tuck you in. And no more sneaking out, okay?"
Lily agreed and said, "Okay, mom. No more sneaking out."
Her mom held her hand and led her upstairs. She tucked her in and kissed her goodnight. She turned off the light and said, "Sweet dreams, Lily."
Lily closed her eyes and said, "Sweet dreams, mom."
She fell asleep and dreamed of the doll, the train, and the book. She was adventurous, but she also learned to respect.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a big wallet in his pocket. Anna thought the wallet looked shiny and wanted to have it. Ben thought the wallet was not theirs and they should not touch it.
Anna said to Ben, "Let's go and take the wallet. The man is not looking. We can buy candy and toys with the money."
Ben said, "No, Anna. That is bad. The wallet belongs to the man. He needs the money. We have our own money in our piggy bank. We should not steal."
Anna did not listen to Ben. She ran to the bench and tried to grab the wallet. But she was not careful. She slipped on a banana peel and fell down. The man heard the noise and turned around. He saw Anna on the ground and his wallet in her hand. He was angry and scared.
He shouted, "Hey, you little thief! What are you doing with my wallet? Give it back to me!"
Anna was scared too. She dropped the wallet and started to cry. Ben ran to her and helped her up. He said, "I'm sorry, mister. My sister made a mistake. She did not mean to take your wallet. She was just curious. Please don't be mad at her."
The man looked at Ben and Anna. He saw that they were adorable twins who were sorry for what they did. He calmed down and said, "It's okay, kids. I forgive you. But you should never take things that are not yours. That is wrong and hurtful. You should always be honest and respectful. Do you understand?"
Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mister. We understand. We are sorry. We will never do it again."
The man smiled and said, "That's good. Here, take this candy as a gift. But remember, candy is not as sweet as being good." He gave them each a candy and patted their heads. Then he took his wallet and left.
Anna and Ben hugged each other and said, "Thank you, mister. You are very kind. We learned our lesson. We will always be good."
The end.

He took two slices of bread and put them in the toaster. He pushed the button.
"Can I have some butter and jam on my toast?" Lily asked.
"Sure, you can have some. But I have a better idea. Let's put some salt and pepper on our toast. It will make it more tasty!" Ben suggested.
He took the salt and pepper shakers from the cupboard and sprinkled them on the toast.
"That sounds fun!" Lily said. She copied Ben and put salt and pepper on her toast too.
The toaster popped. The toast was ready. Ben and Lily took their toast and bit into it.
"Yuck!" they both said. The toast was rough and spicy. It made their mouths hurt and their eyes water. They spit out the toast and ran to the sink. They drank some water to wash away the bad taste.
They felt sick and sorry. They had wasted the bread and the butter and the jam. They had not listened to their mom, who had told them to only put butter and jam on their toast. They had tried to be smart and funny, but they had made a big mistake.
The moral of the story is: Do not put salt and pepper on your toast. It is not good for you. Listen to your mom. She knows what is best for you.

“Stop!” cried Shelly. “That’s not safe!”
The rabbit ignored her, and kept walking towards the shiny object.
Shelly flew down from her perch, landed beside the rabbit and said, “Rise. That’s not wise. It could be dangerous. I have the wisdom to know that.”
The rabbit thought for a moment and realized that Shelly was right. He thanked her for her advice and went back to his burrow.

One day, a big net came to catch all the fish. All the fish swam fast to hide, but Bubbles was too lazy to move. Fin saw Bubbles in danger and asked his friends to help. They all swam fast and pushed Bubbles out of the net. Bubbles learned that being lazy is not good and thanked Fin and his friends for saving him. From that day on, Bubbles played with Fin and his friends and was not lazy anymore.

One day, Mia saw a pink cat outside her house. The cat looked sad and lonely. Mia went to the cat and said, "Hi, pink cat! Do you want to be my friend?" The pink cat looked at Mia and said, "Yes, I would like that."
Mia was very happy to have a new friend. She asked her mom if the pink cat could come inside and play. Her mom said, "Yes, but you must take care of the cat and accept responsibility for it." Mia agreed and brought the pink cat inside.
Mia and the pink cat played all day long. They played with Mia's pink toys and shared her pink snacks. At the end of the day, Mia gave the pink cat a big hug and said, "I am so happy to have you as my friend!"
From that day on, Mia and the pink cat were the best of friends. They played together every day and had many adventures. And Mia always remembered to accept responsibility for her new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jamie. He went to the park with his mom. When they got there, Jamie found a wallet on the ground. He was surprised and he wanted to show his mom. He said "Mommy, look! I found a wallet!"
His mom smiled and said "Wow, that's great! Now, we should try and find the owner of the wallet. Do you want to help?"
Jamie said "Yes!"
So they started walking around the park, looking for its owner. They stopped and asked a few people, but no one knew who the wallet belonged to. After a while, they heard gentle tapping in the distance.
They followed the sound and found a kind-looking old man, hammering something into the ground. Jamie walked up to him and said "Sir, is this your wallet?"
The old man looked up and said 'Yes! My wallet! How did you find it?"
Jamie said "I found it on the ground, sir."
The old man smiled and said "Thank you for being so honest! Here, take this for your trouble." He reached into his pocket and pulled out a shiny coin. He gave it to Jamie and said "You are very gentle. I appreciate that."
Jamie smiled and said "Thank you, sir!" He hugged his mom and they went home.

Once upon a time there was an enormous bull. He lived on a farm with four ducks and a pony. One day, the bull heard something strange coming from a nearby field. He called to the ducks and the pony and asked them if they heard the same sound.
"I think it sounds like something repeating," said one of the ducks.
The bull was curious and so he slowly walked over to the field to investigate. And sure enough, huge and enormous, he saw a little boy, who was repeating the same words over and over.
The bull stepped closer to the little boy and asked him why he was repeating the same words. The little boy said that he was trying to learn to count to ten.
The bull smiled and said, "Well, let me help you with that. I can repeat the numbers after you!"
And so the bull and the little boy declared each number together. The bull shared his great wisdom, repeating louder each time until the little boy could recite all the numbers from one to ten.
The little boy thanked the enormous bull for his help. And from that day onwards, the bull became the little boy's teacher, teaching him new things whenever he visited the farm.

As Tim poked the dust, he found a shiny toy car. He was so happy. He showed it to his friend, Sam. Sam was envious. He wanted a shiny toy car too. So, Sam went to the dust pile and started to poke it.
Sam poked and poked, but he did not find a shiny toy car. Instead, he found a big, green frog. The frog looked at Sam and said, "Hello!" Sam was very surprised. He did not know that frogs could talk. The frog said, "I am a magic frog. I can turn your toy car into a real car if you let me play with it."
Tim and Sam were very excited. They let the frog play with the toy car. The frog turned it into a real car. Tim and Sam were so happy. They took turns driving the car and playing with the frog. And they all lived happily ever after.

Mummy was sad. She had just moved into a new home and it felt gloomy. As she was walking around, she noticed a birdcage in a corner of the room. "I wonder who owns this", she thought.
Mummy asked her three-year-old daughter: "Do you know who owns this birdcage?". But her daughter just shook her head.
Mummy was determined to find out who owned the birdcage, so she asked around the neighbourhood. Everyone kept saying "No, we don't know".
Mummy was starting to get worried. What if no one knew who the birdcage belonged to?
Just as she was about to give up, she heard a voice calling: "It's mine!". Mummy turned around and saw an old woman staggering in the door.
The old woman had a big smile on her face. "This birdcage has been in my family for generations!", she said joyfully.
Mummy was relieved. The old woman showed her a few pictures of her ancestors with the birdcage, and soon Mummy knew all about the birdcage's history.
Mummy thanked the old woman and brought the birdcage home. Now, whenever Mummy feels gloomy, she looks at the birdcage and remembers how she found out its secret.

Once there was a little girl named Anna. She was three years old and loved to walk around the park. Every day, she would bring her teddy bear with her for company.
One day, Anna walked further than ever before, deep into the woods. The trees were tall and the shadows were long. Anna felt scared and her teddy bear couldn't keep her calm.
As she turned around to head back, Anna heard a noise like a deep growl. It was too dark to see and Anna was too scared to move. She hugged her teddy bear tight, waiting for the noise to go away.
Suddenly, from out of the shadows, a tiny puppy stumbled across Anna's path. Anna was scared at first, but then the puppy came towards her and licked her face. Anna laughed and cuddled the puppy, happy it was only a puppy making the noise.
The moral of the story is to not worry when you are scared. Things are not always what they seem and it's best to take a moment to figure out what's really happening.

Sam and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they find some sticks and leaves. They want to make a fire.
"Look, I have a dull rock. It can make sparks," Sam says. He hits the rock on another rock. He tries to make the fire.
Tom watches. He sees no fire. He has an idea. He offers Sam his toy car. "Here, you can play with my car. It is fast and fun. Maybe I can make the fire."
Sam likes the car. He gives Tom the rock. He zooms the car on the ground. He makes car noises.
Tom takes the rock. He hits it harder on the other rock. He sees some sparks. He puts them on the leaves. He blows on them. He makes the fire.
"Wow, you did it!" Sam says. He runs to Tom. He sees the fire. He is happy. He claps his hands.
They both sit by the fire. They share the car. They are warm and cozy. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was very nice boy called Joe. He loved to play in his garden and was very happy. One day, Joe saw his toy gun in the garden and called out to his mom to look.

Daisy was so happy, she clapped her hands together. She opened the box, and there inside was the most beautiful jewel she had ever seen! It sparkled in the sunlight, and Daisy was so jolly she skipped back into the castle with her new jewel.

Ben and Mia like to play in the park. They run and jump and slide and swing. They have fun with their friends and their toys. But sometimes they get hot and thirsty. Then they look for a place to rest and drink.
One day, they find a big rock under a tree. The rock is cool and smooth. They sit on the rock and pause. They drink some water from their bottles. They feel better. They talk and laugh and watch the birds and bugs.
But then they hear a loud noise. It is a big truck. The truck comes to the park. It has a big shovel and a big bucket. It digs up the dirt and the grass. It makes a big hole. Ben and Mia are scared. They wonder what the truck is doing.
They see a man get out of the truck. He has a hat and a vest and a tool. He walks to the rock. He puts the tool on the rock. He pushes a button. The tool makes a loud noise. It breaks the rock. Ben and Mia are sad. They like the rock. They do not want the rock to break.
They run to the man. They shout and wave. They ask him to stop. They tell him the rock is their friend. They tell him the rock is cool and smooth. They tell him they sit on the rock and pause. They tell him they drink water on the rock. They tell him they love the rock.
The man hears them. He looks at them. He smiles. He stops the tool. He puts it down. He walks to them. He kneels. He talks to them. He tells them he is sorry. He tells them he did not know. He tells them he needs the rock. He tells them the rock is hot. He tells them the rock has fire inside. He tells them he uses the fire to make things. He tells them he makes things for people. He tells them he makes things for them.
Ben and Mia listen. They are curious. They ask him questions. He answers them. He shows them the truck. He shows them the shovel and the bucket. He shows them the hole. He shows them the rock. He shows them the fire. He shows them the things. He tells them stories. He makes them laugh.
Ben and Mia are happy. They learn new things. They make a new friend. They understand why he needs the rock. They say goodbye to the rock. They thank the rock for being cool and smooth. They thank the rock for letting them sit and pause. They thank the rock for giving them fire. They hug the rock. They hug the man. They run back to the park. They play some more. They have fun. They are hot and thirsty. They look for a new place to rest and drink. They find a new rock. They hope the truck does not come.

That night, the big, shiny nut started to glow. The squirrel was surprised! The nut cracked open, and a tiny fairy came out. The fairy said, "Thank you for finding me! I was trapped in that nut. As a thank you, I will give you a wish." The squirrel wished for more nuts than he could ever collect. The fairy waved her wand, and the tree was filled with nuts. The squirrel was so happy, and he and the fairy became best friends.

But Tim did not listen. He played with the bug and it got hurt. Tim started to regret what he did. He felt sad for the bug. Sue told Tim, "We should be kind to all living things, even bugs."
The next day, Tim found another bug. This time, he did not play with it. He let the bug go free. Tim learned that being kind is important. And he never hurt a bug again.

The moral of the story is to always build on a strong foundation, both in towers and in life.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom liked to sleep all day on his soft pillow. One day, a little bird named Tim came to play with Tom.

Tom got mad at Tim. He jumped up and chased the little bird. Tim flew away, and Tom followed him. They ran and ran until they reached a big, cold lake. Tom did not like water, but he still wanted to catch Tim.
Tom jumped into the cold lake. He started to shiver because it was so cold. Tim flew away and left Tom in the cold water. Tom could not swim and he was too far from the shore. In the end, Tom was not able to get out of the cold lake.

Tom was a little mouse who lived in a big house. He liked to explore the house and find food to eat. But he was also very careful, because he knew there was a big cat who wanted to make him a meal.
One day, Tom saw a piece of cheese on a table. He was very hungry, so he ran to the cheese and started to nibble it. He did not see the cat hiding under the table, waiting for him.
The cat jumped out and tried to catch Tom. Tom was scared and ran away. He ran into a hole in the wall and hid there. The cat could not follow him, so he went away.
Tom was safe, but he was also sad. He had lost his cheese and he had no friends to play with. He felt very lonely in the hole. He wished he had someone to talk to and share his food with.
Then he heard a squeak from the other side of the hole. He looked and saw another mouse. The mouse smiled and said, "Hello, I'm Lily. I live here too. Do you want to be my friend?"
Tom was surprised and happy. He said, "Yes, I do. I'm Tom. I'm sorry I took your cheese. Do you want some?"
Lily said, "That's okay. I have some bread and nuts. We can share them. Come, let's eat and play together."
Tom and Lily became friends. They ate and played and talked in the hole. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little orange bird named Bobo. Bobo loved to eat prunes. One day, he saw a big prune on the ground. But when he tried to eat it, he could not pick it up. It was too big! Bobo was sad and did not know what to do.
Then, a big blue bird named Kiki came by. Kiki saw Bobo was sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Bobo?" Bobo said, "I want to eat this big prune, but I can't pick it up." Kiki thought for a moment and said, "Let's put the prune in the tree and share it." Bobo liked the idea.
Together, they picked up the big prune and put it in the tree. As they did, the prune split in two! Now, both Bobo and Kiki had a piece of the prune to eat. They were both happy and became good friends. The moral of the story is that when we share and work together, we can solve problems and be happy.

Once upon a time there was a silly rabbit who loved to eat lunch. Every day the bunny would go to the same spot in the woods to look for food.

So, the bunny picked the flower and decided to skip lunch and go home. But when the bunny arrived, he saw that the flower had changed in appearance. Instead of the pretty yellow color it had been before, it was now a dark purple.
The bunny began to laugh and said, "This is so silly! What a strange looking flower! I'm going to put it back outside so it can be closer to its friends."
And so the bunny did just that. But sadly, the bunny was never seen again. Later that night, a heavy rain began to fall and the flower was destroyed. The bunny was nowhere to be found and was never heard from again.
