Tim and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were cowboys and robbers. Tim had a fancy hat and a pistol that made a loud noise. Ben had a scarf and a stick.
"Hands up, robber!" Tim shouted, pointing his pistol at Ben. "Give me all your money or I'll shoot!"
Ben laughed and waved his stick. "No way, cowboy! You can't catch me!" He ran away, dodging behind a slide.
Tim chased him, making his pistol noise. He was having fun. He saw Ben hiding behind a bench. He sneaked up behind him and grabbed his scarf.
"Got you, robber!" Tim said, pulling Ben out. "Now give me your money!"
Ben frowned and tried to get free. He didn't like Tim's game anymore. He saw a lady sitting on the bench. She had a big bag and a shiny necklace.
"Help, help!" Ben yelled. "This cowboy is trying to rob me!"
The lady looked at Tim and Ben. She saw Tim's pistol and got scared. She thought it was real. She screamed and ran away, leaving her bag and necklace.
Tim and Ben stopped playing. They saw the lady's things. They felt curious.
"Wow, look at all this stuff!" Tim said, dropping his pistol and scarf. He opened the bag and saw a lot of money and cards.
"Maybe we should take it," Ben said, picking up the necklace. He liked how it sparkled.
Tim nodded. He thought it was a good idea. He put some money and cards in his pocket. He saw a phone in the bag. He wanted to play with it.
"Let's go," Ben said, putting the necklace around his neck. He saw a man coming. He looked angry.
"Hey, you kids!" the man shouted. "That's my wife's bag and necklace! Give them back!"
Tim and Ben got scared. They tried to run away, but the man was faster. He caught them and grabbed their things. He saw Tim's pistol and got mad.
"What's this?" he said, holding the pistol. "You have a gun? Are you trying to rob my wife?"
Tim shook his head. He tried to explain. "No, no, it's just a toy. We were just playing. We're sorry."
The man didn't listen. He thought Tim was lying. He pulled the trigger, thinking it was a toy. He wanted to scare Tim.
But the pistol was not a toy. It was real. It made a loud noise and a flash. It hurt Tim very much. He fell down and didn't move.
Ben screamed. He saw Tim's blood. He felt very sad and scared. He wished they never played with the lady's things.
The man was shocked. He didn't mean to hurt Tim. He dropped the pistol and called for help.
But it was too late. Tim was gone. Ben was alone. They had a very bad ending.

"Mom, mom, what is happening?" they cried.

"But mom, look at all our things. They are gone!" Tom said.
"Yes, they are. And do you know why? Because you did not organize them. You left them all over the place, and the wind took them away. Now we have nothing to play with, and nothing to use for our work," their mother said.
Tom and Lily felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had listened to their mother and organized their things. They hugged their mother and said they were sorry.
"I love you, my dears, but you have to learn from your mistake. Organizing is important. It helps you keep your things safe and find them easily. It also shows respect for yourself and others. Next time, please organize your things after you play with them," their mother said.
Tom and Lily nodded and promised to do better. But they still felt sad and bored, because they had no toys and no tools. The storm lasted for a long time, and the barn was very dark and cold. They did not have a happy day.
The moral of the story is: Organizing is important. It helps you keep your things safe and find them easily. It also shows respect for yourself and others.

Mommy hears them crying. She comes to the garden. She sees the mushroom and the children. She knows what happened. She hugs them and talks to them.

They both tell Mommy what happened. They both say they are sorry. They both say they want to be friends again.

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks. They wanted to make a big tower. They worked hard and put many blocks on top of each other. They were almost done.
"Look, Lily, our tower is so tall!" Ben said.
"Yes, Ben, it is. We just need one more block to complete it," Lily said.
She reached for the last block, but it was too far. She stretched her hand, but she could not get it. She saw a chair near the block. She had an idea.
"I know, Ben. I can climb on the chair and get the block," she said.
She ran to the chair and climbed on it. She was careful not to fall. She grabbed the block and smiled. She was ready to finish the tower.
But she did not see that the chair was next to the kitchen table. And on the table, there was a bowl of soup. It was very hot and spicy. Mama had made it for lunch.
As Lily moved the block, she bumped the bowl. The soup spilled over the edge. It landed on Lily's hand.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "The soup is spicy! It hurts my hand!"
She dropped the block and jumped off the chair. She ran to Mama, who was in the living room. She showed her hand to Mama.
"Mama, Mama, help me! The soup is spicy! It hurts my hand!" she said.
Mama saw Lily's hand. It was red and wet. She felt sorry for Lily. She hugged her and kissed her hand.
"Oh, Lily, I'm sorry. You burned your hand. Come, let me put some ice on it. It will make it feel better," she said.
She took Lily to the bathroom. She got some ice from the freezer. She wrapped it in a cloth and put it on Lily's hand. Lily felt the cold. It was nice. It made the pain go away.
"Thank you, Mama. You are the best," Lily said.
"You're welcome, Lily. I love you. But next time, be careful. Don't climb on chairs. And don't touch the soup. It is spicy. It is not for little hands," Mama said.
"I know, Mama. I'm sorry. I won't do it again," Lily said.
They hugged and smiled. They went back to the living room. They saw Ben. He was still playing with the blocks. He had completed the tower. It was very tall and beautiful.
"Wow, Lily, look at our tower. We did it!" Ben said.
Lily looked at the tower. She was happy. She forgot about the soup. She clapped her hand. Well, one hand. The other hand still had ice on it.
"Yay, Ben, we did it! Our tower is the best!" she said.

"Arrr, matey, give me your gold or I'll make you walk the plank!" Ben shouted, waving his sword.
"Never, you scurvy dog! I'll defend my treasure to the end!" Lily replied, holding her sword.
They ran around the island, chasing and dodging each other, until they got tired and hungry. They decided to share their treasure and have a picnic on the beach. They opened the chest and took out some rocks and shells. They pretended they were cookies and cakes and ate them with their fingers.

"Indeed, it is, lass. But we made a big mess on the island. Look at all the sticks and leaves and crumbs!" Ben said, looking around.
They saw that their ship and chest were falling apart, and that the sand was covered with bits of rocks and shells. They felt bad for making the island messy.
"We should clean up our mess. The island is our friend, and we don't want to hurt it," Lily said.
"You're right, Lily. Let's put everything back where we found it, and say sorry to the island," Ben said.
They worked together to fix their ship and chest, and to pick up all the sticks, leaves, rocks and shells. They put them back in the bushes and the water, and smoothed the sand. They looked at the island and saw that it was clean and beautiful again.
"Thank you, island, for letting us play here. We're sorry for making you messy. We love you," they said together.
Then they heard a loud noise. They turned around and saw their mom and dad clapping their hands. They had been watching them from the boat.
"Wow, you two are such good pirates! And such good friends to the island! We're so proud of you!" their mom and dad said.
Lily and Ben smiled and ran to hug them. They felt happy and proud too.
"Can we play pirates again tomorrow?" they asked.
"Of course, you can. But only if you promise to clean up your mess again," their mom and dad said.
"We promise!" they said.
They all got on the boat and sailed away from the island. They waved goodbye to the island and thanked it again. The island waved back with its palm trees and smiled with its flowers.

Tim went back inside and took the medicine. It still tasted bad, but he knew it was important. He felt stronger and ran to save Sam. The bird saw Tim coming and got scared. It let go of Sam, who landed safely on the ground. They were both happy and hugged each other.

Anna was scared of the dark. She did not like the shadows and the noises. She wanted to go home and be warm and safe. But Ben did not listen to her. He kept playing with the ball.

"Where were you?" she asked. "It is dark and cold outside. You could have been hurt."
"We were playing with the ball," said Anna. "But Ben did not want to go home. He liked the dark. But then he lost the ball and a big dog chased him."
"I am sorry, mom," said Ben. "I was wrong. I should have listened to Anna. The dark is not fun. It is scary and dangerous."
Mom smiled and kissed them. She gave them some hot soup and a dry blanket. She told them a story and tucked them in bed.
"Next time, when it gets dark, you should go home," she said. "The dark is not a place to play. It is a place to sleep and dream."
Anna and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They said good night and closed their eyes. They slept well and had sweet dreams.

At home, Tim and Sue sat down to eat the lollipop. They took turns and waved it in the air before each lick. They laughed and played together. In the end, they learned that sharing made them happy. And they lived happily ever after.

So, Timmy decided to stay on the island. He played with Benny and all the other animals. They had so much fun every day. Timmy was very happy that he found the brilliant island and made new friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Lila and Tom are playing in the garden. They see a big sheet hanging on the line. It is green and has flowers on it.
"Let's play with the sheet!" Lila says. "We can make a tent or a cape or a dress!"
Tom agrees. He takes one end of the sheet and wraps it around his shoulders. He pretends to be a king. He says, "I am King Tom. You are my queen, Lila. Bow to me!"
Lila laughs. She takes the other end of the sheet and makes a bow on her head. She says, "I am Queen Lila. You are my king, Tom. I bow to you!"
They bow to each other and giggle. They feel happy and silly.
But then they hear a noise. It is the wind. It is blowing hard. It makes the sheet fly away from them. It goes up and up in the air.
"Oh no!" Lila and Tom say. "Our sheet!"
They run after the sheet. They try to catch it. But it is too fast and too high. It flies over the fence and into the street.
They stop at the fence. They look at the sheet. It lands on a car. The car is red and shiny. It has a big horn. It honks loudly.
The driver of the car is surprised. He sees the sheet on his car. He thinks it is unusual. He says, "Hey, what is this? Who put this sheet on my car?"
Lila and Tom are scared. They hide behind the fence. They hope the driver will not see them. They whisper, "Sorry, mister. It was an accident. We were just playing."
They wait for the driver to go away. They hope he will not be angry. They hope he will not take their sheet. They hope they can play with it again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Sue, who liked to play hide and seek. Tom said 'Let’s play in the big cave, it will be exciting!' So the two of them walked to the cave.
When they got inside, Tom shouted 'Sue, come over here and look!' Sue walked carefully towards Tom and was surprised to find an old skeleton. Tom said 'Let's take it with us, it will be fun!'
Sue was scared and said 'No, we shouldn't take it. Let's leave it here, it's safer.'
But Tom didn't listen and picked up the skeleton. Suddenly, there was a loud rumbling and a big rock fell and blocked the cave entrance. They were trapped inside!

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. It was a hot day, so they were thirsty and sweaty.
"Let's go get some water," Lily said. "There is a fountain over there."
"OK," Tom said. They left their ball on the grass and ran to the fountain. They drank some water and felt better.
But when they came back to the grass, they saw a big dog. The dog had their ball in its mouth. It was chewing and biting the ball. The ball was making a loud noise.
"Hey, that's our ball!" Tom shouted. He ran towards the dog. He wanted to get the ball back.
But the dog did not like that. The dog growled and barked at Tom. It showed its teeth. It looked angry and scary.
Lily saw Tom and the dog. She felt panic. She was afraid that the dog would hurt Tom. She did not know what to do.
"Tom, come back!" she cried. "The dog is bad! Leave the ball!"
But Tom did not hear her. He was too close to the dog. He reached out his hand to grab the ball.
The dog snapped at Tom's hand. It bit his finger. Tom screamed. He felt pain. He pulled his hand back. He saw blood on his finger.
Lily ran to Tom. She hugged him. She tried to make him feel better.
"Are you OK?" she asked. "Does it hurt a lot?"
Tom nodded. He was crying. He was scared. He wanted to go home.
Lily saw a man coming. The man had a leash in his hand. He was the dog's owner. He had left the dog open. He was not watching the dog.
"Hey, what happened?" the man asked. He saw Tom's finger. He saw the ball. He looked sorry.
"I'm sorry, kids," he said. "My dog is not good with balls. He thinks they are toys. He did not mean to hurt you. Let me see your finger."
The man took Tom's finger. He wrapped it with a cloth. He said he would take them to a doctor. He said he would buy them a new ball.
Lily and Tom did not say anything. They were still upset. They did not like the dog. They did not like the man. They wanted to go home. They wanted to play with their ball. But their ball was gone. The dog had broken it. It was a bad day.

Dan is a bald man. He likes to play with matches. He thinks they are fun and bright. But matches are not toys. They can make fire and hurt people.
One day, Dan finds a box of matches in his kitchen. He is very happy. He wants to see the matches light up. He takes one match and moves it to the stove. He turns on the stove and puts the match near the flame.
"Whoosh!" The match catches fire. Dan is scared. He drops the match on the floor. The floor has a rug. The rug starts to burn.
"Help! Help!" Dan shouts. He runs to the door. He wants to get out.
But his mom is there. She hears Dan and smells the smoke. She is very angry and worried. She grabs a bucket of water and throws it on the fire. She puts out the fire.
"Dan, what did you do?" she asks. "Why did you play with matches? You could have burned the house and yourself!"
"I'm sorry, Mom," Dan says. "I didn't know matches were bad. I just wanted to see them."
"Matches are not for playing, Dan," Mom says. "They are for grown-ups only. They can make fire and fire is dangerous. You have to be careful and never touch matches again. Do you understand?"
"Yes, Mom," Dan says. "I understand. I won't play with matches again. I'm sorry."
Mom hugs Dan. She is glad he is safe. She tells him to go to his room and think about what he did. She hopes he learned his lesson. She throws away the box of matches. She does not want Dan to find them again.

They ran to the bench and said, "Hello, mister. Do you want our umbrella? It's very nice and yellow."
The man looked surprised and smiled. He said, "Thank you, kids. That's very kind of you. But why are you giving me your umbrella? Don't you need it?"
Lily and Ben said, "We don't mind. We like the rain. It makes us happy. And you look sad. We want you to be happy too."

Jake took a deep breath and clutched onto the trunk. He wobbled and wobbled as he started to carry the tree. Soon he was able to move it with ease, and it felt like the sun was smiling down on him with each step he took.
As he looked back all the way down the creek, it hit him. He was able to carry the tree all this way, with only his determination and bravery. Jake felt accomplished and full of joy. He knew he had done something special, something thoughtful - and it was all by himself.

One day, a fly was buzzing around a kitchen table. Suddenly, the fly wanted to take a drink from the bowl of milk, sitting on the table. The milk looked so wet and yummy! So the fly flew towards the bowl and started sipping.
Suddenly, the mother saw the fly drinking the milk and she started to fill. She grabbed a fly swatter and quickly tried to swat the fly away. The fly tried to escape, but it was too late! The mother hit the fly and the fly fell into the milk, wet and lifeless.
Afterwards, the mother looked at the bowl of milk and saw the wet fly. She felt so sad and she said goodbye to the little fly. The mother and the little fly had a bad ending.

The little boy was so relieved. He thanked the mom and accepted the page. Then, he went back to playing with his friends as if nothing had happened.

Ben does not listen. He grabs his pirate hat and sword. He runs away. He says he will find other pirate friends.
Lily does not know what to do. She wants to go to the party, but she does not want to leave Ben. She thinks Ben is being mean. She thinks he should be happy for her. She thinks he should try something different.
She decides to go to the party. She puts on her princess dress and crown. She takes her invitation and her doll. She says goodbye to her mom. She walks to Anna's house.
She hopes Ben will change his mind. She hopes he will come to the party. She hopes he will not fight with her. She hopes they can still be friends.

They start to jog again. They smile. They have fun. They do not need the prize. They have each other.

Tommy looked at the mouse and said, "No, these are my carrots. Go away and find your own food. I do not want to share with you."
The mouse felt sad and left. He did not have any friends or family to help him. He wandered around the forest, looking for something to eat.
Tommy ate his carrots and felt happy. He did not care about the mouse or anyone else. He only cared about himself and his carrots.

Tommy was scared and cried for help. He wished he had someone to help him. He remembered the mouse and felt sorry for him. He wished he had been gentle and kind to the mouse and shared his carrots with him.
The mouse heard Tommy's cry and saw the hawk. He felt sorry for Tommy and wanted to help him. He ran to the hawk and bit his tail. The hawk was surprised and let go of Tommy. Tommy fell to the ground and ran to his burrow.
The mouse followed him and said, "Are you okay, Tommy? I am sorry the hawk tried to eat you. I wanted to help you because I know how it feels to be hungry and alone."
Tommy looked at the mouse and said, "Thank you, mouse. You are very brave and good. I am sorry I was mean to you and did not share my carrots with you. You are my friend and I want to share with you. Please, come and eat some carrots with me."
The mouse smiled and said, "Thank you, Tommy. You are very generous and kind. You are my friend and I want to share with you. Let us eat some carrots together."
Tommy and the mouse ate some carrots and became friends. They learned to love and share with each other and with other animals in the forest. They were happy and safe.
The moral of the story is: Love and share with others and they will love and share with you. Be gentle and kind and you will have friends. Do not be greedy and selfish and you will have trouble.

As they got closer, they saw a little frog on the raft. The frog said, "Hello, Tim! I brought this raft for you to play with the ducks." Tim was very excited and thanked the frog. Then, with his mom's help, he got on the raft and played with the ducks all day long.

Tim and Lily were friends who liked to swim. They went to the big hall with the pool every week. They had fun splashing and playing in the water.
One day, they saw a sign that said "Quiet please". Tim and Lily did not know what that meant. They thought it was a game. They tried to make as much noise as they could. They shouted and laughed and kicked the water.
The other people in the pool did not like that. They were angry and told Tim and Lily to stop. But Tim and Lily did not listen. They thought it was funny to make them mad.
Then, a big man came. He was the boss of the hall. He was very angry. He said to Tim and Lily, "You are very bad. You do not follow the rules. You disturb the other people. You have to leave now. And you can never come back."
Tim and Lily were scared and sad. They did not want to leave. They liked to swim. They said they were sorry. But the boss did not care. He took them out of the pool and sent them home. Tim and Lily cried all the way. They lost their favorite place to swim. They learned a hard lesson. They wished they had been quiet.

Once upon a time, in a big sea, there was a tall shark named Fin. Fin was very nice and loved to play with his friends. Every day, Fin would wake up early and swim around to find his friends.
One day, while Fin was playing with his friends, he saw a little fish stuck in a net. The little fish was sad and scared. Fin wanted to help the little fish, so he used his strong teeth to break the net. The little fish was free and very happy.
From that day on, all the sea animals loved Fin even more. They learned that being kind and helping others is very important. And Fin, the tall shark, was the best friend they could ever have.

Tom and Sam tried again. They made a new treat for Sue. This time, the treat was sweet. Sue was happy. She said, "Thank you, Tom and Sam!" They all smiled. From that day on, Tom, Sam, and their staff made sure all the treats were sweet, not sour.

Sara and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Sara has a doll and Ben has a car. They are having fun and sharing nicely. But then, Ben sees a shiny crown on the shelf. He wants to wear it and pretend he is a king. He puts down his car and reaches for the crown.
Sara sees what Ben is doing and gets angry. She likes the crown too. It belongs to her. She says, "No, Ben! That is mine! Give it back!" She grabs the crown from Ben's hand and puts it on her head. She says, "I am the queen and you are my servant. You have to do what I say."
Ben feels sad and mad. He does not want to be a servant. He wants to be a king. He says, "No, Sara! That is not fair! You have to share!" He tries to take the crown back from Sara, but she holds it tight. They start to pull and tug and shout.
Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees Sara and Ben fighting over the crown. She says, "Stop, children! What is going on here? Why are you not playing nicely?"
Sara and Ben stop and look at Mom. They feel ashamed. They know they have been bad. They say, "Sorry, Mom." Mom says, "You should not fight over toys. You should share and take turns. Fighting is not love. Love is being kind and gentle and caring. Do you love each other?"
Sara and Ben nod. They do love each other. They are brother and sister. They say, "Yes, Mom. We love each other." Mom says, "That is good. Now, can you show me how you love each other?" Sara and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry for hurting each other. They say, "Yes, Mom." They hug and kiss and say, "I love you." They surrender the crown and decide to play with their toys together. Mom smiles and says, "That is better. I love you too." She hugs and kisses them and says, "Now, let's have some cookies." Sara and Ben smile and say, "Yay! Cookies!" They follow Mom to the kitchen and forget about the crown. They are happy and love each other.

She looked up and saw a bird sitting on the very top.
Mia looked at her mom and asked, "Can I have it?" Her mom said, "No, that belongs to the bird." Mia was very restless and demanded to have the pole. Her mom calmly said, "No, it doesn't belong to us, so we can't take it."
Mia started to cry and her mom hugged her. She said, "Everything in this world belongs to someone, not everything can be ours. We can admire the things that we see, but we must not take anything that doesn't belong to us."
Mia understood and they continued their walk. She learned an important lesson that day. To always respect what belongs to others and never demand things that do not belong to us.

Anna and Ben are playing with blocks in the living room. They are building a big tower with many colors. Anna wants to put a red block on top, but Ben wants to put a blue block. They both reach for the last block at the same time.
"Give me the block!" Anna says.
"No, it's mine!" Ben says.
They pull and tug on the block, but it does not yield. They pull harder and harder, until the block flies out of their hands and hits the lamp. The lamp falls over and breaks with a loud crash. Anna and Ben are scared and stop fighting.
"Uh-oh," Anna says.
"Mama!" Ben cries.
Mama comes running from the kitchen. She sees the broken lamp and the empty block box. She is angry and sad.
"What happened here?" Mama asks.
"Anna and Ben are sorry, Mama," Anna says.
"We were fighting over the block, Mama," Ben says.
Mama sighs and picks up the block. She shows it to Anna and Ben.
"Look, this block has two sides. One side is red and one side is blue. You can both use it to make your tower. You don't have to fight over it. You can share it," Mama says.
Anna and Ben look at the block and nod. They say sorry to Mama and hug her. Mama hugs them back and smiles.
"Next time, use your words, not your hands. And be careful with the lamp. It has a leg that can break easily," Mama says.
Anna and Ben say okay and go back to their tower. They take turns putting the block on top. They are happy and proud of their tower. They are also happy and proud of their Mama.

Lily and Max were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with many nuts on it. They wanted to eat some nuts.
"Let's pick some nuts!" Lily said.
"OK!" Max said.
They ran to the tree and looked for nuts. They saw some big nuts and some thin nuts. Lily liked the big nuts. Max liked the thin nuts.
"I want this one!" Lily said, pointing to a big nut.
"No, I want it!" Max said, grabbing the same nut.
They pulled and pulled. The nut did not move. They got angry.
"Let go!" Lily said.
"No, you let go!" Max said.
They did not see a squirrel watching them. The squirrel was hungry. It saw a thin nut on the ground. It ran to the nut and picked it up. It ran away with the nut.
"Hey, look!" Lily said, letting go of the big nut.
"What?" Max said, letting go too.
They saw the squirrel with the thin nut. They saw the nut was a peanut. They liked peanuts.
"Wow, a peanut!" Lily said.
"Yummy, a peanut!" Max said.
They forgot about the big nut. They ran after the squirrel. They wanted the peanut.
"Give us the peanut!" Lily said.
"Please, give us the peanut!" Max said.
The squirrel did not listen. It ran faster. It climbed the tree. It hid the peanut in a hole.
"Bye bye, peanut!" the squirrel said.
Lily and Max stopped. They looked at the tree. They could not see the peanut. They felt sad.
"Aw, no peanut!" Lily said.
"Too bad, no peanut!" Max said.
They looked at each other. They felt sorry. They hugged.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I was mean." Max said.
"I'm sorry, Max. I was mean too." Lily said.
They smiled. They were friends again. They did not need the peanut. They had each other.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Lola and Jack. They were walking near a harbor, when Lola spotted a big, fat harbor seal. She exclaimed, "Oh my, look at that fat harbor seal! I want it to come with us!"
But Jack said, "No, I don't think it's a good idea. We should recommend we leave it alone, in case it's lost."
Lola was sad, but Jack was determined. He said, "We can come back another day and see if it's still here. Then we can help it find its way back home."
So, the two friends made their way along the harbor and watched the fat harbor seal out of sight. Lola didn't agree with Jack, but she accepted his recommendation.
The End.

The bees hovered around the flower, but it suddenly started to get dark outside. Buzz said to the other bees, "It's getting late, time to head back!" They all flew back to the hive, but not before Buzz said, "Let's come back here again tomorrow and try again!"
The next day, the bee friends returned to the big yellow flower. All of the bees quickly put their buzzers to work and tried their hardest to get the nectar from the flower. After many tries, Buzz finally managed to get the nectar out of the flower.
From then on, Buzz and her bee friends would go to the flower each day and try to get the nectar out. It became a regular happening for them and they even started sharing the nectar with other insects in the flower meadow.
In the end, Buzz and her bee friends were very happy and had a lot of fun!

Lila and Ben were twins who lived in a big house with their wealthy parents. They had many toys and books and clothes, but they did not like to share them with each other. They always fought over who got the best things and who had more space in their room.
One day, their mother told them to clean up their mess and put their things away. She said they had too much stuff and they should give some to the poor children who had nothing. Lila and Ben did not want to do that. They said they loved their stuff and they worked hard to get it.
Their mother was angry and said, "You are selfish and greedy. You do not know how to be kind and generous. You should be thankful for what you have and spread some joy to others. If you do not listen to me, I will take away all your stuff and give it away."
Lila and Ben were scared and sad. They did not want to lose their stuff, but they also did not want to share it. They looked at each other with angry eyes and started to argue.
"No, you give away your stuff. You have more than me," said Lila.
"No, you give away your stuff. You have better things than me," said Ben.
They pushed and pulled and shouted and cried. They made a bigger mess and broke some of their toys. Their mother heard the noise and came to their room. She saw the chaos and was very disappointed.
She said, "That's it. You have left me no choice. I will take away all your stuff and give it away. Maybe then you will learn to be grateful and generous."
She took a big bag and started to put their stuff in it. Lila and Ben were shocked and sorry. They realized they had been foolish and mean. They ran to their mother and hugged her.
They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We don't want to lose our stuff, but we don't want to be selfish and greedy either. We want to be kind and generous. Please don't take away our stuff. We will share it with each other and with the poor children. We will spread some joy to others. Please forgive us."
Their mother smiled and hugged them back. She said, "I'm glad you have learned your lesson. I'm proud of you for being willing to change. I won't take away your stuff, but I will help you sort out what you need and what you can give away. Let's do it together and make someone happy."
Lila and Ben nodded and smiled. They felt happy and relieved. They thanked their mother and followed her to the living room. They took out their stuff and decided what to keep and what to donate. They felt good about spreading some joy to others. They also learned to share and appreciate what they had. They became better twins and better children.

Anna liked to look at the stars at night. She had a book with pictures of the stars and planets. She learned that they were part of the universe, a big space with many things. She wanted to see more of the universe, so she asked her dad to buy her a telescope.
Dad was happy to see Anna's interest in the stars. He found a telescope online and ordered it for her. He told her it would come in a few days. Anna was very excited and counted the days.
When the telescope arrived, Anna and dad opened the box and set it up in the backyard. It was a big telescope, with a long tube and a round lens. Anna looked through the lens and saw the moon. It was bright and white, with many craters. She smiled and said, "Wow, dad, the moon is so beautiful!"
Dad smiled back and said, "Yes, it is. Do you want to see something else?" He moved the telescope and pointed it at another part of the sky. He said, "Look, Anna, that's Mars. It's a planet, like the Earth, but smaller and redder."
Anna looked through the lens and saw Mars. It was a small dot, with a faint pink color. She frowned and said, "Dad, that's not Mars. That's a pink star. Mars is bigger and redder. You made a mistake."
Dad laughed and said, "No, Anna, that's really Mars. It looks small and pink because it's very far away. The telescope makes it look closer, but not as big as the moon. Trust me, I know."
Anna did not trust dad. She thought he was lying to her. She felt angry and sad. She did not like the pink star. She wanted to see Mars. She started to cry and scream. She said, "No, no, no! That's not Mars! That's a pink star! You're wrong, dad! You're wrong!"
Anna panicked. She threw the telescope on the ground and ran into the house. She slammed the door and locked it. She did not want to talk to dad. She did not want to look at the stars. She did not like the universe. She only liked the moon.

Finally, they found the toy under a bush. Lily was so happy! She said, "Thank you, Mr. Raven!" The raven was happy too. From that day, Lily and the raven became best friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a different kind of orange on the ground. It was not like the other oranges he had seen before. Tim picked it up and showed it to his friend, Sue.
"Look, Sue! I found a different orange," Tim said. Sue looked at the orange and said, "Wow! That is different. Let's play with it."
They took turns rolling the orange on the ground. Suddenly, the orange started to run! Tim and Sue were very surprised. They had never seen an orange run before. They ran after the orange, trying to catch it.
The orange ran faster and faster. Tim and Sue could not catch it. They were very tired. Then, the orange stopped running. It opened up and there was a little toy inside. Tim and Sue laughed and played with the toy. They knew that this was a very special orange.

One day, a big truck came to deliver a big structure. The structure was a new playhouse for Tim and his friends. Tim was very happy and excited to have a new place to play.
Tim's friend, Sally, came over to see the new structure. She looked at it and said, "This is a stupid playhouse!" Tim felt sad because he liked the playhouse. He said, "I don't think it's stupid. Let's play in it together."
Sally agreed to play with Tim in the playhouse. They had a lot of fun playing together. After a while, Sally said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I was wrong. This playhouse is not stupid. It's fun!" Tim was happy that Sally liked the playhouse too. They played in the new structure all day long.

Once upon a time, there was an obedient dog named Spot. Spot loved to walk with his best friend, a little girl named Sue. They walked to the park every day. Sue held Spot's leash in her left hand, and they were always happy.
One sunny day, while they were walking, they saw a big box. Spot and Sue were very curious. They walked closer to the box and saw that it was moving! Sue and Spot did not know what was inside, but they were excited to find out.
Sue opened the box, and out jumped a little cat! Spot and Sue were very surprised. The cat was friendly and wanted to play with them. From that day on, Spot, Sue, and their new cat friend walked to the park together, and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to help his mom with her work. Every day, he would step into the kitchen and ask, "Can I help?"
One day, Tim's mom was very busy. She had a lot of work to do. She was making a big cake for a party. Tim wanted to help, but his mom said, "Not now, Tim. I have too much work."
Tim was sad. He wanted to help his mom. He thought, "I will show her I can help." So, Tim stepped up on a chair and tried to help. But, oh no! Tim dropped the eggs! They went splat on the floor.
Tim's mom was not happy. She said, "Tim, you made a mess. Now I have more work." Tim felt bad. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I just wanted to help."
Tim's mom gave him a hug. She said, "I know you want to help, but sometimes you need to wait." Tim was grateful for the hug. He learned that sometimes it's better to wait and not make more work for others.

They leave the rock and go to the flowers. They make a flower crown for each other. They put the crowns on their heads and smile. They look very pretty. They hug and say:
"We are the king and queen of the field!"

Inside the barn, there was a big birthday party! The animals had planned it for the farmer. They had balloons, cake, and games. The farmer was so happy. He did not need his whip after all. The animals had yelled because they were excited to show him the party. They all had a great time, and the farm was peaceful again.

Anna smiles. She feels proud. She values Ben's mom's kindness. She values Ben's friendship. She says, "Thank you, Ben's mom. You are very nice. I like you. And I like Ben. He is my best friend."
Ben smiles too. He feels proud. He values Anna's compliment. He values his mom's cooking. He says, "Thank you, Anna. You are very nice too. I like you. You are my best friend."
Anna and Ben hug. They finish their pasta. They are full and happy. They go to play some more. They have fun. They value their time together.

Once upon a time, there was a big tree. The tree was in a distant place, far away from other trees. The tree was very sad because it had no friends.
One day, a little bird came to the tree. The bird liked to tease the tree. The bird would fly around the tree and say, "You are too big and too far away from other trees! You will never have friends."
The tree felt sadder and sadder. But one day, something special happened. A group of little animals came to the tree. They saw the bird teasing the tree and they did not like it. They told the bird, "Stop teasing the tree! The tree is big and strong, and it gives us shade and a place to play."
The bird stopped teasing the tree. The tree was happy to have friends. The little animals played near the tree every day, and the tree was never sad again.

Max said to the cat, "Please don't take my motor. I love it so much!" The cat looked at Max and said, "I won't take your motor, but I want to play with you." Max thought about it and decided to let the cat play with him and his motor.
As they played together, Max and the cat became friends. They both promised to protect each other and their toys. From that day on, Max and the cat played together every day, and they were never anxious again.

Tommy liked to play with his toys in his room. He had a lot of toys, but his favorite was his crown. He liked to pretend he was a king and he could do whatever he wanted. He wore his crown all the time, even when he ate and slept.
One day, his mom told him he had to share his crown with his sister, Lily. She wanted to play princess and she needed a crown too. Tommy did not like that. He did not want to share his crown. He said no and ran to his room. He was very grumpy.
Lily followed him and knocked on his door. She asked him nicely to share his crown. She said they could play together and have fun. Tommy still said no and locked his door. He hid his crown under his pillow and lay down on his bed.
But then, something strange happened. His crown started to glow and make a noise. Tommy was scared and curious. He lifted his pillow and saw his crown. It was not his crown anymore. It was a different crown. It was bigger and shinier and had jewels on it. It was a magic crown.
The magic crown spoke to Tommy. It said it was the crown of a fairy king. It said it could grant wishes and do magic. It said it was looking for a new owner who was kind and generous. It said it did not like Tommy because he was grumpy and selfish. It said it would disappear and find someone else.
Tommy was shocked and sad. He wanted to keep the magic crown. He wanted to make wishes and do magic. He realized he was wrong to be grumpy and selfish. He wished he could share his crown with Lily and play with her. He said he was sorry and he asked the magic crown to stay.
But it was too late. The magic crown said goodbye and disappeared. Tommy was left with his old crown. He felt sorry and lonely. He opened his door and saw Lily. She was still waiting for him. She smiled and hugged him. She said she forgave him and she still wanted to play with him. She said they could take turns with his crown. Tommy smiled and hugged her back. He said he was sorry and he wanted to play with her too. He said they could share his crown. They went to play together and had fun. Tommy was not grumpy anymore. He was happy.

"Who is it?"
"It's me, Daisy!" Daisy answered.
Her grandmother opened the door and Daisy could see that she was wearing an apron over her coat. "Oh, hello Daisy!" her grandmother said with a big smile. "I'm so glad you're here, come inside and have a taste of the delicious food I'm making!"
Daisy stepped inside and couldn't help but smile as she enjoyed the delicious smells! She couldn't wait to try her grandmother's cooking!

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and has sharp teeth. It barks loud.
"Look, a scary pet!" Tom says.
"Let's go away!" Sam says.
But Tom is brave. He says, "I dare you to touch the dog. I will give you a candy if you do."
Sam is scared. He does not want to touch the dog. But he wants the candy. He says, "OK, I will try."
He walks slowly to the dog. The dog sees him and growls. Sam is very scared. He wants to run away. But he thinks of the candy.
He reaches out his hand to touch the dog. The dog snaps at him and bites his finger. Sam screams and runs back to Tom.
"Ow, ow, ow! The dog bit me!" Sam cries.
Tom feels sorry for Sam. He says, "I'm sorry, Sam. That was a bad dare. Here, have the candy. And let's go to the nurse. She will make your finger better."
Sam takes the candy and nods. He says, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. But next time, let's not play with scary pets."

Sarah replied: "I found this orange magazine, Mommy. It's so pretty!"
Sarah's mother smiled and said, "That's so nice, Sarah. You manage to find such pretty things. Why don't you keep this magazine for yourself."
Sarah was so happy, she hugged the orange magazine tightly and ran off to play with it. She had a wonderful time looking at all the orange pictures and reading the stories that were in the magazine. She kept the magazine forever as a special treasure.

Bob and his best friend, Lucy, had a big problem. They could see some bees buzzing around a pink hive near their house. The hive was buzzing and made a lot of noise.
One day, Bob said to Lucy, "We need to solve this problem. Let's find a way to move the hive away!"
Lucy had an idea. She said, "Let's ask my dad for help! He knows a lot about animals and I'm sure he can help us to move the pink hive away from our house."
So Bob and Lucy went up to Lucy's dad and told him about the buzzing hive. He smiled and said, "I can help you both. I think the best way to solve this is to get the bees some new flowers to eat. That way, the bees can find another place to build their hive."
Bob and Lucy were very happy. The next day, they went out together and found some nice, colourful flowers for the bees. The bees were very happy and soon left their old hive to build a new one somewhere else.
Bob and Lucy were relieved and smiled, happy to have solved the problem.

While skipping, Tim saw a big rock. He heard a tiny voice say, "Hello! Who are you?" Tim looked around and saw another ant named Sam. Tim said, "Hi! I am Tim. I am lonely and want a friend to play with. Can we be friends?"
Sam was happy and said, "Yes! I am lonely too. Let's play together!" But, as they started to play, a mean bug came and wanted to play too. The mean bug did not want to share and tried to push Tim away. Tim felt sad.
Sam saw this and said, "No, that is not nice! We can all play together and be friends." The mean bug thought about it and said, "Okay, I will be nice and share." So, Tim, Sam, and the mean bug played together and became good friends. Tim was not lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a humble cat named Mimi. Mimi had a big dream. She wanted to have the power to fly high in the sky like a bird. Every day, she would sit and watch the birds fly over her head, wishing she could join them.
One day, Mimi met a wise old owl who saw her watching the birds. The owl asked, "Why are you so sad, little cat?" Mimi replied, "I want to fly like the birds, but I don't have the power." The wise old owl thought for a moment and said, "You may not have the power to fly, but you have other powers. You can climb trees and catch mice. Be happy with what you can do."
Mimi realized that the wise old owl was right. She may not have the power to fly, but she was still a special cat. From that day on, Mimi was happy with her own powers and continued to dream big. She knew that even a humble cat like her could do great things.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who loved to play together every day. They were brother and sister, named Max and Rachel.
Max wanted a nice, fancy gift for his friend, so he looked around until he saw the perfect thing. It was a bright, blue ball.
He offered it to Rachel, and she smiled. But then she asked, “What if I want something else?”
Max scowled. “Why would you want something else? This is the best!”
Rachel was not sure what to say. She replied, “Let’s not quarrel, okay?”
Max said, “Okay…”
Rachel thanked him for the nice gift. “Wait until you see what I have for you!” she said.
Max raised an eyebrow. “What is it?”
Rachel smiled and said, “You’ll see!”
The next day, Rachel gave Max a fancy toy fire truck. Max’s eyes lit up and he shouted, “This is so much better than a blue ball!”
Rachel had been right, after all.

Benny was a big dog with thick fur. He liked to run and play in the park with his friends. But he also had a problem. He had many fleas in his fur. The fleas made him itch and scratch all the time. They also bit him and made him feel sick.
One day, Benny met a new dog in the park. Her name was Lila and she had shiny fur and bright eyes. Benny wanted to be her friend. He ran to her and said, "Hi, I am Benny. Do you want to play with me?"
Lila looked at him and saw the fleas jumping on his fur. She felt sorry for him, but she also felt scared. She said, "No, thank you. I do not want to play with you. You have too many fleas. They are bad for you and for me. You should go to the vet and get rid of them."
Benny felt sad and angry. He said, "That is not fair. You do not know me. You do not know how nice I am. You should not judge me by my fleas. They are not my fault. They do not permit me to be happy."
Lila said, "I am sorry, but I have to be careful. My mom told me that fleas can make me sick too. They can give me worms and rashes and fever. They can also make me lose my fur. I do not want that. You should listen to your mom too. She wants you to be healthy and clean. She wants you to go to the vet and get a flea treatment. Then you can be happy and make more friends."
Benny thought about what Lila said. He realized that she was right. He did not like his fleas either. He wanted to be healthy and clean too. He wanted to make more friends and have fun. He said, "You are right, Lila. I will go to the vet and get a flea treatment. Thank you for telling me the truth. Maybe we can play together another day."
Lila smiled and said, "You are welcome, Benny. I hope you feel better soon. Maybe we can play together another day. Goodbye for now."
Benny said goodbye and ran back to his mom. He told her what Lila said and asked her to take him to the vet. His mom was happy and proud of him. She said, "Good boy, Benny. You are very brave and smart. You learned a good lesson today. You learned that you should take care of yourself and respect others. You learned that fleas are not good for you or for anyone. You learned that being clean and healthy is important for your happiness and friendship."
Benny nodded and wagged his tail. He felt happy and hopeful. He knew that he would soon be free of his fleas and ready to play with Lila and his other friends. He knew that he had a good mom and a good heart. He knew that he was a good dog.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park and share their toys. One day, they found a shiny copper coin on the ground. They were very happy and decided to keep it.
"Let's marry with this coin," Lily said. "We can be a family and have a lot of fun."
"OK," Ben said. "But how do we marry?"
Lily thought for a moment. She remembered seeing her aunt and uncle marry at a big party. They wore nice clothes and had a cake and rings.
"We need rings," she said. "And a cake. And nice clothes."
They looked around the park. They saw some flowers, some leaves, some berries and some mud. They used the flowers and leaves to make rings for their fingers. They used the berries and mud to make a cake on a rock. They used their scarves and hats to make nice clothes.
They were ready to marry. They stood in front of the rock and held hands. They said, "I marry you, you marry me, we are happy as can be."
They put the rings on their fingers and the copper coin in their pocket. They smiled and kissed. They ate the cake and played some more.
They did not see the grumpy old man who was watching them. He was the owner of the coin. He had dropped it by mistake. He was angry and wanted it back.
He walked over to them and shouted, "Hey, you little thieves! Give me back my coin!"
Lily and Ben were scared. They did not know what to do. They hugged each other and cried.
"Please, mister, don't be mad," Lily said. "We just wanted to marry. We didn't know it was your coin."
The grumpy old man looked at them. He saw their rings, their cake, their clothes and their tears. He felt sorry for them. He remembered when he was young and happy and in love.
He sighed and said, "Oh, all right. You can keep the coin. But don't steal again. And don't marry so young. You have a lot to learn and enjoy."
He turned and walked away. He was still grumpy, but a little less.
Lily and Ben thanked him and said sorry. They were relieved and happy. They decided to keep the coin as a souvenir of their first marry. They also decided to wait until they were older to marry again. They were still best friends. They liked to play in the park and share their toys.

Sam says, "Tim took my car. He is naughty."

Tim says, "But, Mom, I want to play with it. He has his jet. He does not need his car."
Mom says, "Sam, do you want to share your car with Tim? Maybe you can take turns. That is kind."
Sam thinks for a moment. He says, "OK, Mom. I will share my car with Tim. But he has to be careful. He can not break it."
Mom says, "That is very good, Sam. You are obedient and generous. Tim, are you sorry for taking Sam's car?"
Tim says, "Yes, Mom. I am sorry. I will be careful with his car. And I will let him play with my jet. That is fair."
Mom says, "That is very good, Tim. You are obedient and sorry. Now, boys, you can play together nicely. But remember, you have to clean up your toys when you are done. That is the rule."
Tim and Sam say, "OK, Mom. We will clean up our toys. Thank you for helping us."
Mom says, "You are welcome, boys. I love you both. Have fun."

"What do you think you are doing, little rat?" said the voice.
Startled and unsure, the rat stammered, "I, um, I was just trying to see what is in this box."
The voice replied, "Sometimes trying to take a shortcut can be very dangerous, little rat. You never know what is inside the box, so it is better to go your own way and find a better way to get things done."
The rat understood the lesson and decided to go his own way. From then on, the rat stopped trying to open the box and went looking for his own food.
The moral of the story is that sometimes the most ordinary things can be the most valuable if you take your time and do things the right way. Shortcuts can be tempting, but they can lead to difficult consequences.

"Hello, Lily! Hello, Ben! Thank you for your kind words!" the robin and the daffodil say.
"Can we ask you a question?" Ben says.
"Sure, what do you want to know?" the robin and the daffodil say.
"We want to know how you are so successful. How do you grow and sing so well?" Lily says.
The robin and the daffodil smile. They say, "We are successful because we follow the seasons. We know when to rest and when to work. We know when to eat and when to share. We know when to be quiet and when to be loud. We listen to the sun and the rain and the wind. They help us grow and sing."
Lily and Ben nod. They say, "That makes sense. We want to be successful too. We want to learn from you. Can you teach us how to follow the seasons?"

Lily and Ben follow the robin and the daffodil. They hope to see more birds and flowers. They hope to be successful like them. They are excited to learn from the seasons.

Once upon a time, there was a selfish bear who lived in a forest. Every morning, the bear would stay in his cozy mattress and sleep until noon.
One day, when the bear woke up, he heard a knock on the door. He opened the door and there stood a little rabbit. 'Hello,' said the rabbit, 'I have no place to sleep. Could I please stay in your mattress?'
The bear was feeling very selfish, and said 'No, sorry! This mattress is for me, not for you.'
The rabbit was feeling sad, so he started to cry. 'Please, I just need one night. I'm so tired and I don't know where else to go.'
The bear thought for a moment and then said 'Alright, you can stay in the mattress, but only tonight, and only if you promise to never knock on my door again!'
The little rabbit nodded eagerly and the bear let him have his mattress for the night. The next morning, the rabbit was very grateful and he thanked the bear for being kind. From then on, the bear realized that it was better to be generous and share than to be selfish.

They took the robot to their room and looked for parts. They found some buttons for eyes, some spoons for arms and some cans for legs. They used tape and glue to stick them to the robot. They were very proud of their work. They turned on the robot and waited for it to talk.
But the robot did not talk. It only made a loud beep. Jill and Jack tried to talk to it, but it did not answer. They wondered why the robot was deaf. They looked at the back of the robot and saw a switch. They flipped the switch and hoped the robot would hear them.
But the robot did not hear them. It only made a louder beep. Jill and Jack covered their ears and ran out of the room. The robot was too noisy and scary. They did not want to play with it anymore. They wanted to have lunch and forget about the robot.
They went to the kitchen and saw their mom. She was making sandwiches and soup. She smiled and said, "Hi, kids. How was your morning? Did you have fun with your toys?"
Jill and Jack nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We had fun. But we also found a broken robot and tried to repair it. But it did not work. It was deaf and noisy. We left it in our room."
Mom looked surprised and said, "A broken robot? Where did you find it?"
Jill and Jack pointed to the trash and said, "There, mom. We thought we could fix it and make it our friend. But we couldn't."
Mom frowned and said, "Oh, no. That was not a toy. That was dad's old alarm clock. He threw it away because it was broken and annoying. He said he would buy a new one. You should not have taken it. It could be dangerous."
Jill and Jack felt sorry and said, "We're sorry, mom. We did not know. We thought it was a robot. We wanted to repair it and make it our friend. But we don't like it anymore. Can we have lunch now?"
Mom nodded and said, "Yes, you can have lunch now. But after lunch, you have to go back to your room and turn off the alarm clock. And then you have to put it back in the trash. And next time, ask me before you take something from the trash. OK?"
Jill and Jack agreed and said, "OK, mom. We will do that. Thank you for lunch. We love you."
Mom hugged them and said, "I love you too. Now, enjoy your lunch. And be careful with the alarm clock. It might beep again."

Mom sighed. She knew they were sorry. But she also knew they could not fix the vase. It was too broken. She said, "No, you can't fix it. It is gone. You should not touch the furniture that is old and expensive. It is not for playing. It is for looking and remembering. Do you understand?"
Sara and Tom nodded. They understood. They hugged mom and said, "We are sorry, mom. We love you. We love grandma too. We will not touch the furniture again."
Mom hugged them back. She said, "I love you too. I know you did not mean to break the vase. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Now, let's clean up this mess and then we can read a book together."

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They gave him a name: Frosty.
"Hello, Frosty!" Sara said. "You are our friend. We like you very much."
"Yes, we do!" Ben said. "You are very nice and funny. Do you like us too?"
Frosty did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot nose.
But then the sun came out. It was very bright and warm. The snow started to melt.
"Oh no!" Sara said. "Frosty is melting! He is getting smaller and smaller. He will be gone soon."
"That's not fair!" Ben said. "We want Frosty to stay with us. We don't want him to melt. What can we do?"
They thought hard. They tried to move Frosty to a shady place. They tried to cover him with more snow. They tried to fan him with their mittens. But nothing worked. Frosty kept melting.
Sara and Ben felt very sad. They hugged Frosty and said goodbye.
"Goodbye, Frosty!" Sara said. "We will miss you. You were a good friend."
"Goodbye, Frosty!" Ben said. "We will remember you. You made us happy."
Frosty did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot nose. Then he was gone.
Sara and Ben looked at the pile of snow where Frosty used to be. They felt a big hole in their stomachs. They felt very gloomy.
They went back to their house. They told their mom what happened. Their mom hugged them and said:
"I'm sorry, Sara and Ben. I know you loved Frosty. But don't be too sad. Frosty was made of snow, and snow always melts when it gets warm. That's how it is. But you can always make another snowman when it snows again. And you can always keep Frosty in your hearts. He will always be your friend."
Sara and Ben nodded. They felt a little better. They thanked their mom and went to their room. They drew a picture of Frosty and hung it on their wall. They smiled and said:
"See you soon, Frosty!"

Lily and Sam thought hard. They did not know the answer.

The vendor made a funny face and a sad sound. He squeezed the clown balloon and it made a honk sound.
Lily and Sam laughed. They thought the joke was funny.
"That was a good joke!" Sam said.
"Thank you. Do you want a balloon?" the vendor asked.
"Yes, please!" Lily and Sam said.

Once upon a time, there lived a girl called Ann. She loved jewelry and always set it carefully on her dresser. One day, Ann decided to set her favorite necklace, a shiny green jewel, around her neck.
At that moment, Mama walked into the room. Seeing Ann's necklace, she became very angry. She said sternly, "Ann, why are you wearing my jewelry without asking?"
Ann, feeling very miserable, hung her head down. She apologetically replied, "I'm sorry Mama, I just wanted to set the necklace around my neck because it was so pretty."
Mama let out a long and heavy sigh. She calmly said, "It's alright Ann. Next time, please only set the jewelry on the dresser and not on yourself. Can you promise me that?"
Ann nodded her head and said, "I promise, Mama."
Mama smiled, relieved that her daughter had learnt her lesson. Ann was happy too, and she gave her Mama a big hug. From that day on, Ann only set her jewelry on the dresser, never on her body.

"But it is so loud and scary!" Sara said.
"Sometimes things that are loud are not scary. Sometimes they are gentle and kind. Like a lion's roar, or a drum's beat, or a friend's laugh. You just have to listen with your heart, not your ears." Mom said.

So the bird spread its wings, closed its eyes, and jumped up into the sky. And, guess what? It flew! The bird was so happy that it flew and flew.
The guard watched the bird as it flew around in circles and stretched its wings. The bird thanked the guard for teaching it how to fly.
The guard smiled, knowing that the bird was now free to fly wherever it wanted.

One day, a little fish named Fin was swimming in the sea. He saw an oyster on the sea floor. Fin was very curious and wanted to know what was inside the oyster. He thought, "I wonder if there is something fun inside."
Fin swam closer to the oyster, but his friend, the wise old turtle, stopped him. The turtle said, "Be careful, Fin. Oysters can be dangerous. They have sharp shells that can hurt you." Fin was scared, but he still wanted to see what was inside the oyster.
The wise old turtle saw that Fin was still curious. So, he found a safe way to open the oyster. Inside, they found a beautiful pearl. Fin was very happy and thanked the wise old turtle for helping him. The turtle said, "Remember, always ask for help when something seems dangerous." Fin learned that it is important to be careful and ask for help when he is not sure about something.

The moral of the story is to always listen to your friends and work together to make things better.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a little girl named Lucy. She had a big tree in her backyard. One day, she saw that the tree was not happy. It was starting to rot and the leaves were falling. Lucy felt helpless and sad for the tree.
Lucy went to her mom and said, "Mommy, the tree is not happy. It is rotting. What can we do?" Her mom replied, "Let's ask the wise old owl who lives in the forest. He will know what to do."
So, Lucy and her mom went to the forest to find the wise old owl. They found him sitting on a branch. Lucy said, "Mr. Owl, our tree is rotting and we feel helpless. Can you help us?" The wise old owl thought for a moment and said, "To save your tree, you must sing a song of peace and love. The tree will feel better and stop rotting."
Lucy and her mom went back home and sang a song of peace and love to the tree. Slowly, the tree started to feel better. The rot went away and the leaves grew back. Lucy and her mom were happy that they could help the tree. From that day on, the tree and Lucy's family lived in peace and happiness.

Jimmy was scared, but he mustered up the courage to answer. "I wanted to join in the shower," he stammered.
The voice laughed. "Are you sure about that? You don't look like you belong here," the voice said.
Jimmy was too scared to answer, so he just nodded his head. Suddenly he heard a sinister chuckle. "Too bad," the voice said. "Because now you have to join us forever!"
Jimmy started to cry, but it was too late. He was now a member of the shower forever. Jimmy was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a poor farmer called Paul. Every day, he worked hard in his fields trying to grow vegetables for his family. One day, he realized that his vegetables were not growing very well. He was sad and decided to ask his neighbour for advice.
When Paul approached his neighbour, the neighbour smiled and said, "I have a recommendation for you, Paul. Plant some blueberries in that patch. They love the sun and should thrive in the summer heat."
Paul thanked his neighbour and ventured to buy some blueberry seeds. He followed the neighbour's advice and planted the seeds in the patch. The very next day, the blueberry plants began to grow and soon Paul was harvesting lots of delicious, sweet blueberries!
He was so happy and every day, he recommended blueberries to his neighbours. They were all thankful for the advice and soon they had blueberry plants too! The poor farmer and his neighbours enjoyed many delicious blueberries from then on.
The end.

"Look at me, I am so pretty!" she said to her friends. "Do you want to polish your feathers too?"
But her friends were scared. They saw a big fox hiding behind a bush. The fox was hungry and wanted to eat the geese.
"No, thank you, Gaby. We want to stay away from the pond. The fox might catch us!" they said.
Gaby was not afraid of the fox. She was brave and smart. She had a plan.
"Come on, don't be silly. The fox is too far away. He can't see us. And if he comes closer, I will honk loudly and scare him away. Trust me, it will be fun!" she said.
She smiled and winked at her friends. They did not know that she had seen the fox too. She wanted to trick him and save her friends.
She pretended to polish her feathers more and more. She made a lot of noise and splashed the water. She hoped the fox would hear her and come closer.
The fox did hear her. He thought she was an easy meal. He crept out of the bush and ran towards the pond.
But Gaby was ready. As soon as she saw him, she honked as loud as she could. She flapped her wings and flew away. She also honked to warn her friends. They followed her and flew away too.
The fox was surprised and angry. He missed his chance to eat the geese. He growled and went back to the bush.
Gaby and her friends were safe and happy. They praised Gaby for her bravery and cleverness.
"Gaby, you are the best! You polished your feathers and fooled the fox. You saved us all!" they said.
Gaby blushed and thanked them. She was glad they were all okay.
She said, "You are welcome, my friends. But remember, polishing your feathers is not as important as sticking together. We are stronger as a flock. And we are always brave!"

But then, Lily saw a boat that was different from all the others. It was a boat with a big hole in it. It looked old and sad. Lily felt sorry for the boat. She wanted to help it. She asked her dad if they could go to the boat and fix it.
Her dad said no. He said the boat was not theirs and it was too dangerous. He said they had to go home soon. Lily was very angry and sad. She started to cry. She did not want to leave the boat alone.
Tom saw Lily cry. He did not like to see his sister cry. He wanted to make her happy. He had an idea. He ran to a shop near the port and bought a sticker. The sticker had a picture of a boat with a smile. He ran back to Lily and gave her the sticker. He said, "Look, Lily, this is a boat that is happy. You can put it on your boat at home and pretend it is the boat from the port. Then the boat will not be lonely and you will not be sad."
Lily looked at the sticker. She smiled. She liked the sticker. She hugged Tom and said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. You made me happy." She put the sticker on her boat and held it in her arms.
They went home with their dad. They played with their boats and pretended they were sailors and explorers. They were happy. The end.

Sarah was frightened, but she was still brave. She stayed rooted to the spot and said firmly, "No, I won't leave."
The man looked angry, but he could tell that Sarah was not going to go away. Eventually he muttered something then went back inside his home. Sarah remained where she was until she was sure that the old man was gone. Then she ran home and told her dad all about her brave adventure.

Lily was a little girl who liked to eat candy. She ate candy every day, even before breakfast and after dinner. She did not like to brush her teeth or drink water. She only wanted candy.
One day, Lily had a bad toothache. She cried and held her mouth. Her mom took her to the dentist. The dentist looked at her teeth and said, "Lily, you have a cavity. Your tooth is rotting because you eat too much candy and do not brush your teeth. I have to fix your tooth, but it will hurt a little."
Lily was scared and sad. She did not want the dentist to fix her tooth. She wished she had listened to her mom and brushed her teeth. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I don't want to eat candy anymore. I want to have healthy teeth."
Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm glad you learned your lesson, Lily. Candy is okay sometimes, but not all the time. You have to eat other foods that are good for you, like fruits and vegetables. And you have to brush your teeth every day and drink water. That will keep your teeth strong and clean."
Lily nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will do that. Can we go home now?"
The dentist said, "Yes, you can go home, but you have to rest and take your medicine. Your tooth will be sore for a while. You can eat some soup or yogurt, but no candy or hard foods. And you have to come back next week for a check-up."
Lily agreed and thanked the dentist. She went home with her mom and went to bed. She felt hungry, but she did not want candy. She wanted some soup and a banana. She realized that candy was not worth losing her teeth. She decided to take better care of her teeth from now on. She learned that too much candy can make your teeth rot.

Lily and Ben love to bounce on the big trampoline in their backyard. They bounce high and low, up and down, and laugh and shout. They play games like tag and catch and make funny faces.
One day, they see that the leaves on the trees are changing color. They are red and yellow and orange and brown. Lily and Ben think they are pretty. They ask their mom what is happening.
Mom says, "It is a new season. It is called fall. The leaves change color and fall off the trees. Then it gets colder and we wear warm clothes."
Lily and Ben want to know more. They ask, "What are the other seasons?"
Mom says, "There are four seasons in a year. After fall, there is winter. It is the coldest season. Sometimes it snows and we can make snowmen and snowballs. Then there is spring. It is the warmest season. The flowers bloom and the birds sing. And then there is summer. It is the hottest season. We can swim and eat ice cream and play outside a lot."
Lily and Ben think that all the seasons sound fun. They say, "Thank you, mom, for telling us about the seasons. Can we bounce on the trampoline some more?"
Mom says, "Yes, you can. But be careful and have fun. You are very busy bouncers!"

One day, Jack was walking in the park. He saw a radio on the ground. Jack wanted to play with it, so he pulled it towards him. Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from inside the radio.
"Hello!" said the voice.
Jack was very surprised. He said, "Hello!"
The voice said, "I'm an honest radio. I will tell you the truth, if you ask me a question. Do you have a question for me?"
Jack was very excited. He said, "Yes, I do! How many stars are in the sky?"
The voice replied, "That's a difficult question. We can count them together; let's go outside and look!"
Jack and the radio went outside and looked up at the night sky. They counted all the stars they could see. When they were finished, Jack was so happy. He said, "Thank you, honest radio! You told me the truth!"
And the radio replied, "You're very welcome, Jack!"

Jill and Tom are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom. One day, they see a big, modern slide. It is shiny and blue and has a tunnel.
"Wow, look at that slide!" Jill says. "Can we go on it, mom?"
"Sure, but be careful. It is very high and fast," mom says.
Jill and Tom run to the slide. Jill goes first. She climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. She slides down very fast and goes through the tunnel. She is happy and laughs.
Tom goes next. He climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. He slides down very fast and goes through the tunnel. He is scared and screams.
"Help, help! It is too dark and too fast!" Tom screams.
Mom hears Tom scream and runs to the slide. She waits for him at the end of the tunnel. She hugs him and says, "It's okay, Tom. You are safe. You are brave."
Tom stops screaming and cries. He says, "I don't like the slide. It is too modern. I want to go home."
Mom says, "Okay, let's go home. But first, do you want a treat?"
She takes out a lime from her bag. She cuts it in half and gives one half to Jill and one half to Tom.
"Try this. It is a lime. It is sour and green," mom says.
Jill and Tom take a bite of the lime. They make funny faces and say, "Ew, ew! It is too sour!"
They spit out the lime and laugh.
Mom laughs too and says, "Maybe you don't like the lime either. How about some ice cream?"
Jill and Tom say, "Yes, yes! We like ice cream!"
They go to the ice cream truck and get some ice cream. They lick their ice cream and smile.
They forget about the slide and the lime. They are happy.

One day, while Amy was hugging the tree, a squirrel came down from the branches. The squirrel said, "Hello, Amy! Do you like the tree too?" Amy smiled and said, "Yes, I love the tree! It's my friend!" The squirrel and Amy became friends, and they all played together in the forest every day.

One day, a little bird was flying in the sky. The bird saw a big tree and wanted to sit on it. But a rude cat was sitting on the tree. The cat did not want to share the tree with the bird.
The bird said, "Can I sit on the tree with you?" The cat did not like to share and said, "No, go away!" The bird was sad and blinked its eyes. It wanted to find a way to sit on the tree.
The bird had an idea. It flew up and found a stick. The bird dropped the stick near the cat. The cat loved to play with sticks. The cat jumped down to play with the stick. The bird quickly flew to the tree and sat on it. The cat was too busy playing to notice. The bird was happy that it could sit on the tree and enjoy the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a big wardrobe. The wardrobe was very pretty. It had many clothes inside. The clothes were all different colors. The wardrobe was in a room with a little girl named Sally.
One day, Sally was very impatient. She wanted to wear a new dress. She opened the wardrobe, but she did not know how to pick a dress. She was sad.
Then, a kind fairy came to help Sally. The fairy wanted to teach her how to choose a dress. The fairy said, "Sally, be patient. Look at all the colors. Pick the one you like best." Sally listened to the fairy. She took her time and picked a pretty blue dress.
Sally learned to be patient. She thanked the fairy. From that day on, Sally always took her time when choosing her clothes. She was happy, and the wardrobe was happy too. The moral of the story is to be patient and learn from others.

Ben and Mia like to play with their toys in the living room. They have many toys, but their favorite is the train set. The train set has a big iron engine and many cars that can hook together. The engine can make sounds and move on the tracks.
One day, Ben and Mia are playing with the train set when Mia wants to make the engine go faster. She pushes a button on the engine and it starts to move very fast on the tracks. Ben is scared and tries to stop the engine. He grabs the engine and pulls it off the tracks. But the engine is too heavy and Ben drops it on the floor. The engine makes a loud noise and breaks into pieces.
"Ben, you broke the engine!" Mia cries. "Now we can't play with the train set anymore!"
"I'm sorry, Mia, I didn't mean to break it!" Ben says. "I just wanted to stop it from going too fast. It was too rough for the tracks."
Mia is very angry and sad. She picks up the pieces of the engine and hugs them. She doesn't want to talk to Ben. Ben feels bad and doesn't know what to do. He wishes he could fix the engine and make Mia happy again.
He looks around the living room and sees a box of tools. He remembers that his dad sometimes uses tools to fix things. He thinks maybe he can use the tools to fix the engine. He gets the box of tools and brings it to Mia.
"Mia, can I try to fix the engine?" he asks. "Maybe I can make it work again."
Mia looks at Ben and sees that he is sorry. She thinks maybe he can fix the engine. She nods and gives him the pieces of the engine.
"Thank you, Mia," Ben says. "I'll be very careful and gentle. I'll try my best to fix the engine."
Ben and Mia sit on the floor and use the tools to fix the engine. They work together and help each other. They find the parts that fit and glue them back. They test the engine and see that it can still make sounds and move on the tracks. They are very happy and proud.
"Ben, you fixed the engine!" Mia says. "You are very smart and kind. I'm sorry I was angry at you."
"I'm sorry I broke the engine, Mia," Ben says. "You are very brave and sweet. I'm glad we are friends again."
Ben and Mia hug and smile. They put the engine and the cars back on the tracks and play with the train set. They have fun and share their toys. They are happy and love each other.

One day, a little boy named Tim had a nosy pet cat. The cat liked to look at everything. Tim and the cat played all day. They were very happy.
One day, they heard a loud roar. Tim asked, "What was that?" The cat said, "I don't know, let's go see!" They walked to the big tree and saw a big lion. The lion was sad.
Tim said, "Why are you sad, Mr. Lion?" The lion said, "I lost my family. I don't know where they are." Tim and the cat wanted to help. They looked and looked. Then, they found the lion's family. The lion was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and cat!" They all played together and became good friends.

Once there was a girl named Ruby. She was three years old and very brave. One day, Ruby asked her mum to do something special. Her mum said she had a surprise for Ruby and asked her to go outside.
So Ruby went outside and saw something that made her very scared. There was a big monster waiting for her! It said, "I have a task for you, Ruby. You must be very brave."
Ruby was very impatient. She wanted to go back inside but the monster said if she did not do the task then it would come inside and scare her mum. So, Ruby reluctantly agreed to do the task.
When she finished, the monster said, "Thank you for being so brave, Ruby. Now I am going to go and scare your mum." With that, the monster disappeared.
Ruby ran back inside to warn her mum but it was too late. The monster had already scared her away. Ruby was so sad that she had lost her mum. She learned a valuable lesson that day - don't do tasks for monsters!

The bug said, "Hello, pretty flower! Can I crawl on you and smell you?" The flower smiled and said, "Of course, bug! I would love for you to crawl on me and smell me!"
The bug had a great day crawling on the flowers and smelling them. He was very happy to have met such nice flowers in the row. The bug went to sleep that night, dreaming of the large, pretty flowers and the fun he had crawling on them.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Mia went to visit her grandma. When she got there, she saw many boxes in her grandma's room. Mia asked, "Grandma, what are these?" Her grandma said, "These are my unique things from my past. Let's unpack them together."
