Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Tom had a big case full of cars and trucks. Lily had a small case full of dolls and dresses. They liked to share their toys, but sometimes they fought over them.
"Can I play with your red car, Tom?" Lily asked.
"No, it's mine. You have your dolls," Tom said.
"But I want to try it. Please, Tom, just for a little bit," Lily begged.
Tom sighed. He liked his red car, but he also wanted to be nice to his sister. He decided to let her play with it, but only if she gave him something in return.
"Okay, fine. You can play with my red car, but you have to give me your pink dress," he said.
Lily frowned. She liked her pink dress, but she also wanted to play with the red car. She agreed to the trade, but only for a little while.
They swapped their toys and started to play. Lily zoomed the red car around the floor. Tom put the pink dress on one of his trucks. They were having fun, until they heard their mom call them for lunch.
"Time to eat, kids. Put away your toys and come to the table," their mom said.
Tom and Lily hurried to put their toys back in their cases. But they made a mistake. They put the wrong toys in the wrong cases. Tom put the red car in Lily's case, and Lily put the pink dress in Tom's case. They didn't notice, because they were hungry and wanted to eat.
They ran to the kitchen and sat down at the table. Their mom gave them sandwiches and juice. They ate and talked about their morning.
"Did you have fun playing with your toys?" their mom asked.
"Yes, we did. We shared and traded and played nicely," Tom said.
"That's good. I'm proud of you. What did you trade?" their mom asked.
Tom smiled. He was about to tell her about the red car and the pink dress, when he saw his dad come in. His dad had a big smile on his face. He was holding Tom's case.
"Hey, buddy. I saw your case in the living room. I thought I'd bring it to your room. You have some cool toys in there. Look what I found," his dad said.
He opened the case and pulled out the pink dress. He held it up and laughed.
"Wow, Tom. You like to play dress-up, huh? Is this your favorite outfit?" he teased.
Tom felt his face turn red. He was embarrassed. He didn't want his dad to see the pink dress. He didn't want his dad to think he liked girly things. He wanted his dad to think he was tough and cool.
He looked at Lily. She looked scared. She knew she had put the pink dress in Tom's case. She knew she had made a big mistake. She wanted to tell the truth, but she was afraid of getting in trouble.
Tom and Lily didn't know what to say. They felt bad and sad. They wished they had put their toys in the right cases. They wished they had been more careful. They wished they could balance their toys and their feelings. But they couldn't. They had messed up. And they didn't know how to fix it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Paul. He was a very stubborn young boy.
One day, Paul's mother gave him an important mission. She told him to go to the dark chamber in the back of the house and remember to open the door three times.
Paul was scared, so he asked his mother: "Mommy, why do I have to go to the chamber? It is so dark in there!"
His mother smiled and said: "We have a very special surprise for you in the chamber, Paul. Remember not to forget to open the door three times, okay?"
So Paul walked bravely down to the dark chamber and opened the door three times. He was shocked to see a beautiful birthday cake sitting inside the chamber.
"Mommy, did you remember my birthday?" he asked with a big smile on his face.
His mother laughed and nodded. She said: "We will always remember your birthday, Paul. Now, let's go and enjoy the cake!"
Paul was so happy that he hugged his mom tightly, feeling grateful for the surprise. From then on, Paul never forgot to open the door three times whenever he went to the chamber.

One day, a big flame lived in a small forest. The flame was very selfish. It liked to show how big and strong it was. It would burn all the trees and plants around it. The animals in the forest did not like the flame.
A small bird said to the flame, "Please stop being selfish. You are hurting the forest and all the animals. We need the trees to live." The flame did not care. It wanted to show how big and strong it was, so it kept burning more trees.
The animals in the forest were very sad. They had no place to live. One day, the wind came and blew the flame far away. The flame was now alone. It had no trees to burn and no animals to show how big and strong it was. The flame was sad, but it was too late. The forest was gone, and the animals had to find a new home.

Sara and Ben were having lunch with their mom. They liked to eat pasta with cheese and tomato sauce. Mom gave them each a fork and a napkin. "Please use your fork and napkin, not your fingers and shirt," she said.
Sara and Ben nodded and tried to be good. But Ben saw a jolly bird outside the window. It was red and yellow and blue. It sang a happy song. Ben wanted to see it better. He put his fork down and got up from his chair.
"Ben, where are you going?" Mom asked. "Please sit down and finish your lunch."
"But Mom, look at the bird!" Ben said. He pointed at the window. "It is so jolly and pretty. I want to say hello to it."
Sara looked at the bird too. She thought it was nice, but she was hungry. She picked up Ben's fork and ate his pasta. She liked cheese and tomato sauce. She smiled and said, "Yum, yum, yum."
Mom saw what Sara did. She shook her head and sighed. She got up and went to the window. She opened it and said to the bird, "Hello, jolly bird. You have a lovely voice. But please don't distract my son. He needs to eat his lunch."
The bird heard Mom and nodded. It flew away and sang another song. Ben heard it and smiled. He went back to his chair and saw that Sara had eaten his pasta. He was sad and said, "Hey, that was mine!"
Sara giggled and said, "Sorry, Ben. I was hungry. Do you want some of mine?"
Ben looked at Sara's plate. She had some pasta left. He nodded and said, "Yes, please. Thank you, Sara."
Sara and Ben shared their pasta. They used their forks and napkins. They were happy and full. Mom was proud of them. She gave them each a hug and a kiss. She said, "You are good children. I love you very much."

Sam carried the horn around the woods all day. His friends noticed what he had found, but they were all too scared to touch it. He felt a little bit lonely, walking around with the horn all by himself.
As the day went on, Sam heard strange noises coming from the horn. He couldn't believe his ears, it sounded like music! He looked around and realized he wasn't alone anymore! All his friends had come out to join the fun.
Sam was no longer lonely, he was surrounded by friends who could enjoy the music with him. From that day on, Sam always picked up the horn when he went out to play.

One day, they saw a big hole in the sand. They ran to it and looked inside. There was a copper pot with a lid. It was very old and dirty. Tom felt curious and wanted to open it. Sue felt anxious and wanted to leave it alone.
"Maybe there is treasure inside," Tom said. He reached for the lid.
"Maybe there is a monster inside," Sue said. She pulled Tom's arm.
Tom did not listen. He lifted the lid and looked inside. He saw something move and heard a loud hiss. He felt scared and dropped the lid. He and Sue ran away as fast as they could.
They did not know that they had disturbed a snake that lived in the pot. The snake felt angry and followed them. It wanted to bite them and make them go away.
Tom and Sue did not see the snake behind them. They only felt the wind in their hair and the sand in their shoes. They ran until they reached their mom and dad. They hugged them and told them what they had seen. They felt safe and glad. They did not want to play in the sand anymore.

Tommy loved to watch cartoons on TV. He liked the funny animals and the silly sounds they made. He always laughed when they did something silly or got into trouble. He watched cartoons every day after school.
One day, Tommy had a bad cold. He felt very sick and had a sore throat. He could not go to school or play with his friends. He had to stay in bed and drink hot soup. He was very sad and bored. He wanted to watch cartoons, but his mom said no.
"Mom, please let me watch cartoons," Tommy begged. "I feel very bad and I need something to make me happy."
"Sorry, Tommy, but you can't watch cartoons today," his mom said. "The TV is too loud and it will hurt your ears and your throat. You need to rest and be patient. Maybe tomorrow you will feel better and you can watch cartoons again."
Tommy did not like his mom's answer. He was very angry and unhappy. He did not want to rest or be patient. He wanted to watch cartoons now. He thought his mom was very mean and unfair. He decided to sneak out of bed and turn on the TV when his mom was not looking.
He waited until his mom went to the kitchen to make more soup. Then he got out of bed and tiptoed to the living room. He turned on the TV and found his favorite cartoon channel. He smiled and sat on the couch. He felt very smart and happy.
But he did not notice that his mom had left the soup on the stove. The soup started to boil and bubble. It made a loud noise and a lot of steam. His mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw the soup overflowing and turned off the stove. She was very worried and angry.
She smelled the soup and knew it was burned. She had to throw it away and make a new one. She wasted a lot of time and money. She wondered how the soup got so hot and who left it on the stove. She thought of Tommy and went to check on him.
She walked to the bedroom and saw that Tommy was not there. She heard the TV and followed the sound. She saw Tommy on the couch, watching cartoons. She was very shocked and angry. She turned off the TV and scolded Tommy.
"Tommy, what are you doing here?" she asked. "You are supposed to be in bed. You are very sick and you need to rest. You can't watch cartoons today. You know that. Why did you disobey me?"
Tommy looked at his mom and felt very scared and guilty. He knew he did something wrong. He did not have a good answer. He started to cry.
"I'm sorry, mom," he said. "I just wanted to watch cartoons. I was very sad and bored. I did not mean to make you angry or to burn the soup."

"Like what?" Lily asked.
Ben looked around and saw a pen on the table. He had an idea. He took the pen and put it on top of the blocks. "Look, now the tower is higher!" he said.
Lily frowned. She did not like Ben's idea. She thought the pen did not look good on the tower. She wanted the tower to be all blocks. "No, Ben, that is not a block. That is a pen. Take it off," she said.
Ben shook his head. He liked his idea. He thought the pen made the tower more impressive. "No, Lily, that is a good pen. It makes the tower special. Leave it on," he said.
They started to argue. They both pulled on the pen, trying to take it off or leave it on. They did not notice that the tower was wobbling. Suddenly, the tower fell down with a loud crash. The blocks and the pen scattered on the floor.

They looked at each other and said, "I'm sorry."
They hugged and made up. They decided to work together and build a new tower. They used the blocks and the pen, and they made the most impressive tower ever. They were happy and proud. They had learned to share and cooperate.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to swim in the sea. One day, they saw a big boat with people on it. They wanted to go closer and see what they were doing.
"Let's swim to the boat," Tim said. "Maybe they have something fun to show us."
"I don't know," Sam said. "Mama said we should not go too far from the shore. She said there might be sharks in the water."
"Sharks are not scary," Tim said. "They are just big fish. Come on, don't be a baby."
Tim swam to the boat, and Sam followed him. They saw the people on the boat had long sticks with hooks on them. They were throwing the hooks into the water and pulling them back.
"What are they doing?" Tim asked.
"They are fishing," Sam said. "They are trying to catch fish to eat."
"Can we have some fish too?" Tim asked.
"I don't think so," Sam said. "They might not like us taking their fish. And we have our own food at home."
Tim did not listen to Sam. He saw a hook with a shiny thing on it. He thought it was a toy. He swam to the hook and grabbed it with his mouth.
"Ow!" Tim cried. "This hurts!"
He tried to let go of the hook, but it was stuck in his mouth. He felt a tug on the hook. The people on the boat were pulling him up.
"Help!" Tim shouted. "Sam, help me!"
Sam was scared. He saw Tim was in trouble. He swam to him and tried to bite the hook off. But it was too hard. He could not break it.
"Tim, I'm sorry," Sam said. "I can't help you. You should have listened to Mama. She said we should not go to the boat. She said there might be sharks in the water."
Sam looked around. He saw a big shadow under the water. It was a shark. It was coming to them. It smelled the blood from Tim's mouth.
"Tim, look out!" Sam yelled. "There is a shark!"
But it was too late. The shark opened its mouth and bit Tim. Tim screamed. Sam screamed. The people on the boat screamed. The shark took Tim away.
Sam was alone. He was sad. He wished he had not followed Tim. He wished he had listened to Mama. He swam back to the shore. He hoped Mama would not be too angry with him. He hoped she would still love him. He learned a lesson. He would never go to the boat again. He would never play with hooks again. He would never recommend swimming with sharks.

"Here you go, Sam and Mia. The pizza is ready. Be careful, it might still be hot," she said.
Sam and Mia grabbed the pizza and took a bite. They smiled and chewed. The pizza was yummy. They forgot about being frustrated. They thanked Mom and ate their lunch. Mom smiled and ate her lunch too. She was glad they liked the pizza. She hoped they would learn to be patient.

Once upon a time there was a fisherman who lived in a small village by the sea. He loved going out in his boat every day to fish and he was very happy.

Ben and Lily liked to play with blocks. They could build many things with blocks, like houses, cars, and towers. One day, they wanted to build the biggest tower ever. They used all the blocks they had, and stacked them high and higher.
But they had a problem. The tower was not strong enough. It wobbled and shook when they added more blocks. Ben and Lily did not know what to do. They looked around for something to help them. They saw a fork on the table. It was shiny and pointy.
Ben had an idea. He said, "Let's use the fork to make the tower stronger. We can stick it in the blocks and hold them together." Lily agreed. She said, "Yes, that's a good idea. The fork is important for our tower." They took the fork and ran to their tower.
But they did not ask Mom if they could use the fork. Mom was busy in the kitchen. She did not see them take the fork. She needed the fork to make salad for lunch. She looked for the fork, but she could not find it. She was confused and annoyed. She said, "Where is my fork? I need it for the salad. Who took my fork?"
She went to the living room, where Ben and Lily were playing. She saw their tower, and she saw the fork. It was stuck in the top of the tower. She was angry and shocked. She said, "Ben and Lily, what are you doing? Why did you take my fork? That's not a toy. That's a tool for eating. You could hurt yourself or break the fork. You should not use things without asking. That's not nice or respectful."
Ben and Lily felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to make Mom angry. They did not know the fork was for the salad. They just wanted to build the biggest tower ever. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We did not know. We thought the fork was important for our tower. We wanted to make it strong and tall."
Mom sighed and calmed down. She said, "I understand, Ben and Lily. You have a lot of imagination and creativity. But you also have to be careful and responsible. The fork is important for the salad, not for the tower. The tower is important for you, but not for me. You have to ask before you use things that belong to others. You have to respect their needs and feelings. That's how you show love and kindness."
Ben and Lily nodded and hugged Mom. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We love you and we respect you. We will ask before we use things next time. Can we help you with the salad?" Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said, "Yes, you can. Thank you, Ben and Lily. You are good and sweet. I love you too. Come on, let's go to the kitchen and make the salad together."
The end.

Jenny and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in Sam's room. Sam had a big mattress on the floor. They liked to jump on it and pretend they were flying.
One day, Sam had an idea. He said to Jenny, "Let's play a game. I will close my eyes and you will push me on the mattress. Then I will guess where I am. You have to trust me, okay?"
Jenny nodded. She thought it sounded fun. She pushed Sam on the mattress. He rolled and bounced. He said, "I am in the jungle. I hear monkeys and birds." Jenny laughed. She pushed him again. He said, "I am in the ocean. I feel the waves and the fish." Jenny clapped. She pushed him one more time.
But this time, she pushed him too hard. He flew off the mattress and landed on the floor. He hit his head on the toy box. He cried out loud. Jenny was scared. She ran to him and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. Are you okay?"
Sam rubbed his head. He felt a bump. He was hurt and angry. He said, "You pushed me too hard, Jenny. You didn't trust me. You wanted me to fall. You are a bad friend."
Jenny felt sad and embarrassed. She didn't mean to hurt Sam. She wanted to play with him. She said, "No, Sam. I didn't want you to fall. I was having fun. I am a good friend. Please don't be mad at me."
Sam looked at Jenny. He saw her tears and her sorry face. He remembered how they liked to play together. He felt sorry too. He said, "Okay, Jenny. I'm not mad at you. I know you are a good friend. But please be careful next time. And don't push me too hard."
Jenny smiled. She hugged Sam. She said, "Thank you, Sam. I will be careful. And I will trust you. Can we play again?"
Sam nodded. He hugged Jenny back. He said, "Yes, we can play again. But let's play something else. How about we make a fort with the mattress and the blankets?"
Jenny agreed. They moved the mattress and the blankets. They made a cozy fort. They crawled inside and pretended they were in a castle. They forgot about the bump and the fall. They were happy and best friends again.

"Are we there yet?" Ben asked, looking out the window.
"Soon, buddy, soon," dad said, smiling. "You'll love the yacht. It's big and white and has a sail. It can zoom on the water very fast."
Lily clapped her hands. "I want to zoom on the water too! Can I steer the yacht, dad?"
"Maybe, if you're good," dad said, winking. "But first, we have to meet our friend who owns the yacht. His name is Captain Jack, and he's very nice. He'll show us how to be safe and have fun on the yacht."
They arrived at the beach and saw the yacht waiting for them. It was bigger than they imagined, and it sparkled in the sun. Captain Jack waved at them from the deck and helped them climb aboard.
"Welcome, welcome, my little mates!" he said, giving them each a hug. "Are you ready for an adventure on the sea?"
"Yes, yes, yes!" Ben and Lily shouted, eager to explore the yacht.
Captain Jack showed them around the yacht, pointing out the cabin, the kitchen, the bathroom, and the mast. He gave them each a life jacket and a hat, and told them to always listen to him and their dad.
"Are you ready to zoom?" he asked, starting the engine.
"Yes, yes, yes!" Ben and Lily shouted again, holding their dad's hand.
The yacht zoomed on the water, making waves and splashes. Ben and Lily laughed and cheered, feeling the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They saw dolphins, seagulls, and a lighthouse. They felt happy and free.
But then, they saw something else. Something big and dark and scary. Something that made them scream and hide behind their dad.
It was a pirate ship, and it was coming towards them.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big bird on a branch. The bird was red and yellow and blue. It was very pretty.
"Look, a bird!" Lila said. "I want to touch it."
"No, Lila, you can't touch the bird. It will fly away or bite you." Ben said.
But Lila did not listen. She wanted to touch the bird. She climbed on a bench and leaned over to the branch. She reached out her hand to the bird.
The bird did not like Lila. It was scared and angry. It opened its beak and pecked Lila's finger. Lila cried out loud. She let go of the branch and fell off the bench. She hurt her knee and her finger.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Lila said. "The bird is mean. It hurt me."
Ben ran to Lila and helped her up. He took her to their mom, who was sitting on a bench nearby. She put a band-aid on Lila's finger and kissed her knee.
"Lila, why did you try to touch the bird?" Mom asked.
"I wanted to touch it. It was pretty." Lila said.
"But you can't touch a bird, Lila. It is not a toy. It is a living thing. It has feelings and needs. It does not like to be bothered. You scared it and made it angry. That is why it pecked you." Mom said.
"I'm sorry, Mom. I did not know. I was stupid." Lila said.
"You were not stupid, Lila. You were curious. But you have to be careful and respectful of animals. They are not for us to touch. They are for us to watch and admire. Do you understand?" Mom said.
"Yes, Mom. I understand. I will not touch a bird again. I will only look at it." Lila said.
"That's good, Lila. I'm proud of you. Now, do you want to go back and play with Ben?" Mom said.
"Yes, Mom. Thank you, Mom." Lila said.
Lila hugged Mom and went back to play with Ben. They saw the bird fly away to another tree. They waved to the bird and said goodbye. They learned to be kind and gentle to animals. They had fun in the park.

A stranger walking by noticed Jack staring and said with a kind smile, "It sure seems like a lot of excitement up there! But don't worry, it's nothing to be scared aof."
Still confused, Jack asked him, "What is it?"
"Oh, it's just some planes flying in the sky," the stranger said.
The stranger continued on but Jack stayed, watching the planes in the sky. Gradually, he noticed that the planes had orange tails - like fireworks!
Suddenly, Jack got an idea - he ran home and came back with a sparkler, which he lit and held up in the air. To his surprise, the orange flame seemed to inspire the planes, who flew up and down, spiraling around in circles.
Jack had created a mini war in the sky, and was thrilled by the fireworks he had made!

But then Danny noticed something strange. He could hear a voice from inside the crib! It was his toy bear. He had got lost and was hiding inside to stay safe. Danny's fear quickly went away and he was happy to see his bear was okay.
He opened the crib and hugged the bear. From that moment on, Danny never had to be scared of the dark again.

People heard about the magic tool and came to the man's shop. They were excited to see what it could do. The man showed them how the magic tool could make things move without touching them. Everyone wanted the magic tool and bought many tools from the man. The man was happy and thanked the bird for the idea.

"Yes, it was, Ben!" she says.

When she was finished, Jill stepped back and smiled. The post looked much better now! She grabbed the post and started running around the garden, throwing it up in the sky and catching it.
Just then, her big brother appeared and said, "Hey! What are you doing with that post? That's not yours - it belongs to the neighbours!"

"Is it Elly?" Max asked, looking at the big trunk. "Yes, you guessed it!" Elly said, laughing and coming out from behind the tree. Max and Elly laughed and played the guessing game with their friends until the sun went down.
As the day ended, Elly and Max said goodbye to their friends and went back to their homes. Elly was happy that she had such an adventurous day with her friends. She couldn't wait for the next day to play more games and have more fun in the jungle.

Tom liked to play with his black truck. He had a big yard with dirt and rocks and grass. He drove his truck over the dirt and made tracks. He drove his truck over the rocks and made noise. He drove his truck over the grass and made it flat.
One day, he saw a big hole in the dirt. He wanted to see what was in the hole. He drove his truck closer and closer to the hole. He leaned over the edge and looked down. He saw something shiny and round. He wondered what it was.
He reached out his hand to touch it, but he lost his balance. He fell into the hole with his truck. He was scared and cried. He wanted to get out of the hole. He tried to climb up, but the dirt was too loose. He tried to push his truck up, but it was too heavy.
He remembered that his truck had a button that said "reverse". He pressed the button and hoped it would work. His truck started to move backwards. It made a beep beep sound. It pushed the dirt behind it. It made a path out of the hole.
Tom followed his truck out of the hole. He was happy and relieved. He hugged his truck and thanked it. He decided not to go near the hole again. He drove his truck away from the hole and back to the grass. He played with his truck until it was time to go inside. He learned a new word: reverse.

Bobo was so happy to see the baby bird. He learned that even when bad things happen, sometimes good things can come from it. The moral of the story is to always look for the good, even when things seem bad.

"But it's our car. It belongs to us. We don't want to share it." Ben said.

"Max, no!" Tim and Lily shouted. "That is our cake!"

"That was a bad turn," Tim said. "Now we have no cake for our party."
Lily nodded. "And Max has a brown face from the chocolate. He is a bad dog."
They decided to tell their mom what happened and ask for another cake. They hoped she would not be too mad and that Max would not get sick. They learned that they should not leave their cake alone with a hungry dog.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys on the floor. But today, Mom says they have to study. She gives them a big book with many pictures and words.
"Look, Sara and Tom, this is a book about animals. You can learn their names and sounds. Can you say 'cat'?" Mom asks.
"Cat!" Sara and Tom say together. They point to a picture of a cat.
"Very good! And what does a cat say?" Mom asks.
"Meow!" Sara and Tom say. They make meowing sounds.
Mom smiles. She turns the page. "How about this one? What is this animal?"
Sara and Tom look at the picture. It is a yellow animal with black stripes and a long tail.
"Lion!" Sara says.
"No, no, Sara, that is not a lion. That is a tiger. A lion has a big mane. Can you say 'tiger'?" Mom says.
"Tiger!" Sara says.
"Tiger!" Tom says.
"And what does a tiger say?" Mom asks.
"Roar!" Sara and Tom say. They make roaring sounds.
Mom claps. She turns the page again. "You are doing great, Sara and Tom. Let's see one more animal. What is this one?"
Sara and Tom look at the picture. It is a green animal with a long neck and spots.
"Giraffe!" Tom says.
"Yes, Tom, that is a giraffe. Can you say 'giraffe'?" Mom says.
"Giraffe!" Sara says.
"Giraffe!" Tom says.
"And what does a giraffe say?" Mom asks.
Sara and Tom think. They do not know what a giraffe says.
"Moo?" Sara guesses.
"No, Sara, that is what a cow says. A giraffe does not say moo. A giraffe makes a low sound like this." Mom makes a low sound.
Sara and Tom try to make the same sound. They sound funny.
Mom laughs. She hugs Sara and Tom. "You are very smart, Sara and Tom. You learned a lot of animals today. Do you want a treat?"
"Yes, please!" Sara and Tom say.
Mom goes to the kitchen. She comes back with two apples. She gives one to Sara and one to Tom.
"Here you go, Sara and Tom. Enjoy your apples. They are sweet and juicy." Mom says.
Sara and Tom bite their apples. They make a face.
"Ew!" Sara says.
"Yuck!" Tom says.
They spit out their apples. They look at Mom.
"Mom, these apples are not sweet and juicy. They are sour and bad." Sara says.
"Mom, why did you give us sour and bad apples?" Tom says.
Mom looks at the apples. She sees a sticker on them. It says "lemon".
"Oh, no, Sara and Tom, I am so sorry. I made a mistake. These are not apples. These are lemons. Lemons are sour and bad. They are not for eating. They are for making lemonade." Mom says.
Sara and Tom look at the lemons. They do not like lemons.
"Mom, can we have real apples, please?" Sara says.
"Mom, can we have something else, please?" Tom says.
Mom nods. She takes the lemons away. She brings back two bananas.
"Here you go, Sara and Tom. These are bananas. They are sweet and soft. They are good for you. Can you say 'banana'?" Mom says.
"Banana!" Sara and Tom say.
They peel their bananas. They eat them. They smile.
"Mom, these bananas are good. Thank you, Mom." Sara says.
"Mom, we like bananas. Thank you, Mom." Tom says.
Mom smiles. She kisses Sara and Tom.
"You are welcome, Sara and Tom. I love you, Sara and Tom." Mom says.
"I love you, Mom." Sara and Tom say.
They hug Mom. They are happy. They study and eat and play on the floor.

Now, Tim knew Max was not just amazing, but also very smart. They were happy to be together again. From that day on, Tim and Max stayed best friends forever.

Once upon a time, in a big green field, was a big strong pumpkin. The pumpkin was very light and enjoyed its days in the sun. One day, the pumpkin decided to scatter its seeds around the field. But the sun was becoming too hot and the pumpkin soon started to dry up.
The pumpkin could no longer stay in the sun and wanted to find somewhere cool to stay. It scattered its seeds to the left of the field, but the wind was too strong and they went all the way to the right. The sun continued to get hotter and the pumpkin started melting away.
Soon, there was nothing left of the pumpkin except its dry seeds. Everyone in the field felt very sad and knew that it was important to use time wisely.
The moral of this story is that it is important to be mindful of the time and not scatter your resources too thinly. Otherwise, you will end up with nothing.

Lily and Ben are playing in the garden. They see a big bug on a flower. The bug has many colors and wings. It makes a loud buzz.
"Look, a bug!" Lily says. "It is so pretty and noisy!"
"Can we catch it?" Ben asks. He wants to touch the bug.
"No, we can't," Lily says. "The bug will be scared and sad. We have to leave it alone."
But Ben does not listen. He runs to the flower and tries to grab the bug. The bug flies away and Ben falls down. He hurts his knee and cries.
"Ben, you are silly!" Lily says. "You made the bug leave and you hurt yourself. Why did you do that?"
"I wanted to see the bug," Ben says. He rubs his knee. "It was so pretty and noisy."
Lily feels sorry for Ben. She gives him a hug and a band-aid. She says, "The bug is pretty and noisy, but it is not a toy. It is a living thing. It likes to be free and happy. We can watch the bug, but we can't catch it. Do you understand?"
Ben nods. He says, "I understand. I am sorry, bug. I will leave you alone. Can we still be friends?"
Lily smiles. She says, "Yes, we can still be friends. And maybe the bug will come back and say hello. But we have to be quiet and gentle. Can you do that?"
Ben nods again. He says, "I can do that. I will be quiet and gentle. I like the bug. And I like you, Lily."
Lily and Ben hold hands and sit on the grass. They watch the bug fly from flower to flower. They are quiet and gentle. They are happy.

Sara was a big girl who liked to teach her little brother Ben how to do things. She taught him how to count, how to draw, and how to tie his shoes. Ben loved to learn from Sara and always said thank you.
One day, Sara and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big dog with black and white spots. Sara said, "Look, Ben, that's a spot. Can you say spot?" Ben nodded and said, "Spot. Spot. Spot." He wanted to pet the dog, but Sara said, "No, Ben, you have to ask the owner first. That's polite."
Sara walked up to the lady who had the dog and said, "Hello, can we pet your dog? He has nice spots." The lady smiled and said, "Sure, you can pet him. His name is Spot, too." Sara and Ben were surprised and laughed. They petted Spot and he licked their faces.
Then, Sara said, "Can I teach you something, lady? Do you know how to count to ten?" The lady said, "Yes, I do. Do you want to count with me?" Sara said, "Yes, please." They started to count together, but Sara made a mistake. She said, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, eleven." The lady said, "Oops, you skipped ten. That's okay, everyone makes mistakes sometimes. Can you try again?"
Sara felt embarrassed. She looked at Ben and saw that he was smiling. He said, "Don't worry, Sara, you can do it. You taught me how to count, remember?" Sara smiled back and said, "Thank you, Ben. You're right. I can do it." She counted again and this time she got it right. She said, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten." The lady clapped and said, "Good job, Sara. You're a smart girl and a good teacher."
Sara and Ben hugged each other and said, "We love you, Spot." Spot wagged his tail and barked. They said goodbye to the lady and Spot and went back to their mom. Sara said, "Mom, I learned something today. I learned that it's okay to make mistakes and that I have a great brother." Mom said, "I'm proud of you, Sara. And I'm proud of you, Ben. You're both kind and helpful. You taught me something today, too. You taught me how much I love you."
The end.

The next day she went back to the beehive and she wondered what else she would find. She found a huge strawberry and it made her so happy. She grabbed the strawberry and ran back to her den with it.
The strawberry was so juicy and sweet that Honey ate it all up in one go. She was so full and happy that she went outside and rolled around in the grass.
Honey was so chubby and happy that she went back to the beehive every day to see what other sweet treats she could find.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his red ball. He would kick it all day long. One day, he kicked the ball very far. It went to a distant place, where he could not see it.
Tim walked to find his ball. He saw a small bug. The bug was only an inch long. The bug said, "Hi, Tim! Can you help me find my home?" Tim said, "Yes, I can help you. But first, I need to find my red ball."
They looked for the ball together. They found it under a big tree. Tim was happy. The bug said, "Now, can you help me find my home?" Tim said, "Yes, let's find your home together."
They walked and found the bug's home. It was a tiny hole under a small rock. The bug was happy. "Thank you, Tim!" said the bug. Tim smiled and went back to play with his red ball.

Sara and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big wagon. It is red and shiny. Sara wants to ride in the wagon. Ben wants to pull the wagon.
"Can I ride in the wagon, Ben?" Sara asks.
"OK, Sara. But you have to help me pull it first. It is very heavy," Ben says.
Sara and Ben hold the handle of the wagon. They pull and pull. The wagon moves slowly. Sara and Ben are strong. They pull the wagon to the top of the hill.
"Now I can ride in the wagon, Ben. You can push me down the hill. It will be fun," Sara says.
"OK, Sara. But you have to hold on tight. The hill is very steep," Ben says.
Sara climbs into the wagon. She holds on to the sides. Ben pushes the wagon. The wagon goes fast. Sara and Ben laugh and scream. They have fun in the park.

Once she arrived, the girl couldn't help but marvel at the way the land was so different from her own. She explored, looked at the wild animals, and tried the new foods. She spent the whole day marveling at all the things she never knew existed.
When it was late in the afternoon and it was time for her to go home, her parents were there, both relieved and worried that she'd been gone for so long. "I warned you not to go too far," said her father.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a lazy fox. This fox had a horn. He did not like to work. He would sleep all day and play all night.
One day, a small bird came to the fox. The bird said, "I hate the big, loud horn you blow at night. I cannot sleep." The fox did not care. He kept being lazy and blowing his horn at night.
The bird had a plan. She told all her friends about the lazy fox and his horn. They all came together and took the horn away from the fox. The fox learned that being lazy and not caring about others was not good. From that day on, the fox became a hard worker and never blew his horn at night again. The moral of the story is to be kind and think about how your actions affect others.

Once upon a time, there was a big mosquito. The big mosquito lived in a small house. One day, the big mosquito met a little bug.
"Hello, little bug," said the big mosquito. "Do you want to play with me?"
The little bug said, "Yes, but I am too small to play with you. You are so big."
The big mosquito thought for a moment. "I have an idea," he said. "I can stretch to become small like you!"
So, the big mosquito stretched and stretched. He became small like the little bug. They played together all day long.
But the other bugs did not like the big mosquito being small. They wanted him to be big again. So, the big mosquito stretched and stretched once more. He became big again, and all the bugs were happy. The big mosquito and the little bug stayed friends forever.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Ann. Ann did not like to eat broccoli. One gloomy day, her mom told her to eat her broccoli for lunch. Ann did not want to eat it, but her mom said it was good for her.
Ann had an idea. She thought if she burned the broccoli, her mom would not make her eat it. So, when her mom was not looking, she put the broccoli on the stove. The broccoli started to burn and the house filled with smoke.
The smoke made Ann's mom very sad. The house was smoky and the broccoli was ruined. Ann felt bad for what she did. The moral of the story is to not play with fire and to listen to your mom when she tells you to eat your vegetables.

“I used a special stick to make it”, replied the little girl.

The little girl smiled too. She was so happy to have found such a magical collar. From that day forward, she was always sure to bring her special stick with her wherever she went.

The children quickly gathered the wood and took it back to their house. Using the wood they had found, they built a beautiful birdhouse.
The children felt so proud of their birdhouse and they soon became even wealthier. They thanked the wood for making their family so happy.

Pam put on her warmest coat and hat, and she was ready to go. She was so excited to explore the mill and see what she could find.
When she arrived, the mill was full of surprises. It was bigger than she imagined and she couldn’t believe how generous the people were. They let her explore and gave her some extra treats when she finished.
Pam went home happy and tired. She knew she chose the right clothes to wear. They kept her warm and cozy during her visit to the mill.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They saw many crabs on the rocks. The crabs had big claws and small eyes. They moved very fast.
Ben wanted to catch a crab. He ran after one and tried to grab it. But the crab was too quick and pinched his finger. Ben cried out and let go of the crab. He was angry and kicked the rock. The rock hurt his foot and he cried more.
Lily saw what happened and felt sorry for Ben. She ran to him and gave him a hug. She said, "Don't kick the rock, Ben. It's not nice. The crab was scared of you. That's why it pinched you. Let's find a nice crab to look at."
She took Ben by the hand and led him to a wide pool of water. There they saw a big crab with a blue shell. It was hiding under a seaweed. Lily said, "Look, Ben. This crab is beautiful. It's not mean. It just wants to be safe. Let's watch it and not touch it."
Ben and Lily sat down and watched the crab. They saw it come out of the seaweed and walk around the pool. They saw it find a small fish and eat it. They saw it wave its claws and eyes. They smiled and clapped. They forgot about the pain and had fun. Mom and Dad came and joined them. They all enjoyed the beach and the crabs.

Sara was very happy today. She had a new dress that was pink and shiny. It was a gift from her grandma. Sara wanted to show her dress to everyone in her class.
But when she got to school, no one looked at her dress. They were busy playing with other things. Sara felt sad and angry. She tried to talk to her friends, but they ignored her. They did not listen or answer.
"Why are you ignoring me?" Sara asked Lily, who was playing with a doll. "Don't you like my dress?"
Lily looked at Sara and shrugged. "Your dress is too expensive. It is not for playing. It is for parties. You should not wear it to school."
Sara felt hurt by Lily's words. She did not understand why her dress was a problem. She liked her dress very much. She thought it was pretty and fun.
She decided to ignore Lily and the others. She walked away and found a corner where she could play by herself. She pretended that her dress was a magic dress that could make her fly and sing. She had fun with her imagination.
Soon, the teacher came and called everyone to sit down. She noticed Sara's dress and smiled. She said, "Sara, you have a very beautiful dress today. Did you get it for a special occasion?"
Sara smiled back and said, "Yes, my grandma gave it to me. She said it is for me to feel happy and special."
The teacher nodded and said, "That is very nice of your grandma. You should thank her and tell her how much you love her dress. And you know what? You can wear whatever you want to school, as long as you are comfortable and respectful. Don't let anyone make you feel bad about your dress. It is yours and you can enjoy it."
Sara felt happy again. She thanked the teacher and said, "You are very kind. I like you and I like my dress. And I like my grandma too."
The teacher hugged Sara and said, "I like you too, Sara. You are a sweet and creative girl. Now, let's join the class and learn something new today."
Sara nodded and followed the teacher. She did not care anymore if the others ignored her. She knew that she had a dress that made her happy, a grandma that loved her, and a teacher that cared for her. She felt proud and confident. She was ready to learn and play.

"Mom, help! The dog broke my kite!"
Her mom heard her and came quickly. She saw the dog and the kite. She was angry and brave. She shouted at the dog.
"Bad dog! Go away! Leave my daughter alone!"
The dog was surprised and scared. It let go of the kite and ran away. It did not want to fight with the mom.
Lily hugged her mom. She was glad and safe. She thanked her mom.
"Mom, thank you! You saved me and my kite!"
Her mom hugged her back. She was proud and loving. She comforted her.
"Lily, you're welcome! I love you and your kite!"
They picked up the kite and went home. They fixed the kite with tape and glue. They decided to fly it another day, in a different park, with no dogs. They were happy and hopeful.

Lily and Tom liked to play by the river. The river was cool and made a nice sound. They saw many things in the water: fish, rocks, sticks, and leaves. Sometimes they threw stones and watched the ripples.
One day, they found a big stick that looked like a bow. Tom said, "I can be a hunter with this bow. I can shoot the fish and the birds." Lily said, "No, Tom, that is not nice. The fish and the birds are our friends. You can pretend to shoot the clouds and the trees."
Tom agreed and they took turns with the bow. They aimed at the sky and the forest and made whoosh sounds. They had fun and laughed a lot.
But then, Tom saw a duck swimming in the river. He thought it would be fun to shoot the duck. He did not tell Lily. He took the bow and pulled the stick. He let go and the stick flew towards the duck.
Lily saw what Tom did and shouted, "No, Tom, no! Don't hurt the duck!" The duck heard Lily and saw the stick. It was scared and dived under the water. The stick missed the duck and landed in the river.
Tom felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, duck. I was silly and mean. I won't do it again." Lily said, "It's okay, Tom. I'm glad the duck is safe. But you have to be careful with the bow. It can hurt someone." Tom nodded and said, "You're right, Lily. The bow is not a toy. It is a tool. We should only use it for good things."
They hugged and said sorry to the duck. The duck came out of the water and quacked. It looked at them and nodded. It forgave them and swam away. Lily and Tom smiled and waved. They learned a lesson and went home.

Once upon a time there was a jolly fish. His name was Tommy. One day Tommy was swimming in the ocean when he noticed a little crab.
“Hello,” said Tommy.
The crab said nothing.
“Can you speak?” asked Tommy.
The crab shook his head.
“Oh,” said Tommy. “Do you know a way to talk?”
The crab nodded his head.
“What is it?” asked Tommy.
The crab pointed to his mouth.
Tommy was confused, but then he remembered his mouth was used to talk. He wished he had a crab's mouth too.
“Will you show me how to use my mouth to speak?” asked Tommy.
But the crab just shook his head. He was too scared to answer.
Tommy felt sad that he couldn't talk. He stayed in the ocean for a long time, feeling sad and lonely.
The moral of this story is that it's important to answer questions that someone asks you. If the crab had answered Tommy's question, Tommy wouldn't have felt so sad and lonely.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and fuzzy. Lily wanted to touch it.
She reached out her hand and picked up the caterpillar. It tickled her fingers. She smiled and said, "Hello, caterpillar. You are my friend." She put the caterpillar in her pocket and ran to the house.
She wanted to show her mom and dad her new friend. She ran into the kitchen, where her mom was making lunch. She said, "Mom, look what I found. It is a caterpillar. It is green and fuzzy."
She opened her pocket and took out the caterpillar. But it was not a caterpillar anymore. It was a butterfly. It had wings with many colors. It flew out of her hand and around the room.
Lily was surprised and sad. She said, "Where is my caterpillar? What happened to it? I want it back."
Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't be sad, Lily. Your caterpillar changed into a butterfly. That is what caterpillars do. They make a cocoon and then they open it and become butterflies. They are not your friends. They are wild animals. They need to live outside, not in your pocket."
Lily looked at the butterfly. It was pretty, but she missed her caterpillar. She said, "I'm sorry, butterfly. I didn't know you would change. You can go now. Bye bye, butterfly."
She opened the window and let the butterfly fly away. She watched it until it was gone. She felt a little better. She said, "Maybe I can find another caterpillar in the garden. Or maybe I can make a new friend with a different bug. A bug that doesn't change."
Her mom smiled and said, "That's a good idea, Lily. But remember, bugs are not toys. They are living things. You have to be gentle and careful with them. And you have to let them go when they want to go."
Lily nodded and said, "OK, mom. I will be gentle and careful. And I will let them go. But can I still look at them and talk to them?"
Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. You can look at them and talk to them. But don't put them in your pocket. That is terrible for them. They need air and space and food. They don't like to be in your pocket."
Lily said, "OK, mom. I won't put them in my pocket. I will just look at them and talk to them. And maybe they will talk back to me. Maybe they will say, 'Hello, Lily. You are my friend.'"
Her mom laughed and said, "Maybe they will, Lily. Maybe they will."

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and smooth and had many legs.
"Hello, caterpillar," Lily said. "Do you want to be my friend?"
The caterpillar did not answer. It was busy eating the leaf.
Lily reached out her hand to touch the caterpillar. She wanted to feel how smooth it was. But the caterpillar did not like that. It curled up into a ball and made a hissing sound.
"Ow, caterpillar, you are mean!" Lily said. She felt sad and angry. She wanted to make the caterpillar be her friend.
She tried to grab the caterpillar and put it in her pocket. But the caterpillar did not want to go. It resisted. It wriggled and bit Lily's finger.
"Ouch, caterpillar, you hurt me!" Lily cried. She dropped the caterpillar and ran to her mom.
Mom saw Lily's finger. It was red and swollen. She put some ice on it and gave Lily a hug.
"What happened, Lily?" Mom asked.
"I wanted to play with a caterpillar, but it was mean and it bit me," Lily said.
Mom shook her head. "Lily, you should not touch caterpillars. They are not toys. They are living things. They have their own feelings and needs. They do not like to be bothered or moved. They need to eat and grow and change. Maybe one day, the caterpillar will become a butterfly. Then you can watch it fly and admire its colors. But you have to let it be. Do you understand?"
Lily nodded. She felt sorry for the caterpillar. She realized she had been wrong. She learned to respect the caterpillar and its life.
"Can I say sorry to the caterpillar?" Lily asked.
Mom smiled. "Yes, you can. But be careful. And don't touch it. Just say sorry and leave it alone."
Lily and Mom went back to the garden. They found the caterpillar on the same leaf. It was still eating.
Lily bent down and whispered. "Sorry, caterpillar. I won't bother you again. I hope you become a beautiful butterfly."
The caterpillar did not answer. But it seemed to relax a little. It uncurled and stretched its legs.
Lily and Mom walked away. They left the caterpillar in peace. They did not know that soon, the caterpillar would make a cocoon and transform. They did not know that one day, they would see a bright and smooth butterfly flying in the garden. And they did not know that the butterfly would remember Lily and her words. And it would smile.

Anna loved to sing. She sang all day, at home, at school, and in the park. She wanted to be like the singers she saw on TV, who wore pretty dresses and sang in big buildings. They sang opera, her mom told her. Opera was a kind of singing that was very loud and very long.
One day, Anna and her mom went to the city. They saw many things, like cars, shops, and people. Anna liked the city, but she also wanted to see the big building where the opera singers sang. She asked her mom if they could go there, but her mom said no. She said opera was not for little girls, and it was too expensive and too late.
Anna was sad, but she did not say anything. She followed her mom as they walked around the city. But when they stopped at a crosswalk, Anna saw something. Across the street, there was a big sign that said "Opera Tonight". And next to the sign, there was a door that was open. Anna could hear music coming from the door. It was opera music.
Anna felt a tug in her heart. She wanted to hear more of the opera music. She wanted to see the opera singers. She did not want to wait for the green light. She let go of her mom's hand and ran across the street. She did not see the cars or the people. She only saw the door and the sign.
"Anna, stop!" her mom shouted. But Anna did not hear her. She reached the door and went inside. She wandered into a dark hallway, where the music was louder and clearer. She followed the music, until she came to a big room. It was the opera room. There were many seats, and many people, and a big stage. On the stage, there were opera singers. They wore pretty dresses and suits, and they sang with big voices. Anna was amazed. She had never seen anything like it.
She wanted to get closer. She wanted to see their faces and hear their words. She walked down the aisle, between the seats and the people. She did not care if they looked at her or whispered. She only cared about the opera. She reached the front row, and climbed over the railing. She stepped onto the stage, and walked towards the singers.
The singers did not see her. They were too busy singing and acting. They did not notice the little girl who wandered onto the stage, until it was too late. Anna walked right into the middle of the scene, and bumped into one of the singers. The singer stopped singing, and looked down at her. He was surprised and angry. He shouted at her, "What are you doing here? Get off the stage!"
The music stopped. The lights flashed. The people gasped. Anna was scared. She did not mean to ruin the opera. She did not mean to make the singer angry. She did not know what to do. She looked around, and saw her mom. Her mom was in the audience, and she looked worried and angry too. She called her name, "Anna, come here!"
Anna ran to her mom. She climbed over the railing, and jumped into her arms. Her mom hugged her, and scolded her, "Anna, what were you thinking? You could have been hurt! You could have caused an accident! You should never wander off like that!"
Anna felt sorry. She did not want to make her mom angry. She did not want to cause trouble. She only wanted to see the opera. She whispered, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to sing."
Her mom sighed, and kissed her. She said, "I know, sweetie. I know you love to sing. But opera is not for little girls. Opera is for grown-ups. Maybe when you are older, you can see the opera. But for now, you have to listen to me, and stay with me, and be careful. OK?"
Anna nodded, and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry. I love you."
Her mom smiled, and said, "I love you too, Anna. Now let's go home."
They left the opera room, and walked out of the door. They crossed the street, and took the bus. They went home, and had dinner. Anna did not sing that night. She was too tired, and too ashamed. She went to bed, and dreamed of opera.

One sunny day, a little girl named Amy came to the garden. Amy was looking for her lost toy. Carl saw her and said, "Hello, Amy! What are you looking for?" Amy looked surprised and said, "I lost my toy. Can you help me find it?" Carl agreed to help her.
Together, they searched the garden. As they looked, Carl told Amy to send a message to the butterflies, the bees, and the birds to help them find the toy. Soon, all of Carl's friends joined the search. Finally, a bee found the toy under a big leaf. Amy was very happy, and she thanked Carl and his friends. From that day on, Amy and Carl became best friends, and they played in the ancient garden every day.

When she was ready to put them on, she noticed that the zipper was stuck. She pulled and pulled, but it wouldn't budge. Lucy grew more anxious as she realized her shoe was stuck.
Her mom saw Lucy struggling and came to help. "Don't worry, sweetheart!" Mom said, "I can fix the zipper!" She opened one side of the zipper and saw that it was full of rotted leaves. She picked out the leaves and tried to pull the zipper up. It was still stuck.
Mom had an idea. She grabbed a can of oil and asked Lucy to hold the zipper. Then, she poured the oil onto the zipper and tried one more time. This time it worked! The zipper slid up and Lucy was so happy.
"I'm so glad the zipper is fixed, mom," Lucy said, "Now I can play with my friends!" Mom smiled and kissed Lucy on the forehead.

One day, they found a big tree with a hole in it. They wondered what was inside. Tim said, "Let me look first. I have the axe." He put his head in the hole and saw a shiny thing. He reached for it with his hand.
Suddenly, he felt a sharp pain in his finger. He screamed and pulled his hand out. There was a big rat in the hole. It had bitten him. He dropped the axe and ran to Ben, crying.
Ben saw the blood on Tim's finger. He was scared and angry. He picked up the axe and ran to the hole. He wanted to hit the rat. He shouted, "You bad rat! You hurt my brother!"
But the rat was alert. It heard Ben coming and ran out of the hole. It ran past Ben and into the bushes. Ben swung the axe, but he missed. He almost hit Tim, who was behind him.
Tim saw the axe coming and ducked. He was shocked and scared. He said, "Ben, what are you doing? You could have hit me!"
Ben realized what he had done. He dropped the axe and hugged Tim. He said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I was angry at the rat. I didn't mean to hurt you."
Tim hugged him back. He said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. You were trying to help me."
They went back to their house and told their mom what happened. She cleaned Tim's finger and gave them both a cookie. She said, "I'm glad you're both okay. And I'm proud of you for forgiving each other. That's what brothers do."

“Yes, please!” her friend answered.
Jane quickly climbed the ladder and then lowered her hand down to her friend. Her friend was relieved and quickly grabbed Jane’s hand.

Tom and Anna were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big basket in the grass. They opened it and saw many things inside. There were clothes, books, toys, and food.
"Wow, look at all these things!" Tom said. "Let's take them home and play with them."
Anna nodded and picked up a doll. She smelled it and made a face. "Yuck, this doll is smelly! It smells like old cheese. I don't want it."
Tom picked up a car. He smelled it and made a face too. "Yuck, this car is smelly too! It smells like dirty socks. I don't want it either."
They smelled the other things in the basket and found out that they were all smelly. They wondered why the basket was so smelly and who left it there.
"Maybe someone forgot it here," Tom said. "Or maybe someone wanted to throw it away."
"Or maybe someone wanted to trick us," Anna said. "Maybe they wanted us to take the smelly basket and laugh at us."
They did not like the smelly basket. They decided to leave it where they found it and go back home. They did not want to play with smelly things.
They started to walk away, but then they heard a voice behind them.
"Hey, where are you going with my basket?" the voice said. "That's my basket. Give it back to me."
Tom and Anna turned around and saw a man. He was wearing smelly clothes, smelly shoes, and a smelly hat. He had a smelly beard and a smelly nose. He looked angry and mean.
Tom and Anna were scared. They did not want to talk to the smelly man. They did not want to give him the smelly basket. They wanted to run away.
But the smelly man came closer and closer. He reached out his smelly hand and grabbed the basket.
"Hey, that's mine!" he said. "I found it first. It has all my things. You can't have it."
Tom and Anna did not care. They let go of the basket and ran away as fast as they could. They did not look back. They did not want to see the smelly man or the smelly basket ever again.
They ran all the way home and told their mom what happened. Their mom hugged them and said they were brave. She said they should not touch things that are not theirs. She said they should not complain about things that are smelly. She said they should be happy with what they have.
Tom and Anna agreed. They said they were sorry for taking the smelly basket. They said they were happy with their own clothes, books, toys, and food. They said they did not need anything else.
They went to their room and played with their own things. They forgot about the smelly basket and the smelly man. They were happy and safe. They did not complain.

Sally opened the cage and the bird flew away. But then, she noticed that the lemon was gone! She had dropped it when she let the bird out. Sally and her mom looked everywhere for the lemon. Finally, they found it under a bush. They were very happy and went home to make their cake.

A man hears them. He comes to see. He is not scared. He knows the snake.
"Don't worry, kids," he says. "This is not a bad snake. It is a friendly snake. It is my pet. His name is Ziggy. He likes to lie in the sun and play in the grass. He will not hurt you."
Tom and Anna are surprised. They look at the snake. The snake looks at them. He wags his tail. He seems happy.
"Can we touch him?" Tom asks.
"Sure, if you are gentle," the man says. "He likes to be petted."
Tom and Anna go closer. They touch the snake. The snake feels smooth and warm. He makes a purr sound. He likes them.
Tom and Anna are not scared anymore. They are curious. They ask the man questions about the snake. The man tells them stories about the snake. They learn a lot.
They become friends with the snake. They play with him. They give him a hug. They say goodbye.
They thank the man. They go home. They are not troubled anymore. They are happy. They have a new friend. His name is Ziggy. He is a friendly snake.

One day, they hear a big sound outside. They look out the window and see a big truck. The truck has many boxes and bags. They wonder what is in the truck. They run to the door and ask their mom.
"Mom, what is in the truck?" they ask.
"Those are our things, my dears. We are moving to a new house today. We have to pack and go soon." Mom says.
Anna and Ben feel sad. They do not want to leave their house. They do not want to leave their friends. They do not want to stop dancing.
"Mom, can we dance one more time?" they ask.
"Of course, my dears. You can dance while I finish packing. But hurry up, we have to pass the keys to the new people soon." Mom says.
Anna and Ben smile. They run to their room and turn on the music. They dance with their toys, they dance with their pets, they dance with each other. They are very jolly when they dance.
They dance until they hear Mom call them.
"Come on, my dears. It is time to go. The truck is waiting for us." Mom says.
Anna and Ben turn off the music and grab their bags. They say goodbye to their room, their toys, their pets. They hug each other and walk to the door.
They see the new people waiting for them. They are a mom, a dad, and a little girl. The little girl has a big smile. She sees Anna and Ben and waves at them.
"Hi, I am Lily. I am going to live in your house. Do you like to dance?" she asks.
Anna and Ben look at each other and smile. They nod and say yes.
"Me too! I love to dance. Maybe we can dance together sometime. Do you want to be my friends?" Lily asks.
Anna and Ben nod and say yes.
They pass the keys to Lily's mom and dad. They hug Lily and say goodbye. They get in the truck with their mom and drive away.
They look out the window and see Lily waving at them. They wave back and smile. They are sad to leave, but happy to make a new friend. They hope to dance with her again. They are still jolly when they dance.

Molly was hungry. She sat down at the table.
"I want salad," Molly said.
Her mom put a bowl of salad on the table.
Molly took a few bites, but then she frowned. "This salad is too long!" she said.
Molly's mom tried to explain. "Molly, the salad tastes best when it is crunchy. You need to keep eating it while it is still long."
Molly shook her head. "No, I don't like long salad," she said.
Her mom sighed. "Molly, if you don't eat the salad now, you will be hungry later."
Molly crossed her arms. "I don't want it," she said.
Molly's mom thought for a minute. Then she had an idea. "I know," she said. "Why don't we cut up the salad into tiny pieces? That way you can still enjoy the crunchy taste, but it won't be so long."
Molly smiled. "Yes! I like that idea," she said.
So Molly's mom cut up the salad into tiny pieces. Molly happily ate her salad and was soon full.

Tommy loved spaghetti. He ate it every day for lunch and dinner. He did not like other foods. He did not eat fruits, vegetables, or meat. He only wanted spaghetti.
One day, his mom said, "Tommy, you need to eat other foods too. Spaghetti is good, but not enough. You need to gain some weight and be strong and healthy. How about some chicken and salad?"
Tommy shook his head. He said, "No, thank you, mom. I only want spaghetti. Spaghetti is yummy and makes me happy."
His mom was worried. She said, "Tommy, please try some other foods. They are yummy and good for you too. If you only eat spaghetti, you will get sick and tired. You will not have energy to play and learn. You will miss out on many things."
Tommy did not listen. He said, "No, mom. I don't care. I only want spaghetti. Spaghetti is the best."
The next day, Tommy woke up feeling sick. He had a stomach ache and a fever. He could not get out of bed. He could not go to school or play with his friends. He felt sad and lonely.
His mom came to his room. She said, "Tommy, I'm sorry you are sick. You have eaten too much spaghetti. It has made you ill. You need to eat other foods to get better. Will you try some soup and toast?"
Tommy nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. I'm sorry I did not listen to you. I was wrong. Spaghetti is not the best. I want to eat other foods and be healthy. I want to play and learn and have fun."
His mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Tommy. I'm glad you have learned your lesson. I love you and I want you to be happy and well. Here, have some soup and toast. They will make you feel better."
Tommy ate the soup and toast. He felt a little better. He said, "Thank you, mom. I love you too. Can I have some spaghetti tomorrow?"
His mom laughed. She said, "Yes, Tommy. You can have some spaghetti tomorrow. But not too much. And you have to eat some other foods too. OK?"
Tommy agreed. He said, "OK, mom. I will eat some other foods too. I want to gain some weight and be strong and healthy. And I want to try new things and have fun."
The end.
Moral value: The story teaches the value of eating a balanced diet and listening to your parents' advice. It also shows the consequences of being stubborn and picky.

Billy wanted to go for a run. His mom said that he couldn't go out of their garden, but Billy didn't listen. He put his shoes on and ran to the drain across the street.
When he got there, he was amazed. The drain was really big and had the most delicate little streams of water running all around it. The waters were almost like lazy little rivers winding around each other.
Billy quickly stepped in to discover what it was like on the other side. When suddenly, his mom called out to him, "Billy!!! You are going too far! Get out of the drain right now!"
Billy stopped and thought for a moment. Would he disobey his mom, which led to possible danger, or stay put in the drain. He was conflicted, but then he heard his mom's voice again, more insistent, "Billy, I mean it! Get out now!"
Billy knew he had to choose quickly and cautiously. He decided to take a few steps back and put his foot beside the drain. He said goodbye to the drain, feeling a bit sad, and started to run home. His run was no longer fun, as he thought about the delicate beauty of the drain and what trouble he could have caused if he hadn't listened to his mom in time.

Tom and Ben were brothers who liked to play with tools. They had a big box of tools that their dad gave them. They had saws, screws, nails, and hammers. They liked to build things with the tools, like houses, cars, and boats.
One day, Tom and Ben wanted to build a boat. They found some wood and some nails and started to work. Tom had a hammer and Ben had a saw. They cut the wood and nailed it together. They made a big boat that looked like a ship.
But then, they had a problem. They only had one hammer, and they both wanted to use it. Tom said, "It's my hammer, I found it first." Ben said, "No, it's my hammer, I need it more." They started to fight over the hammer. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They were very angry.
Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom and Ben fighting over the hammer. She was not happy. She said, "Stop fighting, boys. You are brothers, you should share and help each other. Fighting over a hammer is not wise. Do you remember what dad told you about tools?"
Tom and Ben stopped fighting and looked at their mom. They remembered what their dad told them. He said, "Tools are for making things, not for hurting people. Tools are fun, but they can also be dangerous. You have to be careful and respectful with tools. You have to use them the right way and put them away when you are done. And you have to share them with others, because sharing is caring."
Tom and Ben felt sorry for fighting. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We remember what dad said. We were not wise. We will share the hammer and help each other." They gave each other a hug and a smile. They gave the hammer to their mom and said, "Thank you for the tools, mom. We love you."
Their mom smiled and said, "I love you too, boys. I'm glad you remember what dad said. You are wise now. You can have the hammer back, but only if you promise to share it and use it the right way." Tom and Ben nodded and said, "We promise, mom. We will share and use it the right way." They took the hammer and finished their boat. They were happy and proud of their boat. They played with it in the water and had fun. They learned to share and be wise.

One day, Sara and Ben were playing with Bobo in their room, when they heard a loud noise outside. They ran to the window and saw a big truck with a lot of boxes. They wondered what was inside the boxes.
"Maybe they are presents for us!" Sara said.
"Maybe they are new toys!" Ben said.
They ran downstairs to ask their mom, who was in the kitchen. Mom smiled and said, "Yes, they are presents for you, but not for now. They are for Christmas, which is in a few weeks. We have to wait until then to open them."
Sara and Ben felt sad. They wanted to open the presents now. They went back to their room and hugged Bobo.
"Bobo, we wish we could open the presents now. Maybe there is something amazing for you, too. Do you think we can peek inside the boxes?" Sara whispered.
"No, we can't. Mom said we have to wait. Maybe we can pray and ask God to make time go faster." Ben whispered.
They closed their eyes and prayed together. "Dear God, please make Christmas come soon. We want to see what is inside the boxes. We hope there is something amazing for Bobo, too. Thank you, God. Amen."
They opened their eyes and looked at the clock. It was still the same time. They felt disappointed.
"Maybe God is busy. Maybe we have to be patient." Sara said.
"Maybe. But I still want to see the presents." Ben said.
They decided to play with Bobo some more, and pretend that he was a superhero who could fly and save the world. They had fun and forgot about the time.

Inside each box was a new teddy bear, just like Bobo, but bigger and softer. They had different colors and clothes. Sara's teddy bear was pink and had a dress and a hat. Ben's teddy bear was blue and had a shirt and a cap. They also had tags that said their names. Sara's teddy bear was called Lila, and Ben's teddy bear was called Leo.
They hugged their new teddy bears and thanked their mom and dad, who smiled and hugged them back.
"Wow, these are amazing! Thank you, mom and dad!" Sara said.
"Yeah, these are awesome! Thank you, mom and dad!" Ben said.
They looked at Bobo, who was sitting on their bed. They felt sorry for him. They thought he might feel lonely or sad.
"Bobo, don't worry. We still love you. You are our first and best friend. We have a surprise for you, too." Sara said.
They ran to their room and brought back another box with a wrap and a bow. They gave it to Bobo and helped him open it. Inside was a new collar with a bell and a tag that said his name. They put it on him and hugged him.
"Bobo, this is for you. You are a part of our family. You have a new collar and a new bell. You can play with Lila and Leo, too. They are your new friends." Ben said.
Bobo smiled and nodded. He felt happy and loved. He thanked Sara and Ben and God. He played with Lila and Leo and had a lot of fun. He thought that Christmas was a wonderful day. He was glad that he waited and prayed.

After a while, Remy had an idea. "Let's bury the skull and make a secret hiding place!" he said. All his friends agreed, and they started digging a hole in the ground. They put the skull in the hole and covered it with dirt. Then, they placed a big, flat rock on top to mark the spot.
Every day, Remy and his friends would visit their secret hiding place and play with the skull. And every night, they would bury it again, so no one else could find it. They had so much fun and always felt happy in their cheerful forest.
And so, Remy and his friends lived happily ever after, playing in the forest and sharing their secret hiding place. The cheerful forest continued to be a place full of laughter, friendship, and joy.

Ben looked at her and asked, "What is a computer?"
Anna sighed. She tried to explain to Ben what a computer was. She said, "A computer is a thing that helps you do things. You can talk to it and it talks back. You can ask it questions and it gives you answers. You can tell it what to do and it does it. It is like a friend, but not alive."
Ben listened, but he did not understand. He said, "But how does it do that? Where does it get the words and the pictures and the sounds?"
Anna thought for a moment. She did not know how to explain that. She said, "I don't know. It just does. It is very smart, smarter than you and me. Maybe mommy or daddy can explain better. Come on, let's go ask them."
She took Ben by the hand and led him to the living room, where their parents were. She hoped they could explain to Ben what a computer was, and why he should not touch hers.

"Can we make a snowman, Mom?" she asked.
"Sure, we can, but first we have to take a taxi to the park. It's too far to walk in the snow," Mom said.
They waved at a yellow car with a sign on top. It stopped and they got in. The driver said hello and asked where they wanted to go. Mom told him the name of the park.
The taxi drove fast on the road. Lily and Sam looked out the window and saw other cars and people and buildings. They also saw a big red truck with a loud siren. It was a fire truck. It was going to help someone.
"Look, Sam, a fire truck!" Lily said.
"Wow, cool!" Sam said.
They watched the fire truck zoom past them. Then they heard a loud noise. The taxi stopped and the driver said a bad word. Lily and Sam felt a bump. They looked ahead and saw that the fire truck had hit another car. The car was broken and smoking. The fire truck was also damaged. There were people in uniforms and hats who came to help.
"Oh no, what happened?" Mom said.
"There was an accident. The fire truck ran a red light and crashed into the car. We have to wait here until they clear the road," the driver said.
Lily and Sam felt scared and sad. They hoped that no one was hurt. They also felt cold. The taxi had no heat. They shivered and hugged Mom.
"Mom, I'm cold," Lily said.
"Me too," Sam said.
"I know, sweeties. I'm sorry. We have to freeze here for a while. But don't worry, we'll be okay. We have each other," Mom said.
She kissed them and wrapped them in her coat. She told them stories and sang songs to make them feel better. They tried to smile and be brave. They waited and waited for the road to be clear. They hoped to see the park soon. They still wanted to make a snowman. They wanted to have fun in the snow. They wanted to forget the accident. They wanted to have a new day.
