The walk was fine and Lily was enjoying it. She was surprised to find how reliable the stranger was. Little did she know, the stranger had a plan. As they reached the park, the stranger said it was time to go home. Lily was disappointed, but followed the stranger quietly.
On the way back, the stranger stopped at a store. He said that he wanted to buy Lily something as a surprise. Lily felt happy and excited. The stranger bought her a beautiful new dress and gave it to her. She felt so delighted that she thanked the stranger again and again.
Lily returned back home with her new dress. She was excited to show it to her family and the next day she proudly wore it. Everyone praised her for being so brave and trusting the stranger.
Since then, Lily dresses up with her new dress

Once upon a time, there was a cross. It had been sitting in the same spot for a very long time. One day, a careless wind came and started to blow. It spread the cross all over the place. Everything became so messy!
The cross was sad because it had never been away from its spot. But it was excited to explore too. The cross travelled high and low and even bumped into some new friends. It was surprised to see the wonderful things around it.
Soon, the careless wind stopped blowing and the cross was back in its place. Although it missed its adventure, the cross was glad to be back home. It felt happy to be safe and snug again. The cross promised to never be careless again.

Lila and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They gave him two stones for eyes and a smile.
"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Lila said. "Do you like your hat?"
"Yes, I do!" Ben said in a funny voice, pretending to be the snowman. "But I am very cold. Can you give me a hug?"
Lila and Ben laughed and hugged the snowman. They felt his cold and wet snow on their hands and faces.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a big truck with a plow. It was clearing the road from the snow.
"Look out, Mr. Snowman!" Lila shouted. "The truck is coming!"
But it was too late. The truck hit the snowman and broke him into pieces. The hat, the scarf, the carrot and the stones flew in the air. The snowman was gone.
Lila and Ben were very sad. They cried and ran to their mom.
"Mom, mom, the truck killed our snowman!" Lila sobbed.
"Oh, honey, I'm sorry," mom said. "But don't worry, the snowman was not real. He was fake. He was made of snow, and snow melts when it gets warm. See, there is a stream of water where he was."
Lila and Ben looked at the stream. They saw the water sparkling in the sun. They felt a little better.
"Can we make another snowman, mom?" Ben asked.
"Sure, you can," mom said. "But not here. Let's go to the park. There is more snow there. And maybe you can find some friends to play with."
Lila and Ben nodded. They dried their tears and took their gloves and hats. They followed mom to the park, hoping to make a new snowman. And maybe a snowdog, too.

The room was warm, and Mary was feeling happy. She had been playing all day and couldn't wait to have a snack and some playtime before it was time for bed.
Mary settled down to have her snack and gazed out of the window. While she was enjoying her snack, she noticed a judge walking by. He wore a big, long, black robe and had a gavel in his hand.
Mary wondered what the judge was doing and thought that it was strange that he was out and about so late!
The next morning, Mary was very excited because it was her birthday! She had been looking forward to it for weeks and couldn't wait to see what surprises she had in store. That morning she woke up to find that the judge she had seen the night before had left her a very special present – a large, warm, black robe and a gavel.
Mary was so excited she put on the robe and held the gavel tightly. She couldn't believe that a real judge had left a present for her. She knew that someday she would be as important as him and she could not wait to find out what that felt like.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the park with his mom. In the park, there was a tall post. Tom wanted to raise his hand and touch the top of the post. He tried to jump, but he could not reach it. Tom felt uncomfortable because he wanted to touch the post so much.
Tom's mom saw him trying to touch the post. She said, "Tom, do you need help?" Tom nodded his head and said, "Yes, Mom. I want to touch the top of the post, but I can't." Tom's mom smiled and said, "Let me help you."
Tom's mom picked him up and raised him high in the air. Tom was so happy because he could finally touch the post. He said, "Thank you, Mom!" Tom's mom put him down and they continued to play in the park. Tom was no longer uncomfortable and had a great day at the park with his mom.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a kangaroo named Kiki. Kiki had a lot of friends. One day, Kiki and her friends were playing hide and seek. Kiki was very good at this game. She could jump high and far, and she could hide very well. But today, Kiki was feeling a little sorry. She had played a trick on her friend, Tim the turtle, and now he was sad.
Kiki decided to say sorry to Tim. She looked for him everywhere, but she could not find him. "Where could Tim be?" Kiki asked her friend, Bobo the bird. Bobo said, "I saw Tim go to the dark part of the forest." Kiki was scared, but she knew she had to find Tim and say sorry.
Kiki went to the dark part of the forest. She looked and looked, but she could not find Tim. Then, she heard a voice. It was Tim! He was stuck in a hole. Kiki jumped down and helped Tim get out of the hole. "I am so sorry for the trick I played on you," Kiki said to Tim. Tim smiled and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But I have a secret to tell you. I found a magic rock that made me vanish!" Kiki and Tim laughed and played with the magic rock. They knew that saying sorry and forgiving each other was the best way to be friends.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Bob and Jane. They were both three years old and liked to play together. One day, they decided to have a fight. Bob wanted to fight in a round, while Jane wanted to fight in a square. The two friends argued about it for a long time, until Jane said, "Please Bob, let's just fight in a square!"
Bob was feeling very spoiled and didn't want to agree with Jane. But, after a while, he said, "OK, fine. We can fight in a square." Jane was very happy and they both made a big square in the sand with their hands.
Together they each picked a corner of the square to stand in. They both bowed to each other and started to fight! They had a lot of fun pushing, rolling and chasing each other around the square. After a while, they both ran out of energy and stopped fighting.
Bob and Jane laughed and hugged each other, happy that they had been brave enough to fight. From then on, whenever Bob and Jane wanted to have a fight, they would always make a square.

Once upon a time, there was a bird who was different from all the other birds. He wasn't made of feathers, but instead was made out of steel. His name was Soar and although he was a bit dirty, he was very brave.
One day, Soar decided he wanted to fly just like all the other birds. He took some deep breaths and flapped his wings. But couldn't seem to get off the ground. No matter how hard he tried, he couldn't manage to soar.
Just as Soar was about to give up, he heard a voice say, "Don't worry, Soar, I can help you fly". Soar turned around and saw a magic fairy standing before him. the fairy smiled and said, "If you trust me, you can soar". Soar immediately trusted the fairy and the fairy waved her wand.
Suddenly Soar felt a thrill in his body and before he knew it, he was soaring high in the sky like all the other birds. Soar was so happy he started singing, and the other birds joined in. As Soar flew higher and higher, the dirty steel glistened in the sun.

Once upon a time there was a child named Terry who loved to organize things. Every morning Terry would get up early and arrange his toys. One day his mum was trying to organize the kitchen and told Terry to help.
"Come on Terry," his mum said. "Let's organize the cutlery."
Terry was really unhappy because he wanted to play instead. He didn't like the idea of organizing. But he also knew it was important to help his mum. So he took a deep breath and said, "OK, Mum."
Terry started to organize the cutlery and his fingers got sore from all the hard work, but he kept on going until the job was done. By the end of the task Terry was exhausted, but he was also happy to have done something good.
He gave his mum a big hug and said, "Thanks for helping me organize, Mum."
His mum smiled and said, "You're very welcome, Terry. I'm happy to see you were helping your family. And a reward for all that hard work - how about a slice of cake?"
Terry was very happy and this experience taught him valuable lesson: when we help our family, we feel happy and proud of ourselves.

One day, a charming girl named Lucy went for a walk. She saw a big tree with a hole in it. She looked inside and saw something shiny. She said, "I guess there is gold in here!"
A little bird flew by and heard Lucy. The bird said, "I know where more gold is. Follow me!" Lucy followed the bird to a small house. The bird said, "Look inside the house. There is more gold."
Lucy looked inside the house and saw a big, scary bear! The bear said, "This is my house, and that gold is mine!" Lucy was scared, but then she saw the bird fly away with the gold from the tree. The bear was sad, but Lucy had a plan.
She said to the bear, "Let's find the bird and get our gold back together." The bear agreed, and they became friends. They found the bird, and it said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it was your gold." The bird gave the gold back, and they all shared it.
From that day on, Lucy, the bear, and the bird were best friends. They all learned that it was better to share and be kind to each other. And they all lived happily ever after.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play with fire. They found a box of matches in the kitchen and took it to their room. They wanted to see how bright and hot the fire was.
"Look, I can make a fire with this stick!" Ben said, holding a match. He scratched it on the box and it lit up with a yellow flame.
"Wow, let me try!" Sam said, grabbing another match. He did the same and made another fire.
They put the matches on the floor and watched them burn. They liked the sound and the smell of the fire. They did not know that fire was dangerous and could hurt them.
But their mom knew. She smelled the smoke and ran to their room. She saw the matches and the fire and was very angry and scared.
"Ben! Sam! What are you doing? Stop it right now!" she shouted, grabbing a blanket and throwing it over the fire. She took the matches away from them and threw them in the trash.
"Fire is not a toy! It can burn you and the house! You could have been hurt or worse! You are very naughty boys!" she scolded them, with a harsh voice.
Ben and Sam felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to make mom angry or to cause trouble. They did not know fire was bad.
"Mom, we are sorry. We just wanted to play. We did not know fire was bad. Please don't be mad at us," they said, with a small voice.
Mom hugged them and kissed them. She was glad they were not hurt. She loved them very much.
"I'm not mad at you, I'm mad at what you did. Fire is not a toy. It is very dangerous. You must never play with matches or fire again. Do you understand?" she said, with a soft voice.
Ben and Sam nodded. They understood. They learned their lesson. They would never play with matches or fire again. They would listen to mom and be good boys.

Lily wanted to buy a new doll. She saw it in the shop window and it had a pretty dress and long hair. She hoped her mom would give her some money to buy it.
She asked her mom, "Mom, can I have some money for the doll?"
Her mom said, "No, Lily, we don't have enough money for that. We have to save for other things. Maybe you can get it for your birthday."
Lily was sad. She really wanted the doll. She thought of a plan. She waited until her mom was busy and then she took her purse. She hoped her mom would not notice.
She ran to the shop and looked inside the purse. She hoped there was enough money for the doll. But the purse was empty. There was no money at all. Lily felt bad. She had taken her mom's purse for nothing. She wondered what her mom would say.
She went back home and put the purse where she found it. She hoped her mom would not be angry. But her mom was angry. She saw Lily and said, "Lily, did you take my purse?"
Lily nodded. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to buy the doll. But the purse was empty."
Her mom said, "Lily, that was very wrong. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not lie to me. The purse was not empty. There was a surprise for you inside. It was a ticket for the zoo. I wanted to take you there tomorrow. But now you have lost it."
Lily cried. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. I was silly. Can you forgive me?"
Her mom hugged her. She said, "I forgive you, Lily. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be honest and grateful for what you have. And you have to hope for the right things. The doll is not as important as spending time with your family. Maybe we can still go to the zoo another day. But you have to promise me you will never take my purse again."
Lily promised. She said, "I promise, mom. I love you. And I hope you still love me."
Her mom said, "I love you, too, Lily. And I always will."

One day, Lily came home from school and saw her brother Tom in her room. He was holding her diary and reading it. Lily was very angry. She ran to him and snatched her diary away.
"Tom, that is mine! You are not allowed to read it!" she shouted.
Tom laughed and said, "But Lily, your diary is so funny. You write about silly things, like being a princess or a fairy. And you have a crush on Ben from your class. How rare!"
Lily felt embarrassed and hurt. She did not like Tom making fun of her. She said, "Tom, you are mean. You do not understand. My diary is special to me. It is where I keep my secrets and my feelings. You should not read it without my permission. How would you like it if I read your comics or your cards?"
Tom shrugged and said, "I don't care. They are just comics and cards. They are not important."
Lily said, "They are important to you, just like my diary is important to me. Everyone has something that they love and cherish. You should respect that and not tease or bother them. That is what Mom and Dad taught us. That is what being kind and fair means."
Tom thought for a moment. He realized that Lily was right. He had been rude and nosy. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. You are right. I should not have read your diary. It was wrong of me. I will not do it again. Can you forgive me?"
Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I forgive you. But you have to promise me that you will not touch my diary again. And you have to say sorry to Ben too. He is a nice boy and he does not deserve to be laughed at."
Tom nodded and said, "I promise. And I will say sorry to Ben. Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister."
Lily hugged Tom and said, "You are welcome. You are a good brother too. Sometimes."
They both laughed and went downstairs to have some soup. Lily stirred her soup with a big spoon and Tom stirred his soup with a small spoon. They both enjoyed their soup and their conversation. They learned to respect each other's things and feelings. They learned to be kind and fair.

"No, me first!" Sam said.
They pushed and pulled and shouted. They did not share the swing.
A nice old lady was sitting on a bench. She saw the twins and smiled. She walked to them and said, "Hello, children. Why are you fighting?"
"We both want the swing!" Lily and Sam said.
The old lady nodded. She said, "I understand. The swing is very nice. But you know, there is a way to share it. You can take turns. One of you can swing for a little while, and then the other can swing. That way, you can both have fun and be fair. What do you think?"

Soon, all the other animals at the park saw True and Cat acting funny. They all wanted to join in and have fun too. So, all the animals started to act funny, and they all played together. It was a great day at the park for True and his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He lived on a road and liked to ride his bike. One day he decided to ride his bike to a big park.
On his way to the park, he saw a rough road which he had not noticed before. He wanted to take the rough road but his mum told him, "No! That road is rough. It is too dangerous for you."
The little boy was disappointed but he listened to his mum and continued down the smooth road.
When he got to the park, he saw lots of other little kids. He wanted to show them how well he could ride his bike. But before he could show them, he heard a loud crash!
The other kids had decided to take the rough road to the park. They had crashed their bikes and were hurt.
The little boy was glad he had listened to his mum. He realised that it was best to take the smooth road and be safe.
The moral of the story is that it is always wise to take the safe road and never take shortcuts that can be dangerous.

Mr. Fluffy was confused. He did not know what celery was. "What is celery, Lily?" he asked. Lily smiled and said, "Celery is a yummy snack. We can eat it!"
As they talked, they saw a flower bloom near the celery. It was a beautiful red flower. Lily and Mr. Fluffy were very happy to see the flower bloom. They clapped their hands and danced around the celery and the flower.
Lily picked some celery to take home. She said to Mr. Fluffy, "We can share the celery with Mommy and Daddy. They will like it too!" Mr. Fluffy nodded his head and they both went home to enjoy the celery together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a sad, little whale. He lived under the deep blue sea and was feeling awfully alone. One day, he decided to step out of his home and explore the world around him.
He swam and swam, trying to find a friend. Every time he saw a fish, he swam a bit faster, but each fish he saw just quickly swam away from him.
The whale got more and more sad as he realized what a lonely life he was living. But then, as he was ready to turn back home, he saw a friendly fish. He was swimming straight towards the whale!
The whale was overjoyed: finally, he had made a friend. The two swam together all around the sea, playing happy games and exploring beautiful coral reefs.
The little whale was no longer sad. He was thrilled to have a new friend who he could share his adventures with.

The boy got closer and he saw that the mark was made by another person. He realized that the person must have hurt the bird and he got very angry. He wanted to find the person and tell him off.
Suddenly, the boy heard a voice. It was the same person who had made the mark on the ground. The person said, “I am so sorry for what I did. I didn't mean to hurt the bird.” The boy asked the person, “Why did you do it?” The person replied, “I was very angry and my mind was not working properly.”
The boy said, “It's not okay to do something like this when you're angry. You should go to the hospital and talk to someone.” The person agreed and he went to the hospital and talked to a doctor. He learned how to handle his anger better and he never hurt any animals again.
The moral of this story is that it is never okay to hurt animals or other people even if you are angry. You should always find a different way to calm yourself down and get help

Lily and Max are playing in the yard. They have a ball and a stick. They throw the ball and run after it. They hit the stick on the ground and make noise. They are having fun.
But then, a big dog comes out of the fence. The dog is rough and loud. He barks and growls at Lily and Max. He wants the ball and the stick. He runs towards them.
"Go away, dog!" Lily shouts. "This is our yard!"
But the dog does not listen. He jumps and tries to bite Lily and Max. They are scared and run away. They drop the ball and the stick.
The dog grabs the ball and the stick in his mouth. He is happy. He thinks he won the game.
Lily and Max run to the house. They knock on the door. Mom opens the door.
"Mom, mom, a big dog chased us!" Lily cries. "He was rough and tried to bite us!"
"Oh, no, are you okay?" Mom asks. She hugs Lily and Max. "Where is the dog now?"
"He has our ball and our stick!" Max says. "He took them from the yard!"
Mom looks out of the window. She sees the dog playing with the ball and the stick. She knows the dog. He belongs to the neighbor.
"Don't worry, kids," Mom says. "That's Rex. He is not a bad dog. He just likes to play. But he does not know how to share. I will talk to the neighbor and get your ball and your stick back. Come on, let's have some cookies and milk."

Lily and her mom took the lemonade outside to their long, green garden. They sat under a big tree and enjoyed their lemonade together. The sun was shining, the birds were singing, and Lily felt happy. She loved spending time with her mom and making something special with the big, yellow lemon.

Once upon a time there was a chubby rabbit. He lived in a big tall house with lots of stairs. Every day he would hop from one step to another. One day he was so excited that he scattered all around the stairs. He hopped up and down, here and there. He was having so much fun!
Suddenly he heard a loud noise coming from the kitchen. He stopped hopping and froze. It was a cat! The cat had big, green eyes and long, fluffy fur. The rabbit was scared but he was brave. He ran fast and jumped over the stairs. The cat chased him.
The rabbit managed to escape and he ran and ran until he found a big, green bush. He hid behind the bush and waited to see if the cat was gone. When the bunny was sure the cat had gone, he hopped out and kept on exploring!

Spot was sad. He went to his friend, a wise old owl named Hoot. Hoot knew a spell to help Spot. Hoot said, "Stay still, Spot. I will say the spell to make Paws nice." Spot stayed still. Hoot said the spell, and Spot felt happy.
The next day, Spot went to the park. He saw Paws again. This time, Paws was not rude. Paws said, "Hi, Spot! Let's play!" Spot and Paws played all day. They had lots of fun. Spot was glad that Hoot's spell worked. Now Spot and Paws were good friends.

Tim and Sue started to disagree. They both liked different things. Tim liked the bell, and Sue liked the tree. They could not decide which was better.

"Mom, can I have the big chocolate egg?" asked Tim. "No, Tim," said his mom. "It's too big and fragile. It might break. Let's get a small chocolate bar instead."
But Tim did not listen. He took the big chocolate egg and started to walk. He did not see the wet floor sign. Tim slipped and fell. The big chocolate egg broke into many small pieces.
Tim was very sad. He cried and cried. His mom said, "I told you the egg was too fragile. Next time, you should listen and be careful." Tim learned his lesson, but he still had no chocolate to eat.

The next day, Tim went for a jog again. This time, he remembered what his mom said. As he jogged, he saw the tree branch from before. Tim was careful and did not bump his head again. He felt very proud and happy. When he got home, he told his mom, "I did it! I jogged and didn't bump my head!" His mom smiled and said, "Good job, Tim! I'm proud of you."

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with dolls and cars. One day, they find a big black bow in the park. It is shiny and pretty.
"Wow, look at this bow!" Lily says. "Can I have it for my doll?"
"No, I want it for my car!" Tom says. "It is mine!"
They both pull the bow. The bow breaks in two. Lily and Tom are sad and angry.
"You broke the bow!" Lily cries. "You are mean!"
"You broke the bow!" Tom shouts. "You are bad!"
They do not want to play anymore. They sit on the grass and turn away from each other.
A lady comes to the park. She sees the broken bow and the sad children.
"Hello, what happened here?" she asks.
Lily and Tom tell her about the bow. The lady smiles.
"That bow was mine," she says. "I lost it yesterday. I am glad you found it, but I am sorry it broke."
She picks up the pieces of the bow and ties them together. She gives the bow to Lily and Tom.
"Here, you can share the bow," she says. "It is big enough for both of you. Can you say sorry to each other and be friends again?"
Lily and Tom look at the bow and at each other. They feel sorry for being mean and bad.
"I am sorry, Tom," Lily says. "You can have the bow for your car."
"I am sorry, Lily," Tom says. "You can have the bow for your doll."
They hug and smile. They thank the lady and play with the bow. They are happy and friends again.

Finally, Tom jumped high in the air and landed on the shadow. He was so happy and proud of himself. The surprise was that the shadow was his own! Tom laughed and played with his shadow all day long. He knew he had a new friend to play with whenever the sun was out.
